The 2030 men’s World Cup co-host Morocco will be ­favourite to host in 2029 if Infantino is re-elected given his close relationship with King Mohammed VI.

Fifa’s decision to award hosting rights to the first women’s Club World Cup to the US, revealed by the Guardian last month, has strengthened Morocco’s case because the US was in the running for 2029.

A jointly-hosted tournament staged by Morocco and Spain is another possibility. Portugal, the third major 2030 co-host, is understood to have reservations about holding the event.

Sports.title: Nuno Espírito Santo under threat at West Ham after poor start to the season
Sports.content:
Nuno Espírito Santo’s future at West Ham is under threat after a disappointing start to the season. West Ham are struggling to live up to their billing as Championship favourites and dropped to eighth after losing 3-1 to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday.

West Ham are intent on an instant return to the Premier League after Nuno failed to save them from relegation last season, but the setback against West Brom put another dent in their promotion push. West Ham occupy the final playoff spot after consecutive defeats at home and are four points below second placed Swansea. Nuno is expected to be given time to turn the situation around but key figures have become increasingly impatient. The manager faced unrest from supporters during the West Brom game.

The initial expectation was that Nuno would be fired after taking West Ham down last season. Sources indicated that David Sullivan, the club’s largest shareholder at the time, wanted to part company with the former Nottingham Forest manager. Daniel Kretinsky, the Czech billionaire, was in Nuno’s corner and is understood to have argued for continuity.

Sullivan then resigned as a joint-chair and director of West Ham to fight what he described as “false allegations” concerning his personal conduct. Kretinsky became West Ham’s biggest shareholder in September, buying a stake of 46%. The agreement saw Sullivan, who is not on the board, increase his stake from 38% to 40%.

Any decision on Nuno’s future will be a collective board decision. Karim Virani, the interim CEO, and Nils Koppen, the director of recruitment, will have their say. West Ham, who visit Cardiff City on Wednesday, are unhappy after a run of two wins in six games and Nuno is likely to face difficult questions if he cannot inspire an improvement before this month’s international break.

View image in fullscreen Dejected West Ham fans depart early from the London Stadium during their team’s defeat to West Brom at the weekend. Photograph: Martin Dalton/Shutterstock

West Ham turned to Nuno after firing Graham Potter in September 2025. The 52-year-old’s tactics and signings did not convince last season and the problems have continued since relegation. West Ham sold Crysencio Summerville and Mateus Fernandes after going down but they held on to Jarrod Bowen and Tomas Soucek. They broke the EFL transfer record when they signed Arne Engels from Celtic for £22m.

The feeling within West Ham is that they have the best squad in the Championship and should be playing better. But Nuno has struggled to settle on his best 11 and various problems have emerged. West Ham have kept three clean sheets in 13 games. They have started games slowly, conceding the first goal on six occasions.

Their strikers – Joel Piroe, Pablo Felipe and Taty Castellanos – all joined under Nuno and have five league goals between them this season. Bowen is the top scorer with seven but West Ham lack a clear playing identity and have not found the right balance in midfield. The squad contains two holding midfielders but Soungoutou Magassa and Edson Alvarez are both out of favour.

West Ham still hope that Nuno can lead a push up the table. There have been some positive signs, including 6-0 wins over Wrexham and Lincoln, although the latter were reduced to nine men in the first half. West Ham’s best performance of the season was their gritty 1-0 win away to Swansea, suggesting they are better when there is less pressure on them to dominate games.

Sports.title: Furious Matthias Jaissle accuses his Newcastle stars of IGNORING his gameplan against Everton... and relying on long balls against his wishes
Sports.content:
Furious Matthias Jaissle accuses his Newcastle stars of IGNORING his gameplan against Everton... and relying on long balls against his wishes

Matthias Jaissle accused his Newcastle players of failing to follow his plan for the match against Everton – claiming they played long balls against his wishes.

The under-pressure boss, whose side have lost four from five and sit 13th in the Premier League after Monday night’s 1-0 defeat at St James’s Park, saw frontman Will Osula isolated as his team failed to register a shot on target until the 85th minute.

‘There is big frustration and disappointment,’ said the German, who replaced Eddie Howe this summer.

‘We could not transfer what we saw in the week, training in a high level. Since the start of the game, not much was seen. That is difficult to understand.

‘We were not brave enough to break the line and play on the ground. We saw it in training, but there was almost nothing to see from these aspects in the game. In possession, this was not the level we wanted to see.

‘If you just play long balls, it’s not the style Osula prefers and that was not the plan.

'We need to analyse this in depth, why we could not start the game how we planned. I’m responsible for that, to make it work.

‘We have a clear identity of how we want to play. To bring the opposition in stressful situations high in the pitch. We spoke about creating one-on-one situations. The plan was not to shoot the long balls.’

Newcastle frontman Will Osula was unable to make an impression on the game

Matthias Jaissle's side have now lost four of their last five games

Thierno Barry’s second-half goal inflicted Newcastle’s second defeat by Everton in the space of five days, following the 3-1 loss on Merseyside in the Carabao Cup last Thursday.

And Everton boss David Moyes paid tribute to his side. ‘They are so good in what they do as they give everything they’ve got,’ he said.

‘They’re a brilliant group of players and they’ve had it tough as well. They want to keep winning and they’ve found it difficult with the way things have gone, but they’re pulling it out and doing their best to be in all the games.

‘It’s never easy… we beat Newcastle on Thursday night and to beat them again today is not an easy thing to do for any club at this level.

‘To come here and get a good win was a great result for us.’

Sports.title: From Jose Mourinho's Sevilla disaster to Erik ten Hag's dismal group stage exit: Man United's litany of Champions League humiliations since Sir Alex Ferguson - as Michael Carrick fights for his job ahead of Roma clash
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick and Manchester United are enduring the club's worst start to a league season in 40 years, with the Red Devils languishing in 17th place. Their woes in recent years have been well documented, with the club seemingly incapable of finding anyone to match the glory days under Sir Alex Ferguson. Since his departure in 2013, they have had eight managers – seven of whom have managed them in Europe's biggest competition. The three-time champions of Europe have performed particularly poorly in the Champions League in that time, not making it past the quarter-finals once in seven attempts. They have won less than half of their Champions League fixtures since Ferguson left – and only 34 per cent in the current decade. Carrick brought United back into the Champions League last season but since being given the permanent role has hit shocking form And they will be lucky to even reach that stage this season if they continue to play as they have been in the competition, losing to Atletico Madrid away and being embarrassed by Champions League debutants Como. With United set to take on Roma on Tuesday in their fourth game of the competition, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at how each manager on United's carousel has fared in the Champions League... and where it unravelled for all of them.

Your browser does not support iframes.

David Moyes It feels as if it has been an age since David Moyes took the reins at Old Trafford. The Scotsman had a torrid time in his ten-month spell at United. His tenure was characterised by embarrassing losses, a lack of consistency and an inability to transition from the old regime. Moyes was sacked in April after a 2-0 loss to his old Everton side that ended United's hopes of a top-four finish for that season. He was already under serious pressure having been dumped out of the Champions League in the quarter-finals by Bayern Munich. Moyes was handpicked by Ferguson to replace him but didn't even last a season at United The current Everton manager oversaw a 1-1 draw at home in the first leg, with Nemanja Matic's goal being cancelled out by Bastian Schweinsteiger – who moved to Old Trafford a year later. But Bayern – managed by Pep Guardiola – quickly responded to Patrice Evra's goal in the second leg to win it 3-1. They had to battle to even get that far, with a comfortable group stage – four wins and two draws – being followed by an embarrassing 2-0 defeat at Olympiacos in the first leg of the last 16. A Robin van Persie hat-trick in the second leg spared their blushes. Louis van Gaal The big Dutchman came to United with a stellar CV having won both the Champions League and UEFA Cup with Ajax in the 90s, as well as league titles in Spain and Germany. And he seemed the exact kind of serial winner who would be the perfect replacement for Ferguson, but it just didn't work out. Van Gaal spent heavily in the market when he arrived - most notably breaking the British transfer record to secure the services of Angel Di Maria for £59.7million - but he simply couldn't find his feet in England. Van Gaal had just the one season in the Champions League with United before leaving, and it was possibly the most disastrous since Ferguson's departure. They were placed in a group with Wolfsburg, PSV and CSKA Moscow, and were dumped out at the earliest possible stage, finishing third in the group with just eight points. They fell into the Europa League and - after overturning a disastrous 2-1 defeat by Danish side Midtjylland in the first leg of their last-32 game - were sent packing by Liverpool. Jose Mourinho Joining in 2016 after being sacked by Chelsea, Jose Mourinho immediately got busy in the market. And initially it seemed as if he was going to make it work. Paul Pogba and Zlatan Ibrahimovic arrived and United won their first three games. Although their league form dipped, they did go on to win the League Cup and the Europa League in that first season. But then it all began to fall away. Like Van Gaal and Moyes before him, Mourinho only got one try at his favourite competition with United, and exited in a less than graceful manner. Jose won the Europa League whilst in Manchester but never really found success in the big competition He may have won it with Porto in 2004 and Inter six years later but at United he only got as far as the round of 16, and crashed out after a 2-1 home defeat by Sevilla following a 0-0 draw in the first leg. Recently Jose revealed that his relationship with the Red Devils was very nearly different. In his new Netflix biopic, Mourinho, he said that he had agreed to take over straight after Ferguson - only to be lured back to Chelsea by Roman Abramovich instead. Who knows how he would have fared at Old Trafford if he had joined three years earlier. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer Mourinho's successor also had an excellent start to life in the United dugout but ended up being hounded out after a tumultuous three years. When Ole was at the wheel, at first it seemed like United were on course to return to the big time however, slowly but surely, it became clear that it wasn't going to work out. Solskjaer is one of two men on this list to have won the Champions League with United as a player and the Norwegian scored arguably the most historic goal in United's European history, getting the dramatic winner in the 1999 final. And he is probably the only gaffer since Ferguson to have had a positive memorable moment in the competition. It came in Paris in March of 2019, shortly after he took over. After losing 2-0 at home in the first leg of the tie they looked like they were already out but miraculously Ole masterminded a 3-1 victory and won on away goals. Unfortunately that is where the good times as a manager in the Champions League end. After the PSG win United were beaten 4-0 on aggregate by Barcelona and then didn't make it into the competition for the 2019-20 season. They did return with Ole in 2020-21 - only to be knocked out in the group stage, finishing third in a group with PSG, RB Leipzig and Turkish side Basaksehir. They went on to reach the Europa League final that year - losing to Villarreal on penalties - and Solskjaer was gone in November, before the end of next season's group stage. Ralf Rangnick Taking over as interim manager until the end of the 2021-22 campaign - following a caretaker spell from a certain Michael Carrick - Austrian Rangnick was in charge for just three European games. The final game of the group stage saw a 1-1 draw with Swiss side Young Boys, with Mason Greenwood scoring United's goal. Then they took on Atletico Madrid in the last-16, and after a 1-1 draw away, were sent packing with a 1-0 second-leg defeat at Old Trafford. Renan Lodi's header for Atletico Madrid sent United crashing out under Ralf Rangnick Rangnick's spell at United is best remembered for his forthright assessments of the club's dire situation, and he famously likened their situation to that of a patient needing open-heart surgery. 'You don’t even need glasses to see and analyse where the problems are,' he said. 'Now it’s about how do we solve them? It’s not enough to do some minor amendments. In medicine you would say that this is an operation of the open heart. 'If this happens and everyone has realised that this has to happen and if people want to work together then it makes sense and I believe it doesn’t take two or three years to change those things. This can happen within one year.' More than four years on, the fans are still waiting. Erik ten Hag Erik ten Hag came in nine years after Ferguson's exit, and while he brought a League Cup and an FA Cup to Old Trafford it was not enough to stop him being sacked. Like Van Gaal and Solskjaer, Ten Hag's United failed to make it past the group stage of the Champions League. He actually fared even worse than his predecessors by finishing rock bottom of the group in the 2023-24 season, after particularly rough losses away to Copenhagen and Galatasaray. Like Van Gaal and Solskjaer, Ten Hag's United failed to make it past the group stage of the Champions League After a dismal eighth-placed finish in the Premier League the FA Cup win over Manchester City ended that season on a high - and saved Ten Hag's job. He even signed a contract extension that summer, but was ditched by October with United 14th. Michael Carrick Ruben Amorim, who replaced Ten Hag, did not manage United in the Champions League - though he did reach the Europa League final with them in 2025. His sacking in January this year paved the way for Michael Carrick to join as interim and, in steering them to third place, ensured United were back at Europe's top table after two seasons away. That also won him the permanent role, but Carrick has had a torrid start to the new campaign - winning just two of his side's 13 games in all competitions and setting a new club record for the longest winless streak in the Premier League era (nine). One of those wins was in the Champions League against Azerbaijani minnows Sabah, but they followed that with the defeats by Atletico Madrid and Como. Carrick will hope United can finally arrest this run of form at home to Roma on Tuesday, but it will not be easy with the Italians enjoying an excellent start to the season and currently sitting third in Serie A. A win, however, could keep Carrick in a job and breathe some life into a United team that desperately needs it.

Sports.title: Newcastle look like a team bereft of energy and inspiration under Matthias Jaissle - as Everton continue to thrive without Jack Grealish after another impressive victory, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish was pictured enjoying a cracking night out in Newcastle last year. Here, his Everton team-mates had just as good a time, albeit in a far more sober state.

The Manchester City loanee was left at home after last week’s ‘breach of club discipline’. At least, home is where the club hoped he would be.

And, if he was, Grealish would have watched Everton record a deserved win. He might even have raised a toast, so accomplished an away performance was this.

David Moyes had dropped the winger for last Thursday’s 3-1 win over Newcastle in the Carabao Cup after he missed training following another alleged night on the town. And again, without him, they were too good for Matthias Jaissle’s sorry and directionless Newcastle.

It is the Toon Army, rather, in need of a bender right now. They really aren’t very good - no shots on target before injury-time - and it is remarkable to think they would have gone seventh with victory. That position is now occupied by Everton, who were more skilful and more savvy from start to finish and won thanks to Thierno Barry’s goal just after the break. The scoreline was not a reflection of their superiority.

Jaissle said: ‘We were not brave enough to break the line and play on the ground. We saw it in training, but there was almost nothing to see from these aspects in the game.

Everton, who were more skilful and more savvy from start to finish, won thanks to Thierno Barry’s goal just after the break

Jaissle’s promise has been a team who hunt in packs, yet they were hiding en mass here

‘We have a clear identity of how we want to play - to bring the opposition in stressful situations high in the pitch. We spoke about creating one-on-one situations. The plan was not to play the long balls.’

The opening half hour had been a side-show in two managers betraying varying degrees of frustration. Jaissle buried his fist in his palm every time Everton played through his team at will. And Moyes muttered expletives when his side were unable to take advantage. It was clear he sensed this was there to be won. It was less clear how they would achieve that when Barry was swiping at fresh air six yards from goal.

MATCH FACTS Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 4; Dedic 4, Schar 5, Burn 5, Hall 5; Gonzalez 4 (Steur 64, 6), Joelinton 4 (Ramsey 76, 5); Elanga 4 (Murphy 76, 5) Willock 4 (Wissa 64, 5), Barnes 5; Osula 4. Booked: Burn, Schar. Sent off: Ramsey. Manager: Matthias Jaissle 4. Everton (4-2-3-1): Pickford 6; O’Brien 7, Tarkowski 7, Branthwaite 7, Mykolenko 7; Garner 7, Armstrong 7; Rohl 6, DEWSBURY-HALL 8, George 6; Barry 7. Scorer: Barry 49. Booked: George, Johnson. Manager: David Moyes 7. Referee: John Brooks 7. Attendance: 52, 279.

By the 28th minute, the home fans were booing after yet another aimless long ball. Vertical football, Jaissle has called it, getting the ball forward quickly. Yet more boos on the whistle for half-time told you the locals fear they are going backwards. Everton’s Harrison Armstrong, the half’s brightest midfielder, had only just swiped wide from 12 yards when he should have scored, and that would have been deserved.

The Toon Army were soon cheering, when a fella in jeans kicked a ball through a hole to win a trip to Las Vegas. It was the first effort on target by anyone on the field all evening. Newcastle’s first-half woe was summed up by one free-kick, worked short, that was then chipped straight out of play by Amar Dedic. Jaissle shot to his dugout to watch a replay of what had gone wrong - someone should have told him such footage could not be re-shown pre watershed.

The first effort on target brought the first goal in the 49th minute, and it was no surprise when it came Everton’s way. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall played the sort of pass of which Newcastle were seemingly incapable - low, incisive and accurate - and that set Tyrique George away. His shot was not particularly hard, but then Lukas Hornicek’s attempt to save it was not particularly convincing. As the ball squirmed through his grasp, Barry was quickest to follow up for a tap-in. Newcastle appealed offsides against both George and the scorer, but the truth was that Everton’s players were just sharper in every phase. The time afforded to the excellent Dewsbury-Hall to pick that pass was also a scandal.

Jaissle’s promise has been a team who hunt in packs. They were hiding en mass here. The head coach looked to his bench and called for the popular midfielder Sean Steur. The Dutch teenager’s popularity has been enhanced by him not being in the side of late. The cheer for his introduction, as replacement for the leaden-booted Nico Gonzalez, was almost as big as for the sharp-shooter in Levi’s.

Immediately, Steur impacted. From one smart pass to Harvey Barnes the winger crossed and Anthony Elanga almost stole in to score at the far post. The Geordies have been right to call for his involvement in a team so void of inspiration and positive energy.

It was not long, however, before a chorus of ‘attack, attack, attack’ emerged from the Gallowgate End, and that is never a good sign. Substitute Jacob Ramsey was then sent off for a second booking to compound the home misery.

Meanwhile, the fan bound for Vegas was probably checking for the next flight.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish left at home AGAIN for Everton's clash with Newcastle... but boss David Moyes says there IS a way back for on-loan winger
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish was not fit enough to feature for Everton at Newcastle on Monday night after he missed training following a night out last week.

The 31-year-old was dropped for Thursday’s 3-1 Carabao Cup win at home to Newcastle following a ‘breach of club discipline’.

Grealish had failed to show for Monday’s session and it is understood staff struggled to make contact with the winger.

But despite returning to training, the Manchester City loanee was left behind on Merseyside yesterday after it was decided he was still not ready to play. In his absence, the Toffees won 1-0. Everton manager Moyes said after the game: ‘He’s just not available yet.’

Asked if the situation was repairable, the Scot paused, and added: ‘Of course it is.’

Grealish had made four successive starts before he missed Everton’s 2-0 defeat by Arsenal on October 24 due to illness.

He will be given this week to build fitness ahead of Friday’s visit of Coventry.

Jack Grealish missed Everton's Premier League win over Newcastle on Monday night

Daily Mail Sport understands Grealish, 31, is building fitness after being left out of David Moyes's squad for their Carabao Cup tie with the Magpies last week

It is thought Moyes had reservations about re-signing Grealish this summer after similar issues last season. He said he was not sure if the player would be available on Friday.

Moyes backed the 'club decision' following the 3-1 victory, which saw the Toffees advance to the quarter-finals.

'You probably know I’m not going to give any details, it is a club decision and I support that decision. It is something I don’t want to speak too much about,' Moyes said on Thursday.

'The one thing about Everton is that we have got really good values behind it. All the players stand up to the values and accept the values, on the pitch and off the pitch. From that point of view, I think the players did a brilliant job.

'It’s a small squad we have got, we are limited in some areas but we are doing our best to keep challenging. You can see what it meant to the supporters, this is a big moment for them, the players need to keep at it and we are not accepting any excuses. There’s a humility about us tonight.'

Grealish has made seven appearances since rejoining Everton for a second season-long loan spell in the summer.

Sports.title: Nicky Butt tears into 'bluffer' and 'cheat' Lisandro Martinez after his red card against Chelsea - and insists he should be the first player on Man United's chopping block in January
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt has ripped into Lisandro Martinez following the defender's red card at Chelsea on Saturday.

The United centre-back was given his marching orders in the second half of the 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge for picking up two yellow cards in the space of 82 seconds.

The second of those cards came when Martinez flung an arm into the face of Wesley Fofana in the penalty box with the crucial game hanging in the balance. Cole Palmer ultimately squeezed the spot kick past Senne Lammens to secure three points for the Blues.

Martinez has been solely blamed by many for the defeat and Nicky Butt, who has previously criticised the Argentine, ripped into the 28-year-old on Piers Morgan's show Football Uncensored, dubbing him a 'cheat' for elbowing Fofana.

'Performance-wise, he's been lacking so much,' Butt said. 'And again, I was never the best player. I know my level, I know I had a lot of bad games, but one thing I did every time I went out was run myself into the ground. He threw it in the other day.

'He threw it in with that elbow because that was the most obvious thing anybody could do. And the reason he did it is because he's not strong enough to defend properly.'

Nicky Butt has hit out at Man United defender Lisandro Martinez for getting sent off at Chelsea

Butt called Martinez a 'bluffer' and a 'cheat' during a near three-minute-rant on the player

Martinez has hit the headlines more than once in the last month after he hit out at United's Director of Football Jason Wilcox for the club's lack of business, following a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

However, Butt, who was a part of United's famous 1999 treble-winning team, has claimed that if Martinez made those comments as part of former squads, he would have come in for harsh treatment.

'He has got the audacity to go out onto an interview and s**g off the powers that be about buying players when he is not even playing well himself. And if they were going to spend money on players, he'd [ought to] be careful because he's the first one they'd replace.'

He added: 'If it was back in my day, he would have completely had his head ripped off. Everyone would have said, "Who do you think you are talking about me like that with the performances you're putting in?". And even if you're European Player of the Year, you still don't talk like that about your team-mates.

'He has now gone from - I have no idea why - someone that the fans loved to someone the fans loathe and want out of their football club.'

It is not the first time Butt has had his say on Martinez, with the pair embroiled in a feud earlier this year. Back in January, Martinez hit back at comments made by Paul Scholes and Butt mocking his size, and dared the former United duo to repeat them to his face.

Martinez was given his marching orders and conceded a penalty after striking Wesley Fofana's face during a 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge

The Argentine told them they can come 'to my house' and 11 months on Butt started his near-three-minute rant by referencing the back and forth.

'That lad's a bluffer, full stop,' Butt said. The Butcher his nickname is. With him, he called out my mate; it was probably my fault because I said something tongue-in-cheek on a podcast.

'It was like, "Haaland would pick up and carry him". It was tongue-in-cheek, even though Solanke did it one week ago.

'He's come out and called out a player who has won 11 Premier Leagues for Manchester United, and played for god knows how many years, about you come and see me and knock on my front door.

'You can't say anything about these players because they get all touchy with it.'

Sports.title: Ex-Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United star Sebastien Bassong is fined for dodging £7 Tube fare by using someone else's travelcard
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Sebastien Bassong has been fined for dodging a £7 Tube fare after he was caught using someone else's train driver pass illegally.

The Frenchman, 40, who spent several seasons in the Premier League with Spurs, Newcastle and Norwich, was stopped by a Transport for London (TfL) officer after he was spotted tailgating a friend through the barriers at St Paul's station in May.

The ex-footballer was carrying the Oystercard of the friend's ex-girlfriend, which had been issued to her as a driver on the Docklands Light Railway (DLR), court documents showed.

The TfL officer was then told that Bassong, who was an £8 million signing for Spurs in 2009, had been using her travelcard because he was 'experiencing financial and personal hardship due to a divorce and unemployment'.

Bassong was convicted of using the rail network without a valid ticket at Wimbledon Magistrates Court on October 30.

Magistrate Graham Burbage fined him £220, ordered him to pay the £7 fare for his journey from Arnos Grove to St Paul's, and directed him to pay £250 in prosecution costs and an £88 victim surcharge.

Bassong did not enter a plea to the charge, and was convicted behind closed doors in a Single Justice Procedure hearing.

Adebukola Anifowose, a revenue control officer for TfL, told the court in a statement she spotted Bassong at 1.08pm 'pretend to tap an Oystercard enclosed in a white wallet before tailgating through the wide-aisle gate behind another male'.

Sebastien Bassong in action during a Premier League match between Chelsea and Tottenham at Stamford Bridge in 2009

Bassong attended the 2026 PFA Awards at the Manchester Opera House

The star playing for Spurs during the UEFA Champions League match between BSC Young Boys and Tottenham Hotspur in 2010

She said Bassong offered up a TfL staff nominee pass when challenged, which allows free travel on London transport.

'System checks later confirmed that the pass did not belong to him and had last been used in October 2025,' she said.

'The accompanying male was spoken to – this individual later informed me that he was assisting Mr Bassong, who was experiencing financial and personal hardship due to a divorce and unemployment, by providing him with the nominee pass.

'It was subsequently established that the pass was registered to an ex-girlfriend of this male, who reportedly claimed to be a DLR driver.'

A notice about the prosecution was sent to Bassong's north London home, and he did not respond before the court hearing.

Bassong, who now runs a motivational coaching business, has been given 28 days to settle the court bill totalling £565.

Sports.title: This is the England starting XV Steve Borthwick should pick to beat Australia - all the key selection battles from flying full-backs to race for No10, and what to do with Henry Pollock
Sports.content:
This is the England starting XV Steve Borthwick should pick to beat Australia - all the key selection battles from flying full-backs to race for No10, and what to do with Henry Pollock

Steve Borthwick yesterday named a 36-man squad for England’s crunch Nations Championship opener with Australia on Sunday at Twickenham.

It was one without injured scrum-halves Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland but it did include first-choice No10 Fin Smith, despite the Northampton man's calf worry.

England are preparing for four crucial matches this month which will start the countdown for next year’s World Cup, with a raft of selection battles across the starting lineup.

Here, Daily Mail Sport’s ALEX BYWATER assesses how Borthwick’s party is shaping up for the Wallabies on Sunday - and picks his starters to take down the Wallabies.

Steve Borthwick as named his 36-man squad for the autumn slate of the Nations Championship

Front row

Promising 21-year-old hooker Kepu Tuipulotu suffered a leg injury in England training last week and has been replaced by Saracens' Theo Dan.

England’s front row has significant experience otherwise and pretty much picks itself - Jamie George is the likely starting hooker with Ellis Genge and Joe Heyes propping up the scrum either side of him.

Luke Cowan-Dickie and the fit-again prop pair Fin Baxter and Will Stuart provide strong options from the bench.

Daily Mail Sport’s starters: Ellis Genge, Jamie George, Joe Heyes

Second row

After missing the summer as part of a scheduled rest period, Maro Itoje is back in the England squad and is close to certain to start at lock against Australia as captain.

Even though his club side Saracens have struggled so far this season, Itoje demands inclusion. The question is who partners him.

Ollie Chessum, fresh from signing a new Leicester deal, has been in regal form and is now one of England’s best and most important players. But despite him playing lock at club level, it seems Borthwick wants him to provide extra physicality and another lineout jumping option in the No 6 jersey, where he starred in the Stade de France in March.

That leaves a space for either Alex Coles or George Martin. Martin’s grunt is invaluable, but Northampton's Coles has shown more so far this term.

Daily Mail Sport’s starters: Maro Itoje (captain), Alex Coles

Second-rowers Ollie Chessum, Alex Coles and Maro Itoje have been in fine form, and Chessum's versatility means he should slide over to No6

Back row

England have a wealth of resources in this area but also questions to answer.

Chessum excelled on the blindside flank in the Six Nations finale with France. But in their recent struggles, England have struggled to get their breakdown firing.

Borthwick has pointed out the difference between the way the ruck is refereed at PREM level and internationally and that his team has to adapt better. Issues there have led to England conceding too many penalties and subsequently, yellow cards.

Australia are dangerous but inconsistent. They do, however, play with pace and are battle-hardened from a busy summer schedule, which included beating a weakened South Africa side. England, by contrast, only arrived at their Pennyhill Park base on Monday night and haven’t played since July.

‘Facing Australia is an exciting challenge,' said Borthwick. 'They have played a significant amount of Test rugby in recent months. We know the quality and experience they will bring,’ Borthwick admitted.

To slow down the Wallabies, Borthwick’s most sensible bet is to go with the experience of Tom Curry in the No7 jersey, alongside Chessum and Ben Earl who is an automatic pick at No8. That can leave Henry Pollock to bring his athleticism and dynamism from the bench in a battle with a team he scored against this time last year.

Daily Mail Sport’s starters: Ollie Chessum, Tom Curry, Ben Earl

Half-backs

This is where England’s problems begin. Mitchell and McParland were two of England’s three scrum-halves in training last week, alongside Jack van Poortvliet.

Mitchell is awaiting the results of a scan on a hamstring injury suffered in club action for Northampton against Gloucester, but won't face Australia as he wasn’t named in Borthwick’s squad for the game. Neither was McParland who suffered a calf problem in England camp last week.

Leicester's Jack van Poortvliet and Northampton's Fin Smith (both centre) got to grips in their recent PREM clash - now they need to put England on their back and lead them to victory

That leaves Leicester's Van Poortvliet as the man to start, with one of Ben Spencer or Harry Randall – who have both had late call-ups – in reserve.

There is also a lack of clarity at No10. England are hopeful Smith will recover from a calf injury of his own to start against Australia. Marcus Smith and George Ford are the other options. Fin Smith has to start if fit. But if not, namesake Marcus is in better form than Ford and would deserve a chance.

Daily Mail Sport’s starters: Jack van Poortvliet, Fin Smith

Centres

This has been England’s big problem for a long time now. Seb Atkinson is the man in pole position at inside centre and played well for Gloucester at Northampton at the weekend, proving he is over his knee issue.

Who starts in the No 13 shirt is a bigger question. After missing the 2023 World Cup, Henry Slade is now back in favour.

One of Will Joseph or Joe Marchant would be bolder picks and the former, who has just one cap, has been a form horse in the PREM. But Borthwick places a great deal of emphasis on cohesion. Slade is the right call for this game.

Daily Mail Sport’s starters: Seb Atkinson, Henry Slade

Borthwick places a great deal of emphasis on cohesion and the returning Henry Slade is the right call for this game

Back three

Immanuel Feyi-Waboso has shown defensive frailties for Exeter, but his game-breaking ability means he has to start on the wing after he played club rugby last week following a hamstring worry.

Borthwick has dallied with Tommy Freeman at outside centre, but he has to start on the other wing to Feyi-Waboso. It's not rocket science - pick your best players in their best positions.

Full-back is a straight shootout between George Furbank and Freddie Steward. Furbank has had rotten luck at Test level, summed up by the appendicitis that forced him to miss South Africa in July. His ball-playing ability makes him perfect to help what has been a stuttering England attack.

But Freddie Steward is pushing him hard, after revitalising his game at Borthwick’s request. Whichever Smith starts at fly-half, Furbank knows both well as team-mates past and present, so that’s an extra tick in his box.

Daily Mail Sport’s starters: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman, George Furbank

George Furbank is in a tight race for the No15 shirt with Freddie Steward but his partnerships with Fin and Marcus Smith may just settle the matter

Sports.title: Spanish match abandoned as footballer is rushed to hospital after sickening collision with goalkeeper left him unconscious - with team-mates in tears as he is revived in ambulance
Sports.content:
Tenerife striker Jesus de ​Miguel has been admitted to intensive care after collapsing during a Spanish second division clash with Andorra on Monday.

The 30-year-old is in stable condition, the club has confirmed, after a horrifying collision with goalkeeper ‌Jesus Owono led to the fixture being abandoned deep into stoppage time with the scores level at 2-2.

A club statement read: 'CD Tenerife player Jesús de Miguel is admitted to the ICU at the University Hospital of Nuestra Señora de Candelaria, stable despite the severity of his condition.

'The medical services at said hospital will be present and will report when there are updates.'

De Miguel is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance, according to Spanish media outlet Marca.

It has also been reported that while the Spaniard is stable, he remains unconscious.

Jesus de ​Miguel (pictured playing for former club Castellon) has been taken to intensive care

Tenerife's De ​Miguel was wiped out by Jesus Owono during a Spanish second tier match

The game had entered the seventh minute of stoppage time when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker appeared to be struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

De Miguel was seen to for over five minutes while his team-mates were visibly distressed, with some appearing to be in tears.

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

The stadium has been in complete silence while De Miguel was being treated, but as he was taken off the pitch the striker was given a standing ovation by the crowd.

De Miguel was rushed to hospital following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch

After being taken to an ambulance on a stretcher, there is believed to have been an approximate 15-minute wait before they made their way to the hospital.

Andorra also released a statement, which read: 'We want to send all our strength and best wishes to Jesus de Miguel after the serious incident suffered during today's match.

'We hope he recovers soon. A very strong hug to the player, his family and Tenerife.'

Despite remaining unconcsious in intensive care the player is believed to be 'breathing on his own'.

Sports.title: Footballer in intensive care after sickening foul sees Spanish second tier match abandoned
Sports.content:
Footballer in intensive care after sickening foul sees Spanish second tier match abandoned

The Segunda Division match between Tenerife and Andorra was abandoned in stoppage time after Jesus Owono collided with Jesus de Miguel, who suffered serious injuries

View 2 Images Both sets of players were visibly distressed

Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel is in a stable condition in intensive care after being on the receiving end of a sickening foul - before going into cardiac arrest. The incident happened on Monday during a match between Tenerife and Andorra in the Spanish second division, which was level at 2-2 before the referee chose to abandon the game in stoppage time.

‌



‌



De Miguel, 30, sustained injuries around his head and chest after Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono came rushing out to clear a long ball and appeared to hit the Spaniard with his knee. De Miguel was left laying motionless inside the centre circle, with some players in tears while he received medical attention. Footage shows Owono making a U-turn to check on De Miguel.

‌



On his way to hospital, the Madrid-born forward suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated by paramedics in the ambulance. Tenerife confirmed in a statement that the De Miguel was admitted to the University Hospital of Nuestra Senora de Candelaria on the island and is 'stable despite the severity of his condition'.

‌



"The medical services at said hospital will be present and will report when there are updates," the club added.

Andorra posted on social media: "We want to send all our strength and best wishes to Jesus de Miguel after the serious incident suffered during today's match.

"We hope he recovers soon. A very strong hug to the player, his family and Tenerife."

Owono's red card was the third of the match. Earlier in the game, Tenerife had surrendered their 2-0 lead which came courtesy of first-half goals from Christian Gomis and Enric Gallego.

Andorra's Lautaro De Leon replied with a penalty in the 83rd minute, but he was remarkably sent off after a skirmish with Tenerife goalkeeper Dani Martin while attempting to get the ball back. Martin was then shown two yellow cards in quick succession, and Andorra soon found an equaliser through Stefan Golubovic to set up a grandstand finish at Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.

De Miguel signed for Tenerife in 2025, signing a three-year contract after the club had been relegated to the third tier. He helped Tenerife earn promotion back to the Segunda Division, scoring 11 goals in 29 games along the way. After spending most of his career in the lower leagues, De Miguel played his first professional match with Castellon in 2024.

Sports.title: Man Utd told only two managers can turn them around if Michael Carrick is sacked
Sports.content:
Man Utd told only two managers can turn them around if Michael Carrick is sacked

Manchester United have been sent a message about potential replacements for Michael Carrick as the club's manager

View 2 Images Michael Carrick, manager of Manchester United (Image: Pedro Porru/MB Media/Getty Images)

Former Liverpool star Jamie Redknapp has explained why there are only two suitable candidates to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United. Carrick has faced an uncertain future in the Old Trafford dugout over the last few weeks, with the rumours intensifying amid their ongoing struggles in the Premier League.

‌



‌



United lost 2-0 to Chelsea at the weekend and are now in 17th place in the table, and are only outside of the relegation zone on goal difference. Bottom-placed Sunderland are only two points behind United in the Premier League standings.

‌



The last time United won a Premier League game was on August 30 against Ipswich Town, and the club are now without a victory in all competitions in nine matches.

‌



Consequently, there have been suggestions that United might be considering a managerial change, despite only appointing Carrick to the role permanently during the summer.

The 4 Man Utd stars Michael Carrick should be pointing his finger at after Chelsea farce READ MORE :

Redknapp has contended that ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and current Aston Villa manager Unai Emery would be the only realistic options for the United position should the club opt for a change.

"There are only, I think, two runners," Redknapp told Sky Sports. "Listen, Michael Carrick is still in the job, so it's unfair to be saying it.

‌



"But if that's the case, if this doesn't improve, it's inevitable that he's going to lose his job.

"It can only be him [Emery] really and Eddie Howe."

‌



Redknapp also shared his thoughts on former Bayern Munich boss Julian Nagelsmann, who has been linked with the United job since stepping down as Germany's national team manager in the summer.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

‌



View 2 Images Eddie Howe has been mentioned as a potential Carrick replacement (Image: Getty Images)

"Julian Nagelsmann has done pretty well in Germany," Redknapp said. "I think he started off his career so good... last few years, not quite so good, obviously with Germany at the World Cup.

‌



"I can only really see him [Emery]. It depends, does he want to leave Aston Villa? He's got a project, he can do what he likes there, he's running the club, whatever he says goes.

"But he might think, 'This is the challenge for me', and every manager has an ego. Everyone will believe that they can turn Manchester United around, they will genuinely believe that.

‌



"With his abilities, he would probably be the only one that I would trust to be able to do it.

"I don't believe anyone else is just going to go in there with a manager and an assistant and change it. There are so many things behind the scenes that need to change."

Sports.title: Nicky Butt demands Lisandro Martinez is axed from Man Utd in extraordinary rant
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United star Nicky Butt has lambasted 'bluffer' Lisandro Martinez and called for him to be sold in an extraordinary rant. Martinez, 28, topped off a woeful October during Saturday's dire 2-0 defeat away to Chelsea by getting sent off after conceding a penalty for an elbow.

It came little over a fortnight after the Argentine hit out at the club's board in an explosive post-match interview. Martinez slammed the United hierarchy for not doing enough in the transfer window, criticising director of football Jason Wilcox.

The defender was fined for his comments but has remained a starter for Michael Carrick's floundering side - despite his string of errors, such as when he was outmuscled by Tottenham striker Dominic Solanke and allowed him to score a stoppage-time equaliser earlier this month. Butt is fed up with Martinez - who he and Paul Scholes have history with - and would sell him if he was in charge.

"That lad's a bluffer, full stop," the ex-United midfielder began on Football Uncensored. "Just a bluffer. The Butcher, his nickname is. I mean it's... yeah."

‌

"He called out my mate (Scholes) and it was probably my fault, I said something tongue-in-cheek on a podcast and it was like, '[Erling] Haaland would pick up and carry him'. It was tongue in cheek, I didn't think for one minute he would even though Solanke did about a week ago.

"But with him, he's come out and called out a player (Scholes) who's won 11 Premier Leagues for Man United and played for god knows how many years. 'You come and see me and knock on my front door', you can't speak anything about these players because they get all touchy with it.

‌



"Then he's got the audacity to go out onto an interview and slag off the powers that be about buying players when he's not even playing well himself. If they were going to go and buy players, he'd be careful because he's the first one they'd replace. Performance-wise, he's been lacking so much.

"Listen, I was never the best player; I know my level, I know I had a lot of bad games. But one thing I did every single time I went out was ran my myself into the ground and was honest when looking at my team-mates in the eye and said, 'I gave you everything I've got. I might've been crap today but I worked hard'.

Do you agree with Nicky Butt? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez had a nightmare October (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



"He (Martinez) threw it in the other day. He threw it in with that elbow because that was the most obvious thing anyone could do. The reason why he did it is because he's not strong enough to defend properly.

"He thought, 'You know what, I'll cut corners, I'll cheat, I'll put my elbow is someone's face and I'll get sent off and I'll leave all the other 10 lads, who by the way I said two weeks ago that these aren't good enough to play with me'.

"I'm getting changed in the changing room and I'm sitting next to these lads and they're going, 'he thinks I'm not good enough'. If that was back in my day, he would've completely have had his head ripped off. Everyone would've said, 'who do you think you are talking about me like that with the performances you're putting in?'

"Even if he was European Player of the Year, you still don't speak like that about your team-mates and your powers that be upstairs. No matter what you think behind closed doors, you don't go and say that.

‌



"He has now gone from - I don't know why, I have no idea why - he's gone from someone the fans love to someone the fans loathe and want out of their football club. He's absolutely killed himself.

"Not only that, he lives in our country and he's dancing around with an Argentinian flag in the World Cup. What are you doing? And you expect people to go and pat your on the back when you've had a bad game.

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez held the flag referencing the Falkland Islands (Image: Sebastian Frej/Getty Images)

"Some of these people need to understand... so what if you're on £200,000 a week and you're driving your Rolls Royce through your little village thinking you're King Dick. You can do that all you want but you can't have people tapping you on the back when you're playing so badly and you're slagging people off.

‌



"So I agree with you, Piers (Morgan), I'd be taking him straight out."

Regarding his reference to Martinez's behaviour at the World Cup, he was among the Argentina players to hold a flag which claimed that the Falklands Islands belonged to their country rather than the UK. It came after they beat England 2-1 in the semi-finals.

Martinez will be banned for United's next Premier League game at home to Aston Villa on Sunday. But the 28-year-old is available for Tuesday's Champions League clash with Roma in which the Red Devils will aim to win their first game after nine without a victory.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League boss Pepe Mel in intensive care after suffering stroke
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League boss Pepe Mel in intensive care after suffering stroke

Pepe Mel had a brief stint as manager of West Bromwich Albion during the 2013-14 season, one of 16 different clubs he's taken charge of across his long coaching career

View Image Pepe Mel needed surgery after his stroke (Image: Rafa Babot/Getty Images)

Former West Bromwich Albion manager Pepe Mel is recovering in intensive care after he suffered a stroke. Mel, 63, had to undergo surgery after having the stroke on Sunday.

‌



The Spaniard underwent a successful operation and is now recovering at Virgen del Rocio Hospital in Seville. Real Betis, who Mel managed twice, announced the news at the request of his family.

"From Real Betis, we send all the support in the world to Pepe Mel, whom we wish a speedy recovery," the La Liga side posted on social media platform X. "We're with you, Pepe."

A product of Real Madrid's academy, most of Mel's career has been in Spain. West Brom were one of 16 different clubs that he's managed over a 27-year period, starting in 1999.

Mel took over at the Hawthorns in January 2014, with Steve Clarke having been sacked the previous month. At the time, West Brom were hovering four points above the relegation zone and there was growing discontent inside the dressing room.

Although the Baggies survived under Mel, they only finished one place above the drop. He oversaw just three wins in 17 matches while drawing six and losing eight.

Mel was sacked the day after their final game of the season. West Brom sporting and technical director Richard Garlick explained that decision was made due to events both 'on and off the field'.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Mel's most recent position was in Morocco with IR Tangier. Mel left his post in March to bring to an end a brief seven-game spell.

Alongside Betis, more of Mel's former clubs have sent him messages of support. "From Rayo Vallecano, we want to convey all our support and affection to Pepe Mel, after suffering a stroke for which he has had to undergo surgery. We wish him a swift and complete recovery," the Spanish club posted.

Another message read: "From La Liga we send all our affection and a speedy recovery to Pepe Mel. We're with you, Pepe."

Sports.title: Leeds fan dies after medical emergency at Man Utd clash as club pay tribute
Sports.content:
Leeds fan dies after medical emergency at Man Utd clash as club pay tribute

A Leeds supporter suffered a medical emergency during their 1-1 draw with Manchester United last month, leading to him being rushed to hospital and put on life support

View Image Leeds have paid tribute to the supporter (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

Leeds have paid tribute to a fan who sadly died after suffering a medical emergency in the stands during their game against Manchester United last month. Colin Westby, 68, was watching the Premier League clash which took place at Elland Road on Sunday, October 18 before being rushed to hospital.

‌



‌



Upon his arrival, Westby was placed medically induced coma. Leeds said in a statement that after a 'period of unresponsiveness', the decision was made to withdraw life support.

‌



The club posted on their website: "Leeds United are heartbroken to learn of the passing of supporter Colin Westby at the age of 68. Colin was a long-standing Season Ticket Holder at the club, attending matches for over 50 years.

‌



"We will pay tribute to Colin in the 68th minute of our next Premier League fixture with Tottenham Hotspur, on Saturday 7 November."

Full plans for Saturday's tribute are yet to be released. Following Westby's illness, Leeds praised the supporters and stewards who ensured that he received medical attention as soon as possible.

A statement at the time read: "The club is grateful for the rapid action of our stewards and medical support team and appreciates the many notes of interest and support that have been sent in the past 24 hours."

‌



Tributes to Westby continue to flood in across social media. "Awful news, so sorry to hear," one Leeds fan posted on X. "Rest easy Colin, thoughts with his family and friends."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Another wrote: "Really sad, sending love strength and condolences to his family and friends and all those that tried to save him ALAW (All Leeds Aren't We)."

A former colleague of his said: "Thoughts and prayers to his family & friends. I worked with Colin for a good few years - enjoyed a pint and a football chat."

Sports.title: Truth behind Mikel Arteta's comment on 'incredible' Eberechi Eze after Liverpool win
Sports.content:
Truth behind Mikel Arteta's comment on 'incredible' Eberechi Eze after Liverpool win

Eberechi Eze did not get off the bench for Arsenal at Anfield but even making the matchday squad was a huge bonus for boss Mikel Arteta

View 2 Images Eberechi Eze in action for Arsenal (Image: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Eberechi Eze was a surprise name on Arsenal’s team sheet at Liverpool on Sunday. In fact, Mikel Arteta said it was “incredible” that Eze was in the squad for Arsenal’s win at Anfield.

‌



‌



That is because at one point last week there were fears that Eze could be missing for a while - and yet his determination to be ready for his team speaks volumes about his character.

‌



Eze’s presence and availability has only served to further enhance the way the England star is viewed behind the scenes at the Emirates for his attitude and mindset.

‌



That Arteta remark got slightly lost because it was in an answer to a question about Christos Tzolis and the risk in throwing the winger straight into the starting XI after injury.

Gunners boss Arteta said: “It’s the energy that he had in training. When I asked him the question, how convinced he was. We had an issue with Ebs as well, it was incredible that he was in the squad.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“I want to give credit to all the medical and performance team. What they are doing with those boys is incredible. Every three days, to keep everybody at this level.

‌



“These are the margins sometimes when you win a football match, whether you have somebody available or not. They deserve that credit.

“With Christos, incredible. He didn’t want to come off, he wanted to complete the game. We took some risks, but at a point we decided enough was enough.”

‌



It is fair to say that Eze has had a mixed start to the season because he was excellent from the bench at Aston Villa but has struggled from the start in games when he has played from the left.

But then he scored at Bayern Munich - a brilliantly taken goal in an epic Champions League tie - and then was pretty ineffective and frustrating as a substitute in Arsenal’s humiliating exit at Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup.

‌



However, Eze was actually playing with some niggles and injury issues which have bugged him this season. After that Fleetwood game, he underwent some checks and there were fears he could be out for a few games because of injury.

But Eze shrugged off pain and fitness issues last season to help Arsenal when they needed him most - and has stepped up again this time.

‌



View 2 Images Eberechi Eze celebrates Bayern Munich goal (Image: Adam Davy/Press Association)

Eze battled on, trained ahead of the Liverpool game and made himself available because he knew the team was short on numbers and options.

‌



Bukayo Saka is out injured while Max Dowman was suspended after the club’s unsuccessful appeal against his red card at Fleetwood.

Even though Eze did not get off the bench at Anfield, his willingness to make himself available, to be ready to step up should he be required has earned him not just glowing praise from his manager but also a lot of respect among the coaching staff.

‌



Some players have to be just right to deem themselves fit to play. Tzolis pushed himself to be back and fit to start and he is known as being tough, resilient and determined.

Eze is also showing those same qualities in abundance to ensure that he is ready to support his team. It has definitely been noticed - and marked him out as a special character.

Sports.title: Everton make decision on Jack Grealish facing Newcastle after 'breach of discipline'
Sports.content:
Everton make decision on Jack Grealish facing Newcastle after 'breach of discipline'

Jack Grealish missed training ahead of Everton's Carabao Cup tie against Newcastle last Thursday and also won't feature when the two teams meet in the Premier League

View 2 Images Jack Grealish was punished by Everton (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Jack Grealish has been left out of Everton's matchday squad for the second time following his 'breach of discipline'. Grealish, 31, was absent for last Thursday's 3-1 win at home to Newcastle in the Carabao Cup, with it later emerging that the Manchester City loanee had missed training in the lead-up to the game.

‌



‌



And Grealish will remain sidelined when the two teams meet again for a Premier League fixture at St James' Park on Monday. The Athletic report that the forward is yet to regain his fitness since his last appearance on October 17.

‌



It's unclear whether Grealish will be involved when Everton face Coventry this Friday. Toffees manager David Moyes confirmed after beating Newcastle last week that the decision to leave him out was made by the club's hierarchy.

‌



"You probably know I'm not going to give any details," Moyes explained. "It's a club decision, it's something I don't want to speak too much about."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Grealish also missed Everton's previous game, a 2-0 loss away to Arsenal on October 24, through 'illness'. The former Aston Villa star is on loan at Everton until the end of the 2026-27 season.

His contract with City expires next summer when it'll be six years since they shelled out a British-record £100million to sign him from Villa. After falling out of favour at the Etihad Stadium, Grealish was loaned to Everton last term.

‌



The 31-year-old enjoyed a decent campaign which was curtailed by injury. Grealish made two appearances for City this season before rejoining the Toffees on transfer deadline day.

Will Everton beat Newcastle? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Jack Grealish is yet to regain his fitness (Image: Tony McArdle/Everton FC via Getty Images)

While refusing to give any details about Grealish's absence, Moyes praised his players for not allowing it to be a distraction. "The one thing about Everton is that it has got good values behind it," the Everton boss said.

‌



"All the players stand up to the values on pitch and off the pitch. The players did a brilliant job tonight. We are limited in some areas but we are doing our best to keep challenging."

Everton travel to the North East sitting one point and two places behind the hosts. A win for either side would lift them to at least seventh place.
