Sports.title: Social Media: Russell vows to rediscover his performance after “more bad days than good” in 2026 | Brief
Sports.content:
George Russell said he has found the 2026 season difficult to deal with as he missed out on his first chance to win the world championship.

He also offered his congratulations to team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli , who won the title yesterday.

“Now feels like a pretty suitable moment to speak from the heart,” said Russell in a post on social media. “This season started off exactly how I had hoped but it very quickly unravelled with tough luck and poor performances. It’s been the first proper season of my career where I’ve had more bad days than good.

“Has it been tough to deal with? Yes, very. Has it been tough to pick myself up week in, week out? Yes, very. Confusion at times? Often. All I know is that I’ve given it my all and 2026 was not meant to be my year.

“I want to sincerely congratulate Kimi on what has been an absolutely incredible season. You truly deserve the championship.

“Thank you to the team for producing the best car and power unit this season; it’s been inspiring to see everyone coming together over four tough years to bring Mercedes back to the top.

“Now, all I can promise is that for the rest of this season, and into the next one, I will be giving my absolute all to rediscover the performance I have been capable of producing for the majority of my career and fingers crossed a little bit of luck returns.

“Thanks for all the support.”

Sports.title: Leclerc has wrong mentality, says Hamilton: ‘It’s ‘do-or-die, either I win or none of us do” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari would have lost more wins this year if he had the same “kamikaze” mentality as team mate Charles Leclerc.

The seven-times world champion blamed his team mate for costing Ferrari victory in yesterday’s Mexican Grand Prix. Both he and Leclerc went off at turn four while fighting over the lead on lap one.

Hamilton said he’d noticed Leclerc’s battles with his predecessor Carlos Sainz Jnr cost Ferrari points in the past.

“Before I joined this team, when I was at Mercedes, I watched and witnessed the back and forth between Charles and Carlos several races, where they were battling so much that the person ahead just pulled away, and they had the pace to actually win,” he said. “But it is one thing when that’s happening in fourth and fifth, as opposed to first and second, and you lose the win. That’s significant.

“The guy [Leclerc] is 28 years old, so I don’t think it’s an age thing. I think it’s a mentality thing. It’s like, “Do-or-die. Either I win or none of us do,” and it shouldn’t be that. It should be us having, getting that one-two.”

Hamilton pointed out he did not compromise Leclerc’s race when he won at Silverstone earlier this year. “In Silverstone, I could have gone all kamikaze on him and taken him off and lost us the win, but instead the one-two was there.” They finished first and third but were holding the top two positions before Hamilton pitted when the Safety Car was deployed.

“For me, I’m happy for the team to have experienced that, but I’m hopeful we’ll work towards a better working place in the future.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

In remarks similar to those of Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur, Hamilton said the result did not do justice to the effort made by the team.

“I think the core thing to remember, which maybe comes with age, is that every decision you make in the car impacts all the people that work in the background for the whole team,” he said. “So, working as a team is a part of our job and a part of our contract.

“We have to work as a team, which we could have easily done today. So, it’s a shame to see us lose this, as we did. That will just continue unless action is taken, if a real deep, serious conversation is had. So, it shouldn’t happen [again] moving forward.

“Of course, I’ve had close battles with team mates in the past, and you can’t always get it right, but nine times out of ten we should be able to. So, I think we’ll take it offline and we’ll have some good conversations, hopefully. For sure, it won’t be easy, but it must be done.”

However Hamilton admitted he’d experienced tougher situations previously at other teams, such as at Mercedes, where he and team mate Nico Rosberg once took each other out at the start of a race.

“I’ve had way worse times at Mercedes. There were some really bad moments. I don’t really see there being huge differences. I think it was managed well at Mercedes, and I think Fred’s doing his best.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Fred came and spoke to me before the race, and I think he was nervous. Of course, he wants [his] two drivers to do well.”

He said he would have had to explain his actions had he attacked his team mate from behind the way Leclerc did.

“From my side, if I’m coming from behind and I’m taking all the risk and it ends up that we lose as a team, then I think I have some answering to do, because it impacts a lot of people. But the other way around, I’m in the lead, and it was just unnecessary.

“I think we could have easily had that one-two today, which would have been huge for the team and for everyone back at the factory who’s worked so hard to bring us these upgrades. I don’t really know what will be done because up until now nothing really has been done.”

Sports.title: Antonelli “lost two seconds because I was crying” at end of Mexican GP | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli admitted he was already crying before he took the chequered flag to win the world championship.

The Mercedes driver finished third in Mexico, clinching the title in his second season as a Formula 1 driver. The 20-year-old was so emotional he was struggling to see the track and he lost 1.8 seconds to the leaders on his final lap.

“I lost probably two seconds because I was already crying, basically,” Antonelli admitted. “I couldn’t see clearly ahead.

“I could see two Ferraris, somehow, with the tears. So it was very special.”

Antonelli became the youngest world champion in F1 history, just five years after moving from karts to cars. “A lot of memories went through my mind in that moment,” he said, “all the memories since karting all the way to here.

“It was a very special final lap, and definitely when I crossed the line, I let it all out because it was just achieving one of my biggest dreams. It was very special.”

The championship outcome was a foregone conclusion before the weekend began: Antonelli needed to score only two points to be certain of the title even if his closest rival won all the remaining rounds. Nonetheless he felt the weight of expectation during the weekend.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“I knew I was very close. However, I still needed to get the job done, and, of course, you still want to do a good race. You want to do a good performance, so that was the goal.

“But it hasn’t been the easiest weekend either. Physically, I haven’t been in the best shape, but also yesterday we had a bad qualifying execution, and emotions were a bit high overall.

“But I’m really happy that today we did a strong race and really happy that we managed to finish the job. And then now we’ve got a few races to go, and we’re just going to enjoy all the way and try to finish on a high.”

He made a careful start to the race, ceding a position to eventual winner Max Verstappen on the run to turn one. However he decided to risk more at the second standing start following a red flag period.

“At the start I was very cautious, and I gave a lot of room. So I was probably playing it very much on the safe side.

“But then I saw I had the pace, and especially that first stint, I knew we would be in the fight because the pace was very good on used tyres.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Then with the red flag, it kind of all went back to zero. And in that moment I was like, ‘You know what? I’m just going to take more risks.’

“I had the opportunity to gain a few places, and that move on Charles [Leclerc] was crucial to get on the podium. I tried until the end to stay close, and it was very fun, the last stint, because we were all, I think, the three of us within two seconds, and we were all pushing. It was just difficult, of course, to overtake, but it was high intensity, and it was fun.

“Then on the last lap I just backed off because I just couldn’t see the track. I was getting emotional, and I said, ‘I’m just going to back off because otherwise I crash here.’ So it was just good to bring it home.”

Sports.title: Call this the ‘Maxico’ Grand Prix says Verstappen after sixth Mexican GP win | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen joked Formula 1 should rename Mexico’s round of the world championship after him following his sixth victory in the race.

The Red Bull driver has now scored more wins in Mexico City than he has at any other venue. He became the fourth driver to score more than five wins at the same venue and the first to do so at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez

“They should actually call it the ‘Maxico’ Grand Prix,” said Verstappen. “That would be great.”

His five previous wins at the track came between 2017 and 2023. Verstappen said he saw no obvious reason why he had been particularly successful at this venue.

“I honestly love being here,” he said. “I love the city, I love the environment, I love the fans, but I have no idea why.

“It just happens. Sometimes your car just comes alive and you’ve had good races and not a lot of bad luck sometimes as well. So it’s just always come together for me here and, of course, I happily take that.”

Verstappen said he was surprised to move into a strong position immediately after the start of the race, thanks partly to Ferrari drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton going off at turn four.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The first start already made my race a bit better, getting into turn one, and then, of course, the battle that I saw unfold in turn four put me in a quite nice spot.”

Leclerc received a five-second time penalty for his infringement and Verstappen jumped ahead of him when they pitted on the same lap.

“It was a bit tough, to be honest, I think Charles just pulled away. I could not really stay with him. I did not have the pace to follow him, but at the same time, I was still within that five-second window.

“So, then the team did a really good job to follow him in [to the pits]. It’s always very tough when you have a five-second penalty to actually make it exactly five seconds. So, I jumped him, and honestly, after that, it was quite tough.”

The race winner said he feared for his chances when the Safety Car was deployed following Valtteri Bottas’s crash. The race was stopped and restarted, and Verstappen maintained his lead ahead of Hamilton.

“Kimi [Antonelli] was flying, still, out there on the first set of tyres, and I just did not really have the grip for whatever reason. Charles was very close, but at the same time, it’s very hard to follow around here because everything overheats, and that probably helped me as well because I think at one point Charles had to back off just for cooling, and that was quite nice for me.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But at the same time, when I saw the Safety Car come out just out of the last corner and I couldn’t box, I was like, ‘There’s no way this is happening now,’ because that was then probably game over for me.

“Then, of course, it ended up being a red flag, so then it reset everything. I was a bit worried because our starts this year have not been amazing, but luckily today, twice, they have actually been good, and that then made my way ’til the end.

“But it was not made easy. I mean, Lewis was in my gearbox, pushing hard. It was basically a qualifying lap ’til the end. Yeah, it was tough out there. It was a tough race to the end, just to not make any mistakes. But, of course, I’m happy to win today.”

The major Italian daily sports newspaper La Gazzetta dello Sport delivered a stark verdict on Ferrari’s performance as Andrea Kimi Antonelli clinched the 2026 world championship.

“Kimi Antonelli is a Formula 1 world champion,” read the commentary on the front page of Monday’s edition. “Thanks to his talent, the car and the fact that he isn’t racing for Ferrari.”

Sports.title: “I’ll stay with number 12” – no number one in 2027 for new champion Antonelli | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli will not use the number one on his car, which is reserved for world champions, next year.

The Mercedes driver succeeded Lando Norris as the reigning world champion with his third-place finish in yesterday’s Mexican Grand Prix. But while Norris swapped his regular number four for the champion’s one, Antonelli will not do the same.

“I’ll stay with number 12 because, obviously, it’s a very special number for me,” he said. “But also it’s a way for me to stay grounded, to stay humble.

“I feel like by keeping number 12 it allows me to have a new point where to start and build on everything again and try to improve.”

Antonelli admitted there is an element of superstition in his preference to stick with his current number.

“Also, to be honest, I’m very superstitious, and number one has never been a good number for me. Whenever I [used] it, it went extremely badly. So that’s one more reason to stay with number 12.”

Prior to racing in F1, Antonelli used number 12 when he won the European and Middle East Formula Regional championship titles in 2023, and the Italian Formula 4 title the year before.

He is the first driver to win the world championship using number 12 since Ayrton Senna in 1988. Both drivers also scored their first grand prix victories with number 12: Antonelli this year, Senna in 1985.

Antonelli is planning a tribute to the Brazilian three-times world champion at this weekend’s Brazilian Grand Prix.

“I will have a special helmet for Brazil, for Ayrton,” he said. “Also because it’s going to be 35 years since he won [while stuck] in sixth gear in his home race.

“I think it’s one of my best helmets that I’ve made, hopefully you guys, everyone, will like it.”

Sports.title: Yoenli Hernandez Ordered To Fight Michael Zerafa For Vacant WBO Belt
Sports.content:
Yoenli Hernández could have to go through a second purse bid just to get his first WBO title fight. The WBO has authorized negotiations between Hernández and Michael Zerafa for its vacant middleweight belt after stripping Denzel Bentley, whose mandatory defense against Hernández had already gone to bid.

Zerafa, ranked fourth by the WBO, moves ahead of two contenders who are unavailable. No. 2 Vito Mielnicki Jr. is unavailable, and No. 3 Tim Tszyu is under contract to face Erislandy Lara. WBO president Gustavo Olivieri said formal notice would follow. The fighters’ teams will have 20 days from the issuance of that order to reach a deal.

Hernández Has Already Been Through One Purse Bid

“The parties shall have 20 days from the issuance of the formal negotiation order to reach terms, pursuant to WBO Regulations or purse bid proceedings,” Olivieri said on X.

Warriors Boxing was the only bidder for Bentley’s mandatory defense and secured the promotional rights with a $200,000 offer on September 29. Bentley stood to receive $150,000, with the remaining $50,000 going to Hernández. Bentley had asked to fight Shane Mosley Jr. first and defend against Hernández afterward, but the WBO denied his appeal on October 22. He kept the Mosley fight, scheduled for November 7 in London as his Zuffa Boxing debut, and the WBO stripped him.

That first bid shows why the next 20 days matter. Hernández’s promoter did what the WBO process required and put up the money to stage the defense. Bentley still had a fight he preferred to take, and Hernández came out of the process with the same No. 1 ranking he had going in. A deal with Zerafa would spare him another round of bidding and give both camps a chance to settle where the fight takes place and what they’ll be paid.

Hernández (11-0, 9 KOs) brings the bigger punch, but his last fight gave Zerafa something to study. Francisco Verón took him the distance in August and held him to a majority decision. For all the talk about why Bentley took the Mosley fight, that result matters more to Zerafa. There are rounds to win against Hernández if Zerafa can keep him from setting his feet and make him work to close the distance.

The opening for Zerafa came from the two names above him being unavailable. What he can do with it is another matter. Hernández has the power to make this a short night if Zerafa stands in front of him, but the Cuban still has to show he can take charge when an opponent makes him work deep into a fight. That’s what makes the pairing worth seeing once the teams get it signed.

Sports.title: Can Anyone Outside Of  Terence Crawford Defeat Canelo At 168?
Sports.content:
On Halloween night, Canelo Alvarez defeated Christian Mbilli to become a three-time super-middleweight world champion, and now the question is: outside of Terence Crawford, can any other boxer defeat Canelo at 168?

When Christian Mbilli entered the ring to face Canelo Alvarez, a reasonable number of boxing pundits thought Mbilli was going to pull off the upset. Alvarez has a history of stamina issues, and many assumed Mbilli could take advantage.

The idea was for Mbilli to overwhelm Canelo with his high-volume punching, wear him down, take over in the later rounds, and win a close decision. Unfortunately for Mbilli, the bout didn’t go that way.

Canelo Alvarez was able to dictate the range and the pace of the fight. Canelo’s defense was sharp, his stamina was good, and on offense he dominated the action with skillful counterpunching and pinpoint accuracy.

Mbilli fought the wrong type of fight, as most of the bout took place at mid-range as opposed to close quarters. Mbilli gave Canelo too much respect, and on multiple occasions he looked confused.

Christian Mbilli was severely outclassed, and because of that, the fight looked like a glorified sparring session. As a result of the bout, Canelo Alvarez (64-3-2, 39 KOs) is the new WBC super-middleweight world champion.

The sport of boxing is based on levels, and on the night of October 31st, Canelo Alvarez proved he was levels above Christian Mbilli. Now fight fans are wondering: are any of the current top super-middleweights close to being on Canelo’s level?

Terence “Bud” Crawford defeated Canelo Alvarez with his skill set and his ring IQ. None of the top super-middleweights have a skill set compatible with Crawford’s, and none of them come close to Crawford when it comes to ring intelligence.

With that being said, one would ask, outside of a rematch with Crawford, what would be the ideal fight for Canelo at 168? If Terence Crawford can’t be convinced to come out of retirement, then Hamzah Sheeraz is probably the best candidate.

The former WBO world champion Hamzah Sheeraz is a 6-foot-3-inch super-middleweight who is skilled, and he can effectively fight from long range. On Halloween night, Sheeraz was ringside analyzing the fight.

Back in July 2025, Hamzah Sheeraz looked sharp as he stopped Edgar Berlanga in the 5th round. A year later, Sheeraz had a lackluster performance, as he scored a majority decision victory over Simon Zachenhuber.

Now Hamzah Sheeraz (24-0-1, 19 KOs) appears to be the frontrunner in regards to facing Canelo in 2027. If Sheeraz doesn’t get the match, then Canelo may choose to fight one of the other champions at 168.

Sports.title: Lester Martinez Targets Canelo Alvarez With BoMac Behind Him
Sports.content:
Lester Martinez would give Canelo Alvarez a dangerous first defense of his reclaimed WBC super middleweight title. The aggressive Guatemalan can punch and has Brian “BoMac” McIntyre in his corner, giving him access to the trainer who helped Terence Crawford beat Canelo.

“My dream now is to fight Canelo because he’s the champion,” Martinez said to Izquierdazo Boxeo in a quote shared by The Ring. His WBC interim title gives that ambition substance, although it does not establish that Canelo has been ordered to face him next.

The McIntyre connection makes this more interesting than another contender requesting a payday. BoMac knows what went into preparing Crawford for Canelo and could bring that knowledge into Martinez’s camp. The WBC lists McIntyre as Martinez’s trainer. wbcboxing.com

Crawford could also offer firsthand advice about Canelo’s timing, counterpunching and habits under pressure. His involvement in a potential camp has not been announced, but Martinez would have an obvious reason to seek his stablemate’s input.

Mbilli took too long to alter his approach when Canelo’s jab and head movement disrupted his pressure last weekend. He continued following Canelo without consistently changing how he attacked. Martinez would likely arrive expecting those tactics, with McIntyre preparing ways to get past the jab and vary his attack.

That would not make Lester immune to Canelo’s counters. It could, however, reduce the rounds spent trying to work out what to do next. BoMac could prepare alternatives before the opening bell and help Martinez adjust between rounds when Canelo starts frustrating him.

Martinez would still need to win with his own tools. He cannot copy Crawford’s performance. His route would involve sustained pressure, body punching and enough variation to prevent Canelo from anticipating each attack.

His 2025 draw with Mbilli gives him a relevant result against the man Canelo just defeated. Beating Canelo is another matter, but an aggressive puncher arriving with informed preparation would be a serious undertaking for the 36-year-old champion.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder’s Power Puts Jai Opetaia’s Chin On Trial
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder has plenty of reasons to believe he can catch Jai Opetaia. The unbeaten cruiserweight champion handles pressure well, but flush right hands consistently cause trouble. That crack in the armor turns their planned December 11 meeting into an explosive collision.

Trainer Stephen Edwards spotted the opening on the proposed Fury vs Joshua card in Cardiff. While he figures Opetaia enters as the favorite, he doubts the Australian stays out of danger for twelve full rounds.

I think Deontay Wilder has a chance vs Jai Opetaia. Opetaia will most likely be the favorite but he’s not refined or smooth defensively. If he doesn’t clip Deontay, he’s in serious danger throughout. Risky fight but I respect it. Especially for this era,” said Edwards on X.

The real test is Opetaia’s chin. Crisp southpaw boxing gives him an edge in ring generalship, yet recent cruiserweight defenses have shown concerning moments whenever opponents land cleanly.

Huseyin Cinkara rattled him during the second round of their clash in late 2025. Opetaia rallied to score an eighth round knockout, though the early scare arrived against an opponent everyone expected him to run through.

Noel Mikaelian produced an identical scare in September. A crisp right hook connected in round seven, forcing Opetaia to clinch immediately. He rallied once more, stopping Mikaelian in the ninth, yet the warning sirens rang out loud.

Opetaia is taking a risk here because a knockout loss wrecks the financial engine behind a David Benavidez clash. Benavidez wants Opetaia for legacy, unified belts, and a high-profile scalp. If Opetaia comes off a brutal stoppage, Benavidez gains almost nothing from beating him. The narrative shifts from “daring to be great against the division monster” to “picking up the pieces of damaged goods.”

Wilder must still land the equalizer. If Opetaia’s speed freezes the former heavyweight champion, Wilder might spend the night waiting for an opening that never arrives. His right hand remains the great equalizer, but banking on it to bail him out against Opetaia ignores what happened to his punch resistance and his trigger.

Zhilei Zhang needed only one clean counter right hand to completely turn Wilder around and leave him staring at the rafters.

Opetaia does not need to hit as hard as Zhang. He punches with devastating leverage from the southpaw stance, throws tight combinations rather than looping singles, and refuses to let opponents recover once they’re hurt.

When Cinkara and Mikaelian found Opetaia’s chin, Opetaia still walked through the fire to stop both men. Wilder, by contrast, has shown zero ability to absorb heavy contact and rally back since 2020.

Sports.title: Revitalization in Riyadh
Sports.content:
Saturday afternoon saw Saul “Canelo” Alvarez (64-3-2, 39 KOs) defeat Christian Mbilli (29-1-1, 24 KOs) by unanimous decision over 12 rounds. For all the talk of Canelo being washed after his dismantling at the hands of Terence “Bud” Crawford last year, Canelo looked quick, efficient, and energized on both offense and defense from beginning to end.

Some major differences in his performance included a low lead hand stance as his primary, with the high guard as a secondary; a return to the head movement that was once touted as among the best in boxing; and the most consistent and effective jab we’ve seen from him in close to a decade. He also threw a hell of a lot of feints and changed up the velocity of his punches rather than throwing everything hard as he has tended to do. This not only helped him conserve energy, but it also deterred Mbilli’s aggressiveness. In a fight that many expected to be a war, Canelo focused on pure boxing and high-level defense to slow the action down and prevent Mbilli from launching an all-out attack in the pocket.

In the early rounds, Canelo played a little rope-a-dope, laying against the ropes while slipping, ducking, and blocking the younger fighter’s shots. When the action made its way back to the center of the ring, Canelo popped Mbilli with sharp, well-timed jabs at mid-range. After four rounds, Mbilli had slowed enough for Canelo to begin finding big, clean counters in exchanges. Six rounds in, Canelo started circling more rather than going to the ropes. At times, he would touch the ropes with his back to bait Mbilli in, and then flurry with rapid combinations as Mbilli stepped in thinking Canelo was going back on defense.

From the seventh round on, it was a basic boxing clinic, with Canelo showing that he can still box his ass off when he isn’t in love with his power. The eleventh and twelfth rounds were competitive as Mbilli tried to finish strong, yet Canelo consistently landed the bigger, cleaner shots, even wobbling Mbilli toward the close of round 12.

Mbilli simply was never able to mount a consistent attack because Canelo had an answer for everything he attempted. Against Terence Crawford, Canelo simply sought to overpower what he perceived as a naturally smaller man, but Crawford was able to blunt everything coming from Canelo with sophisticated defense and control at midrange. When Canelo went back to the drawing board with his team, he must have been kicking himself for never attempting to establish the jab, failing to use his head movement, and allowing Crawford to maintain foot control all night.

When Mayweather dominated Canelo over 12 rounds with superior defense and intelligent punch selection, the takeaway was that brute force isn’t enough to topple the fighters at the top. Somewhere during his 168 lb undisputed run, he lost sight of that and locked into a seek-and-destroy mindset. It seems like the Crawford loss may have initiated a similar reboot, which could carry Canelo into a final run at undisputed before retirement.

One point of concern Saturday night took place outside of the ring, with the commentary team missing as much as Christian Mbilli was. Notably, Todd Grisham seemed intent on dragging Canelo. At one point, he implied that Canelo got the benefit of the doubt against Daniel Jacobs, which was actually a clear and decisive win for Canelo. He also mentioned a fight between Canelo and Derevyanchenko, which does not exist. In the opening rounds, when Mbilli would miss six or seven punch combinations, the commentary team would praise the guy who missed rather than the guy who made him miss.

In round eight, after multiple fouls, when Mbilli drove a palm into the back of Canelo’s head, the referee separated the two and walked Mbilli to the center of the ring. He clearly had Mbilli’s glove in hand, preparing to take a point, when Canelo tapped his shoulder to complain about the fouls as fighters often do. When the referee proceeded to dock the point, Grisham erupted into an accusation that Canelo had forced the referee to penalize Mbilli. The ref was clearly already preparing to take the point, but furthermore, Canelo has zero power to force a referee’s hand. What Canelo apparently stated was that if he was fouled again, he would kick his opponent. He didn’t use his name or influence to sway any decision-making; he simply made a statement out of anger.

Of course, many viewers who aren’t familiar with the intricacies of the sport rely on the commentary team to provide an accurate analysis of the fight. Much of the post-fight narrative following Saturday’s bout has been centered around the perception that Canelo had the referee in his pocket and that the fight was a robbery, simply because the commentators seemed to favor ineffective aggression over defensive prowess.

Outside of whatever bias he has against Alvarez, there wasn’t much technical analysis from Grisham. Sergio Mora, though he has experience as a fighter and sometimes points out strategies or techniques, is often unable to articulate what he sees clearly. Grisham frequently views fights as a casual fan might: “Throw punches = good. Not throw punches = bad. Move forward = good. Block punches = getting hit.” DAZN would do well to bring on an individual who truly understands the nuances of the sport and can convey them effectively to the common fan.

One thing that hasn’t been prevalent in the aftermath of the fight is anyone accusing Canelo of “running,” even though he more or less did to Mbilli what Crawford did to him. People who accuse boxers of running because they do not sit and slug it out at close range are generally uninformed or unwilling to give credit to certain styles of fighters like Crawford, Foster, or Mayweather. Canelo rarely sat still for exchanges, yet he is (rightfully) being praised for his high defensive IQ. Now, what could that double standard possibly be about?

So, what impressions did Saturday’s main event leave on us?

First, Canelo didn’t learn any new tricks; he simply brushed the dust off his old tool bag and returned to the basics. The jab was tweaked, but overall, the head movement, feints, and punch variety are elements fans have been asking him to bring back for years.

Secondly, DAZN needs to step up its commentary game. The broadcast should accommodate the casual viewer while remaining educated and informed enough for die-hard boxing fans. You simply cannot skimp on commentator quality at this level of production.

Lastly, Canelo’s future. Alvarez remains a polarizing figure. But love him or hate him, it is hard to deny that he has been boxing’s biggest star since Mayweather retired. What might his plans be moving forward, and how will the boxing world react? Given the promotional tagline of “Return of the King,” it seems reasonable to assume he will once again seek to become the undisputed champion of the 168 lb division before retiring. Ideally, he would collect all the belts and gain one more signature victory, though that is a steep path for a 36-year-old.

Wherever the future leads him, he has carried the sport at several key points in his career. He is a reminder that greatness and perfection are not one and the same, and are often at odds. Steadfast determination and a true, honest love for boxing have defined Canelo’s persona inside and outside the ring. Despite falling short against generational greats, he remains an example of how passionate dedication to a dream can endure long after achieving everything you set out for.

Sports.title: Andy Cruz Faces Artur Subkhankulov November 27 For IBF Title
Sports.content:
Andy Cruz has found a fresh path to the IBF lightweight crown, even if picking up the belt leaves his loss against Raymond Muratalla unanswered. The Cuban standout meets undefeated Artur Subkhankulov on November 27 in Ufa, Russia, battling for the vacant title now that Muratalla has jumped up in weight.

Ring Magazine broke the news of the matchup, dropping Cruz right into his opponent’s backyard.

Muratalla moving up for 140 pounds without settling things leaves a sour taste, especially when so many ringside observers believed Cruz (7-1, 4 KOs) did enough to earn the decision last January. Walking away with the belt and immediately going to light welterweight lets Muratalla hold onto bragging rights without having to solve Cruz a second time.

That controversial loss against Muratalla basically gave Cruz the best of both worlds. The disputed cards shielded him from the career damage of a decisive defeat, while the sting of leaving with an empty hand shook him out of his amateur habits.

Amateur legends often stay stuck in neutral because their pure boxing ability bails them out. Cruz could have spent years coasting on touch-and-move tricks, flicking jabs, and winning rounds by narrow margins. Instead, that decision forced him to confront the cold reality of professional prize fighting: relying on judges to appreciate finesse will get you robbed.

Shifting toward sitting down on his punches and hunting real damage is the exact adjustment he needed. If he had been given the decision against Muratalla, he probably would have stayed comfortable. Taking the hit turned him into a far more dangerous fighter.

Going into Russia against Subkhankulov with that mean streak makes him a completely different situation. Subkhankulov is walking in prepared for an Olympic stylist. If Cruz shows up planting his heels and looking to take his head off, that wake-up call against Muratalla might end up being the best thing that ever happened to his career.

Cruz, 31, last fought in July, stopping Abraham Montoya in three rounds in his first appearance since losing to Muratalla. The change was dramatic. He fought with greater aggression and looked intent on hurting Montoya rather than allowing his cleaner boxing to carry him through the rounds.

Sports.title: David Nyika Ready To Spoil Usyk Retirement Plans
Sports.content:
Oleksandr Usyk‘s planned farewell tour has hit an unexpected roadblock. David Nyika’s team intends to enforce his mandatory standing with the IBF, putting a wrench in the Ukrainian’s plan to capture another undisputed cruiserweight crown.

Trainer Noel Thornberry confirmed he reached out to Usyk’s management regarding a potential clash. He made it clear that while they want the fight, stepping aside for a different matchup will require serious negotiation. As Thornberry told AAP, everyone would need to sit down to reach a deal.

Usyk’s camp envisions a two-bout cruiserweight run in 2027. Step one involves claiming a vacant belt. Step two targets David Benavidez for all four titles. For that scenario to materialize, Benavidez must defeat WBC titlist Michal Cieslak on December 5 to unify three belts, leaving the IBF strap as the final piece Usyk must supply for the undisputed finale.

Mapping out that schedule on paper is simple enough, but executing it requires cooperation from fighters who have no interest in playing along. Nyika wants to build his own legacy, giving him zero incentive to stand down just to accommodate a heavyweight champion’s retirement timeline.

Ranked as the IBF’s top contender, Nyika sits in prime position. The division remains murky, however, with former champion Jai Opetaia currently contesting the stripping of his belt following his jump to Zuffa Boxing. Opetaia stopped Nyika in January 2025, meaning any legal resolution reinstating Opetaia would shake up Usyk’s options even further.

Thornberry’s approach prepares for either scenario. His team welcomes a direct shot at Usyk, but also acknowledges that a lucrative deal would be required to let an Opetaia bout happen first. While these statements make Nyika’s ambitions obvious, the IBF has yet to issue an official fight order.

Weight presents another major hurdle. Usyk turns 40 in January and hasn’t made 200 pounds since knocking out Tony Bellew in November 2018. While advisor Serhii Lapin maintains Usyk will be at peak form against Benavidez, dropping back down after eight years at heavyweight creates real physical uncertainty.

Thornberry openly questions whether an aging Usyk can handle the cut, stressing that Nyika views the former undisputed ruler as a beatable target rather than an intimidating legend.

Regardless of past victories or legendary status, securing another championship still demands a sanctioning body belt, an eligible challenger, and signed paperwork. Before Usyk can lock in his grand exit, Nyika’s camp plans on forcing its way to the negotiating table.

Sports.title: Jake Paul Opponent set for MVP Christmas Eve Spectacle in Dubai
Sports.content:
Cédric Doumbé will swap MMA for boxing on December 24 when he faces Jake Paul at Coca-Cola Arena in Dubai. The former two-time GLORY welterweight champion has signed for an eight-round cruiserweight bout, giving him his second professional boxing appearance.

Doumbé wasted little time taking aim at his opponent after Most Valuable Promotions announced the Christmas Eve fight.

“Jake Paul calls himself the Problem Child, but he’s never faced a problem like me. He has no idea what a Frenchman is capable of, and on Thursday, December 24 in Dubai, I’m going to eat ‘El Poulet’ for dinner.”

The Cameroon-born French fighter built most of his career in kickboxing, compiling a 75-7-1 record with 45 knockouts. He then moved into MMA, where he stands at 6-1 with six stoppage wins, including his nine-second knockout of Jordan Zebo in Paris in September 2023.

His professional boxing record is 1-0. That leaves a sizeable gap in boxing experience against Paul, who has fought 14 times since turning professional in 2020 and holds a 12-2 record with seven knockouts.

The contest is scheduled at the 200-pound cruiserweight limit with 10-ounce gloves. Broadcast details and the fight-night start time were not included in the announcement.

For Paul, the booking adds another opponent from outside traditional boxing to a record that includes victories over Tyron Woodley, Anderson Silva and Nate Diaz. He also beat former middleweight champion Julio César Chávez Jr. in June 2025 before facing Anthony Joshua that December.

Paul said the challenge from Doumbé had been brewing for two years.

“Cédric Douchebag was calling me out two years ago after knocking some dude out in 9 seconds. Well Douchebag, now you get your chance.”

Their first face-to-face meetings are set for next week, with public press conferences in Paris and Dubai. Paul challenged Doumbé to bring the same talk with him.

“You like to talk a lot, so let’s see what you have to say in person at the press conferences next week in Paris and Dubai.”

The Paris stop takes place at Pavillon Cambon on November 10 at 6 p.m. CET, followed by Dubai on November 12 at 6 p.m. GST. Both events are free and open to fans.

Tickets for the fight go on general sale November 15 at noon GST, or 9 a.m. CET. A registered-fan presale opens November 14, with PFL Dubai ticket purchasers getting access from November 6.

The card marks Paul’s first professional fight in Dubai. MVP has yet to name any undercard fights in the supplied announcement.

Ghana News.title: 8% pay rise: Workers will be better off in real terms— Dr Acheampong
Ghana News.content:
Workers in the public sector are expected to be better off in real terms than they were in several previous years, as easing inflation helps preserve the purchasing power of their salaries, Technical Adviser at the Ministry of Finance, Dr Theo Acheampong, has said.

He said the impact of salary adjustments should not be assessed solely by the percentage increase workers receive but by how much of that increase remains valuable after accounting for inflation.

Dr Acheampong explained that a moderate wage increase accompanied by lower inflation could improve workers’ real incomes more effectively than a substantial salary adjustment in an economy experiencing rapid price increases.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, November 2, on the 8 per cent increase in base pay for public sector workers in 2027, he said the government’s objective was to pursue sustainable wage adjustments while keeping inflation under control.

“The fundamental issue is how much purchasing power those salaries are able to actually retain,” he said.

Dr Acheampong illustrated the point with a hypothetical 9 per cent salary increase against inflation of between five and six per cent, which, he said, would translate into a real wage improvement of about three to four per cent.

Under such circumstances, workers would be better off because their earnings would have gained value after accounting for the rise in the cost of goods and services.

He argued that this was preferable to granting a 25 per cent salary increase in an environment where inflation exceeded 40 or 50 per cent, as the rapid rise in prices could erode the gains from higher pay.

Lessons from previous years

Dr Acheampong said historical figures dating back to 2010 showed that there had been several years in which inflation exceeded adjustments in base pay, leaving public sector workers worse off in real terms.

He cited 2022 as an example, when the base pay adjustment was seven per cent, while the Cost of Living Allowance (COLA) was increased by 15 per cent, bringing the combined adjustment to approximately 22 per cent.

However, inflation stood at about 54 per cent that year, meaning the combined wage adjustment fell significantly short of the increase in prices.

In 2023, public sector workers received a 30 per cent salary adjustment, but inflation was still about 23 per cent, limiting the improvement in their purchasing power.

He said the trend began to change in 2025, when end-of-year inflation stood at 5.4 per cent, compared with a 10 per cent salary adjustment.

For 2026, he said the government was working with a projected inflation rate that was likely to remain within the single-digit target band, against a salary adjustment of nine per cent.

The figures, he argued, demonstrated why the relationship between wage increases and inflation was critical in determining whether workers were actually making financial progress.

Dr Acheampong’s comments come amid public discussion of the 8 per cent base pay increase agreed for public sector workers in 2027.

He maintained that the measure of a successful wage adjustment should be the extent to which it improves workers’ ability to meet their needs, rather than the headline percentage announced.

Ghana News.title: UK and EU agree draft deal to scrap Brexit red tape over food exports
Ghana News.content:
The UK and EU have agreed a draft deal to remove post-Brexit checks on food and agricultural exports, ahead of the UK-EU summit later this month.

The BBC understands the 200-page draft text for this so called "SPS" [sanitary and phytosanitary] agreement has been circulated to EU nations in Brussels for consideration at a meeting on Wednesday.

Similar texts for deals on emissions trading and a youth travel and work scheme have also been circulated alongside a 15-page draft joint statement for UK and EU top leaders.

The food deal is the most significant part of the so-called Brexit reset agreed so far, removing checks and red tape that hit exporters after the UK exited the EU's single market.

The deal should remove the need for £200 Export Health Certificates, £25 Phytosanitary certificates, inspector fees, organic certificates, some port fees, sampling fees and other checks for exports and imports to and from the EU.

The government claims the UK economy will eventually see £5.1bn worth of annual benefits.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen with Prime Minister Andy Burnham

UK exports to the EU of fresh sausages, burgers, shellfish from domestic waters and seed potatoes will also be able to resume.

The agreement will also allow UK pets to enter the EU with passports.

Under the agreement the UK will commit to observing and adapting to existing EU regulations on plant, animal and food trade standards. This process is called "dynamic alignment".

While UK rules remain mostly aligned with EU ones, England has diverged in some areas, for example on "precision breeding" of plants, previously known as gene editing. In recent weeks, agreement has been struck on transition arrangements while the EU's new regulations come in to force.

The government has already announced a European Partnerships Bill, which will provide a legal mechanism to apply new EU rules and regulations. This will also allow the necessary alignment to link the UK emissions trading scheme with the EU's, and save UK exporters from paying the EU's new carbon border tax.

EU ambassadors will discuss the draft agreements at a Coreper meeting on Wednesday, with key details on the planned numbers in a Youth Experience Scheme to be finalised at a political level in the coming days. EU students are likely to get a discount on full foreign student fees, with the plan to reconnect electricity markets pushed to next year.

The BBC understands the draft agreements will also reference UK involvement in defence cooperation schemes, access to law enforcement databases, and reassurances on the EU's "Made in Europe" plans.

While the food trade plans have been backed by supermarkets and farmers representatives, some pro-Brexit campaigners have criticised the reapplication of EU rules. The post-Brexit trade deal signed by Boris Johnson's government prioritised regulatory freedoms for the UK over avoiding new regulatory red tape, checks and delays.

The British Chamber of Commerce released a new analysis of its members' views on Monday suggesting options for a closer relationship.

The business lobby group says the current trade relationship is "failing to deliver", leaving firms "struggling with a thicket of Brexit red tape" nearly six years after the UK's exit from the bloc.

It also pointed to economic analysis of more fundamental changes to the UK-EU relationship, suggesting the largest long-term economic boosts from rejoining the single market or the EU itself. The BCC called on government to analyse and publish options, as it consults its members.

The BCC is calling for an exploration of what a new relationship could look like, and offers nine options, including a customs union, a "Swiss-style" Single Market relationship, and a "Canada model" associate membership.

"The evidence from businesses suggests that the prime minister is right to have initiated a conversation on our future relationship with Europe, and he deserves real credit for having done so.

"Government needs to examine all of the options, remain clear-headed about the trade-offs each involves, and involve business in the decision-making process from the start," Shevaun Havilland, director general of the BCC, said.

More than half (56%) of exporting businesses in a BCC survey said they wanted EU customs paperwork and delays removed so they can grow. That rose to 58% of manufacturers.

The prime minister has said he wants to use this month's summit to launch a conversation on a longer term path for the UK's relationship with the EU, including "going all the way", meaning rejoining the bloc.

Ghana News.title: North Korea denies being behind record $6.3bn Binance hack
Ghana News.content:
North Korea has denied claims that it was behind the record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack of cryptocurrency exchange Binance, calling the allegations "absurd rhetoric".

Kim Yo-jong, a top Democratic People's Republic of Korea official and the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said on Tuesday that the accusations are another "sinister attempt" by the US to damage Pyongyang's public image.

The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the Secret Service, and cyber analysts have said North Korea orchestrated the hack, described as the largest in history.

This is the latest hack to be linked to North Korea, which has been accused of relying on cybercrime to help finance its sanctioned economy.

Blockchain analysts and the FBI say the state-backed hacking group TraderTraitor led the attack.

The FBI has called on industry partners to help block transactions involving cryptocurrency accounts linked to the group.

"The US has made a trite provocation of linking it with the Democratic People's Republic of Korea again," Kim Yo-jong, the director of North Korea's General Affairs Department, said in a statement.

"It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads international public opinion as if all the cybercrimes in different parts of the world are our deeds," she said.

But Pyongyang has been blamed for a number of major cyber attacks in recent years - accusations that it has denied.

The TraderTraitor unit, also known as the Lazarus Group, was blamed for a then-record $1.5bn hack of the crypto exchange Bybit in 2025.

Pyongyang has systematically built its cyber operations by recruiting promising university students and sending them to hacker units overseen by North Korea's intelligence agency, research groups like the S Rajaratnam School of International Studies think tank have said.

The country has consistently denied such claims.

Kim Yo-jong said, "It is the consistent policy stand of the DPRK government to resolutely oppose all sorts of malicious acts in cyberspace".

The BBC has contacted Binance for comment. Since the hack, the crypto giant has largely focused its public statements on the breach's technical nature and its response to protect users.

The company said initial checks indicated that an engineer's laptop had been compromised, enabling an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals.

Trading in major cryptocurrencies on Binance has since resumed after the exchange worked with issuers to freeze assets impacted by the hack.

Binance said on Sunday that customers pulled out more than $3.6bn in assets as it reopened after suspending all transactions following the hack.

The company has repeatedly said it would cover all losses linked to the attack and has so far covered around 95% of the assets stolen in the breach.

Ghana News.title: Chief of Staff urges African leaders to see diaspora citizens beyond remittances
Ghana News.content:
The Chief of Staff, Julius Debrah, has urged African leaders to see diaspora citizens beyond remittances.

He disclosed this at the launch of a new trade desk by Elevate Africa Convening.

The desk is expected to connect African businesses with their potential markets within the continent.

The Chief of Staff applauded the organisers for the initiative and called for a diaspora beyond just remittances.

“We must see the diaspora beyond the form of support and remittances to our families. Diaspora can create businesses; Diaspora can create trade channels and businesses that will support economic growth across the continent. We commend the work of Elevate Africa in championing the African dream”.

In his opening remarks, Co-Founder of Elevate Africa, Ogiame Atuwatse III, the 21stOlu of Warri challenged the youth not to waste their talent due to lack of opportunities.

Former President of Nigeria, Goodluck Jonathan, also urged the youth to develop a clear vision to transform the continent.

The Trade Desk was launched in a symbolic exercise to indicate the readiness of African countries to trade among themselves and provide a stronger front for investor engagements.

Elevate Africa believes the continent of Africa is ripe for more investments than concentrating on aid for development.

Ghana News.title: MTN sets December 10, 2026 as interim dividend payment date
Ghana News.content:
MTN Ghana has set Thursday 10th December 2026 as the interim dividend payment date for quarter 3, 2026 to shareholders.

This was captured in its 3rd Quarter Financial Report.

The payment will be made electronically to the bank accounts or mobile money wallets of shareholders who make use of these facilities.

The Board of the firm declared a gross interim dividend of GH¢0.03 per share for the third

quarter ending 30 September 2026. All dividends are, however, subject to the deduction of applicable taxes.

The number of ordinary shares in issue as of the date of this declaration is 13,236,175,050.

All shareholders registered in the books of Scancom PLC (MTN Ghana) at the close of business on

Thursday, 26 November 2026, would qualify for the quarter three interim dividend.

In view of the foregoing, the ex-dividend date has been set as Tuesday, 24 November 2026.

Consequently, an investor purchasing MTNGH shares before this date will be entitled to the quarter three interim dividend. However, an investor buying MTN Ghana shares on or

after Thursday, 26 November 2026 will not be entitled to the quarter three interim dividend.

MTN Ghana recorded a profit of GH¢7.7 billion in the third quarter of 2026, a 42.0% increase over the same period in 2025.

Ghana News.title: 8% pay rise: We’ll reopen negotiations if economic conditions worsen – NAGRAT warns
Ghana News.content:
Jacob Anaba

The President of the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT), Jacob Anaba, says organised labour may return to the negotiating table over the eight per cent base pay increase for public sector workers in 2027 if economic conditions change during the year.

He said organised labour had already informed the government and the Minister of Finance that developments affecting workers’ purchasing power could necessitate fresh negotiations on the agreed pay adjustment.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, November 2, Mr Anaba said the agreement must be assessed against the cost of living, particularly rising fuel prices and the cost of food.

“We have indicated to the Minister of Finance and Government that if anything happens within the year, we'll come back and have a new negotiation for whatever we have agreed on because it's very important,” he said.

His comments suggest that organised labour remains concerned about whether the agreed increase will provide meaningful relief if the prices of essential goods and services continue to rise.

Rising costs under scrutiny

Mr Anaba cited fuel prices and the cost of preparing everyday meals as examples of the economic pressures facing workers.

He questioned the relationship between the cost of maize and the prices consumers pay for kenkey, pepper and fish, arguing that the cost of basic meals continued to place pressure on household budgets.

“If you take a bag of maize today and then the amount that they charge for kenkey, pepper and the fish is not commensurate with the bag of maize. So as a country, we need to do something,” he said.

He expressed concern that salary increases could fail to translate into improved living standards if the cost of essential goods continued to rise.

“It looks as if somebody is pretending to be giving something and it's not adding up,” he said.

Calls for collective action

To illustrate his concerns about the relationship between workers’ remuneration and productivity, Mr Anaba recalled a remark attributed to former President John Agyekum Kufuor.

“I remember His Excellency John Kufuor said something. He said that we are pretending to be paying the worker and the work is also pretending to work,” he said.

Mr Anaba said that the situation was not in the country's interest and urged stakeholders to work together to address the underlying challenges.

“That is not good for us. We need to come together and see how we can resolve this issue,” he said.

The comments come after an agreement to increase base pay for public sector workers by eight per cent in 2027.

Mr Anaba's position is that the agreement should not prevent further engagement if developments during the year undermine the value of workers’ earnings.

Ghana News.title: Beyond survival: The unseen battles breast cancer survivors continue to fight
Ghana News.content:
Surviving breast cancer is a blessing, but for many, the journey towards recovery continues long after treatment ends.

Every October, breast cancer awareness campaigns remind us of the importance of early detection, prevention and access to treatment. Advocates call on governments to equip health facilities, strengthen cancer services and ensure that patients receive timely care. These demands are necessary. In Ghana, delays in accessing treatment remain a concern, with a 2025 study of patients referred for breast biopsies in the Oti and Volta regions documenting substantial gaps in treatment initiation.

But there is another conversation we must have. What happens after treatment? What becomes of the people who survive cancer but continue to struggle with its physical and emotional consequences?

As a breast cancer survivor, I write this from the deepest part of my heart. I know that surviving cancer is a blessing, but I also know that the end of treatment does not necessarily mean the end of suffering.

I was diagnosed with stage three invasive carcinoma, grade three, triple-negative breast cancer. In simple terms, invasive carcinoma means the cancer had spread beyond its point of origin within the breast tissue. Grade three means the cancer cells looked very abnormal and were likely to grow and spread more quickly. Triple-negative means the cancer cells lacked three important markers: oestrogen receptors, progesterone receptors and excess HER2 protein. This makes hormone therapy and HER2-targeted treatment unsuitable, leaving chemotherapy, surgery, radiotherapy and, in some cases, immunotherapy among the treatment options.

I underwent eight gruelling cycles of chemotherapy, surgery and 16 fractions of radiotherapy during the COVID-19 lockdown.

I remain deeply grateful to God Almighty for the gift of life. I do not take for granted the opportunity to watch my daughter grow, continue my work and pursue the things that matter to me. My gratitude, however, does not mean that I am free from the consequences of the treatment that helped save my life.

The battle does not always end when treatment ends.

According to the US National Cancer Institute, some cancer-treatment side effects persist for months or years, while others emerge long after treatment has ended. Their nature and severity vary from one survivor to another.

Peripheral neuropathy, for instance, is nerve damage that can cause pain, tingling, numbness or weakness, particularly in the hands and feet. Some chemotherapy drugs can cause this condition, and symptoms may persist after treatment. Survivors may also experience persistent fatigue, joint and muscle pain, restricted movement, lymphoedema (swelling caused by a build-up of lymph fluid), sleep difficulties and problems with memory or concentration.

Surgery and radiotherapy can leave lasting pain, tightness and changes in movement. Some survivors also experience early menopause, sexual difficulties, anxiety and depression. Nausea and dizziness can occur during treatment, but persistent or recurring symptoms years later should not automatically be attributed to cancer treatment. They require appropriate medical assessment.

For some survivors, these struggles become part of daily life. The pain may come and go. It may last for minutes, hours or days. A person may appear perfectly fine at work, in church or at a social gathering, yet return home exhausted and hurting.

I know what this feels like.

Sometimes, the muscle pain I experience lasts about some minutes and subsides. At other times, it persists for days, becoming so intense that I struggle to cope. I sometimes take painkillers, but I worry about relying on them too frequently. On other occasions, I endure the pain, hoping it will pass. Even when medication is taken, the relief is not always what I need.

There are nights when sleep becomes difficult, and occasions when I wake up vomiting without an obvious explanation. Sometimes, I seek medical attention and undergo laboratory investigations, only for the results to provide no clear explanation for what I am experiencing.

Imagine being in pain for days, taking medication that offers limited relief, trying to carry on with your responsibilities at the same time. Imagine then encountering someone who dismisses your struggles and suggests that you are pretending to be sick. And oh! The forgetfulness and extreme fatigue ! That is a story for another day!

It is painful enough to live with symptoms you cannot always explain. Having your honesty questioned adds an unnecessary emotional burden.

I share this not to invite sympathy but to highlight a reality that many survivors face. The cruelty of being judged by people who have no idea what it takes to get through an ordinary day.

Those who are quick to accuse others of pretending to be sick must understand the harm their words can cause. Such remarks can deepen emotional distress, undermine trust and leave survivors feeling isolated. Before questioning someone's health, pause and consider what that person might be enduring in silence.

The need for compassion and continued care

Breast cancer survivors should be able to speak about their struggles without fear of ridicule. They need employers who recognise that recovery is not always linear, colleagues who exercise understanding and health services that provide follow-up care beyond the completion of treatment.

The World Health Organisation's Global Breast Cancer Initiative recognises comprehensive care, including rehabilitation and services to relieve pain, as essential parts of breast cancer management. This means survivorship must be taken seriously. Access to appropriate medical reviews, pain management, physiotherapy, psychological support and regular follow-up should not be treated as luxuries.

In Ghana, conversations about cancer care must therefore extend beyond awareness campaigns and treatment facilities to include the quality of life of those who survive. Survivors need support to manage lasting complications and live with dignity.

Choosing gratitude and hope

To fellow survivors who have encountered insensitive people, please do not allow their words to define your experience. You do not need to spend your energy proving your pain to everyone. Seek medical care when you need it, lean on people who understand, and speak up when you have the strength to do so. Protect your peace without feeling compelled to harbour bitterness.

I belong to survivor support groups where we share our experiences, encourage one another and realise that many of us are fighting battles that the outside world cannot see. Some endure challenges more difficult than mine. Our experiences remind me that compassion is not optional, it is part of how we help one another live beyond cancer.

Above all, I remain grateful to God for preserving my life. Cancer changed my life, but it did not become my whole identity. I am more than my diagnosis, more than the treatment I endured and more than the symptoms I continue to manage.

This October, as we speak about preventing breast cancer and saving lives through early detection, let us also remember those who have survived. Let us ask what support they need, listen when they speak and create room for them to recover at their own pace.

Because the goal should not simply be to help people survive breast cancer. It should be to help them live well afterwards, without stigma, without shame and without having to fight for the basic dignity of being believed.

Ghana News.title: T-bills auction: Government borrowed GH¢14bn in October 2026
Ghana News.content:
A total of GH¢19.9 billion was tendered for treasury bills by investors in October 2026, as against a target of GH¢16.37 billion.

This represented a 21.99% oversubscription.

However, the government accepted GH¢14.97bn, a GH¢1.40bn short of its target.

Importantly, investor demand was relatively high as the Treasury exceeded most of its target.

Last week, investor appetite for T-bills moderated at October’s final auction, with total bids declining by 40.28% week-on-week to GH¢2.55bn.

Despite softer demand, subscriptions exceeded the Treasury’s GHS2.45bn target by 4.13%.

However, the government accepted only GH¢1.92bn.

The yields eased across all tenors, with the 91-day, 182-day and 364-day rates declining by 1.0 basis point, 3.0 basis points and 7.0 basis points to 4.60%, 6.26% and 9.60%, respectively.

Meanwhile, the government is seeking to raise GH¢3.54bn through the issuance of 91- day, 182-day, and 364-day bills this week,

This will cover maturing bills of GH¢3.21 billion.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
