World.title: Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
World.content:
At least 26 people were killed after Russian bombs hit an aid distribution centre, in an attack that Ukraine's leader has called "utterly horrific".

Five people were injured and 27 initially reported missing after at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit the village of Komyshuvakha in the southern Zaporizhzhia region, regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said that after the first strike on the local school "used for humanitarian needs", there was a second attack on the place where people were sheltering.

He posted a video showing a huge crater left after Monday's attack, and rescuer teams searching through the rubble.

The Russian military has not publicly commented.

World.title: Thousands of European troops to rehearse Ukraine deployment in event of peace
World.content:
Britain and France are to lead a military exercise to test a multinational force's ability to deploy to Ukraine, if there is a peace deal.

Nearly 3,000 military personnel from 12 European nations will take part in the rehearsal in neighbouring Poland this month.

Plans for a reassurance force for Ukraine were set out last year as one of the long-term security guarantees being proposed by European nations.

But there are still more questions than answers as to how such a military force might work in practice. Western officials stress that any force sent to Ukraine would not take part in offensive operations or be involved in peacekeeping or ceasefire monitoring missions.

Nor would they be operating under the command of Nato or on the front line.

Officials say their presence would be to provide reassurance to Ukraine and to help rebuild its armed forces.

The US has been involved in discussions, but is not contributing to the mission.

Russia has already voiced opposition to foreign troops being stationed in Ukraine and, last year, President Vladimir Putin said they would be "legitimate targets".

Western officials have declined to spell out the rules of engagement if any international troops were to be attacked in Ukraine. Though they say the force would be able to defend itself.

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the exercise showed Britain, France and their allies were stepping up preparation for the day when peace came to Ukraine.

He said: "This is not a hypothetical plan, it's a real force, ready to help Ukraine once the fighting stops."

Lt Gen Tom Bateman, the UK commander of the Multi National Force â Ukraine (MNF-U), said the exercise represented an important step in translating political commitments into credible military readiness.

He said it was a "real, capable, readily deployable force that represented a serious commitment from Coalition of the Willing nations to Ukraine's long-term stability and security".

World.title: Plane may have broken apart ahead of deadly Florida jet crash, say investigators
World.content:
It confirmed that, after the jet took off from Austin, the crew transmitted to air traffic control that they were encountering ice and moderate turbulence.

"We are picking up precipitation, requesting to climb to 37,000 feet if able," the crew said.

NTSB member Tom Chapman said that less than 30 seconds later, the plane began to descend and the crew issued a mayday call.

The transmission then became "unintelligible", he said, adding that: "Sadly, all aboard were lost."

The NTSB said that ice and turbulence were factors in the crash but that determining its probable cause will be a "lengthy investigatory process".

Thunderstorms had been reported in the area at the time.

Officials are also trying to find out whether a cockpit voice recorder was on board at the time of the crash and if it can be recovered.

As part of the investigation, the NTSB is working with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), representatives from Learjet as well as meteorologists and air traffic control experts.

Recovering the wreckage from the crater on the roadway will be a "daunting challenge", said Timothy Monville, an air safety investigator with the safety board.

World.title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
World.content:
Stephan Moelans, the CEO of Sabcobel, which operates Delhaize's systems, on Monday told the Belga news agency that the incident was a cyber-attack and that the company had been "working all night and morning to disconnect the affected units from the network".

He said since the French attack in early October, the company had been working to "protect our customers fridges against this vulnerability" but that the units needed physical modifications, not just software updates.

Most supermarkets across Europe are linked to the internet, and maintenance and troubleshooting can be done remotely.

"The simplest solution is to manage the fridges over a secure internet connection. Most of our customers switched to that after the attack in France," Moelans added.

The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C (122F).

It is unclear who is behind the latest apparent attack.

In the US, authorities are investigating what caused refrigeration malfunctions at a number of American military bases in August and working together with French officials to examine whether the incidents could be linked.

Both Belgium and Sweden's national cyber-security agencies said they were monitoring the incident.

The UK's National Cyber Security Centre said it was working with international partners and industry to "fully understand details of an incident". No incidents have been reported in the UK.

In Flanders, northern Belgium, a Delhaize branch in Hoeilaart told news website Het Laatste Nieuws it had lost â¬100,000 (Â£83,500) worth of produce.

The manager said that estimate did not even take into account further losses that would result from closing the shop.

Carrefour, a French-owned supermarket, said the incident had only affected 15 of its Belgian stores, adding that measures had been taken immediately to ensure all shops remained open.

A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, told Reuters news agency five shops had their fridge systems attacked.

Sweden's budget furniture retailer Ikea said refrigeration systems of its store in the western Belgian city of Mons were affected, with a spokesman quoted by Reuters as saying "we cannot rule out that additional locations may be affected".

World.title: Fighting returns to Kherson region after longest Ukraine war ceasefire
World.content:
Fighting has resumed in Ukraine's Kherson after a six-day truce brought quiet to the front-line region for the first time in years.

The ceasefire - the longest since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022 - allowed hundreds of people trapped in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky and its surroundings to be evacuated.

On Monday morning, local authorities confirmed that strikes had resumed, saying Moscow had hit a medical facility in Kherson city centre. They also said a 62-year-old woman and a 73-year-old man were injured when a Russian drone attacked the car they were travelling in.

Ukraine also accused Russian forces of using the humanitarian ceasefire to strengthen their military positions, rotate units and deliver ammunition.

"The enemy used the humanitarian pause to set up their positions," said Ukraine's General Staff, adding they had recorded rotation of Russian units, expansion of anti-drone equipment on the roads, and delivery of ammunition.

The Kremlin appeared to corroborate this when spokesman Dmitry Peskov said it was "reasonable to assume that the Ukrainian army also used this period for the necessary regrouping".

"It is a completely standard practice in such situations," he added.

The ceasefire had been brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. Both Kyiv and Moscow thanked her repeatedly, though no details of her involvement were shared.

An unusual show of cooperation came from Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova and her Ukrainian counterpart Dmytro Lubinets. The pair oversaw the ceasefire, travelled into Oleshky and were filmed speaking to residents together. They publicly thanked each other for their work, often highlighting that no violations of the ceasefire had been observed.

Both Lantratova and Lubinets called for the initiative to be repeated elsewhere, and Ukraine repeatedly said it would be prepared to observe similar ceasefires on a national level too.

But many have questioned whether this will lead to more cooperation and further truces.

In fact, the Kremlin swiftly dismissed the idea even as the ceasefire was under way, calling Oleshky "an isolated case" which would not affect the "settlement process" â a euphemism for the stalled peace talks. "There are no similar plans or initiatives," Peskov reiterated on Monday.

And although last week the guns fell silent in Kherson region, elsewhere in Ukraine Russia's air strikes continued, killing scores of civilians and destroying crucial infrastructure.

The decision to observe an unusually broad and comparatively lengthy ceasefire in and around Oleshky was therefore a notable exception.

The ceasefire's observance appears, at least in part, to have been linked to Melania Trump's reported involvement. By violating the truce, Moscow would have risked undermining its own efforts to cultivate the crucial relationship with her husband, US President Donald Trump.

Some commentators have argued that Trump himself would be interested in presenting the Oleshky ceasefire as a foreign policy achievement scored days before the US midterm elections on Tuesday.

"I totally get why our official representatives need to 'play along' with the US first lady on Oleshky," said Artyom Sheynin, a prominent figure on Russian state TV.

"I understand why it's so important to create a 'success story' ahead of the elections for the US president, whose wife 'achieved a ceasefire' in Oleshky."

Kyiv, too, had its reasons to be fully compliant. Although relations with the US and its president are often fraught, Ukraine continues to rely heavily on US intelligence and US-made Patriot air defence missiles to counter Russian aerial attacks. Ahead of another tough winter of war, continued American support is essential to protect Ukrainian skies from Russia's assaults.

But though the ceasefire may have been born out of political calculation rather than purely humanitarian compassion, it also resulted in hundreds of civilians escaping.

There were emotional scenes when hundreds of Oleshky residents arrived in northern Ukraine on Saturday. Many were met by tearful relatives they had not seen in years. To the journalists waiting, the evacuees told of years of hunger and hardship in a destroyed town.

The hundreds of residents who decided to stay behind will receive monthly humanitarian aid deliveries, Lantratova said, adding that decision too was the result of Melania Trump's mediation.

Yet the troop rotations and resupply efforts show that neither side is expecting Oleshky to be a blueprint for lasting respite in the future.

As Kherson came under fire again, Ukrainian drones hit several energy facilities across four Russian regions. In Samara, residents reported hearing explosions and seeing black plumes of smoke rising into the sky as an oil refinery was hit for the fifth time in a month.

If the truce brought a rare moment of relief to Oleshky, it has done little to alter the wider trajectory of a war that grinds on for now.

World.title: Legal challenge to Australia's social media ban to start in High Court
World.content:
Two days of hearings on a challenge to Australia's landmark social media ban for children will begin at the country's highest court on Tuesday.

In a major test of the world-leading policy, a digital rights group will argue that the ban for under-16s robs children of their right to free communication. A separate challenge launched by platform Reddit will be jointly heard.

Introduced last December, the ban is a key part of sweeping changes the Australian government has spearheaded in recent years on online safety.

Supporters say the ban protects children from harmful content but critics say it is too blunt an instrument and efforts should focus on improving online safety.

The constitutional challenge in Australia's High Court was filed by the Digital Freedom Project a few weeks before the ban started on 10 December last year. The group is lead by New South Wales parliamentarian John Ruddick.

Two teens who originally spearheaded the case, Noah Jones and Macy Neyland, have since withdrawn as plaintiffs though Jones is still expected to attend Tuesday's hearing.

Speaking about the legal challenge last November, Jones told the BBC that there were bad things online but a blanket ban for under-16s was not the right answer.

"We shouldn't be using the resources and money of these social media platforms to try to avoid fines from our government," he said.

"They should be using this money and resources to try to get rid of the predators and harmful content out there."

Reddit also launched a High Court challenge to the ban, arguing the policy has serious implications for privacy and political rights.

The company said it shared Australia's goal of protecting young people online "but there are better and more effective ways" than a ban.

"As we challenge this law in court, we'll continue to comply with it and advocate for more effective youth safety measures," said Reddit's chief communications officer Adam Collins.

Communications Minister Anika Wells last year said the government would not be "intimidated by legal threats."

"We will not be intimidated by big tech. On behalf of Australian parents, we will stand firm," she said last November.

Under the ban, ten platforms - Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, Snapchat, X, Kick, Threads and Twitch - must take "reasonable steps" to ensure no one under 16 years old can access its site.

Platforms risk fines of up to A$99m (US$70m, Â£52m) for serious or repeated breaches, but since the ban started, no company has been fined.

World.title: North Korea denies being behind record $6.3bn Binance hack
World.content:
North Korea has denied claims that it was behind the record $6.3bn (Â£4.7bn) hack of cryptocurrency exchange Binance, calling the allegations "absurd rhetoric".

Kim Yo-jong, a top Democratic People's Republic of Korea official and the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said on Tuesday that the accusations are another "sinister attempt" by the US to damage Pyongyang's public image.

The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the Secret Service and cyber analysts have said North Korea orchestrated the hack, which has been described as the largest in history.

This is the latest hack to be linked to North Korea, which has been accused of relying on cyber-crime to help finance its sanctioned economy.

Blockchain analysts and the FBI have said the attack was led by state-backed hacking group TraderTraitor.

The FBI has called on industry partners to help block transactions involving cryptocurrency accounts linked to the group.

"The US has made a trite provocation of linking it with the Democratic People's Republic of Korea again," Kim Yo-jong, the director of North Korea's General Affairs Department, said in a statement.

"It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads the international public opinion as if all the cyber crimes in different parts of the world are our deeds," she said.

World.title: Man and boy arrested after allegedly attacking One Nation volunteer with baseball bat in Australia
World.content:
Two people have been arrested after a volunteer for Australia's right-wing populist party One Nation was allegedly assaulted with a baseball bat.

A man, 37, and a boy, 14, were arrested on Sunday night after an incident outside the volunteer's home in Torquay, about 100km (62 miles) south-west of Melbourne.

The man was charged with assault offences and remanded in custody while the boy was issued with a caution. The volunteer was hospitalised with non-life threatening injuries, police said.

One Nation's Victorian leader Warren Pickering claimed the attack happened after the pair "interfered with" election signs on the volunteer's property.

Pickering said the alleged assault was "un-Australian and unacceptable".

"Political violence or intimidation of any kind against anyone is unacceptable in this country," he said.

"If you don't like someone's politics, you vote accordingly. You don't assault them."

Victorian Premier Ben Carroll described the attack as "shocking".

"Whether you're wearing a red, a blue, an orange, or a green T-shirt, they are volunteers," he said.

"They are out there doing what they believe is right, and no one should be coming under attack."

The alleged attack comes during a state election campaign in Victoria, and amid a reckoning in the country more broadly over the tone of political debate, after the attack on Federal MP Helen Haines last month.

Police have not detailed a motive for the incident - which left Haines needing both of her legs amputated - but politicians, law enforcement, and experts have said heated public discourse is heightening the threat of political violence in the country.

World.title: APC Rally: Hard part of our economic reset over; next term is pure harvest – VP Shettima
World.content:
Vice President Kashim Shettima has said the toughest phases of Nigeria’s aggressive economic reset undertaken by the administration of President Bola Tinubu are officially over, clearing the runway for an era of pure harvest, nationwide growth and prosperity.

He said the administration’s painful but necessary economic reforms have laid the groundwork for prosperity, promising that the next phase will deliver tangible fruits of these sacrifices to citizens.

Speaking on Monday in Calabar, Cross River State, during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally, Mr Shettima rallied support for the re-election of President Tinubu and the state governor, Bassey Otu, as well as other APC candidates in the 2027 general election, describing them as trustworthy friends of the people.

Saying the administration has completed the hardest part of the economic reset, he argued that no rival political party has the capacity to alter the nation’s economic trajectory.

VP Shettima assured that the upcoming second term will focus entirely on delivering prosperity and tangible rewards for all citizens if President Tinubu’s mandate is renewed.

“We are confident of this promise to deliver for this nation because we have already done the most difficult job of economic reset. None of the other options available has the capacity to move the needle of the economy. We have rescued the economy, and the road ahead is one of harvest. This second term is one of harvest, for you and all Nigerians.

“I therefore stand before you today to ask you, once again, to renew the mandate of His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, as President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and myself as Vice President. And another term for Senator Bassey Edet Otu and Hon. Peter Odey as Governor and Deputy Governor of Cross River State, respectively,” he stated.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The vice president maintained that what has brought the APC and Nigerians together is an alliance for progress, prosperity, opportunity and dignity, stressing that the conviction that must govern every decision is that the people are the purpose.

He noted that the Tinubu administration and the APC are seeking the opportunity to carry their work into a second term because authority belongs to the people, and those entrusted with authority must return with an account of stewardship and a programme worthy of further trust.

Mr Shettima commended the APC in the state for keeping its house in order and becoming a model of strength and vision, unity and discipline, courage and conviction, loyalty and service, sacrifice and solidarity, noting that the discipline within its ranks has produced diligence in government.

He said when the administration took office in 2023, it did not doubt the need to open up Cross River State to the world, which informed the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway.

“This is the wisdom behind the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway. This transformative infrastructure project will connect coastal communities. It will ease the movement of goods and people. It will expand tourism. It will attract investors and create thousands of direct and indirect jobs. Our vision is for Cross River to become a major beneficiary of this economic revolution,” he stated.

The VP also said the Bakassi Deep Sea Port has received federal government approval and support under President Tinubu, pledging to make the dream come true as an international maritime gateway.

This gateway, according to him, will attract shipping companies, generate employment, stimulate industrial development, and open enormous economic opportunities for factories, businesses, and households sustained by trade.

He added that proposing Calabar as the location for the Gulf of Guinea Commission Secretariat would strengthen the state’s international visibility, attract diplomatic and commercial activity, stimulate hospitality and tourism, create employment, and translate regional cooperation into economic opportunities.

VP Shettima assured that the federal government not only recognises Cross River’s littoral status but also acknowledges its efforts toward resolving the dispute over 46 oil wells.

He further stated that the government is prepared to ensure a resolution is reached to strengthen the state’s maritime identity and open prospects for greater participation in the blue economy, maritime investment, and potential derivation benefits.

On education, the Vice President said the state is well represented in the disbursement of education funds through NELFUND, which drives human capital development, provides relief for parents, ensures continued schooling for young people, and widens access to higher education.

He maintained that no parent should have to watch the abilities of their kids surrender to a shortage of money, saying the initiative aligns with Project HOPE Education for stronger foundational learning, teacher development, better school management, improved access to quality education and greater accountability.

Insisting the administration has much to finish, the VP demanded continuity with scrutiny, saying citizens should never have to surrender their questions to show support.

He assured that the government will keep the affairs of the people at the centre, listen when households speak of hardship, act when communities identify neglect and correct what fails the public. The People Are the Purpose.

Earlier, the National Chairman of the APC, Nentanwe Yilwatda, appealed to the people of Cross River to support the party in the forthcoming elections at all levels, saying President Tinubu is a change agent who deserves re-election on many grounds.

He cited the consolidation of the Deep Sea Port project, the resuscitation of the Calabar Port, the Trans-Saharan Super Highway, and other projects as reasons to support the APC ticket in the 2027 presidential election.

In his welcome address, Governor Otu saluted the courage and farsightedness of President Tinubu, particularly in leading Nigeria at a difficult time and yet on the path of genuine prosperity and sustainable development.

Highlighting the president’s policies in agriculture, education, industry and security, the governor assured that the people of Cross River would unanimously ensure President Tinubu’s re-election, noting that the benefits of the administration’s reforms were already manifesting and would yield greater benefits in the years to come.

For his part, the Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Abdulaziz Yari, said President Tinubu had performed creditably well and is deserving of a second term, dispelling rumours that the northern part of the country would not support the president’s re-election bid.

Earlier, on a courtesy visit to the Palace of the Obong of Calabar, Edidem Otu, the vice president, said the visit was to acquaint him with the party’s aspirations in the 2027 general elections and to pay homage to the traditional institution in the state.

He applauded the paramount ruler of the Efik people for his steadfast devotion to preserving the cultural heritage and virtues of the Efik nation, which he said is worthy of emulation by political leaders across the country.

For his part, Governor Otu sought royal blessings and support for the APC and the federal government under President Tinubu.

In his remarks, the Obong of Calabar thanked his guests for the visit and the honour of presenting their wishes, aspirations and requests for royal recognition and approval.

He said the visit to the palace was the beginning of greater unity among traditional rulers in the state and urged unity and peaceful coexistence among leaders and people of the state.

He also applauded the reforms and policies of the Tinubu administration, describing the president as a man with the heart to take on difficult reforms with long-term benefits for the country and its citizens.

Also present at the Calabar campaign rally were Senate President Godswill Akpabio; Governors Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom; Monday Okpebholo of Edo; and Hope Uzodinma of Imo; members of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, and party leaders from Cross, River State, the South-south region and beyond.

Stanley Nkwocha

Senior Special Assistant To The President on Media & Communications

(Office of The Vice President)

2nd November, 2026

World.title: Less than 10% of Nigerian property have proper land titles – Finance Ministry
World.content:
The Managing Director of the Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI), Armstrong Takang has said that less than 10 per cent of properties across Nigeria have proper land titles, a situation that limits access to credit, discourages investment and weakens confidence in the country’s real estate market.

Mr Takang made the disclosure on Monday in Abuja at a stakeholder conference organised by the House of Representatives on a proposed legislation to establish the National Real Estate Regulatory Authority (NRERA).

He said the lack of reliable property documentation has left many Nigerians unable to use their assets as collateral to secure loans, thereby restricting the economic benefits they could derive from property ownership.

“Less than 10 percent of the properties nationwide have proper titles,” he said.

“So we invariably are creating a scenario where people own assets but are not able to use those assets for things that could deliver more value.”

Mr Takang linked the problem to Nigeria’s low credit penetration, noting that lending stood at about 12.9 per cent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), compared with 20.1 per cent across sub-Saharan Africa and 34 per cent in lower-middle-income countries.

He explained that real estate is a major source of collateral for lending, but the absence of verifiable ownership records makes it difficult for financial institutions to accept properties as security.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, weak regulatory oversight, fraudulent land transactions and the absence of a national licensing framework have further undermined the sector’s capacity to attract investment.

He also raised concerns about the prevalence of building collapses, disclosing that more than 270 deaths had been recorded in recent years, although the actual figure could be higher because some incidents go unreported.

“Over 270 deaths have been recorded in just a few years, and this is what we know and on record. I believe the number is higher than that because many of them are not reported because of poor buildings and building collapses,” he said.

The MOFI chief said the proposed regulatory authority would introduce standards for property transactions, establish licensing requirements for real estate agents and developers, and provide safeguards for funds paid by prospective property buyers.

He warned that the absence of effective regulation had enabled unlicensed operators to collect billions of naira from investors without delivering the properties promised.

Abdulmumin Jibrin, chairman of the House Committee on Housing and Habitat, said the proposed legislation was intended to address institutional gaps and overlapping responsibilities that have weakened the regulation of Nigeria’s housing and real estate sector.

Mr Jibrin said the Minister of Housing and Urban Development currently lacked direct jurisdiction over all agencies and institutions involved in the housing sector, creating gaps in coordination and duplication of responsibilities.

“There are enormous challenges. We have a wonderful minister of housing. But as the Minister of Housing of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, he does not have jurisdiction over all the agencies and institutions involved in housing. There is a link; there is a gap. So, there is duplication of functions,” he said.

He compared the situation with sectors such as oil and gas, electricity and telecommunications, where regulatory structures provide clearer oversight of industry operators.

The lawmaker said the absence of a comprehensive regulatory framework in real estate had allowed individuals and companies to undertake property development without adequate accountability.

He, however, clarified that the proposed legislation would not encroach on the constitutional powers of state governments or take over the statutory responsibilities of existing professional bodies.

Rather, he said, the authority would promote cooperation between the federal and state governments while preserving the functions of professional institutions operating in the sector.

Nigeria’s mortgage penetration remains low

The Minister of Housing and Urban Development, Muttaqha Darma, also identified limited access to mortgage financing as a major obstacle to homeownership in Nigeria.

He said mortgage penetration in the country remained below 10 per cent, significantly lower than the levels recorded in some other countries.

“Our population, as of today, is estimated to be about 240 million. But, as speakers after speakers mentioned, mortgage penetration is very low. It is less than 10 percent, as against 38 percent in Malaysia and 40 percent in South Korea,” he said.

Mr Darma said the federal government was addressing structural and institutional challenges in the housing sector, adding that the proposed authority would strengthen efforts to improve regulation and access to decent, affordable housing.

He also suggested that the authority, once established, should operate under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Development to ensure effective coordination with existing government housing policies.

Abbas advocates digitised property administration

In his remarks, Speaker of the House of Representatives, Abbas Tajudeen, called for a centralised and digitised real estate administrative system to simplify property transactions, improve transparency and attract investment.

He said Nigeria’s challenge was not a shortage of property but the lack of confidence in the systems governing ownership and transactions.

“Nigeria does not lack property. Nigeria lacks enough trust in property,” Mr Tajudeen said.

The speaker argued that an effective regulatory framework would help protect property buyers and investors from fraudulent transactions, exploitation, and unfair competition.

He added that stronger oversight was necessary to restore confidence in the real estate market and ensure that property ownership translates into economic value for Nigerians.

World.title: 2027: PDP expels aspirants challenging Pantami’s candidacy as Gombe governorship candidate
World.content:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has expelled two of its governorship aspirants in Gombe State, Khamisu Mailantarki and Usman Garry, over alleged anti-party activities and a breach of its constitution.

The expulsion was announced in a statement issued on Monday by the party’s National Publicity Secretary, Jungudo Mohammed.

Messrs Mailantarki and Garry contested the Gombe governorship primaries but lost to Isa Pantami, a former minister of Communications and Digital Economy.

The PDP conducted two governorship primaries in Gombe State after a court nullified its first exercise, which had produced Mr Pantami as its candidate for the 2027 election.

The first primary was held on 26 May, with Mr Pantami emerging as the party’s candidate through voice affirmation after he defected from the All Progressives Congress (APC).

His emergence was challenged by other aspirants, particularly Messrs Mailantarki and Garry, who argued that the process was irregular and excluded eligible contestants.

On 24 September, the Federal High Court in Gombe, presided over by Justice Amina Mohammed, nullified the primary and ordered the party to conduct another election within 30 days.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The court found that the exercise did not comply with the party’s internal rules and relevant electoral laws, particularly because some screened aspirants were excluded from the process.

However, the court did not disqualify Mr Pantami from the PDP or invalidate his party membership.

The rerun was held on 29 September across the state’s 11 local government areas, with Mr Pantami again declared the winner after securing the most votes.

Both Mr Mailantarki and Mr Garry rejected aspects of the rerun, although they raised different objections.

Mr Mailantarki challenged Mr Pantami’s eligibility to participate, arguing that he joined the PDP after the party had submitted its list of aspirants to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). He also questioned Mr Pantami’s participation in the APC governorship primary before defecting to the PDP.

He maintained that the contest should have been between him and Mr Garry and argued that he should have been declared the winner after Mr Pantami’s votes were discounted.

Mr Garry, on the other hand, alleged irregularities in the exercise in his area. He claimed he was prevented from voting and that only five votes from his supporters were counted after he insisted that voting should take place.

For rejecting the outcome, the Gombe PDP suspended both aspirants for one month over alleged anti-party activities and referred them to the party’s disciplinary committee.

Meanwhile, Mr Garry is still challenging Mr Pantami’s candidacy in court. He is seeking to join an ongoing suit filed by Mr Pantami and the PDP against INEC. The case concerns Mr Pantami’s eligibility to participate in the PDP primary and the commission’s initial decision to exclude him from the list of candidates for the 2027 Gombe governorship election.

Anti-party allegations

In the expulsion notice, Mr Mohammed said the decision followed the findings of the party’s disciplinary committee, which found the two aspirants guilty of anti-party activities.

“Their expulsion followed the findings of the Party’s Disciplinary Committee and due consideration by the relevant organs of the Party, in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution of the Peoples Democratic Party (as amended in 2017), particularly Section 57, Section 58(1), and Section 59, which deal with offences and disciplinary measures.

“The affected persons were found to have engaged in conduct inconsistent with the Party’s Constitution, including anti-party activities, gross misconduct, and acts capable of bringing the Party into disrepute, contrary to Section 58(1)(a), (b), (h) and (j) of the PDP Constitution,” he said.

Mr Mohammed said the decision was taken in compliance with the principles of fair hearing as provided for in the party’s constitution and the Nigerian Constitution.

“The decision was taken in strict compliance with the principles of fair hearing as enshrined in Section 57(6) of the Party Constitution and Section 36 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended).

“Accordingly, by virtue of Section 59(1)(j) of the PDP Constitution, Hon. Khamisu Ahmed Mailantarki and Hon. Usman Aliyu Garry cease to be members of the Peoples Democratic Party and shall have no rights, privileges, or affiliation with the Party at any level.”

The PDP spokesperson urged members to refrain from activities that could undermine the party.

“The Party reiterates that its Constitution remains supreme and binding on all members. No member, regardless of status, is above the party’s laws and disciplinary framework.

“The party urges all members to remain loyal, disciplined, and committed to the ideals of the PDP and to work collectively towards strengthening the Party at all levels,” he said.

World.title: IPI Nigeria to examine AI’s threat to media integrity
World.content:
The International Press Institute (IPI) Nigeria will examine the growing threat artificial intelligence (AI) poses to media integrity and explore how newsrooms can use AI-powered verification tools to detect and counter misinformation at its 2026 conference and Annual General Meeting (AGM).

According to a statement jointly signed by the organisation’s Deputy President, Fidelis Mbah, and Secretary, Ahmed Shekarau, the two-day conference, themed “Truth Under Pressure: Journalism, AI and Information Integrity,” will be held on 2 and 3 December 2026, at the Bolton White Hotel, Wuse Zone 7, Abuja.

The conference will examine emerging challenges confronting the Nigerian media industry, particularly the impact of AI on journalism, information integrity, disinformation, press freedom and journalists’ safety.

It will also provide a platform for deliberations on critical national and industry issues, with a view to advancing the cause of free, independent and responsible journalism.

A key focus of the gathering, the statement added, will be strengthening collaboration between the media and security agencies.

The event is expected to attract policymakers, subject-matter experts, media executives, journalists and media freedom advocates.

Participants will examine how AI-generated deepfakes and other forms of synthetic media threaten public trust in journalism, particularly as Nigeria approaches the 2027 general elections.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Speaking ahead of the conference, IPI Nigeria President Musikilu Mojeed said the gathering would also explore how journalists could use AI-powered tools and transparent verification processes to safeguard the accuracy and integrity of information in their reporting.

Mr Mojeed said the conference would further provide an opportunity to assess the state of media freedom and journalists’ safety in Nigeria, discuss policy and legal reforms needed to strengthen independent journalism, and foster constructive engagement between the media and government on transparency and accountability.

He added that the gathering would facilitate the exchange of best practices and global perspectives on protecting press freedom and promoting responsible journalism.

The conference will also feature the induction of new members into IPI Nigeria, further expanding the organisation’s network and strengthening its commitment to defending press freedom and promoting responsible journalism in the country.

The second day, December 3, will be devoted to the organisation’s Annual General Meeting, an exclusive session for IPI Nigeria members.

The AGM will provide an opportunity to receive and deliberate on reports from the Executive Committee, review the organisation’s activities and strategic direction, and consider new initiatives and partnerships to strengthen press freedom and journalists’ safety in Nigeria.

Founded in 1950, IPI is a global network of editors, media executives and leading journalists spanning more than 100 countries. For over seven decades, the organisation has championed the promotion, protection and defence of press freedom and independent journalism around the world.

World.title: Failure to prosecute electoral offenders, threat to free, fair elections, says NHRC
World.content:
The Executive Secretary of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), Tony Ojukwu, identified, on Monday, the non-prosecution of electoral offenders as a challenge to free and fair elections.

Mr Ojukwu, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), said electoral offences will remain a problem in Nigeria as long as people can commit the crimes and get away without consequences.

He spoke when he hosted a delegation from the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel (UNOWAS) at the NHRC headquarters in Abuja.

The visiting delegation was led by the Representative of the United Nations Secretary-General for West Africa and the Sahel (SRSG) and Head of UNOWAS, Leonardo Simao.

The visit discussed Nigeria’s political and security developments, particularly preparations for the 2027 general elections, emerging challenges and opportunities, and efforts to promote peaceful elections.

Mr Ojukwu spoke of the commission’s preparedness towards ensuring a smooth conduct of the upcoming elections.

He said the commission had discovered that “people who are committing these election offences are acting on behalf of key politicians.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

This, according to him, makes it difficult for the politicians “to be held accountable for the acts of their agents.”

“And this continues to make the environment very fragile. Because as long as people can commit these election-related offences and go scot-free, then anybody can try anything they like,” the senior advocate said.

He expressed displeasure over the failure to implement a recommendation of the Justice Mohammed Uwais electoral reform report for “the establishment of an election offences framework, which is supposed to deal disproportionately with any election-related offence.” The committee was set up by the then-President Umaru Yar’adua to reform the nation’s electoral system after admitting that the 2007 election that brought him into office was flawed.

Mr Ojukwu noted that the visit was a very good occasion to bring this issue to the limelight, expressing confidence that the delegation would further interface with key government officials.

Mechanisms in place

Mr Ojukwu observed that political campaigns for the 2027 general elections have been marked by controversial remarks from public figures.

Prominent Islamic cleric Sani Jingir controversially described Nigeria as a Muslim-majority country and called for mass support for the Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in 2027 while condemning whoever opposed it.

This generated backlash and even led to the NHRC’s demand for Mr Jingir’s arrest for inciting religious hatred and hate speech.

Similarly, the senator representing Osun East Senatorial District, Francis Fadahunsi, issued death threats to members of the Accord Party found in the Ilesa axis of the state days before the Osun State governorship election in August.

In the same month, the Chairman of Kuje Area Council in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Danjuma Shekwolo, was seen in a video asking residents to either vote for the APC or leave the council areas.

Mr Ojukwu noted that all these do not encourage a level playing field for the campaign.

To curb this, Mr Ojukwu disclosed that the commission was preparing an advisory to guide the behaviour of political actors, security operatives and for the government to know its limits in interfering with citizens’ rights.

He also said another advisory to guide the government’s response to civic space is also in place to help address the fear induced by the misuse of the Cybercrime Act.

Campaigns must occur within the limits of the law

Mr Simao commended the NHRC for its effort. He noted that campaigns must occur within the limits of the law, the preservation of human life, and particularly the prevention of violence.

He noted that the essence of the visit was to work with different institutions, different stakeholders, and to learn from them how their institution is being prepared for this upcoming period.

“When elections go without violence, there is a lot of work that happens before. Sometimes it is not visible to the general public. Our role as a United Nations, and Nigeria is an important member of the United Nations, is to assist when necessary to reach the objective that the elections take place in a serene, peaceful atmosphere.”

Mr Simao encouraged NHRC to continue with that patriotic attitude and patriotic engagement to conduct peaceful elections.

He noted that the delegation did not come as inspectors to police the activities of the NHRC: “Our objective is that Nigeria continue to be an example of other kinds of support. So you cannot afford to fail. It’s forbidden for Nigeria to fail.

“Our work is continuing to remind you that you can do it and you are going to do it,” he said.

World.title: Foundation rolls out N4 billion empowerment programme in Kwara
World.content:
Businessman Yahaya Seriki has launched a N4 billion empowerment programme to support residents of Kwara State. The programme involved the distribution of cash, luxury cars and equipment to beneficiaries.

Through the Yahaya Seriki Foundation, Mr Seriki unveiled the initiative at an event held at Arca Santa Arena in Ilorin on Saturday.

The programme, supported by the Kursi Group, attracted a senator, Saliu Mustapha, Sulaiman Bolakale-Kawu and other dignitaries, including traditional and religious leaders.

Wealth creation and financial independence

The event, themed “Beyond Enterprises: Creating Wealth, Transforming Lives,” featured a panel discussion on financial independence, business development and wealth creation.

The session was moderated by Nasir AbdulKadir, chief executive officer of NAS TV Africa. Panellists included Sa’adat Bibire, a digital growth strategist and founder of Eight30Media; Halimat Gegele, a certified life coach; Deji Adeyanju, a lawyer and human rights activist; and Seyi Adekunle, a fashion entrepreneur and chairman of Seyi Vodi Group.

The panellists discussed strategies for building sustainable businesses, creating wealth and maintaining financial integrity. They urged beneficiaries to treat the intervention as an opportunity to build long-term financial security rather than spend the proceeds on immediate personal needs.

Mr Adeyanju said financial responsibility was essential to earning people’s trust, particularly in business, where individuals must demonstrate that they can manage money responsibly.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He urged beneficiaries to invest the support in activities that would improve their livelihoods.

“If you’re among the people privileged to receive this grant today, never use the money to do marriage or buy a new phone. This is money meant to change your life for good forever. You should use it to invest in your future,” he said.

Reasons for the intervention – Yahaya Seriki

In his opening remarks, Mr Seriki, a former governorship aspirant of the All Progressives Congress (APC), said the programme included the distribution of about 150 cars valued at N3.2 billion to people in Kwara State and neighbouring areas.

He said another N1 billion had been earmarked for cash empowerment, while artisans received industrial sewing machines valued at N350,000 each to support their businesses.

Mr Seriki urged the beneficiaries to use the items and financial support productively, stressing that building a successful business required commitment and responsible management.

“The purpose of this empowerment is to help people move forward in their own way of life. I’m doing this to give back to the society that contributed so much to my life,” he said.

He said the programme was also intended to support President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima, adding that its goal of promoting economic independence aligned with the federal government’s policies.

Mr Seriki, the founder and managing director of Kursi Group, said he had benefited from similar interventions in the past. He described those experiences as a motivation for supporting others and giving back to society.

He also urged Nigerians, particularly young people, to support Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Mr Seriki said the initiative aligned with the president’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which he described as a framework for improving the country’s economic prospects.

“We have a president who believes in building a better country and changing the narrative for the better. I believe we have never had it this good in the history of Nigeria,” he said.

Also speaking at the event, Yahaya Oloriegbe, a lawmaker representing Kwara Central Senatorial District, commended Mr Seriki for his efforts to improve the welfare of residents.

Mr Oloriegbe said the programme reflected the commitment of G-15, an APC political coalition, to building an inclusive Kwara State.

“This intervention by Mr Seriki is a laudable one. It is exactly what we promised in the previous years. What we promised by all of us at G-15 is to build Kwara where everybody lives at large,” the senator said.

Beneficiaries speak

Ishola Rosheedah, one of the beneficiaries, told PREMIUM TIMES that the car she received would ease the challenges of combining her university education with the responsibility of raising three children.

She said the cost and stress of commuting to school had been a major concern, adding that the car would provide much-needed relief.

“I have three children, but I am currently a student at a Nigerian university. The challenges of motherhood and commuting to school are things that disturb me badly. But this empowerment comes as a relief; no more transportation issues for me with this car. This car means a lot to me,” she said.

Another beneficiary, Sani Gbodofu, urged influential individuals within and outside Kwara State to support similar initiatives in their communities.

He prayed for God’s continued protection and blessings for Mr Seriki and his family.

World.title: 2027: Wike mobilises grassroots support for Tinubu’s re-election in FCT
World.content:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has urged residents to mobilise grassroots support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, saying a multi-party rainbow coalition will unite political stakeholders across party lines.

Mr Wike made the call on Monday during the commissioning of the Gwagwalada Civil Centre in Abuja, where he met political stakeholders from the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the area council.

In a statement signed by his spokesperson, Lere Olayinka, Mr Wike said the coalition showed that the collective interest of the people mattered more than individual political ambitions.

He urged Nigerians to embrace the rainbow coalition as a platform for national unity, political cooperation and sustainable development.

Mr Wike also criticised politicians who opposed the alliance, accusing them of failing to understand the value of unity and of being unable to command support within their communities.

“Some greedy and selfish politicians do not understand what we call unity. They have no capacity to hold their space; they have no capacity to even hold their families, and they have no capacity to hold their communities. So they can open their mouths and say there is no Rainbow Coalition,” he said.

He challenged critics to explain why political leaders who had previously disagreed could not work together to pursue common interests.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The minister described the political cooperation in Gwagwalada as a departure from confrontation, saying the FCT needed collaboration rather than unnecessary political hostility.

Wike urges residents to vote for Aduda

Mr Wike urged FCT residents not to repeat what he described as their mistake in the 2023 general elections, stressing the need for effective representation in the National Assembly.

He said the territory needed representatives who understood the challenges facing residents across its six area councils and could communicate their demands effectively to the federal government.

The minister also canvassed support for former FCT senator, Philip Aduda, and other candidates endorsed by the coalition, saying elected representatives should be accessible to their constituents and understand their concerns.

He urged residents to turn their support for Mr Tinubu into votes in the 2027 presidential election.

“On the day of the election, it will not be a day for market or fishing. It is the day all of us have decided to come together and demonstrate our strength through our votes. Go to the polling units, districts and communities and mobilise the people to vote for Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.

APC, PDP leaders welcome coalition

The Gwagwalada APC chairman, Ishaku Yamawo, described the mobilisation as historic, saying Mr Wike’s political intervention had brought together leaders and politicians who previously belonged to opposing camps.

READ ALSO: Wike praises Dunamis Church for building pedestrian bridge in Abuja

He said politicians who had not regarded one another as brothers because of party differences were now sitting together and agreeing to work under one political platform in Gwagwalada.

Mr Yamawo also commended the minister for reducing political tensions in the area, saying the campaign had become more peaceful and reduced violence.

The FCT PDP chairman, Ismaila Dogara, also praised Mr Wike for the development and for addressing the abandonment of projects in Gwagwalada over the past 16 years.

Mr Dogara said the presence of political leaders from different parties demonstrated the minister’s commitment to fostering cooperation among stakeholders.

World.title: Reflections on the 10th coronation anniversary of the Oba of Benin, By Samson R. Osagie
World.content:
For centuries, the Kingdom of Benin stood as a beacon of African civilisation, sophisticated governance, and artistic brilliance. At the centre of this magnificent heritage is the Monarch himself: the revered Oba of Benin, not just a traditional ruler but the living soul, spiritual anchor, and historical custodian of the Edo people.

The Benin Monarchy has survived empires, colonial invasions, the systematic theft of its sacred artefacts, and, more recently, the Obaseki administration’s attempt to denigrate, undermine, and dilute the Monarchy’s significance in contemporary governance. Yet a new and deeply painful threat is emerging. It is not coming from foreign adversaries, but from within our own house, driven by certain Benin and Edo indigenes living in Europe and the West.

A deeply disturbing trend has taken root across digital spaces: a coordinated wave of social media attacks, insults, and systematic denigration aimed directly at the revered stool of the Oba. Shielded by geographical distance and emboldened by the anonymity of the internet, these diaspora elements, backed by disgruntled political interests, have weaponised social media platforms to launch reckless assaults on a throne that our ancestors defended with their blood and sustained with their resilience.

This is not harmless modern commentary, progressive dialogue, or standard political debate. This is a direct assault on our collective identity, culture and heritage. When sons and daughters of the soil, enjoying the comforts of Europe and the West, turn around to insult the Oba of Benin, it is cyberbullying, stalking and a digital desecration of the entire Edo nation and the traditional institution in general.

Thanks to the United Nations General Assembly, which passed Resolution 79/243 against Cybercrimes, intended to strengthen international cooperation in combating certain crimes committed through information and communication technology systems and to share evidence in electronic form of serious crimes. This Convention, which is currently open for signature by States, is expected to remain open until 31st December 2026, hopefully until the fortieth signatory endorses the treaty. It is expected to provide States Parties with a range of measures to combat cybercrimes on the international stage.

For us as Edolites and particularly as Benins, we must not spare any opportunity to bring to justice those who have weaponised social media platforms to launch unreasonable attacks both on the person and institution of the Oba of Benin. No, we will confront this contemporary challenge to the throne the same way our forebears confronted all the historical challenges the Kingdom has faced.

Happily, the absolute absurdity and hollowness of these attacks were laid bare during the historic 10th Coronation Anniversary of His Royal Majesty, Oba Ewuare II, Commander of the Federal Republic. While a tiny fraction of disgruntled voices spewed bile online, the rest of the world gathered in Benin City to witness a breathtaking display of royal splendour, an intellectual discourse in honour of Oba Erediauwa hosted by the University of Benin, a spectacular royal Durbar, and global reverence, amongst other cultural activities. While online detractors tried to diminish the Crown, leaders at the highest levels of governance poured out unreserved accolades on the Royal Stool of Benin, exemplified by His Royal Majesty Oba Ewuare II.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu congratulated the Oba of Benin, warmly describing the monarch as “an enduring symbol of cultural heritage, dignity, and integrity”. State governors, including Edo State Governor Monday Okpebholo, alongside political leaders and first-class traditional rulers such as the Sultan of Sokoto, unreservedly affirmed the supremacy and sanctity of the Benin Royal Stool. The Vice-Chancellor of the University of Benin, Learned Professor Edoba Omoregie, SAN, acknowledged “His Royal Majesty’s role in fostering social cohesion, peaceful coexistence and strengthening the identity and cultural heritage of the Benin people.”

Social and cultural groups were not left out of the outpouring of eulogies for what many consider the most revered Monarch in Sub-Saharan Africa. The President of the Benin Club 1933, Professor Evbaziegbere Isibor, said in a goodwill message, “We celebrate your reign of peace, unity and progress, which continues to inspire hope and strengthen our culture and bring pride to the Benin Kingdom.” On its part, the Benin Consultative Forum, through its Acting President, Samson Osagie, noted: “that the reign of His Royal Majesty has ushered into the Kingdom a new lease of life characterised by positive traditional reforms that will further consolidate the global respect for the Kingdom, and that the unprecedented number of artefacts that have been returned from various parts of the world since the enthronement of His Royal Majesty is an attestation to the greatness of the Oba.”

All told, the pomp and pageantry that attended the 10th Coronation Anniversary celebration of His Royal Majesty has unequivocally proved that the Oba’s influence is not a localised affair; it remains a globally recognised institution of monumental importance.

It is profoundly tragic that while the President of Nigeria, state governors, and international delegations bow in respect to our heritage, some Edo people living in Europe and the West are attempting a new form of cultural vandalism. By trying to strip the monarchy of its reverence and reduce a sacred institution to an object of social media ridicule, they are doing the work of dismantling Edo pride from within.

We cannot, and will not, fold our arms and watch this happen.

The freedom of expression and living abroad should never become a license for renegades, fugitives and cultural infidels to continue to denigrate our age-old and God-ordained monarchy.

For as it is often said:

“Aisagbonrioba, Erinmwin Na Ke riore.”

As a community, both at home and in the diaspora, Edo people must rise with fierce urgency to defend the sanctity of the throne.

While appreciating a few who have risen to the occasion to defend the inviolability of our sacred monarch, if we continue to remain silent, we will be inviting further disrespect and assault on our collective identity and cultural heritage.

We must make it unequivocally clear to these foreign-based elements that the Oba of Benin is a red line that cannot be crossed.

Digital platforms must not become tools for cultural self-sabotage, nor should individuals use them to settle personal or political grievances against an ancient civilisation.

The strength of the Edo people has always lain in our unyielding unity and our fierce loyalty to the Royal Court of Benin, much as the British remain unconditionally loyal to the British Monarchy, regardless of the liberal democracy the United Kingdom practises.

The overwhelming success of the 10th Coronation Anniversary showed that the bond between the Oba and his people remains completely unbreakable.

Now more than ever, the global Edo community must channel that ancestral resilience to consolidate the pride of place the Benin Monarchy has always had in the world. The vast majority of Edo people in the diaspora who still hold their culture dear must speak up, isolate these toxic voices and recidivists and protect the custodian of our culture.

The Oba of Benin remains an enduring symbol of African dignity, a bridge to our glorious past, and the compass for our future. The modern world and its digital platforms will change, but the honour of the Benin Kingdom is eternal. Let those who launch arrows of disrespect from afar know this: the Edo soul is fiercely protective of its king, and we will completely reject, expose, and defeat any attempt to diminish the glory of the ancient Kingdom of Benin.

Oba gha t’o kpere, Ise!

Dr Samson R. Osagie is a lawyer, former minority whip of the House of Representatives and the immediate past Attorney General of Edo State.

World.title: Women in Politics: Nigeria’s political structure not built for women —  Adeola Azeez
World.content:
By Ebunoluwa Sessou

As Nigeria prepares for another general election in 2027, the question of women’s participation in politics and access to elective offices remains a subject for debate.

Read Also: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters

Adeola Azeez, a daughter of the late Afenifere leader, Pa Ayo Adebanjo and one of the Founders of Women in Management, Business & Public Service, WIMBIZ, a founding member of Women in Politics (WIMPol) and a former Deputy Country Representative, Nigeria, of Deutsch e-Bank; was recently declared winner at the Ijebu Central Federal Consistency primary election on the platform of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Ogun State.

In this interview, she speaks on her experience contesting for the House of Representatives, the challenges of securing a party ticket, the influence of party structures on women’s political ambitions and her determination to contest again in 2027.

She also discusses the need for women who have secured elective positions to support aspiring female politicians and explains why she believes women must remain committed to political participation despite the barriers they face.

Excerpts:

You transitioned from the corporate world to politics after your retirement in 2020. What informed that decision?

I have always believed in the importance of women’s participation in leadership. By the time I retired in 2020, I had prepared myself for a career in politics. From 2013, I knew that politics was something I wanted to pursue, so I began preparing for it.

I eventually contested for the House of Representatives in 2023 to represent Ogbomoso Central Federal Constituency. I approached the contest with the same seriousness, preparation and determination as any other candidate.

What were the major challenges you encountered as a woman contesting for political office?

The challenges women face in politics are well known. They include political violence, limited access to funding and other barriers.

Interestingly, funding was not a major challenge for me because of my corporate experience and the relationships I had built over the years. Having supported, mentored and nurtured women in business, I had established a strong network of sponsors and supporters. My reputation also helped me attract people who believed in my ambition.

However, the major challenge was the political structure itself. Nigeria’s political system is not structured to accommodate women adequately.

Despite your corporate experience, network and supporters, you did not secure your party’s ticket in 2023. What went wrong?

I believe the challenge was the party structure and the people who control access to political opportunities.

I had expected that my pedigree, experience and contributions to society would count for something. I did my research, reached out to my constituency and carried out the necessary groundwork.

I wanted to become a symbol of a new chapter for women in Nigerian politics. I believed that if more women with experience, credibility and the capacity to lead could successfully navigate the political system, it would encourage others to participate.

Unfortunately, I did not secure the ticket.

You have said that funding was not a major problem for you. Did you face pressure to engage in money politics?

I was determined not to engage in money politics or buy votes. I believed doing so would compromise my principles and disappoint the people who had supported me, including my family.

I wanted to run a campaign based on my record, ideas, engagement with the people and the support I had earned.

Although I had supporters and people who believed in my ambition, that was not enough to overcome the challenges within the party structure.

There was also the question of whether I would play politics in the same way as others. I believe women should be able to participate in politics without being expected to compromise their values to gain acceptance.

Do you think the political system discriminates against women who refuse to play by the established rules?

The political structure presents significant challenges for women. My experience made me realise that having the qualifications, resources, networks and willingness to serve does not automatically translate into securing a party ticket.

Women must navigate party structures and the interests of those who control them. This is one of the reasons we must continue to examine the barriers preventing women from participating fully in politics.

We need a system that recognises competence and allows women to compete meaningfully for elective positions.

What lessons did you learn from your 2023 electoral experience?

I learnt that political participation requires persistence. I did not give up after 2023 and I remained committed to my constituency.

Although I did not secure the ticket, the experience gave me visibility. People in my constituency came to know me, my ambition and the kind of campaign I ran.

I believe political participation should not begin and end with winning an election. There is a responsibility to continue contributing to the development of the people, regardless of whether one occupies political office or not.

What are your plans for the 2027 general election?

I am preparing to contest again in 2027, this time on a different party platform.

My experience in 2023 has strengthened my resolve. The people in my constituency know me, and I believe my previous campaign helped establish a relationship with them.

I am determined to continue and look forward to the next election.

Beyond your political ambition, what have you done to improve the lives of people in your constituency?

I have continued to support initiatives that respond to the needs of the people.

This year, I facilitated the establishment of a technology hub and supported a back-to-school initiative. These projects were funded with the support of my partners.

For me, leadership is about impact. Even when you are not holding an elected office, you can still contribute to the development of your community.

I want people to understand that political aspirations should not prevent anyone from serving. We must continue to identify needs and provide support where possible.

Some women who have secured elective offices are criticised for not doing enough to support other aspiring female politicians. Do you share this concern?

There is still a lot of work to be done. We have women who are interested in politics, women who are preparing themselves and women who have the capacity to lead. The challenge is creating an environment where they can participate meaningfully.

One concern is that some women who eventually get elected may not use their positions and influence to create opportunities for other women.

When women get into the Senate or the House of Representatives, they should remember the challenges they faced on their way to those positions.

They should use their influence to support other women who are trying to enter the political space. Women’s political representation should not be about individual achievement alone but creating a pathway for others.

What practical steps should political parties take to improve women’s representation?

We must move beyond simply encouraging women to participate, we must address the structural barriers that prevent them from securing party tickets and winning elections.

Women need support, access to political opportunities and a system that recognises their capacity to lead.

We must also build stronger networks of women who are willing to support one another. Those who have the resources, experience and influence should help aspiring female politicians navigate the political process.

There are women who are prepared to serve, but we must create an environment where their preparation and capacity can translate into meaningful political participation.

What is your message to women who are discouraged by the challenges of Nigerian politics?

Women must not give up. We are trying, and we are rebuilding. There is a growing pool of women who are interested in politics and willing to contribute to national development.

However, the fact that many women are trying but are not making significant progress in representation shows that there is still much work to do.

We must continue to organise, support one another, build networks and challenge the barriers within the political system.

I remain committed to that cause, and I believe women must keep pushing for their place in leadership.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu inherited Nigeria on brink of collapse — Mutfwang
World.content:
Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang

•Declares no vacancy in Aso Rock, Plateau Govt House •Says no rainbow coalition, Plateau going APC

By Golok Nanmwa

JOS — Plateau State governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has said President Bola Tinubu inherited an economy that was tottering on the brink of collapse from the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari in 2023.

Read Also: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters

He also declared there was no vacancy in the Presidential Villa (Aso Rock) and Plateau Government House in 2027, equally dismissing any talks of rainbow coalition.

Mutfwang, who stated this during the formal inauguration of All Progressives Congress, APC, Campaign Council in Jos yesterday, also defended Tinubu administration’s economic reforms and urged Plateau residents to support the President in the 2027 election.

“Where did President Tinubu meet Nigeria in 2023? He met Nigeria tottering on the brink of collapse; Nigeria that could not service its external debts; Nigeria that would not even allow businesses outside the country to take their proceeds back home. And that is why some international airlines stopped flying to Nigeria because they could not get the dollars to take back their money.

“Our external reserve was down to just a little over $3 billion, from the over $40 billion it had accumulated for decades. Today, by the grace of God, we have a healthy external reserve of over $50 billion,” the governor said.

He alleged further that the previous administration resorted to printing money to manage the economy, claiming more than N30 trillion was printed.

Governor Mutfwang said: “When the President took over in 2023, the government he succeeded had run out of ideas on how to manage the economy and they resorted to printing money in the Central Bank.

“They printed over N30 trillion which went down the drain. Today, by the grace of God, Central Bank has stabilised and that deficit has been done away with.’’

On fuel subsidy, Mutfwang described the system under the previous administration as fraudulent, alleging that the country borrowed money to pay claims supported by what he called fictitious documents.

“I say it was a fraud because we were borrowing money to pay people who brought fictitious documents. They never brought any wealth. They brought fictitious documents, claimed monies and subsidies.

“You cannot continue to borrow money to give to thieves. You have to stop it at some point. And when it is stopped, there will be a payback; there will be a recovery time,” he said.

The governor said the availability of fuel had improved, despite the increase in its cost, recalling the long queues that previously characterised fuel stations across the country.

“Today, by the grace of God, we have solved one side of the equation. Today, fuel is available. It may not be cheap but it is available.

“Those of us who are of my age bracket or little below will remember the times we spent days in petrol stations queuing for fuel that we could hardly get. But we have been able to resolve that,” Mutfwang said.

He also claimed that the previous administration had sold crude oil in advance, saying the country was now servicing obligations arising from such arrangements.

“Part of the problem of the Buhari regime is that they got to a point that they didn’t know what to do, so they sold our future crude. The crude we are yet to dig from the ground has been sold in advance. And today, we are paying that debt. And so we cannot expect things to simply change overnight,” he said.

The governor said his administration was taking steps to cushion the effects of the economic adjustment on Plateau residents, citing the introduction of metro buses and revival of the railway system within Jos metropolis.

“I’m glad that Plateau people have commended us for the metro buses we bought early in the regime. I’m glad we’re able to revive the railway system within the metropolis. I’m glad that we’re able to reduce school fees for our students in tertiary institutions by 50 per cent. I’m glad that we’re able to raise their allowances by about 300 per cent,” he said.

He also commended the federal government’s student financing initiatives, saying Plateau indigenes studying in universities had benefited from the scheme.

“It is also a great joy in my heart that the President also came up with a new scholarship for students called NELFUND. Today, hundreds of millions have been given to Plateau indigenes who are studying in different universities. Some are getting N20,000 monthly, N40,000 monthly. It has never happened before,” he said.

On the 2027 elections, Mutfwang called for power rotation between the North and South, saying political arrangements should be respected.

“We must agree that power should rotate between the North and the South. And if the North spends eight years, which we have nothing to show for, it is only fair that we allow the South to do eight years because if we don’t respect that sharing arrangement, it will come back to haunt us someday,” he said.

Mutfwang also declared that there was no vacancy in Plateau State Government House, ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

“That is why in Plateau State, we have already agreed that it is two terms per senatorial zone. Except the northern zone does not want to produce a governor until 2035, then you can toy with my mandate,” he said.

Governor Mutfwang urged APC candidates and campaign council members to communicate the achievements of the administration to the electorate and avoid actions capable of deepening divisions.

“We must, therefore, go about this campaign with facts, with honesty, with seriousness. Part of the reason people are still apprehensive is because we have not communicated the real message, and we have a responsibility to ensure that that message is properly communicated.

“I’d like to urge all our candidates for the various positions, you must lead from the front. You must be bridge-builders.”

“I am confident that come January 16, 2027, by the grace of God, Plateau State will return President Bola Ahmed Tinubu with a resounding victory. And two weeks later, the people of Plateau will renew their mandate for us to continue on the good journey we have started,” he said.

On security, Mutfwang acknowledged the persistence of insecurity, adding that his administration was taking steps to strengthen security and facilitate the return of displaced persons to their communities.

“On security, I know our opponents will say there is hunger in the land. We don’t deny it. They will say that the insecurity situation has not abated. We don’t deny it. But if they say we have not taken steps at all to address those issues, they know they are lying.

“Insecurity is not like tap water, where you simply turn on the tap and it flows down. It requires concerted, deliberate, intentional, sustained efforts before you get results.

“By the grace of God, we have understood what the issues are, and we have begun to make sure we propose solutions in the right places that matter,” he said.

The governor said his administration would continue to protect communities and disclosed plans to deploy additional security personnel.

“One thing I have committed myself to is that I will ensure the protection of every inch of land in Plateau State.

“Very soon, we are going to be taking practical steps to facilitate the return of internally displaced persons back to their communities. And so, all we are asking is for Plateau people to trust us, be patient with us, and by the grace of God, you will not regret it.”

No rainbow coalition, Plateau going APC

The governor dismissed talks of any “rainbow coalition” ahead of the 2027 elections , declaring that there was no vacancy in Aso Rock and the Plateau Government House as he inaugurated the presidential and state campaign councils of the All Progressives Congress, APC.

Mutfwang said Plateau people had chosen the APC as their political vehicle for the 2027 elections, urging party faithful and campaign officials to mobilise across the state.

“Some people are talking about rainbow, we are talking about a unification movement. Plateau people have decided 2027 to go one direction. And we have chosen that the wings on which we have chosen to fly in 2027 are the wings of the APC,” the governor declared
