World.title: Give Tinubu, Otu another term for Bakassi seaport, coastal highway — Shettima
World.content:
Vice President Kashim Shettima

By Ike Uchechukwu

CALABAR — Vice President Kashim Shettima has assured Cross River residents that the proposed Bakassi Deep Seaport and Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway will be delivered, urging them to re-elect President Bola Tinubu and Governor Bassey Otu in 2027.

Shettima gave the assurance yesterday while representing Tinubu at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at the U.J. Esuene Stadium, Calabar.

He thanked the people of Cross River for supporting the administration over the past three years, describing the relationship between the government and the electorate as “an alliance of prosperity, an alliance of opportunity.”

“Over the past three years, you have shown us support, and you have resisted the lies and propaganda intended to misrepresent us,” he said.

The Vice President urged voters to renew the mandates of Tinubu, Otu and APC candidates seeking election into the National Assembly and the state House of Assembly.

He said the party was seeking another mandate based on its stewardship, stressing that elected officials must account to the people who entrusted them with power.

On infrastructure, Shettima said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway would link coastal communities, ease the movement of goods and people, boost tourism and attract investment to the region.

He added that the project would create thousands of direct and indirect jobs, while opening up economic opportunities for communities along the corridor.

On the Bakassi Deep Seaport, the Vice President said the project had received Federal Government approval, expressing optimism that it would become an international maritime gateway upon completion.

“When completed, it will become an international maritime gateway. It will attract shipping companies. It will generate employment,” he said.

Shettima said the seaport and coastal highway were central to efforts to position Cross River as a major beneficiary of Nigeria’s maritime economy.

On education, he said the government’s student financing initiative would promote human capital development, reduce the financial burden on parents and expand access to higher education.

He added that the intervention was intended to ensure that financial constraints did not prevent children from pursuing their education

World.title: FG disburses N75bn to 104 manufacturers, N65.8bn to MSMEs
World.content:
President Tinubu

By Yinka Kolawole

The Federal Government has fully disbursed the N75 billion Manufacturing Sector Fund to 104 manufacturing businesses, while N65.8 billion has been disbursed to 15,018 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to boost domestic production, expand businesses and create jobs.

Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole, disclosed this in an address on “Harnessing Nigeria’s Economic Potential for Greater Prosperity”.

Oduwole said the interventions were part of the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen local industries, improve productive capacity and drive sustainable economic growth.

The disbursements were made under the Federal Government’s N200 billion intervention package, managed by the Bank of Industry (BoI), to support businesses, boost domestic production and create jobs.

The package comprises the N50 billion Presidential Conditional Grant Scheme for nano businesses, the N75 billion FGN MSME Intervention Fund for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, and the N75 billion FGN Manufacturing Sector Fund for manufacturing businesses.

Oduwole noted that the N75 billion Manufacturing Sector Fund had been fully disbursed to 104 manufacturing businesses, while N65.8 billion had been disbursed to 15,018 businesses under the MSME Intervention Fund as of the first quarter of 2026.

She, however, stressed that the impact of government funding should be measured by stronger businesses, increased production and improved livelihoods rather than the amount disbursed alone.

The minister acknowledged that access to finance remained a major challenge for manufacturers seeking to acquire equipment, purchase raw materials, expand production capacity and create employment.

She said Nigeria’s economic transformation required fiscal discipline, monetary stability and policies that supported domestic production and competitiveness.

According to her, the government is working to remove barriers to investment, production and trade while creating an enabling environment for businesses to thrive.

Highlighting developments in the manufacturing sector, Oduwole said cement manufacturing grew by 11.53 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, while motor vehicle assembly expanded by 5.44 per cent during the period. She added that vehicle assembly grew by 40.6 per cent in 2025, while cassava starch production recorded growth of 474.74 per cent.

“Processing locally grown cassava into industrial starch will support manufacturers, while vehicle assembly will create opportunities for engineers, technicians and supply-chain businesses,” she said.

The minister also highlighted opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), noting that intra-African trade had grown by 21 per cent.

World.title: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

*Taraba, Plateau, Jigawa, Bayelsa, Benue among states with thousands of cards awaiting collection *Sokoto, Nasarawa, Zamfara, Yobe record significant increase in voter population *Kano yet to compile collection figures; Borno, Bauchi, Kebbi withholding data *Lagos, Ondo, Ogun, Ekiti, Osun, Kaduna, Adamawa report growing voter numbers *INEC intensifies mobilisation ahead of January 16 presidential election

By Soni Daniel

ABUJA — Three weeks after the collection of Permanent Voters Cards, PVCs started across the country, the failure of no fewer than 14 million eligible voters to collect their PVCs, is emerging as a major concern for the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC.

Read Also: Critics of Rainbow Coalition can’t unite their families – Wike

Investigations by Vanguard across several states show that while the Continuous Voter Registration, CVR, exercise attracted millions of new registrants, a significant number of produced PVCs remain uncollected, potentially denying their owners the opportunity to participate in next year’s elections.

Vanguard’s checks showed that 6.26 million PVCs were not collected before the 2023 general elections. In the last Continuous Voters Registration, CVR, exercise, the electoral commission registered 10,772,421 new voters. At press time, many states are yet to release their tallies of uncollected voter’s cards estimated at over 14 million.

The situation is particularly worrying in states like Plateau, Taraba, Jigawa, Benue and Bayelsa, where INEC has disclosed substantial numbers of cards awaiting collection.

In Plateau, about 95,000 PVCs from previous registration exercises remain unclaimed. Taraba has 29,314 outstanding cards, while Jigawa has 33,079 cards ready for collection. Bayelsa, on its part, has 52,225 PVCs from the first phase of the recent registration exercise awaiting collection.

Benue has also recorded considerable activity, with 58,581 PVCs collected during the recent display of the voters’ register, although thousands of additional cards are still being processed or await collection.

Beyond the collection challenge, voter registration figures indicate growing electoral participation across the country, with Sokoto, Zamfara, Nasarawa, Benue, Ogun, Kano and other states recording significant additions to their voter registers.

However, the picture is incomplete in some states. While Kano is yet to compile its PVC collection figures across its 44 local government areas, INEC officials in Borno, Bauchi and Kebbi declined to provide updates, describing the requested information as sensitive.

In the South-West, Lagos says its final register will not be available until December 15, after conclusion of the claims and objections exercise. Ondo, Ogun, Ekiti and Osun have reported increases in registered voters, although some are still compiling their PVC collection figures.

The findings raise questions about whether the increasing number of registered voters will translate into participation in the 2027 elections, beginning with the presidential and National Assembly polls on January 16.

Taraba: 29,314 PVCs uncollected

In Taraba State, the number of registered voters stands at 2,254,380, according to INEC.

However, no fewer than 29,314 PVCs remain uncollected across the commission’s offices in the state.

The Resident Electoral Commissioner, REC, Dr Sa’ad Umar Idris, said the outstanding cards comprise 13,826 legacy PVCs from previous electoral cycles between 2011 and 2023 and 15,488 cards processed during the latest registration exercise.

He explained that the commission processed 31,676 cards arising from new registrations, voter transfers and replacements during the 2025–2026 exercise. Of these, only 16,188, representing about 51 per cent, had been collected.

Expressing concern over the low collection rate, Idris appealed to political parties, traditional rulers, religious leaders and civil society organisations to mobilise residents to visit INEC local government offices and collect their cards.

Plateau: 121,821 new voters, 95,000 PVCs uncollected

In Plateau State, INEC recorded 121,821 new voters during the latest CVR exercise, while about 95,000 PVCs from previous registration exercises remain uncollected.

The REC, Prof. Samuel Egwu, disclosed this during a meeting with political party leaders and other stakeholders in Jos.

He said women accounted for 65,928 of new registrants, while men represented 55,893.

The commission also received 38,399 requests for voter transfers within and outside the state.

Egwu said the outstanding PVCs remained a major concern as INEC intensified preparations for the 2027 elections.

Jigawa: 33,079 PVCs ready for collection

Jigawa State has 2,351,298 registered voters, according to the REC, Prof. Muhammad Bashar.

Bashar said 33,079 PVCs are ready for collection by people who registered for transfers, corrections and replacements between August and December 2025.

He also disclosed that the state recorded 515,878 new voters during the three phases of the recent CVR exercise.

Jigawa has 27 local government areas, 287 registration areas and 4,522 polling units.

Zamfara adds 313,115 voters

In Zamfara State, INEC recorded 313,115 new voters under the CVR exercise as of August 2026.

The REC, Dr. Mahmud Isa, disclosed this to Vanguard in Gusau, explaining that the new registrants are additional to the 1,952,060 registered voters recorded in the state for the 2023 general elections.

Kaduna: 61,494 PVCs collected

In Kaduna State, 61,494 PVCs had been collected as of October 28, according to figures obtained from INEC.

An official of the commission, Hajiya Rukaiyatu, said the figure comprised 12,741 old PVCs and 48,753 newly-issued cards.

Women collected 32,589 cards, comprising 6,782 old and 25,807 new PVCs, while men collected 28,905, comprising 5,959 old and 22,946 new cards.

The figures indicate a higher collection rate among female voters.

Nasarawa: Voter population hits 2.1m

Nasarawa State’s registered voter population has risen to approximately 2.1 million, following registration of 247,000 new voters between 2025 and July 2026.

The REC, Mallam Mohammed Abullahi Sadiq, disclosed this, commending residents for their response to the registration exercise.

He urged those yet to collect their PVCs to visit INEC offices in their respective local government areas.

Sokoto: 2.63m registered voters

Sokoto State has recorded 2,633,113 registered voters, including 461,057 captured during the latest CVR exercise.

The commission’s Public Relations Officer, Hassan Kaoje, said the figure represented 2.55 per cent of the national voter register.

He said INEC was intensifying efforts to ensure that all eligible registrants collected their PVCs before the 2027 elections.

Kaoje urged those who had completed registration but were yet to collect their cards to visit designated INEC offices and collection centres.

Adamawa: 2.43m million registered voters

Adamawa State has 2,431,146 registered voters as of July 2026.

INEC’s Head of Voter Education and Information in the state, Alhaji Aliyu Shaba Lafiagi, disclosed that 49,304 PVCs had been collected as of October 23.

He also reported that 11,725 voters’ cards had been transferred into the state, comprising 6,255 belonging to men and 5,520 belonging to women.

Borno, Bauchi, Kebbi withhold figures

In Borno State, INEC declined to provide the latest figures on registered voters and PVC collection, describing the information as sensitive.

Officials said the commission is yet to ascertain the actual number of newly-registered voters and PVCs collected because the exercise is ongoing.

However, the 2023 register put the state’s voter population at 2,564,197.

A similar situation played out in Bauchi, where INEC officials declined to release requested figures, insisting that the information is not for public consumption.

Efforts to obtain updated figures from Kebbi also proved unsuccessful.

Benue: 3.05m registered voters, 279,498 new registrants

Benue State has 3,057,225 registered voters, including 279,498 new registrants across its 23 local government areas.

The REC, Mallam Aminu Idris, said INEC received 101,695 PVCs from its headquarters for the first phase of the CVR and voter transfers.

The consignment comprised 54,724 new PVCs and 46,971 transferred cards.

During the display of the voters’ register between October 9 and 15, 2026, at registration area level, 58,581 PVCs were collected.

The breakdown showed that 9,139 were old cards previously held in storage, 28,854 were new CVR cards, 12,707 were transferred cards and 7,881 were replacement cards.

Idris said all existing PVCs remained available for collection at INEC offices in the state’s 23 local government areas.

He added that the commission would announce the availability of cards processed during the second and third phases of the CVR exercise after receiving official notification from its headquarters.

Kano yet to compile PVC collection figures

Despite having one of the country’s largest voter populations, Kano State is yet to determine the total number of PVCs collected across its 44 local government areas.

INEC’s Public Relations Officer, Nahila Bello Dandago, said the commission was still compiling the figures because the collection exercise was ongoing.

She disclosed that Kano had 6,570,276 registered voters, making it the state with the second-highest voter population after Lagos, which has 7,488,633.

Yobe: 283,525 new voters

In Yobe State, the voter population has increased from 1,485,146 in 2022 to 1,768,671 in 2026, representing an addition of 283,525 voters.

In Damaturu Local Government Area, 11,911 PVCs had been collected, leaving 9,137 unclaimed.

The Electoral Officer for Damaturu, Ahmed A. Waziri, said INEC had 21,048 cards available for collection, comprising 8,100 outstanding cards from the 2023 exercise and 12,948 received during the first phase of the latest distribution.

He said Damaturu was yet to receive cards under the second and third phases of the distribution exercise.

Waziri added that the commission’s ICT department was better positioned to provide comprehensive figures for the state’s 17 local government areas.

Lagos: Final register expected December 15

In Lagos State, INEC said the final Register of Voters would not be available until the conclusion of the claims and objections exercise on December 15, 2026.

The commission’s Public Affairs Officer, Tope Adenuga, said the final figures for newly registered voters could not be provided until the exercise was completed.

He said: “The final Register of Voters requested will be made available until after the conclusion of the ongoing claims and objections exercise.”

According to him, the final list is expected to be ready on December 15.

The state recorded 7,488,633 registered voters in the figures available to Vanguard.

INEC was yet to provide the latest PVC collection statistics.

Ondo: 2.05m registered voters

In Ondo State, the total number of registered voters stands at 2,053,061, with 76,285 new registrants.

The Head of Voter Education and Publicity, Olayinka Ogunseye, disclosed that 1,771,326 PVCs had been collected.

He, however, cautioned that the figures were preliminary and not final.

Ekiti: Voter population rises to 1.05 million

Ekiti State’s registered voter population has increased to 1,055,708, according to INEC.

The figure represents an increase of 68,061 over the 987,647 registered voters recorded during the 2023 general elections.

The commission could not immediately provide the latest PVC collection figures because the exercise was ongoing.

Ogun: 348,703 additional voters

Ogun State has recorded an increase of 348,703 registered voters, bringing its voter population to 3,037,008 as of October 2026.

The figure represents an increase from the 2,688,305 registered voters recorded for the 2023 general elections.

INEC officials said PVC distribution was still ongoing at the commission’s local government offices.

Osun: 2.33m registered voters

In Osun State, the total number of registered voters stands at 2,339,233.

The INEC Public Relations Officer, Musa Olurode, said the figure was the same as that used for the August 2026 governorship election because no fresh CVR exercise was conducted after the poll.

He disclosed that 1,906,390 PVCs had been collected as of August, adding that the figure would be updated after the ongoing collection exercise.

He said: “As at today, the total voters register in Osun State is 2,339,233. This is the figure for the governorship election and it cannot change because the Continuous Voters Registration did not take place in the state after the August poll.”

He added that the number of collected PVCs would change as more registered voters collected their cards.

Delta: INEC declines to release PVC figures

In Delta State, INEC officials declined to provide statistics on PVC collection, directing enquiries to the ICT department.

The Head of Voter Education, Nse Abasi Udom, said the ICT unit was responsible for monitoring and keeping the relevant records.

However, she declined to provide the contact details of the department’s head, saying officials were in an important meeting.

A similar experience occurred during a previous visit to a PVC collection centre at Uzor Igwe Primary School, Nnebisi Road, Asaba, where an INEC official declined to disclose the number of cards available or collected.

The official, however, acknowledged an impressive turnout of residents.

“What I can tell you, which you can verify from the atmosphere here, is that the turnout is impressive. People are coming and collecting,” the official said.

The commission’s inability to provide the figures has made it difficult to establish the number of PVCs still awaiting collection across the state.

Bayelsa: 52,225 PVCs await collection

In Bayelsa State, INEC has put the total number of registered voters at 1,200,691, with 52,225 PVCs from the first phase of the recent CVR exercise awaiting collection.

Ekeremor and Sagbama local government areas recorded the highest numbers of registered voters, with 12,023 and 10,080 respectively.

Ogbia recorded the lowest figure of 3,132, followed by Nembe with 3,620 and Kolokuma/Opokuma with 3,712.

INEC said collection commenced at registration area level on October 9 and ended on October 15, after which the exercise was moved to the commission’s offices across the state’s eight local government areas.

The commission urged eligible registrants who missed the ward-level distribution to visit the respective local government offices to collect their cards.

With thousands of PVCs still awaiting collection in several states, the findings underscore the challenge facing INEC as it prepares for the 2027 general elections.

While the increasing number of registered voters points to growing interest in the electoral process, the commission’s ability to translate registration into actual voter participation will depend significantly on the success of its PVC collection and mobilisation campaigns.

Clifford Ndujihe, Dayo Johnson, Umar Yusuf, Ndahi Marama, Femi Bolaji, Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo, Peter Duru, Hadiza Yusuf, Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman, Musa Ubandawaki, Idris Salisu, Edwin Philip, Golok Nanmwa, Muhammad Inuwa, Christopher Ameh, Egufe Yafugborhi, Rotimi Ojomoyela, Olayinka Ajayi, Shina Abubakar, Emem Idio & James Ogunnaike contributed to this report.

World.title: YPP’s Agada wants end to raw material exports
World.content:
By John Alechenu

ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), Arch. Peter Agada, has called for an end to the export of Nigeria’s raw materials without adding value, saying the practice deprives the country of greater economic benefits.

Agada spoke in an interview in Abuja on Monday while outlining his economic blueprint ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He said his proposed administration would prioritise electricity supply and promote industrialisation from the ward level to ensure that value was added to Nigerian produce before export.

“The industrialisation we all talk about can only happen when we fix power and put in place policies that will promote investments from the ward level upwards,” Agada said.

He said rural communities would be made attractive to agro-allied industries capable of processing agricultural produce for export and generating foreign exchange.

“Our rural communities will attract agro-allied industries to promote export of produce after value has been added to earn foreign exchange. Enough of sending raw materials only to collect peanuts in return,” he said.

The YPP candidate also said his proposed administration would mobilise Nigerians at home and in the diaspora to build a country citizens would be proud to call home.

He said this would involve building on the country’s strengths while addressing areas of weakness.

On politics, Agada urged members of the political elite, irrespective of party affiliation, to allow Nigerians to freely choose their leaders at all levels.

He said the practice of imposing leaders on the electorate on the basis of ethnic or religious considerations should become a thing of the past.

World.title: Customs appoints Mamman Ali acting Adamawa/Taraba Comptroller
World.content:
Customs officers

By Umar Yusuf, Yola

The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has appointed Deputy Comptroller Mamman Ali as the Acting Area Comptroller of its Adamawa/Taraba Command.

Ali, who was until his appointment the Coordinator of the Customs Anti-Smuggling Unit, Operation Whirlwind, Zone E, takes over from Mohammed Tako, who has been promoted to Assistant Comptroller-General of Customs in charge of Zone B, Kaduna.

At a brief handing-over ceremony in Yola on Monday, Tako said the command recorded significant achievements during his tenure despite directives on strict border closure.

He said the command strengthened security along critical border corridors through enhanced joint operations and patrols with sister security agencies.

Tako disclosed that the total Duty Paid Value (DPV) of seizures recorded by the command during his one-year tenure stood at ₦535,975,190.

He commended officers and men of the command for their cooperation during his tenure and urged them to extend the same support to his successor.

In his remarks, the new Acting Area Comptroller, Ali, pledged to build on the achievements of his predecessor.

He solicited the support and cooperation of sister security agencies, officers and men of the command to strengthen border policing and curb smuggling activities across Adamawa and Taraba states.

World.title: Ogun 2027: Adebutu dismisses INEC list omission
World.content:
….Receives over 1,000 APC defectors into PDP

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

ABEOKUTA — The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has described the omission of his name from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) list of governorship candidates as a temporary distraction, insisting that it would not stop him from contesting the 2027 election.

Adebutu spoke on Monday while receiving more than 1,000 defectors from the All Progressives Congress (APC) into the PDP at the party’s state secretariat in Abeokuta.

The defectors were led by a former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Segun William, and received by Adebutu alongside other party leaders, including the PDP’s Ogun Central senatorial candidate, Iyabo Obasanjo.

Addressing the gathering, Adebutu expressed confidence that the controversy surrounding his omission from INEC’s list would be resolved, maintaining that he remained a bona fide member of the PDP.

He cited his participation in elections under the party’s platform over the past two decades as evidence of his loyalty and challenged those questioning his membership to provide evidence that he had defected.

“I have been the candidate of the PDP for the last 20 years, in every election cycle. My question is: at what stage did I leave or vacate the party? Where is the proof that, for one day, I have even visited the APC office, let alone joined the party?” he asked.

Adebutu also said he played an active role in organising and financing the party’s recent membership registration exercise in Ogun, which he claimed recorded more than 19,800 members.

He said his registration number in the exercise was 1536, describing it as further evidence of his continued membership of the party.

The PDP chieftain alleged that the controversy over his omission from the INEC list was intended to distract the opposition and disenfranchise voters.

He, however, urged party members to remain focused, saying the development would not disrupt the PDP’s mobilisation activities across the state.

Adebutu disclosed that the party’s campaign team had visited 12 of the state’s 20 local government areas and more than 140 of its 236 wards.

He said the grassroots mobilisation exercise would continue despite what he described as attempts to distract the party.

“We have visited 12 of the 20 local governments. Of the 236 wards, we have visited over 140. Tomorrow, we continue again because we know that the trick is to get us distracted. We will not be distracted. We will keep our eyes on the ball, and we shall win,” he said.

Earlier, William said the defectors decided to leave the APC because of their dissatisfaction with the party’s approach to governance and what he described as its failure to uphold democratic principles and deliver development in Ogun State.

Recounting his political journey, William said he joined partisan politics in 2007 and eventually aligned with the APC, despite earlier advice from friends and associates to join the PDP.

He said his experience in the ruling party had convinced him that it no longer represented the democratic ideals and developmental aspirations he believed in.

William said the defectors were joining the PDP to contribute to the political and socio-economic development of Ogun State, expressing confidence in the party’s leadership.

He also described the APC as no longer capable of accommodating the democratic aspirations of its members and residents of the state.

“We are seeking the progress of our dear Ogun State. My sincere appreciation goes first and foremost to our incoming governor, who has made this occasion possible, with the assistance of our deputy governor, our senator, the directors-general, party members, the party hierarchy and the state chairman,” William said.

The defection comes as political parties intensify mobilisation and positioning ahead of the 2027 general elections.

World.title: Okorocha’s Vendetta Gamble With Imo APC
World.content:
By Declan Emelumba





The frenzy with which Senator Rochas Okorocha has been celebrating his pyrrhic victory at the Federal High Court, Abuja, over the Imo West senatorial primary of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has more than confirmed that the judgment was premeditated. As loquacious as ever, Okorocha has gone to town to thank those who facilitated that travesty of justice. His mention of help from high places, and his speedy embrace of the so-called Rainbow Coalition without any contact with the APC at the grassroots, have given him and his co-conspirators away. But Nigerians are not fooled. Many have recalled the old saying: the witch cried in the night, and the child died at dawn.

One sharp observation came from Sam Amadi, a lawyer, rights activist and politician from Imo State, who is no fan of Governor Hope Uzodimma. In a Facebook post the day after the judgment, Amadi wrote: “Hope Uzodimma may be guilty of many things. But it does not mean he is guilty of everything.” He pointed to the footage of Uzodimma voting on the primaries election day, with his wife by his side and a large crowd of APC members behind him. Then he threw down a simple challenge: “Let us see the evidence of Okorocha’s primary election.”

That may sound academic in a courtroom, but it confirms what APC members in Ideato South, Okorocha’s home, and across Imo State have said all along: he was an absentee aspirant who neither campaigned nor took part in the primary. His son Amen, who swore to the affidavit used to procure this phantom judgment, is not even known to the party.

As Jesus said of Judas, it was written that the Son of Man would be betrayed, but woe unto the man who betrays him. Chief Sam Mbakwe spoke in the same manner about the vexed abandoned property issue, under which Ndigbo were dispossessed of their property in Rivers State. He said that whenever that infamy was mentioned, the man who chaired the Abandoned Properties Implementation Committee, David Mark, would be remembered on the wrong side of history. In like manner, whenever controversial Federal High Court judgments are mentioned, the name of Justice Obiora Egwuatu will be remembered. That he set aside Supreme Court rulings duly cited before him to hand a questionable victory to Okorocha seals his place in the hall of infamy.

What is baffling is the way Okorocha has been moving from one media house to another, gloating over this so-called victory, vilifying the governor and speaking as if the judgment were the final word. Unless he knows something that is not written in the Electoral Act or the Constitution, or unless those pulling his strings have given their puppet overwhelming assurances, Uzodimma retains the right to appeal this judgment all the way to the Supreme Court. Okorocha’s faith in a judgment that cannot stand the test of the law is curious, especially as the Imo APC has already disowned him.

On Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, the very day of the judgment, Okorocha declared: “Hope has never won an election in his life.” The record says otherwise. Uzodimma won the Imo West Senate seat twice and sat in the 7th and 8th Senates. In the 2023 governorship election, he polled 540,308 votes against 71,503 for the PDP and 64,081 for the Labour Party. INEC’s returning officer, Prof. Abayomi Fasina, declared him winner and returned him elected. Now contrast that with Okorocha’s own route to the Senate in 2019. Announcing the Imo West result, the returning officer, Prof. Innocent Ibeawuchi, told the nation: “I declared this thing before under duress; I’m still under duress declaring this one.” INEC initially refused Okorocha a certificate of return. So which of the two men has never truly won an election?

On the same programme, Okorocha said: “There’s no single project initiated by Hope and finished by Hope.” He should ask his own people. The road Okorocha built to his village collapsed, cutting his community off from the rest of Imo and subjecting his people to untold hardship. Three governors, Okorocha included, could not fix the Orlu–Mgbee–Akokwa–Uga federal road, the only accessible route to his village. Uzodimma rebuilt it from end to end, together with the Umuchima Bridge linking Orlu and Ideato, which Okorocha failed to build in all his years as governor and senator. The Auxiliary Bishop of Orlu, Most Rev. Thomas Ifeanyichukwu Obiatuegwu, publicly praised the project and thanked the governor. The road and bridge Okorocha’s own people now use were delivered by the man he mocks.

He went further: “He can’t beat my record. He can’t even get close to it. Not one, one hundredth of my record.” Every Imo person knows that Okorocha’s so-called projects fell into ruin even before he left office. The International Conference Centre, a stone’s throw from Government House, lost its roof, and its ceiling caved in. The Mother and Child Hospital on Douglas Road, Owerri, was left to mechanics, hoodlums and reptiles; it is not fit to be called a poultry farm, let alone a hospital. Chukwuma Nwoha Road, Dick Tiger Road and other urban roads had become swampy bush paths until Uzodimma rebuilt them. And in the name of urban renewal, Okorocha savagely destroyed the piped water system he inherited. It is hard to believe that the Imo of today is the same Imo that Okorocha spent eight years spoiling and pillaging. That old Imo was truly nothing to write home about.

Acting like a bull in a china shop, Okorocha accuses Uzodimma of humiliation and intimidation. That bears the mark of envy and an outsized grudge, which only facts can heal. He has not told Nigerians why security agencies arrested his son-in-law, Uche Nwosu. He has not told Nigerians that the EFCC secured forfeiture orders on properties traced to him, his wife and his daughter. He has not explained the Royal Spring Palm Estate on Akachi Road, Owerri: government land developed and claimed as private property by his wife, Nkechi. He has not explained how Eastern Palm University, built with public funds, came to be claimed as his own until the Uzodimma government recovered it and renamed it K.O. Mbadiwe University. Nor has he mentioned the state panel that found he used soldiers and hoodlums to seize the land of Alvan Ikoku Federal College of Education and demolish 101 staff buildings. He speaks today as a free man only because Uzodimma, against wise counsel, refused to prosecute him and his family for widespread corruption. Okorocha ought to be answering for his record, not comparing it with Uzodimma’s.

Indeed, he already has charges to answer. A Senior Magistrate Court in Abuja has issued a bench warrant against Okorocha and his son Amen, on charges of criminal conspiracy, forgery, perjury and false documents over the primary results he paraded. The police confirmed that they arrested him at the REIZ Continental Hotel in Abuja on 12 October and released him on bail. Yet on live television he insisted: “Never was I arrested.” A man who can obtain a dubious court order while facing forgery charges, and then deny an arrest the police have confirmed, is capable of anything. Is this the character the APC wants to fly its flag at next year’s senatorial election?

Like the proverbial nza bird that eats its fill and then challenges its chi to a wrestling match, Okorocha has stepped back onto his familiar terrain of deceit. He now claims that his name on the ballot guarantees Tinubu’s victory in Imo, while “Hope cannot carry Imo. Cannot carry South East.” The figures tell a different story. In 2015, as a first-term governor seeking re-election and the de facto leader of the APC in Imo, Okorocha delivered Muhammadu Buhari 133,253 votes, about 19 per cent, well short of the 25 per cent he now brags about. Only in 2019, after Uzodimma joined the APC, did Buhari cross the mark, with 140,463 votes, or about 27 per cent. Instructively, most of the votes came from Oru East local government, Uzodimma’s home, where Buhari secured over 90% of the votes cast.

In 2023, when an Igbo son was on the presidential ballot and Ndigbo were emotional about his candidacy, Tinubu polled 66,406 votes in Imo, about 14 per cent and his best result anywhere in the South-East. He got 8,914 votes in Abia, 5,111 in Anambra and 4,772 in Enugu. And where was Okorocha, the self-acclaimed founder of the party? By his own admission on Arise Television, he preferred Peter Obi.

This self-righteous man, who claims to be a victim and prances around Abuja without touching base at home, has labelled Uzodimma greedy. I will not dignify his beer-parlour gossip about what the governor wants. Let us instead examine the facts in the public domain. In December 2014, as a sitting governor, Okorocha contested the APC presidential primary and polled 624 votes. When he lost, he went back home and secured a second term as governor. In 2019, still a sitting governor, he ran for the Senate while sponsoring his son-in-law to succeed him. In 2022, as a senator, he contested the APC presidential primary against Tinubu and scored zero. If that is not greed, what is?

When Uzodimma defeated his son-in-law for the APC governorship ticket, Okorocha moved Nwosu to another party and worked against the APC. Adams Oshiomhole, then national chairman of the APC, called him “an embarrassment to APC” and accused him of trying “to create a dynasty” in Imo. So why is Uzodimma’s senatorial ambition a mortal sin in Okorocha’s eyes? It is the case of the man with a log in his own eye shouting about the speck in another’s.

Okorocha knows he cannot win a councillorship election in his hometown of Ogboko. In September, councillors from Ideato North and Ideato South held a special plenary on the Umuchima Bridge, endorsed Uzodimma for the Imo West Senate seat and barred Okorocha from using roads and bridges he never built. The man who calls himself the Abraham of the APC is today represented in the House of Representatives by an opposition lawmaker, Ikenga Ugochinyere. So much for his electoral value.

These basic facts should guide those goading Okorocha into this political gamble, in which he has sold his soul to betrayal rather than repent of the atrocities of his eight-year imperial reign in Imo State. The APC and its leaders must not allow this perfidy to stand. The party’s fate in Orlu Zone hangs in the balance. Its fate in Imo State also hangs in the balance. Rochas Okorocha is deficient in honour and integrity, carries no electoral value in the state, and has lent himself to the destruction of the APC’s pillar in the South-East.

•Emelumba is Imo state Commissioner for Information, Public Orientation and Strategy

World.title: Future of American Democracy, Tinubu And The Machete That Spared Sowore
World.content:
REUBEN ABATI

“My brother, is President Tinubu back from Umrah, in Saudi Arabia?”

“I don’t know. How would I know? I am not one of those people who go to the Nnamdi Azikiwe Airport in Abuja to see him off, or travel ahead to his destination to receive him, and then make it back in time before him, to receive him when he gets back to the country?”

“You know the way some faces tend to show up at every airport to receive the President, I am beginning to suspect that the Nigerian government may have acquired a transponder, and that airport protocol has also become the job of some Ministers and Governor who just want to be seen by the President no matter what it takes. The Rankadede crowd of Nigeria, the affliction of the Nigerian sycophant and the idle class.”

“Name them. Mention them. Give us names.”

“I can’t do that. My children are still young. They can’t afford to lose their father. Certainly not at this time when politicians are branding anyone who opposes them as an enemy that must be eliminated. There is too much talk about AK 47 in the country. Fire them. Kill them. Burn them. The last time I had a comprehensive medical check-up, my doctor didn’t find a trace of suicidal tendencies in my blood and he advised me to keep it that way.”

“Who is that doctor testing for suicide in a normal medical check-up?”

“In some countries, the doctors do, especially if you are Nigerian and it is a political season in your country. I will give you the contacts. No matter how tough things get in this country, just maintain your sanity.”

“You are justifying cowardice. An active citizen must stand up to be counted. Courage is the name of the game.”

“Go and say that to Comrade Omoyele Sowore. He almost lost his life over the weekend in Ado Ekiti when some hoodlums, wielding machetes attacked him and his supporters at a restaurant and descended on them with venom. They managed to survive and now Sowore and the Ekiti State Police Command are arguing over the details. But it could have been worse. I saw the CCTV video showing a Nigerian who was using a machete to cut into the flesh of another Nigerian as if he was cutting a helpless cow at an abattoir. Omo, the thing scare me! They are almost turning Nigeria into Kenya as in the electoral disorder in that country in 2007.”

“No. I don’t think so. That was an ethnic blow-out they had in Kenya. I don’t think we are dealing with the same thing here. The problem we have in Nigeria is the greed of our politicians and the disappearance of the citizen, and along with it, the Nigerian spirit. But I am optimistic, the President has gone to Saudi Arabia to pray for peace and stability. He prayed at the Grand Mosque in Makkah. He had the privilege of entering the Holy Kaaba, the Holy of Holies, the Makama Ibrahim, to pray. And that is a special privilege. Before Tinubu, only two other Nigerians have had the privilege of entering the Holy of Holies – Sir Ahmadu Bello and Sheik Abubakar Gumi, the father. You can’t get closer to God than that. And I believe God still answers prayers.”

“I don’t know much about that. But you have not answered the question: is the President back?”

“The Presidency has formally announced that he has completed his Umrah trip to Makkah, which has turned out to be both a resounding diplomatic and religious success. He even used the opportunity to sell Nigeria’s economy again to the Arabs. And the Crown Prince gave him a gift. But why is his return important to you?”

“Good. Thank you for asking. You know when he announced that he was travelling for Umrah, the opposition parties led by the ADC and its Presidential candidate, Waziri Adamawa Atiku Abubakar started the propaganda that he was instead going on a medical trip because he lacks the capacity to campaign. They demanded for proof of his presence in Makkah and concrete evidence that he was going there for spiritual reasons.”

“That is why we need the opposition. But he has shocked them, anyway, by providing every photo and every video evidence of his arrival in Saudi Arabia, and his activities. He has been transparent. His spokespersons had announced that he will return this week, Nov. 2 – 8, so he should be on his way back”

“Precisely my point. He should return and make the point clear that it is the opposition that is mischievous. Nobody should come up with any press statement that the President is going to stop by in London or France for two days before returning to Nigeria! No. No. He should head home right-away. You know this superstitious thing about prayers. When you go to the church or the mosque or wherever for prayers, and you have been blessed, you are obliged to carry the blessings straight to your home. The belief is that if you stop here and there, some of the blessings may drop elsewhere. Home, straight.”

“You Nigerians and your superstitions, even when Section 10 of the Nigerian Constitution says there shall be no state religion in Nigeria. They have held elections in Brazil. Neither Lula nor Flavio Bolsonaro, his opponent went anywhere to pray. Israel has announced the results of its recent 120-seat Knesset elections. I don’t think any of the leaders of the parties in the election went to pray anywhere not even inside the same Israel where Christian Nigerian leaders say they must commune with Jesus before any election. America votes today, midterm, 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 seats in the Senate and 36 Governorship positions up for grabs across America. I have not heard that any of the contestants has been going around looking for prayers and blessings.”

“You cannot compare America with Nigeria when it comes to matters of faith. Every individual can choose to worship God the way he chooses. America proclaims “In God We Trust.” But is America a Godly country? Is Trump a Christian? This mid-term election in the United States is about the future of American democracy.”

“Not quite. The core issues as America votes are: inflation and the cost of living, Trump’s tariffs which ended up putting pressure on the average American consumer, the affordability of things, the war in Iran, immigration. healthcare, government corruption, AI and data centres and social security.”

“I think the key issue is Donald Trump himself, and the future of American democracy is tied to him, and where he has brought America. He had said “Pretend I’m on the Ballot” and clearly America has to decide whether they can put up hereafter with his authoritarian, isolationist, island style which has reduced America’s stature in the world, or they want back that old America, the land of dreams, the country that was once known as God’s own country. How American democracy turns out after these mid-term elections will have implications for global relations and the balance of power in that country.”

“So, your predictions, then? The main battlegrounds are in Michigan, Texas, Kansa, Iowa, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and Alaska and the rising blue wave. What do you predict?”

“It is very difficult to predict. What we know is that the polls favour the Democrats 51. 5 % to 43.1% for the Republicans. But the Democrats must win 3 House seats extra and 4 more in the Senate to win the majority in Congress. The Republicans are working hard to stop that from happening. The question is: are the polls accurate? Out of 210 million registered voters, 53.14 million voted early, even before November 3, especially in Georgia. The polls also show that President Trump has the lowest approval rating mid-term since Harry Truman, with 33% on the eve of the midterm elections in November 1946. In 1994, Bill Clinton lost 54 seats in the House of Representatives. In 2010, President Obama lost 64. In 2018, Trump himself lost 42 seats. Will Trump defy history in 2026? Will he escape the mid-term penalty? The political party that controls Congress can redraw the shape of American politics. But anything can happen? I think we should watch. The voting must have started by now.”

“I have enjoyed the drama though. Obama on the stumps pulling apart Trump at every opportunity on Middle East politics, White House renovation, the drama in Ohio about racism allegations concerning Amy Acton (D), an ad, and her mother, Michigan Congresswoman Haley Stevens, rejecting Abdul El-Sayed (D) and endorsing Republican rival, Mike Rogers, and Trump threatening that he will become Mr. Veto if Democrats take control of Congress.”

“Whatever drama you may have seen in the US, it is still all very healthy compared to what we are seeing here in Nigeria. The American voters are not going about with machetes or AK 47, and shooting people because of elections. We didn’t see that also in Brazil and Israel. Here in Nigeria, threats everywhere. Reign of impunity. It is as if we are preparing for war. The rhetoric of war is getting louder.”

“That is what happens during every election cycle in Nigeria. Don’t worry Nigeria will survive. Some people will die. Some will end up in hospitals, Nigeria will remain. No be we, we? Who wan die, make he die, carry go.”

“No. It is the primary duty of government to protect and care for the people.”

“Okay, dey there. Make your Folorunso or Godwin go dey sleep for train track. Come see, if train no go kpai am. Delete. Unalive. State. Citizen. Shey na him make Sowore dey go chop for roadside canteen for Ado Ekiti? Him wey wan be President of Nigeria dey go siddon for Mama Tawakalitu joint dey ask for amala and gbegiri. E siddon for roadside make street urchins or political thugs or what did he call them, to come and argue with him? Na so dem dey do politics?”

“He can choose to eat anywhere, travel anywhere, campaign anywhere. He is an active citizen”

“Very good. My point is that to join Nigerian politics, you must understand the grammar of Nigerian politics. To be a politician in Nigeria, you must learn to protect yourself. This is a Do-It-Yourself country. People build their own boreholes in their homes, they install solar panels to give them electricity, they hire guards to protect their properties, but when it comes to politics, they say they want their opponents to protect them. Yes, in theory. But there is no ideal situation here, Sowore should go and get his own bodyguards and able-bodied men. He was lucky the machete missed his head in Ekiti.”

“You are saying the Nigerian state has failed.”

“Don’t put words in my mouth. I am saying that heaven helps those who help themselves. The saying is not in the Bible as many people think. But it is basic common sense. If you are looking for the source of the saying, go to Benjamin Franklin’s Poor Richard’s Almanac (1757) or Algernon Sydney’s Discourses Concerning Government” (1798).”

“I am not looking for any sources. Must you quote this and that in a normal conversation.? It is beginning to look like some kind of sickness. Say what you want to say, don’t disturb me with what some dead persons said 100 years ago. I don’t care. I don’t want to have a headache”

“I am saying Nigerian politicians ahead of the 2027 elections should also be security and safety conscious. Look at Peter Obi. He went to Bayelsa state to campaign in the company of Countryman, Chairman of the NDC, Seriake Dickson and others. He was inside a canoe, with an ill-fitted life jacket. He was even holding it with his hands. Does he know how to swim? If that canoe capsized, he would have been surprised that all the Ijaw guys on the canoe will swim ashore. People wey be say na fish appearing in human form. Peter Obi should not take such risks. If anything happened to him, we would have been told that it is because President Tinubu forgot to pray for his protection in Makkah.”

“Is President Tinubu supposed to pray for those who want him out of power?”

“Yes, including Sowore. Don’t be surprised that some people are already saying the President forgot to pray for him in Makka.”

“Dey there. He probably did. But the heavens help those who help themselves, not so? You can’t refuse to wear a seat belt, you get into an accident and you complain about your step-mother having witchcraft.”

“Let this election just come and go.”

“INEC don ready so?”

“INEC will be ready when it is ready”

World.title: FG Redeems 2024 WAFCON  $100,000 Largesse to Super Falcons
World.content:
Duro Ikhazuagbe

Finally, the wait is over as Super Falcons have started to receive alerts for the $100,000 (about N140 million) promised each of the players by President Bola Tinubu after they won the 2024 WAFCON.

Before the payments of the cash reward, players and officials had earlier been presented with 3-bedroom flats in Abuja in addition to Officer of the Order of the Niger (OON) National Honours.

A press statement from the apex sports body in the country, the National Sports Commission (NSC), and signed by Kola Daniel, the spokesman for the Director General of the commission, announced that the players have begun receiving payments of about ₦140 million each, representing the Naira equivalent of the $100,000 reward promised by the President after the team staged a remarkable comeback to defeat hosts Morocco 3-2 in the final played in July 2025.

The Super Falcons, who were trailing 2-0, produced a spirited second-half performance to stun the hosts and reclaim the African crown, further cementing their status as the continent’s most successful women’s national team.

Team Officials were similarly each rewarded with $50,000, national honours and 3-bedroom flats in Abuja.

Team Captain, Rasheedat Ajibade, was quoted to have expressed gratitude to President Tinubu on behalf of the players for fulfilling his promise, describing the gesture as a welcome recognition of the team’s achievement and contribution to Nigerian sports.

The payment is another demonstration of President Tinubu’s commitment to rewarding sporting excellence and motivating Nigerian athletes to achieve greater success on the international stage.

The President had similarly promised and delivered $100,000 rewards to each member of the country’s senior women’s basketball team, D’Tigress following their triumph at the 2025 FIBA Women’s AfroBasket, where Nigeria secured a fifth consecutive continental title.

Super Eagles were similarly rewarded for winning the silver at the AFCON 2023 final played in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire early 2024.

World.title: Will Osimhen Be Able to Revive Galatasaray’s League Phase Ambition?
World.content:
*Olise, Neuer with Bayern in Madrid for Lookman’s Atletico Clash

Super Eagles stars, Victor Osimhen and Ademola Lookman will be in action for their respective teams in the UEFA Champions League as the league phase resumes from this evening.

Osimhen who is just back from injury lay-off will be in action as Galatasaray with only one win in three previous games and 23rd on the log, will be hoping to return to winning ways as German side VfB Stuttgart visit The Rams Park in Istanbul.

Stuttgart are sixth on the log with two wins and a draw from their previous three matches. Galatasaray will need an outright win today to stand any chance of making it to the group stage.

The two clubs have never met in UEFA competition before, making this a genuinely fresh contest between two sides with contrasting European ambitions this season.

Galatasaray arrive off the back of a derby win, having beaten Fenerbahce 2-1 in the Super Lig last Sunday. Okan Buruk’s side have won four of their last five across all competitions, and their 4-2 Champions League victory over Lille last week showed they carry a real goal threat at this level.

Stuttgart, managed by Sebastian Hoeness, have genuine momentum in Europe and the cushion to approach this fixture with confidence rather than desperation.

Stuttgart drew 1-1 with Atletico Madrid in their most recent Champions League outing and beat Slovan Bratislava 3-0 before that, demonstrating they can handle both elite opposition and must-win nights. Their Bundesliga form has been inconsistent, but in Europe they have been measured and effective.

In Madrid this evening, Osimhen’s national teammate, Ademola Lookman will be hoping that he gets a starting shirt as Atletico Madrid play hosts to Bayern Munich with fresh crowned Ballon d’Or winner, Harry Kane.

The Three Lions Captain will not be the worry for Diego Simeone alone, he has in company Captain Manuel Neuer and Michael Olise as they are expected to be available for the clash in Metropolitano this evening.

Both Neuer and Olise joined Bayern Munich’s team training session at Säbener Straße on Monday lunchtime before travelling to Madrid in the afternoon with the official squad.

Neuer had missed recent matches with a foot injury. Olise wore a bandage on his right knee during training. He had been substituted after suffering an injury late in Saturday’s match against Borussia Dortmund (2-2), then left the stadium limping.

In Madrid that evening, interim coach Aaron Danks said both were “available” against Atletico: “We just have to see whether they are ready to start or whether they come off the bench.” Sporting director Max Eberl had earlier said of Olise: “It is positive that he is with us because he is an outstanding player who is always an asset to us. But we will also avoid the risk of it becoming a longer-term injury.”

However, Bayern will definitely be without Luis Diaz, Jamal Musiala, Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari in Madrid. The Moroccan international underwent surgery on Sunday for a tear of the syndesmotic ligament in his right ankle and will not be available again until the new year. Gnabry also suffered a muscle injury in his left thigh against Dortmund.

Signs point to an easing of the squad situation for the matches after the international break through to the end of the year.

On Monday, Diaz completed his first individual session with the ball since suffering a muscle bundle tear in his left thigh in the Champions League match against Arsenal (2-2) on 22 October. Jamal Musiala, who suffered a torn muscle fibre while with the national team at the end of September, also completed his first individual session with the ball since his injury

World.title: Edo Gov’s  Special Adviser Hails Flamingos, Insists Brazil Will Fall
World.content:
Hon Frank Ilaboya, the Special Adviser on Grassroots Sports Mobilization to the Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okphebolo, has joined millions of Nigerians in congratulating the Flamingos over their victory against Venezuela in the quarterfinals of the ongoing FIFA Women’s U17 World Cup in Morocco.

The Nigerian Girls edged Venezuela 1-0 in a tense fixture last night thus booking a place to face Brazil on Wednesday in the semi finals

Hon Ilaboya said Flamingos’ performances so far in the tournament reinforces the need to get young talents from the grassroots, both in the boys and girls categories.

According to Hon Ilaboya, the encouragement given by Governor Okphebolo to scout for raw talents at the grassroots in Edo State must be extended to the girl child, stressing that diverting girls away from societal vices could only be possible when they are engaged at younger age, especially through sports.

Hon Ilaboya, while commending Gov Okpebholo for his foresight in creating a specialised department for grassroots sports, added that his responsibility is to change the narrative by going into the nook and cranny of the state to scout for talents that will make Edo State and the nation proud.

“This opportunity created by His Excellency for grassroots sports department must be fully extended to the girl child by engaging them early through constructive sports activities,”the one time Chairman of the Edo State Football Association said.

“We are putting together a comprehensive programme that will bring Edo State back to her dominance in age grade tournaments.”

The Nigerian U-17 girls have had a great run in the tournament beating the defending Champions, North Korea, 3-1 in the group stage and their hard won victory against Venezuela on Sunday night is pointer that they have what it takes to be champions.

As they face Brazil in another testy semi final clash on Wednesday, Hon Ilaboya is sure of another victory for Nigeria.

“With what we have seen of these girls so far, defeating Brazil is not impossible. These young girls have exhibited strong character, resilience and great determination and these are the ingredients of Champions.

“This is why I am confident of victory over the Samba Girls come on Wednesday. If they put up the same scintillating performance displayed against the defending Champions, North Korea, who they brushed aside 3-1, I can see Brazil falling,” he added.

World.title: Wike Pledges Completion of Abandoned Gwagwalada Mini-Stadium
World.content:
Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Ezenwo Nyesom Wike, has assured residents of Gwagwalada Area Council that the FCT Administration will complete the long-abandoned Gwagwalada Mini-Stadium to provide sporting opportunities for youths and promote grassroots sports development.

Wike gave the assurance yesterday during an interactive town hall meeting with stakeholders of the Rainbow Coalition at the newly constructed Gwagwalada Civic Centre.

He said the completion of the facility would provide young people in the area with a platform to engage in sporting activities, develop their talents and potentially produce athletes capable of representing Nigeria at national and international competitions.

The minister described the youths’ request for a functional sporting facility as modest but important, stressing that access to basic sports infrastructure could help discover future stars.

“The youths have said here that they are not asking much. Where they can play sports morning, evening, weekend, play football. You never can tell, one day we will have somebody like Lionel Messi, we are talking about Mbappé. We may have him here. Give them the opportunity. You are not asking for money. You are not asking for too much,” he said.

Wike subsequently assured the community that the administration would revisit the abandoned project and ensure its completion.

“Let me assure you, that project (Gwagwalada mini-stadium) that was abandoned, we will make sure we come back and complete it,” the Minister stated.

The pledge is expected to address longstanding concerns among residents, particularly young people, over the absence of adequate sporting facilities for recreation, talent development and organised sporting competitions.

Wike stressed that providing opportunities for young people to participate in sports was important to national development, noting that talents capable of achieving global recognition could emerge from communities such as Gwagwalada if given the necessary support and facilities.

The town hall meeting also provided an opportunity for community stakeholders to present other pressing concerns to the FCT Administration.

Responding to environmental and public health concerns, Wike directed the Agriculture and Rural Development Secretariat to liaise with the Gwagwalada Area Council Chairman, Kassim Mohammed, and ensure the immediate relocation of the local abattoir.

He also highlighted ongoing infrastructure development in the area, particularly road construction projects, recalling that the road leading to Zuba, which was requested during his earlier visit, was expected to be completed in December.

The engagement formed part of the minister’s ongoing consultations with stakeholders across the six Area Councils of the FCT.

World.title: Lagos, Owerri, Calabar Set for Zonal Finals of Sam Okwaraji Memoir Cup
World.content:
After the conclusion of the Northern Zonal playoffs of the Samuel Okwaraji Foundation national secondary schools football competition, the Memoir Cup, all is now set for the Southern Zonal finals.

The Maracana Stadium, Ajegunle in Lagos, the Dan Anyiam Stadium, Owerri as well as the UJ Esuene Stadium, Calabar have been picked, and are ready for the Zonal playoffs of the competition for the South West, South South and South East regions.

These Zonal playoffs represent the second stage of the national championships after the State Finals were played across the country earlier in the year.

According to the Chairman of the competition’s organising committee, Senator Osita Izunazo, the southern Zonal playoffs will take place starting from today, Tuesday, November 3 and end on Saturday, November 7, 2026.

Izunazo explained that the three Zonal champions that will emerge from the southern region will join the other three that had emerged from the Northern region earlier for the national finals in Lagos at a later date this month.

The technical partners of the competition, the Nigeria School Sport Federation(NSSF) have also announced their readiness for the Zonal playoffs in the south while applauding the standard of the competition.

Olabisi Joseph, President of the Nigeria School Sport Federation said the high standards, thorough and transparent systems put in place for the competition will ensure that the main objective of the competition, which is to discover football talents in secondary schools, is achieved.

“We have ensured that all the processes and systems in place for this tournament are very thorough, efficient and transparent and these standards will not drop or be lowered.

“We are ready for the Zonal playoffs in the south and they will be organised with the same standards used for the Northern region.

“I can assure you that these will also be maintained for the national finals later this month,” Joseph added.

The Memoir Cup as the Samuel Okwaraji national secondary schools football competition sponsored by First Bank is called, is organised in memory of Nigeria’s fallen football hero Samuel Okwaraji who slumped and died while on active service for the Nigerian senior men’s national football team – the Super Eagles on August 12, 1989 during a 1990 World Cup qualifying game against Angola inside the main bowl of the National Stadium, Surulere, Lagos.

World.title: Kuti, Ojo Exit Table Tennis Event at 2026 Youth Olympics Games
World.content:
Nigeria’s deputy captain, Matthew Kuti, and teammate Favour Ojo played their final matches in the table tennis event at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal after losing their respective final preliminary-round fixtures.

Earlier in the day, Ojo was defeated by her Hong Kong counterpart, suffering her third loss in a group of four players. Only the top two players in each group advanced to the knockout stage.

Kuti, who was one victory away from securing a place in the men’s singles knockout stage, lost 0-3 to Italy’s Francesco Travesan, joining the list of African players eliminated in the opening round of the competition.

Of the 15 African players who began their quest for podium finishes in the table tennis event, only Algeria’s Tania Morice and Egypt’s Abdelmalk Elsayed remain in contention.

Both players will be aiming to match or surpass the quarter-final achievement recorded by Nigeria’s Ojo Onaolapo at the 2010 Youth Olympic Games in Singapore.

In the men’s singles, Algeria’s Aylan Goudjil, Benin Republic’s Ganiou Abdourahaman, Senegal’s Amador Ferrer, Tunisia’s Youssef Aidli, and Uganda’s Joseph Sebatindira were all eliminated in the preliminary round.

In the women’s singles, Egypt’s Yara Elbadawy, Ghana’s Joanita Borteye, Madagascar’s Tina Andriantahina, Senegal’s Marieme Diallo, Tunisia’s Ela Saidi, and Uganda’s Jemimah Nakawala have also exited the tournament following defeats in the preliminary stage.

Top Players Scramble to Qualify for ProvidusUnity Bank Tennis Masters

Top Nigerian senior tennis players excited about the impending debut of a year- end tournament, are now scrambling to attend the last three tournaments of the year in order to qualify for the prestigious and lucrative ProvidusUnity Bank Tennis Masters.

The tournament will feature eight men and women. Six will qualify based on their ranking on the Nigerian Tennis Federation ranking list, while the International Tennis Academy, organizers of the tournament will choose the two wild cards to make up the number.

Daniel Adeleye who was national No.1 in singles and doubles from 2024 to April 2026 is now ranked 14 because he spent more time trying to play ATP tournaments to get a world ranking.

“I was not planning to play the Dala Hard court in Kano this year,” he told the Masters Tournament organizers, “but because of this ProvidusUnity Bank Masters, I have bought my ticket for Kano and luckily we have the Destiny Da Silva tournament which will count for ranking before then. I will have to fight to qualify,” Adeleye said.

The ladies are not left out in the scramble. Bright Emmanuel, Favour Moses and Blessing Omotayo who are ranked seventh, eight and ninth respectively, said they have increased the intensity of their training to get into the top six..

Godwin Kienka, director of the international tennis Academy said one of the players being considered for a wild card is Seun Ogunsakin, who got to the semifinals of the junior Wimbledon event this year and won the ITF J200 tournament for 18s in Egypt in October.

With three tournaments – The Destiny Da Silva Championships, the Dala Hard Courts and the JIO Tennis Championships in Makurdi – coming up this last quarter, the ProvidusUnity Bank Masters will be a truly end of year and holiday event to take place in Lagos from Tuesday December 22 to Saturday December 26

World.title: Google launches FREE AI, digital skills hub in SA with isiZulu and isiXhosa support
World.content:
The new African skills hub has also been designed with connectivity challenges in mind. Image: Pixabay

Google has launched a free online learning hub aimed at expanding access to artificial intelligence (AI) and digital skills across Africa, including South Africa.

Called Skilling Africa with Google, the new platform brings more than 15 training initiatives together in one place.

“Today, more than 90% of companies across the region report a critical deficit in AI-ready professionals,” the tech giant said on Monday.



“[The] new learning hub [is] designed to expand access to digital and AI skills, equipping three million people across the continent by 2030.”

Google said the initiative builds on its existing training programmes, which have already provided foundational digital training to more than seven million young Africans.

Free digital training at your fingertips

The hub gives learners access to a range of courses and programmes, including Google Career Certificates, Hustle Academy and Google Cloud Skills.



These cover everything from IT support, data analytics and cybersecurity to entrepreneurship and cloud technology.

Learners can also access bite-sized modules covering AI, career development and other technical skills.

Getting started requires a Google account, with one-click sign-in available. There is no need to download an app.



Google said the platform is entirely free and open to everyone, from students and entrepreneurs to developers and IT professionals.

AI learning platform adds African language support

The new hub has also been designed with connectivity challenges in mind.

Users can download lessons while connected to Wi-Fi and complete them offline. The platform is also optimised for low-bandwidth connections and entry-level smartphones.



Another feature is SCOUT (Smart Companion for Online Understanding and Training), an AI-powered study assistant.

It can answer questions, recommend next steps and tailor study schedules to individual learning goals.

According to BizCommunity, Google said it is also adding support for more African languages, with isiZulu and isiXhosa among the first planned additions.



English, Swahili and Arabic are currently available.

The platform launched across Africa on 2 November 2026, with Google positioning it as a way to help bridge the continent’s AI skills gap.

World.title: Transfer report: Kaizer Chiefs sign 11-capped Bafana Bafana winger
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs are expected to announce the 27-year-old winger. The KwaMhlanga-born attacker has been a free agent since leaving Tunisian giants Esperance in September.

According to Unplayable, the speedy winger, who has two goals in 11 games for South Africa, has put pen to paper at Naturena.

KAIZER CHIEFS TO ANNOUNCE ELIAS MOKWANA

“UNPLAYABLE can reveal Kaizer Chiefs have signed Elias Mokwana. Deal done. Official announcement this week,” the outlet reported on X.



Known for his blistering pace, agility and dribbling ability on the right flank, Mokwana never enjoyed a smooth rise.

Financial difficulties forced him to quit his sports science studies, but he continued pursuing his football dream. He began making a name for himself in the ABC Motsepe League with Gemsbok Classic before earning a move to National First Division side Platinum City Rovers.

His performances at Platinum City Rovers attracted attention from top-flight clubs. During the 2021/22 season, he made 22 appearances and scored three goals, paving the way for a major breakthrough.



ELIAS MOKWANA’S BREAKTHROUGH AT SEKHUKHUNE UNITED

In May 2022, Mokwana signed a three-year contract with Sekhukhune United. He quickly adapted to the demands of the Betway Premiership, becoming a regular starter and an important attacking player. Across two productive seasons, he made more than 50 league appearances, contributed goals and assists, and earned several Player of the Match awards.

His club performances also opened the door to international football. Mokwana received his first Bafana Bafana call-up in November 2023 and went on to be part of the South African squad that claimed bronze at the Africa Cup of Nations. He also scored important goals in international matches against Andorra and Congo.

In August 2024, Mokwana took the next step in his career by joining Tunisian giants Espérance de Tunis on a three-year deal. He made an immediate impact, becoming the first South African player to win the Tunisian Ligue Professionnelle 1 title.



His debut season in Tunisia proved highly successful. He featured in more than 30 matches across all competitions, including the CAF Champions League, and helped Espérance secure a domestic treble consisting of the league title, Tunisian Cup and Tunisian Super Cup.

Mokwana then moved to the Saudi Pro League in August 2025, joining Al-Hazem on a season-long loan. He became an important part of the team, making 24 appearances and 16 starts. The winger also opened his scoring account in the Gulf region with a memorable individual goal against Al-Taawoun.
