World.title: Four arrested as illegal firearms and ammunition found in vehicle
World.content:
Four men have been arrested after illegal firearms and a large quantity of ammunition were found in the vehicle they were driving in.

On Sunday, 1 November 2026, City Highway Patrol officers stopped a vehicle at the N2 weighbridge in Somerset West. They found four illegal firearms and ammunition within the vehicle.

The officers then arrested four of the five occupants and transported them to Somerset West Police Station. The fifth occupant reportedly fled the scene, per a media statement from the City of Cape Town.



INFLUX OF ILLEGAL FIREARMS ‘DEEPLY CONCERNING’

Alderman JP Smith, the mayoral committee member for Safety and Security, lauded the officers for their efforts on Sunday.

“I want to commend the Highway Patrol officers for their vigilance,” said Smith. “Their sharp observation skills led to more illegal guns being taken out of circulation, and possibly fewer crimes committed or lives destroyed.”

He continued: “The influx of weapons, including more and more automatic and semi-automatic assault rifles, remains deeply concerning, and it’s one of the reasons we have long called for better and more aggressive policing along the metro’s borders to curb the smuggling of firearms into the Metro.”

CITY ENFORCEMENT MAKES 199 ARRESTS

In this past week, the City of Cape Town’s enforcement departments made 199 arrests.

In addition to the Somerset West bust, these arrests include the detainment of 70 suspects by Traffic Officers. Fifty-three were for drunk driving, seven were for reckless and negligent driving, and ten were on other charges. Officers executed 2 076 warrants, impounded 118 public transport vehicles and issued 46 511 fines.

On the Metro Police front, they arrested 105 suspects. They also recovered eight hijacked and/or stolen vehicles, four firearms and 63 rounds of ammunition and issued 4 445 fines for various transgressions.



As for Law Enforcement officers, they made 24 arrests and issued 7 405 notices.

Members of the public are encouraged to report incidents, emergencies or suspicious/criminal activities to the Public Emergency Communication Centre on 021 480 7700. Alternatively, you can log by-law and traffic-related complaints using the Safety and Security feature on the City App.

In other Cape Town news, an eight-year-old Grade 1 learner has passed away following a suspected firecracker incident in Manenberg.

World.title: SAHRC responds to Andile Mngxitama’s farm attack tweet
World.content:
The SAHRC has responded to backlash of Andile Mngxitama's farm attack tweets about Donovan Marx. Images via X

The South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC) has responded to widespread backlash over comments by MK Party MP Andile Mngxitama condoning the attack on North West cattle farmer Donovan Marx.

In a tweet, Mngxitama claimed that the attackers’ decision to chop off Marx’s ears was “symbolic”.

Five suspects have since been arrested in connection with the Ventersdorp attack.



SAHRC RESPONDS TO ANDILE MNGXITAMA TWEET ABOUT FARM ATTACK

Over the weekend, social media users have called on the SAHRC to investigate and take action against Andile Mngxitama.

On Monday, 2 November, SAHRC Commissioner Tshepo Madlingozi told The South African in a statement: “The South African Human Rights Commission confirms that it has received complaints against Mr Andile Mngxitama regarding a post on Mr Donovan Marx. The Commission is assessing the complaints in line with its Complaint Handling Procedure.

“The decision of the assessment will be communicated in due course as empowered by section 13(3)(b) of the South African Human Rights Commission Act 40 of 2013 (SAHRC Act), read with section 20 of the Equality Act, 2000”.

It continued: “The Commission wishes to remind members of the public that the right to freedom of expression is not absolute. The Constitution and the Promotion of Equality and Prevention of Unfair Discrimination Act of 2000 prohibit utterances that are intended to be harmful or propagate hatred on any of the listed grounds. ”

HISTORY OF TWEETS ABOUT RACISM, FARM ATTACKS AND WHITE SOUTH AFRICANS

Andile Mngxitama began trending over the weekend, when he tweeted: “Ventersdorp white farmer Donovan Marx had his ears cut off during a Plaas moord aanval [farm murder attack]. Attacking the ears is symbolic to denote the refusal of land thieves to listen. No land, no peace.

He added, “Farm life is overdetermined by systematic violence! Blacks got killed and fed to pigs!”



The MK Party MP later deleted the tweet but did not deny having posted it. In several responses, he poked fun at the backlash of his racially inflammatory comments.

Andile Mngxitama, a former member of the EFF who later started his own party, Black First Land First (BLF), has a long history of controversial social media and public comments on race, land ownership, white South Africans, and farm attacks.

His comments on X [formerly Twitter] have led to his account being permanently suspended.

Here are a few of his most controversial statements…

“We take the land by force. We’re not going to buy this land because it was stolen from us.” – October 2016, speaking at a rally.

“For those claiming the legacy of the holocaust is ONLY negative, think about the lampshades and Jewish soap.”

“I concur with @helenzille that the aroma of the burning flesh from the furnace of the holocaust may whet the appetite of the S.A. cannibals.” – August 2017 via X.

“All land owned by white people should be returned to black people. That includes land in Orania and Stellenbosch; all that land must be returned” – September 2018, speaking in parliament.

“For every one black life taken, five whites would be taken!” – December 2018 during a rally.

“Let’s repeat: if you kill black people. Will kill you too! Tell Johann Rupert” – December 2018 via X.

“I agree with Trump: the land thieves must leave SA and go to the USA. Our land shall be free of colonialists – Mabahambe!” – February 2025 via X.

World.title: Orlando Pirates have something Kaizer Chiefs don’t have
World.content:
Soweto giants Kaizer Chiefs finally tasted defeat in the Betway Premiership this season. Coach Da Cruz’s side succumbed to a 2-1 loss to rivals Orlando Pirates.

The result left Amakhosi 11 points behind the second-placed Buccaneers.

FERNANDO DA CRUZ ON KAIZER CHIEFS’ EXPLAINS THE GAP

The result was a heavy one to take but Da Cruz feels his side showed promising signs. According to the Frenchman, the Glamour Boys have some work before matching the likes of Pirates.



Da Cruz believes Pirates’ experience has played a major role in their consistency, something he wants to see his young Chiefs squad develop.

“The difference between Pirates and us, they have more experienced players and they have more consistency because of that,” he said.

“Our young players need to develop this consistency game by game. It takes time, it’s a process we need to take step by step and for the moment we’re not there. We will work hard to reach this step.”

The Chiefs coach was particularly pleased with his team’s first-half performance against the Buccaneers. However, he stressed that positive spells are not enough to compete at the highest level.

“We must use this type of game to grow up. The players must reach the next steps, but the players must understand we played well, we did good things, but it’s not enough. We must reach the next steps now,” he added.

A PLEA TO AMAKHOSI FANS

The Frenchman also warned against expecting an immediate turnaround, explaining that experience is something players develop over time through training and exposure to different competitions.



“We must continue to work but it takes time, it takes time, it’s not overnight these things can be fixed. We cannot get experience from one day to the next day. It’s training, many games and we must continue to learn, with competitions of different levels,” he added.

In the meantime, Kaizer Chiefs have a cup game to focus on. The Carling Knockout quarter-finals are coming up. The Glamour Boys will be home to Siwelele FC at FNB Stadium this Friday, kick off time to be confirmed.

World.title: Phala Phala judgment: Two convicted, third accused acquitted
World.content:
Imanuwela David and Froliana Joseph were convicted in the Phala Phala theft case, while Ndilinasho Joseph was acquitted. Image: X @Abramjee

The Modimolle Regional Court delivered the Phala Phala judgment on Monday, 2 November, more than six years after a break-in at President Cyril Ramaphosa’s Limpopo game farm.

On Monday, 2 November, the Modimolle Regional Court convicted two of the three accused. The third walked free.

Magistrate Peter Manthata found Imanuwela David and Froliana Joseph guilty.



Meanwhile, Joseph’s brother, Ndilinasho Joseph, was acquitted on all charges.

The trio stood accused of stealing $580 000 (R9.6 million) from Ramaphosa’s Phala Phala farm near Bela-Bela in February 2020.

What the court found

Manthata convicted David of conspiracy to commit housebreaking with intent to steal, housebreaking with intent to steal and theft, and money laundering.



The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) alleged he was the mastermind.

Froliana, a former temporary worker at Phala Phala, was convicted of conspiracy to commit housebreaking with intent to steal.

Manthata found that she and David communicated by cellphone before and after the break-in.



He also rejected a defence argument that the State’s cellphone analyst was not qualified to give that evidence.

The court found that Froliana’s duties on the farm gave her access to the house.

The State says she tipped David off about the cash, which was hidden under a couch.



Why Ndilinasho Joseph walked free

Manthata said Ndilinasho had never worked at Phala Phala.

He found no evidence that Ndilinasho knew what was happening there.

The magistrate also found nothing in the siblings’ possession.



Their bank accounts showed no sign that they had benefited from the theft.

Attorney Mike Mokgobo, who represents the siblings, welcomed the outcome.

“We have managed to achieve the acquittal of accused three,” he said, adding that Froliana had been acquitted on two of the three counts she faced.



All three were found not guilty of a separate break-in at Stokkiesdraai, a neighbouring farm.

Gaps in the Phala Phala theft case

Manthata pointed to weaknesses in the investigation.

There were no fingerprints and no usable video footage showing who broke into the president’s house.



The State called more than 20 witnesses during the trial, which began in September 2025.

The court declared at least four of them hostile after their evidence departed from their police statements.

The court also heard that David allegedly used part of the money to buy his girlfriend a car and an apartment.



He later took the car back after the relationship ended.

David had denied stealing the money, claiming it came from a friend in Namibia.

What happens next after the Phala Phala judgment

Manthata postponed the case to 13 November for pre-sentencing proceedings.



David has been in custody since being denied bail in 2023.

Bela-Bela sits roughly 100km north of Pretoria.

Most people know the quiet bushveld town for its hot springs, not for courtroom drama.



Yet this case drew national attention because of who owns the farm.

The theft only became public in June 2022, when former spy boss Arthur Fraser laid a criminal complaint against Ramaphosa. Monday’s convictions relate only to the theft.

They are separate from the political and parliamentary fallout over Phala Phala.

World.title: 42 days later: PSL club to fire new coach?
World.content:
According to the latest report, Richards Bay FC management are seemingly set to hit the panic button following the results under the Pantev.

The Bulgarian was appointed on 21 September 2026. Unfortunately, the former Simba SC, Gaborone United and Jwaneng Galaxy coach is under scrutiny on the East Coast.

DIMITAR PANTEV UNDER PRESSURE AT RICHARDS BAY

The club known as the Natal Rich Boyz are yet to register a victory in nine Betway Premiership matches this season. Their struggles have also extended to other competitions, with the club enduring six successive defeats across all competitions.



According to FARPost’s Sinethemba Makonco, Richards Bay management are weighing up the 50-year-old coach’s future. Internal talks are expected to determine whether he remains in charge.

The situation leaves the club facing a difficult decision. The results have been disappointing. But Pantev has had limited time to implement his ideas and turn the team’s fortunes around.

The Natal Rich Boyz have suffered several damaging defeats since his arrival, with their latest setback coming against Kruger United.

Their recent results include:

13 October 2026: Lost 1-4 to Mamelodi Sundowns

Lost 1-4 to Mamelodi Sundowns 25 October 2026: Lost 1-3 to Sekhukhune United

Lost 1-3 to Sekhukhune United 31 October 2026: Lost 1-3 to Kruger United.

The defeats have left Richards Bay rooted to the bottom of the Betway Premiership standings. It has put high pressure on the club’s technical team.

RICHARDS BAY FACED WITH A DIFFICULT DECISION

The prospect of another coaching change comes at a challenging time for the club, with the league campaign already proving difficult.



Pantev’s short tenure has been marked by poor results, but the club must also consider whether changing coaches so early would provide the necessary improvement.

With management reportedly assessing the situation, the coming days could prove decisive for the Bulgarian coach.

For now, Pantev’s future at Richards Bay remains uncertain, with the club yet to make an official announcement regarding his position.

World.title: IEC reminds voters of do’s and don'ts
World.content:
MIDRAND - With local elections taking place on Wednesday and the final day of special voting on Tuesday, the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) has once again reminded voters to follow the rules at the voting station.

This, according to the Commission, is to protect the secrecy of one's vote, but the integrity of the electoral process as well.

The IEC lists the do's and don'ts :

The Do’s

Mark your ballot paper in private inside your designated voting compartments

Follow instructions of election officials throughout the process

Respect other voters

Maintain order at the voting station

Co-operate with election officials and observe rules of special voting

The Don’ts

World.title: High Court sets aside awarding of Lotto licence to Sizekhaya Holdings
World.content:
PRETORIA - The High Court in Pretoria has set aside the Lotto licence awarded to Sizekhaya Holdings.

The agreement between the DTIC Minister, the National Lotteries Commission, and Sizekhaya Holdings has been suspended for 12 months.

This allows Minister Parks Tau to decide whether to award the licence afresh or negotiate a new deal if it is not given to Sizekhaya.

READ | New Lotto operator Sizekhaya begins eight-year term

World.title: Two accused in Phala Phala Farm theft found guilty of housebreaking
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Modimolle Regional Court has convicted two people in connection with the theft of $580,000 from President Cyril Ramaphosa's Phala Phala farm in February 2020.

Imanuwela David was found guilty of conspiracy to commit housebreaking and theft, as well as money laundering, while Froliana Joseph was convicted of conspiracy to commit housebreaking.

READ | Impeachment shouldn’t be taken lightly – expert

The court found that the State had presented sufficient circumstantial evidence despite shortcomings in the investigation and the absence of direct evidence identifying the perpetrators.

A third accused, Ndilinasho Joseph, was acquitted of all charges, while all three accused were found not guilty of charges relating to a separate incident at Stokkiedraai farm.

The case returns to court on 13 November for pre-sentencing proceedings.

World.title: New vehicle sales climb more than 10% in October
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Car sales in South Africa show no signs of slowing down.

According to the industry body, NAAMSA, the number of cars sold in October was more than 10% higher than during the same time last year.

New Energy Vehicles, including electric vehicles and hybrids, showed the most acceleration.

Cumulative sales for the first nine months of the year were above 22,000, which is already more than the whole of last year.

One in every nine cars sold in September was a New Energy Vehicle.

World.title: High water consumption blamed for reservoir shortage in Joburg
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Johannesburg Mayor Dada Morero has blamed the rapid rate of water use for reservoirs being unable to keep up with demand.

He was providing an update on the water situation on Monday alongside Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi

According to Morero, the city’s overall water storage has improved to 41% after days of supply problems.

But he warned residents that they may still experience throttling or low pressure as teams adjust flow and network pressure to divert water to areas that need it.

“Our reservoirs have struggled to recover because water is being used faster than reservoirs and towers can refill, and high-lying areas have been hit the hardest. Some reservoirs, including Hursthill, remain bypassed because of leaks. “Labour action in Johannesburg also contributed to delayed interventions, which we needed to do to stabilise the system. However, overall storage across the Johannesburg water supply system has improved to 41 percent and up from 37 percent.”

Joburg Water is also acquiring its own water tanker fleet. This is to help reduce pressure on the municipality and avoid outsourcing when times get tough.

Morero said approximately 60 trucks will be made available.

“In 2025, 20 tankers were procured and are fully operational. In the second phase, 16 tankers have been procured; six are active, five have been delivered and have been prepared for operation this month, and the remaining five are due during 2026-2027 budget. “A further 20 tankers are planned for the 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 budget, and once complete, the fleet of approximately 60 trucks will replace contracted vehicles for daily services to informal settlements, and the savings will be redirected to other demand management projects that reduce physical losses, bulk purchases, and consumption," Morero explained.

Meanwhile, Lesufi said he continues to hold weekly meetings with municipalities and the water and sanitation minister to find permanent solutions for the ongoing water crisis.

He said his priority is to ensure all communities have water.

World.title: IEC presiding officer dies another hospitalised during first day of special voting
World.content:
MIDRAND - An Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) presiding officer collapsed and died at a voting station in Mahikeng during the first day of special voting for the 2026 Local Government Elections, which got underway on Monday.

Another official, a deputy presiding officer from Gauteng, was hospitalised after she was involved in a car accident.

The IEC confirmed that the Gauteng official remains in hospital.

Additionally, the Commission has provided necessary support to affected officials who were at the stations and the family of the deceased.

READ | Reporter Diaries | Special voting under way in Knysna

Despite the two incidents, Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) of the IEC, Sy Mamabolo, reported that the IEC recorded a strong performance of special votes across the country.

Special Voting concluded at 5pm on Monday, with Mamabolo expressing satisfaction with the day's proceedings.

But the day was not without hustles.

Earlier, it was reported that 217 voting stations in Cape Town opened later than scheduled due to delays in the delivery of ballots.

READ | Special voting hit by delays as 217 Cape Town stations open late

The IEC attributed the issue to ballot reprinting and delivery delays. But Mamabolo confirmed that this issue has been attended to.

“We are pleased to announce that subsequently, all affected voting stations opened and remained operational," he said.

Mambolo has also issued a final call to approved special voters to cast their ballot on Tuesday.

Voting stations are expected to open from 8am to 5pm.

Mambolo said those who fail to make use of this final special vote opportunity will only be able to vote on 4 November at the same voting stations they registered at.

Meanwhile, voters approved for home visits are urged to remain at the addresses provided in their application.

World.title: Trump terminates South Africa from AGOA
World.content:
WASHINGTON - The United States Trade Representative on Monday said Washington would exclude South Africa and Rwanda from a major Africa-US duty-free trade deal, a blow to both economies, over practices "inconsistent" with the deal's eligibility criteria.

"These concerning and pervasive practices include, but are not limited to, barriers that undermine American trade and investment and practices that pose a threat to US national security and foreign policy interests in the region," Jamieson Greer said in a statement.

The exclusions will take effect from January 1, the statement said.

The African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), which grants eligible sub-Saharan African countries preferential access to the US market, has been renewed until the end of 2028, but is reviewed annually.

South Africa is the program's largest beneficiary but its eligibility has come under scrutiny as Washington steps up criticism of Pretoria, including false allegations of discrimination against white Afrikaners that South Africa rejects.

On Thursday, South Africa's trade minister said the country hoped for a favorable decision from Washington on the issue, arguing that continued market access would be in the best interest of both countries.

A little over a week earlier, however, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said the country should "prepare" for an adverse decision.

The US president reviews countries' eligibility for AGOA annually.

Any removal requires 60 days' notice to Congress and the country concerned.

South African Trade Minister Parks Tau told reporters in Johannesburg last week that regardless of Trump's decision on AGOA, his country's economy would remain stable as it seeks other international markets.

Increasing pressure on Rwanda

Washington has been increasing economic pressure on Rwanda over its alleged backing of the armed M23 rebel group in neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo.

Last week, the United States sanctioned the Rwandan defense ministry over those ties, which the Rwandan government denies.

With Rwandan help, the M23 movement has seized swathes of the eastern DRC -- home to valuable minerals coveted by world powers -- since it took up arms again in 2021.

Rwanda's foreign minister told AFP last week that his country should not be a "scapegoat" for events in DR Congo.

"The situation in the DRC, the political situation, the security situation, is mainly a Congolese issue," Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe told AFP on the sidelines of a Russia-Africa summit in Moscow before the US sanctions were imposed.

"Rwanda must not be held as a scapegoat for what is happening in Congo forever," he added.

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

World.title: KCSE candidates relocated in Moyale after stray bullets hit school
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba. [File,Standard]

Two Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) examination centres in Moyale have been relocated after stray bullets hit a school amid cross-border clashes between Ethiopian communities.

Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba said the decision followed clan clashes along the Kenya-Ethiopia border, which raised security concerns in Moyale Sub-County, Marsabit County.

In a statement on Monday, November 2, Ogamba said the government had moved the two centres to address the security threat and protect the examination process.

The relocation comes as fighting between Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regional administrations continues to drive civilians across the border into Kenya.

The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said on October 28 that local authorities estimated up to 50,000 people had crossed into Kenya seeking safety.

The figure remained subject to registration and verification.

Women and children make up a large proportion of those fleeing the violence. Some have sought shelter with relatives and host communities while others are staying in temporary facilities, including schools and churches.

UNHCR identified food as the most urgent need among the displaced, alongside safe drinking water, emergency shelter, sanitation and healthcare.

The agency deployed an emergency team to Moyale to support the response with the Kenyan government and humanitarian organisations.

The Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR) has also warned the influx was putting pressure on resources in Moyale, including food, clean water, shelter and healthcare.

Meanwhile, the 2026 KCSE examination began its compulsory, large-candidature papers on Monday after two weeks of examinations in elective subjects with smaller candidature, including foreign languages, music and technical subjects.

This year's examination involves 1,048,355 candidates sitting their papers in 10,693 centres across the country.

The ministry has also made special arrangements for seven hospitalised candidates and five others in correctional facilities to undertake their examinations.

Ogamba said the government was prepared to take measures to address any emerging challenges during the examination period.

The Kenya Primary School Education Assessment (KPSEA) concluded on October 28, while the Kenya Junior School Education Assessment (KJSEA) ended on October 30.

The national examinations and assessments began on October 19.

Ogamba commended candidates, contracted examination personnel and members of the public for supporting the administration of the examinations.

World.title: Kenyans stranded after Saudi Arabia blocks entry over Ebola concerns
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

More than 300 Kenyans who travelled to Saudi Arabia in search of employment have been forced to return home after authorities blocked their entry over Ebola-related restrictions, leaving them stranded at the airport for two days.

The group, which departed Kenya on October 30, had travelled to the Gulf country on valid work visas but was denied entry upon arrival and subsequently repatriated, arriving back in the country on Monday.

The return follows a warning by Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale on Saturday, October 31, over restrictions imposed by Saudi Arabia on travellers from countries flagged over Ebola concerns.

Speaking to the media at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) on Monday, the affected workers recounted their ordeal, accusing authorities at the airport of subjecting them to harsh conditions as they waited to be repatriated.

“We were treated so harshly as though we had leprosy. We only took one meal per day and slept on the cold floors at the airport in Saudi Arabia,” said Kanyi Njau, one of the affected workers, claiming that some have even lost their luggage.

Beyond the difficult experience at the airport, the workers said their biggest concern was the financial loss incurred while preparing for the promised jobs.

Some said they had sold land, household belongings and other property, while others borrowed money to pay recruitment agents, process visas and secure travel documents in preparation for their departure.

Njau said the abrupt disruption had shattered the hopes of many who had invested heavily in securing employment abroad.

“Some of us sold things in our houses, even land. Some even took loans from shylocks just so that we could travel over there for the jobs, but now we are back with no hope,” she said.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The workers are now appealing to the Kenyan Government to intervene and resolve the standoff with Saudi authorities before their visas expire, allowing them to return and take up the jobs they had secured.

Meanwhile, recruitment agencies have called on the Government to urgently clarify the restrictions, warning that uncertainty over a 21-day provision could disrupt the country's labour mobility programme.

Monika Mwema, the Secretary General of the Association of Skilled Migrant Agencies of Kenya (ASMAK), said recruiters had been caught off guard, with some workers already repatriated while others had confirmed tickets and were scheduled to travel.

“We are caught off guard. We have people who are coming back because they could not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia, while others have confirmed tickets and are even supposed to leave tonight and tomorrow,” she said.

Mwema said the association was seeking clarification on what the 21-day provision meant for workers holding stamped Saudi work visas, including whether they would be required to undergo quarantine in Kenya or in a third country before being allowed into the Kingdom.

“Does it mean we have to quarantine our people here for the 21 days, then they are allowed to enter the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia? Or does it mean that we need to seek an alternative quarantine area where there is no case of Ebola?” she asked.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

She said recruiters were also concerned about the 90-day period within which migrant workers are required to travel after their visas are stamped, warning that delays could result in significant losses for agencies and prospective employees.

Mwema added that some workers had already undergone training and completed examinations in preparation for their deployment, while recruitment partners in Saudi Arabia were demanding to know when the workers would arrive.

“The losses are just too many. We have people who have already gone to school for training; others have done their examinations and are waiting to go. Our partners are calling us, asking when these people are coming, but we are all in the dark,” she said.

ASMAK is now seeking urgent engagement with the Kenyan Government and Saudi authorities to establish a clear way forward.

Mwema said the association was ready to engage the Government, including through a meeting with President William Ruto, to discuss the future of labour mobility between the two countries.

Saudi Arabia remains Kenya's biggest market for labour mobility, with recruiters warning that continued uncertainty could affect workers awaiting deployment and agencies with visas already processed.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses Uhuru reconciliation calls, says 'we are one team'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua received at PCEA Kamangu in Kikuyu constituency by former Kiambu governor James Nyoro on November 1, 2026. [George Njunge, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed calls for mediation between him and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, insisting that the two leaders remain in contact and have no differences requiring reconciliation.

Gachagua said attempts by Mount Kenya elders to broker peace between them were unnecessary, maintaining that he and the former Head of State continue to communicate, meet and share meals despite perceptions of a political fallout.

He challenged elders calling for reconciliation to instead focus on uniting the Mount Kenya community, warning that internal divisions could weaken the region's political voice and influence.

“On unity, as a community we have to remain united. Our unity is strength. Nimeona some elders in the newspaper wakisema tunataka to reconcile Rigathi Gachagua and Uhuru Kenyatta. How do you reconcile two brothers, who love one another and work together?” he posed.

The former Deputy President maintained that he and Uhuru were still on the same team, dismissing claims that their relationship had deteriorated to a point requiring third-party intervention.

“President Uhuru Kenyatta and I are one team. We work together. Please elders don’t reconcile us because there is no need for reconciliation. We are working together. There is no work there, we are one. We talk the same language, we meet, talk, we agree,” he said.

Gachagua further urged Mount Kenya elders to resist attempts to divide the community along political lines and instead promote dialogue and cohesion among its leaders.

“Our unity is our strength as a community. Please help me to unite Mount Kenya elders and tell people not to accept to be divided,” he added.

His remarks come amid growing calls by sections of Mount Kenya elders for reconciliation among influential political figures from the region following political differences that have emerged since the 2022 General Election.

Uhuru, who served as Kenya's fourth president from 2013 to 2022, remains an influential political figure in the region, while Gachagua has continued to position himself as a key voice in Mount Kenya politics.

World.title: Sifuna rallies opposition leaders to unite against Ruto in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leader Edwin Sifuna adresses a rally at Ukunda in Kwale County on 31st October, 2026. [Omondi Onyango, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi movement took its grassroots mobilisation tour to Kwale County, a day after unveiling its secretariat and leadership, with leaders urging the opposition to unite behind one candidate to face President William Ruto in 2027.

The unveiling had been marred by disagreement, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka jeered. Addressing a rally at Masai Grounds in Ukunda town, Sifuna said Kenyans were yearning for a single, strong opposition candidate and asked other leaders not to let them down.

“To send Ruto home, we need a strong team and a strong presidential candidate. I will ask other leaders to listen to the voices of the people politely because this is the voice of God,” he said.

The team made stopovers in Samburu, Kinango, Kwale town and Kombani during the day-long tour. Unlike earlier rallies in Mombasa, the Kwale events drew modest crowds, amid claims that local organisers had failed to mobilise supporters.

The mobilisation tour covered Samburu Town, Kinango Town, Kombani Junction, Lunga Lunga Town, and culminated in a major public rally at the Ukunda Showground.

The movement officially opened its new Kwale County office as part of a push to build county-level structures ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Addressing supporters in the rain, Sifuna declared that he will continue to build consensus among the opposition to ensure that they are united to send Ruto home in 2027. he said that divisions of the opposition leaders will guarantee Ruto a second term.

He warned against schemes to elbow local leaders out of the front lines, stressing that Kwale residents and local aspirants must drive the agenda on regional issues like water shortages and mineral exploitation. The Kwale tour marks the first public rallies after weeks without a large-scale county mobilisation exercise.

It has previously held gatherings in Mombasa and Taita Taveta as part of its plan to reach all 47 counties. The tour took place the same day the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) was holding a rally at Jacaranda Grounds in Nairobi's Embakasi East constituency.

Embakasi East MP Babu Owino urged Sifuna, Musyoka, DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i to agree on one presidential candidate, warning that time was running out.

“We are urging all opposition leaders to sit down and talk. We only have nine months to the General Election, and you should agree on one presidential challenger to President Ruto,” he said. “Sifuna, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i should come together now. United we stand, divided we fall.”

isii Senator Richard Onyonka said it was time for opposition leaders to lock themselves in a room and emerge with a single candidate to face Mr Ruto. The call was backed by Linda Mwananchi chairman Godfrey Osotsi and Secretary General Caroli Omondi.

Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, however, said Sifuna was best placed to challenge the President and asked Mr Gachagua and Mr Musyoka to back him.

“I want to urge Gachagua and Kalonzo to back Sifuna for the opposition to secure an easy win against Ruto. I want to assure you that there will be no rigging of the election,” he said.

Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza said Kenyans would reject Ruto at the ballot for failing to honour pledges, including those on women’s empowerment.

Sifuna accused the President of failing to protect the Constitution and the rights of Kenyans. “He has focused more on building houses and markets and failed to protect lives,” he said.

He also claimed the government had issued title deeds for smaller parcels than residents used to own, while land was stolen. He further alleged that the government was plotting to plunder mineral resources at Mrima Hill in Kwale and demanded that an agreement with American investors be made public.

World.title: Musonye to lead AFCON 2027 preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya with Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee chairperson Nicholas Musonye on October 29, 2026. [Jonah Onyango, Standard]

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya has unveiled the Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON PAMOJA 2027), with Nicholas Musonye appointed chairman to oversee Kenya’s preparations for the continental football tournament.

Musonye will be deputised by Hussein Mohammed, while Anthony Lung’aho Inzihuli, also known as Antony Emmanuel Inzahuli Lung’aho, will serve as head of the secretariat and chief executive officer.

The committee is tasked with coordinating Kenya’s preparations, including stadium renovations, infrastructure development, operational planning and logistical arrangements ahead of the tournament, which Kenya will co-host with Uganda and Tanzania.

Mvurya said the committee brings together individuals with experience, professional expertise and leadership to help deliver a successful competition that meets the expectations of football fans, participating teams and the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

“I have unveiled the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) PAMOJA 2027 LOC Standing Committee, entrusting its members with the national responsibility of coordinating and overseeing Kenya’s preparations towards delivering a world-class, memorable and successful continental football tournament,” Mvurya said.

He challenged members to move from planning to implementation, emphasising operational readiness, coordination, strategic partnerships, financial accountability and adherence to delivery timelines.

“With less than eight months to kick-off, I challenged the committee to move decisively from planning to execution,” he said.

Besides Musonye, Mohammed and Lung’aho Inzihuli, the listed committee members include Football Kenya Federation (FKF) Vice-President McDonald Mariga and FKF National Executive Committee representative Robert Macharia.

Other members named in the roster are Timothy Nabea, a former FKF NEC member; Gabriel Mghendi; Peter Kamau; Kerubo Momanyi; Benard Lagat; Collins Kalee; Caleb Amwayi; Ken Rungu; and Dan Shikanda, the former AFC Leopards chairperson.

The list also includes Charles Njagi, Thomas Karugu, Evelyn Cheluget, Miriam Chepkoech, Rodgers Chimega, Diana Injendi Manyengo and Collins Were.

The 38 committee members also comprises representation across functional areas, including finance, technical matters, refereeing, legal affairs and youth development.

The committee is expected to coordinate the different aspects of tournament preparation and ensure that the relevant agencies and stakeholders work towards agreed targets.

Kenya’s preparations also include the development of Talanta Sports City, officially known as the Raila Odinga International Stadium, which is expected to strengthen the country's capacity to host major international football matches.

Mvurya said the planned high-profile encounter between German giants FC Bayern München and Dutch powerhouse AFC Ajax, scheduled for January 5, 2027, would provide an opportunity to assess the country’s readiness.

The event is expected to test security arrangements, transport and logistics, crowd management, operational systems and the overall fan experience.

The CS also disclosed that representatives of the two European clubs had visited Kenya to assess its capacity to host the proposed fixture.

He said the government was adopting a whole-of-government approach, involving relevant agencies responsible for security, immigration, tourism, travel and hospitality.

AFCON 2027 is expected to attract thousands of supporters, officials and international visitors, creating opportunities for hotels, airlines, tour operators, transport businesses and other service providers.

The government is also positioning the tournament as an opportunity to promote tourism, attract investment, develop sporting infrastructure and inspire young footballers.

Mvurya said the committee carries the responsibility of delivering an event that would bring national pride while creating a lasting legacy for the country.

“I reaffirmed their mandate and reminded them that they carry the hopes and aspirations of over 55 million Kenyans to deliver a tournament that brings pride and joy to the country while securing a lasting legacy in sports development, tourism, investment and economic opportunities,” he said.
