World.title: Kikuyu PCEA church loses 2.7-acre illegally acquired land
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

The Presbyterian Church of East Africa (PCEA) has lost its 2.7-acre piece of land to a school.

This is after the Environment and Lands Court at Thika established that the land under the church's Ruguthi Women's Guild was a school playground and was illegally allocated.

Presiding Judge Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property, and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent.

According to her, the land had been reserved for use as a playground by Kanyiha, Lusigetti and Njumbi Primary Schools.

The verdict follows a case filed by the Law Society of Kenya, with the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) participating as an interested party.

In a statement on Monday, EACC's head of Corporate Affairs and Communication Stephen Karuga said the anti-graft agency presented evidence demonstrating that the land had been reserved for public use and therefore, any allocation to third parties was irregular. Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

"Our investigations established that the land was set aside in 1957 by the former County Council of Kiambu for use as a school playing field," Karuga said, adding, "the investigations further revealed that there was no letter of offer or acceptance, no evidence of payment of rent rates and no proof that the Women's Guild had paid any consideration to the council for the land."

According to Karuga, the judgement safeguards a vital public facility used by more than 1,300 pupils, ensuring that the playground remains available for learning, sports and recreation for the current and future generations.

As a result, the judge said the allocation, transfer and registration of the land LR. NO KARAI/350 and subsequent issuance of a title deed in 2001 was unprocedural, illegal, null and void.

"An order of Mandamus is hereby issued directing the 3rd respondent, the Land Registrar, Kiambu Chief Land Registrar, to forthwith cancel and revoke the Title Deed and all register entries in respect of the land issued to the 1st respondent on Dec 6, 2001, or at any subsequent date," the Judge said.

The judge further ordered that the said parcel of land be handed over to the Board of Management of the two schools and the Education Ministry.

"An order of permanent injunction is hereby issued restraining the 1st respondent, whether by herself, her church officials, agents, servants, assigns or anyone claiming through her, from entering into, taking possession of, fencing, depositing construction materials upon, transferring, charging, developing or in any other manner dealing or interfering with the land," she ordered.

World.title: World’s largest crypto exchange hit by suspected North Korean hack in world’s largest heist
World.content:
Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has suspended withdrawals after hackers broke into its digital wallets and stole six billion dollars in what appears to be the biggest crypto heist ever.

The exchange said Friday that it has begun recovering affected assets and was continuing to work with law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace additional funds.

An initial investigation suggested the hack went through an engineer’s laptop, “which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions,” Binance said late on Thursday. Blockchain evidence suggests the hack originated in North Korea, according to multiple crypto-tracing firms.

A team of cryptocurrency firms managed to freeze about three billion dollars of the stolen loot amid a frenetic battle with the hackers to find and control the digital money.

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said on X that the attack was not a “one-click” action, but rather a complex process. The investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual nor found evidence of any wallet private key leak.

Binance said it would cover all losses from the company’s funds and an emergency assets fund, adding “user funds are safe.” The crypto exchange said it had temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals to allow security checks to be completed and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds. The crypto exchange expects withdrawal services to resume by Sunday morning.

Crypto-tracing firm TRM Labs attributed the heist to an elite North Korean hacking unit “based on robust on and off-chain intelligence,” pointing out that “several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists.”

Pangolin Intelligence, another blockchain-tracking firm based in Singapore, said it also believed that a North Korean hacking unit was behind the heist.

“Analyzing the on-chain activity related to this hack and correlating with information gathered from previous known incidents” led to the attribution, said an analyst with Pangolin Intelligence, who did not want to be named for privacy reasons.

“I think the cat and mouse game has barely begun yet,” the Pangolin Intelligence analyst told CNN, adding that North Korea was likely poised to tap a network of money laundering organizations to try to cash out the stolen funds.

Chainalysis, another crypto-tracking company, said it was monitoring stolen funds “moving across multiple blockchains,” including bitcoin and ethereum. A Chainalysis spokesperson told CNN the firm had “high confidence” North Korea was behind the hack.

CNN has reached out to North Korea’s mission at the UN for comment. Pyongyang has previously denied hacking allegations.

In past investigations of big crypto hacks, the FBI has had an on-call team of analysts that worked to freeze some of the money.

The FBI said in a statement Friday that it is “aware of the incident and is engaged with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity, evaluate potential impacts, and coordinate appropriate investigative steps.”

A spokesperson for the US Secret Service, which also investigates cybercrime, said the agency’s “investigators are working around the clock with our private-sector partners, including Circle [the company behind the US dollar-backed stablecoin USDC], to identify, freeze, trace, and recover funds stolen from Binance on Thursday. We are also coordinating closely with the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia and law enforcement partners to identify the cyber criminals responsible and bring them to justice.”

If North Korea is proven to be the culprit, it would be little surprise to US law enforcement officials and private experts. North Korean hackers were blamed for the previous record-high crypto hack, when they allegedly stole $1.5 billion from Bybit, another major cryptocurrency exchange. In that case, the attackers stole an amount equal to a significant portion of North Korea’s reported annual gross domestic product in a matter of minutes.

North Korea’s formidable hacking teams are a key source of revenue for the nuclear-armed, sanctions-battered regime, according to current and former US and South Korean officials. Pyongyang-linked hackers have stolen billions of dollars from banks and cryptocurrency firms in the last several years, according to reports from the United Nations and private firms.

A 2023 CNN investigation spotlighted how the South Korean intelligence service worked with private crypto-tracking experts to seize about $1 million in cryptocurrency that North Koreans had stolen from a victim.

Unlike platforms for trading stocks, cryptocurrency exchanges tend to hold digital assets on their users’ behalf, which make them more vulnerable to hackers and theft, particularly given a lack of regulatory oversight within the relatively nascent industry.

Binance was co-founded in 2017 by Canadian national Changpeng Zhao, becoming the world’s largest crypto trading platform within a year of its launch.

However, Zhao stepped down in 2023 after pleading guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws in the US. He was sentenced to four months in federal prison, and was pardoned by President Donald Trump in October last year.

Zhao, who no longer manages the platform but remains its largest shareholder, said on X that he expects user funds to be fully covered by the exchange, pushing back against any suggestion to the contrary in a spat on X with Elon Musk.

Prices of bitcoin and ether, the most widely traded cryptocurrencies, plummeted following news of the Binance breach, but regained some losses to trade about 2-3% lower midday Friday in Hong Kong.

This story has been updated.

World.title: Coffee’s new status symbol is a machine without plastic
World.content:
New York —

For decades, it was the all the bells and whistles that was the selling point for a fancy coffee machine. Now, consumers are looking for what it lacks.

Growing concern over microplastics and sustainability is sparking a wave of plastic-free coffee pods and machines.

Coffee companies and appliance makers have released new machines and redesigned capsules in recent months. Keurig and Lavazza’s new pods ditch the traditional plastic cups for compostable coffee tablets. Caraway’s new machine uses traditional coffee grounds, but unlike a conventional drip machine, the stainless steel and glass machine doesn’t have plastic in its brew path.

More research is needed to determine the actual harm microplastics cause. But nine in 10 Americans are concerned about the effect of the miniscule plastic pieces on the planet and their bodies, according to a 2025 poll conducted by environmental group 5 Gyres; and studies have shown that pods shed microplastics.

The growth in pricey equipment and plastic-free pods fits a broader pattern of consumers trading up on home coffee equipment since the pandemic, said Peter Giuliano, senior advisor for research at Specialty Coffee Association.

The appeal and growth combine three things: health worries about microplastics, concern about plastic in the environment and the “feeling that metal and glass are more ‘luxury’ than plastic,” he told CNN.

New pods

In June, Lavazza introduced Tablì in the US, a $129 machine that uses only single-serve espresso tablets made with compressed ground coffee — a shift from its capsules made from plastic and aluminum.

The tablets are made by a custom technology that “compresses precisely dosed, ground, and tamped coffee into a solid, ready-to-use tab,” Lavazza said in a press release.

The Italian company says the new machine is its “largest investment yet” in the United States as it looks to double revenue to $1 billion by 2029, unlocking the stranglehold Keurig Dr. Pepper has on the coffee market.

Tablì is aimed at customers that want a sustainable alternative to the traditional pod, according to Daniele Foti, vice president of marketing for Lavazza North America.

The first release of the new Lavazza Tablì machine quickly sold out. Lavazza

“Consumers want to enjoy their coffee without the waste that usually comes with single-serve,” she told CNN.

Keurig, which ushered in the boom of plastics with their K-Cups back in the 1990s, launched in October a new line of compostable pods with a specially designed machine called the Alta. (The new pods don’t fit in the old machines.)

Called AltaRounds, the pods have been in development since 2020 in response to consumers’ shifting sustainability and health preferences.

The new pods represent a “significant reduction in plastic compared to our K-Cup pods,” said Phil Drapeau, senior vice president for Keurig’s Future Coffee Systems unit.

“We’ve heard clearly from customers that they want more sustainable products and specifically less plastic and plastic waste,” Drapeau told CNN. “Our data shows that drink variety, quality, and less plastic waste are high priorities across almost every group.”

Keurig has come under fire in the past over its pods, agreeing in 2022 to pay $10 million to settle a class-action lawsuit alleging it misled consumers by marketing its plastic K-Cups as recyclable, though it denied any wrongdoing.

But while the pods and the machine contain less plastic, they are considerably more expensive than a traditional Keurig machine. The Alta bundle that includes glassware and pods costs $499.

Melissa Valiant, director of communications for 5 Gyres, said that both the Lavazza and Keurig products still use plastic, which “ends up in a landfill, incinerator, or our environment after use, contributing to the planet’s growing plastic pollution crisis.”

New machine

Caraway has focused on developing a $495 coffee machine, released last month, that’s created entirely of stainless steel and glass, ensuring that no plastic touches the ground coffee. (Lavazza’s and Keurig’s machines contain some amounts of plastic.)

Developing a coffee machine with plastic-free brew path was challenging, according to Caraway CEO Jordan Nathan. That’s because the pricey glass and steel parts all need to be custom-made.

“We had to make the best coffee possible with no plastic on the interior with a full metal body, but also in a small (counter) footprint that had a single dial,” he told CNN.

Caraway’s new machine is sold out until January. Caraway

Concern over plastic in the kitchen and its affects on the endocrine system has been growing for the past few years, Nathan said, referencing a viral article that linked black plastics in the kitchen to alarming levels of toxic flame retardants.

Social media, influencers and various scientific studies have all fueled the conversation, with parents and other health-conscious shoppers avoiding plastic where they can, including in makeup, food and bedding. Caraway’s other plastic-free products, like cutting boards, have soared in sales over the past three years.

Coffee is a natural next step, Nathan added, because “you never want to heat plastic.”

Demand for Caraway’s new 10-cup coffee maker has been so strong that it’s sold out until January, forcing the company to ramp up production. Meanwhile, Keurig and Lavazza reported similar interest with both company’s product selling out quickly after their initial release.

That appetite for these pods and machines signals the industry will move toward more plastic-free alternatives, Nathan said.

“If you’re not doing it, you’re behind where the puck is moving,” he concluded.

World.title: Fake warnings of nuclear attack posted on hacked Russian and Ukrainian emergency apps
World.content:
Emergency warning apps in Russia and Ukraine were hacked overnight Sunday into Monday, according to authorities in both countries. It’s not clear whether the hacking of the apps is linked.

The apps warn the public of missile, drone and other threats.

But rather than spread panic, the fake messages appear to have had little impact on war-weary civilians – and instead began to generate some imaginative memes.

The messages posted on Ukraine’s public air raid app late on Sunday claimed that the capital Kyiv and other areas were subject to nuclear ⁠and chemical alerts as well as the threat of street combat.

Another fake message said Russia’s ⁠hypersonic Oreshnik missile had been deployed.

“The air alert app appears to have been subjected to enemy influence,” the Ukrainian air force said ‌on Telegram. “There ⁠is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel!”

The app had been recently updated to show the movement of drones in real time.

Stepan Tanasiychuk, who leads Ukraine’s Air Raid Alert project, said Monday it was gradually being restored, with new yellow and red alert levels currently available on the map.

“The team is taking additional measures to secure the app in order to prevent similar situations in the future, Tanasiychuk said on Instagram. “We realise how much unnecessary worry and inconvenience this has caused.”

In a separate event, ⁠the mobile app of Russia’s emergencies ministry – Emercom – was hit by a “massive cyberattack” early Monday that resulted in ⁠”the spread of false information to the public,” state news agency TASS quoted ⁠the ‌ministry as saying.

A fake alert was sent to 33 Russian regions, the ministry said.

The message claimed that “NUCLEAR WARHEADS ON P1-SUN DELIVERY SYSTEMS have been launched across ALL regions of Russia,” and added an expletive-laden warning.

“The app is currently operational, and its full functionality will be restored by the end of the day,” the emergencies ministry said later Monday. “EMERCOM specialists have analyzed the incident and identified the vulnerability exploited by the attacker.”

The ministry played down the significance of the incident, saying that alerts are distributed through regional and municipal systems such as sirens and loudspeakers, SMS messages and media broadcasts.

“All electronic resources belonging to our government agencies are under constant threat of cyberattacks,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Monday.

“As technologies, including AI, continue to evolve, the threat of cyberattacks is growing,” he said.

Few people appear to have fallen for the false messages. Some suggested it had undermined their trust in official warnings.

One Russian user said they had deleted the Emercom app “and I won’t be installing anything like that again. How can they leave apps like this vulnerable? It’s complete nonsense, of course, but what if it weren’t?”

Among comments on Instagram among Russian users of the app, one said the fake alert “was written in such a way that it’s impossible to believe it’s real.”

Another wrote: “It was hard to believe such nonsense. … How did (the Emergencies ministry) even let this happen.. let themselves get hacked.”

“You wake up, open Threads and see tons of posts like this,” another commented. “BUT THANKFULLY IT’S FAKE!”

Others joked that they had not even received the warning, with one writing: “This information was reserved for the chosen ones, don’t worry, you’re not important enough to be hacked.”

One resident of Kyiv responded to the alert about street fighting by posting: “Good thing our mayor is a boxer.”

Another social media post made up a long list of additional threats, including:

“Cat invasion – Cats are taking over the city. Hide the sausages. Pancake emergency – The city has run out of pancakes. Stay home. Clown attack – Clowns have been spotted in the city. Do not go outside without a mask. Alien invasion – UFOs are approaching Earth. Prepare for contact.”

World.title: Bitter spat between Poland’s pro-Europe PM and pro-Trump president erupts
World.content:
Poland is in the throes of a constitutional crisis as a battle over the future of the country’s highest court ignites another confrontation between the country’s president and prime minister.

The crisis came to a head on Friday when center-left Prime Minister Donald Tusk moved to remake Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal, whose chief justice was appointed by the previous government – the far-right Law and Justice party (PiS).

The judge, Bogdan Święczkowski, was suspended after refusing to allow a new member of the Tribunal, who had been nominated by Tusk and approved by the Polish parliament, from taking his seat. His deputy was also suspended.

The current crisis is the latest and possibly most serious chapter in a long-running dispute over the rule of law in Poland.

Tusk’s pro-European Civic Coalition was elected in 2023, after an election campaign in which he promised to restore the Tribunal’s independence. President Karol Nawrocki, who belongs to PiS, was elected separately last year. Poland’s president has little executive power but plays an important constitutional role.

Since then, deadlock has become crisis.

Nawrocki described Święczkowski’s removal as the chief judge as “a forcible takeover of a constitutional body.” On hearing the news, he abandoned a trip to Africa, ordered his aircraft to turn round and headed straight to the Tribunal.

Police block the entrance to the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw, Poland, preventing the entry of Tribunal President Bogdan Swieczkowski. Piotr Lapinski/NurPhoto/Getty Images

Nawrocki is a vocal supporter of US President Donald Trump, who said in September: “I endorsed him, and now he’s president and he’s doing a fantastic job.” Nawrocki has suggested a new US military base in Poland will be called “Fort Trump”.

During its eight years in power – until 2023 – PiS appointed several judges to seats on the Tribunal already filled by the previous government.

In 2021, the European Union warned that PiS’ actions posed a “systemic risk to the rule of law in Poland” in undermining the Tribunal’s independence. The European Commission froze $137 billion in EU funding for Poland over concerns about the independence of Polish judges.

The PiS-appointed judges remained in place after Tusk was elected and have obstructed his efforts to nominate new judges. Nawrocki has refused to swear in three of six judges nominated by ‌parliament, ‌while Swieczkowski declined to seat the judges chosen by parliament.

Last week, the latest judge to be approved by parliament – Maciej Berek – was prevented from taking his seat amid scuffles outside the Tribunal in Warsaw.

On Saturday, riot police reinforced security measures around the court in central Warsaw.

‘There is no other way,’ says Tusk

Tusk, who has spent much of his time as Prime Minister trying to unstitch the PiS changes to the judiciary, said his government was seeking to restore the rule of law.

“This process is difficult, at times even painful, ‌and requires decisive action. There is no other way,” he said on X Saturday.

In a televised speech Tusk said that “shouting, lies, and brawling cannot be the source of law in Poland, and they never will be.”

He insisted the Tribunal “will function as it should. Also, independently of me and in line with the constitution.”

Analysts say the crisis deepened when parliament approved the nomination of Berek, a close ally of Tusk.

It “contradicts the government’s pledge to depoliticise the Tribunal,” wrote Alberto Allemano, a professor of law at the HEC Paris Business School.

“The Friday suspension of the Tribunal’s president and vice-president, ordered by one judge and accompanied by a police presence outside the building, is not in itself a “coup”: the stated aim is to restore a lawfully functioning court. But restoring the rule of law must itself be done lawfully,” Allemano wrote on X.

At the same time, “If the Polish government is trying to repair an institution captured under PiS, its opposition is striving to retain some control through illegal means,” he added.

The US ambassador to Poland Tom Rose warned on Friday night that “thousands gathering outside the tribunal make an already dangerous situation more combustible. The last thing Poland needs is a confrontation that spirals into something far worse.”

“I hope everyone involved—government officials, law enforcement, and demonstrators alike, to take a deep breath, and don’t take any action that could provoke violence or further escalation,” Rose said on X.

But it’s unclear how the standoff between Tusk and Nawrocki can be resolved. Neither seems ready to compromise at a time when Poland faces growing security threats – with the war across the border in Ukraine, and sabotage attacks inside Poland that Tusk has attributed to Russia.

Tusk said Saturday of his opponents that it was “no coincidence that they find support among pro-Russian forces around the world.”

Fresh elections are due next year, with Poland’s constitutional order and its political direction – towards or away from deeper integration with Europe – high on the agenda.

World.title: Egypt, Qatar discuss boosting air traffic, civil aviation cooperation
World.content:
Minister of Civil Aviation Sameh al-Hefny underscored the importance of continued coordination among Arab countries in addressing regional challenges, particularly amid developments affecting civil aviation traffic.

He said cooperation and the pooling of efforts were essential to ensuring the safety and smooth flow of air transport.

Al-Hefny made the remarks during a meeting on Sunday, November 1, 2026, with Qatar’s Minister of Transport Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdullah bin Mohammed Al Thani, Qatar’s Ambassador to Egypt and Permanent Representative to the Arab League Sheikh Jassim bin Abdulrahman bin Mohammed Al Thani, and their accompanying delegation.

The meeting was attended by Civil Aviation Authority President Sameh Fawzy and Ministry of Civil Aviation Director General of International Relations Lamia Sami.

The talks were held within the framework of fraternal relations between Egypt and Qatar and the two countries’ keenness to strengthen cooperation in air transport.

They addressed ways to enhance coordination between the civil aviation authorities of both countries, mechanisms for supporting and developing air traffic between them, and the exchange of technical and operational expertise to improve the air transport system and enhance its efficiency, while opening up broader prospects for future cooperation.

Al-Hefny said Egyptian-Qatari relations were making continued progress, noting that civil aviation was a promising area for deepening cooperation between the two countries. He added that the ministry was keen to expand cooperation and had directed a study into the possibility of increasing air traffic between the two countries.

For his part, the Qatari minister voiced appreciation for the fraternal ties between Egypt and Qatar, affirming his country’s interest in strengthening cooperation with Egypt and its desire to increase air traffic between the two countries.

He said this would support growing travel, tourism and trade exchanges and enable both sides to make better use of their capabilities in air transport. He also expressed Qatar’s aspiration to continue coordination with the relevant Egyptian authorities to make further progress in areas of cooperation.

World.title: FM discusses regional stability with former European Council president
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty stressed the importance of intensifying efforts to restore regional calm and stability during his meeting with former European Council President and former Belgian Prime Minister Charles Michel.

Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Nader Zaki stated that the meeting saw the exchange of views on prominent regional and international issues.

Abdelatty stressed the importance of mediation efforts to contain tensions and avoid slipping into military confrontations that deteriorate regional security.

Abdelatty added that intensifying coordination between regional powers and European countries is imperative to avoid the negative repercussions of successive crises on the global economy especially food and energy security stressing the importance of ensuring freedom of navigation in main maritime corridors.

World.title: FM signs $1 billion financing agreement with World Bank
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation, and Expatriates Affairs Badr Abdelatty, who also serves as Egypt’s Governor to the World Bank and Alwaleed Alatabani, Regional Director at the World Bank, signed a financing agreement on Sunday, November 1, 2026, under Phase II of the Development Policy Financing (DPF) program.

The agreement is part of the “Building Resilience, Opportunity, and Wealth for Egypt’s Prosperity and Stability” program.

The signing ceremony was attended by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, Minister of Planning and Economic Development Ahmed Rostom, and Vice Minister of Finance Yasser Sobhi.

In his address during the ceremony, the Foreign Minister emphasized that the agreement forms part of Egypt’s broader efforts to expand cooperation with international and regional financial institutions.

He noted that mobilizing concessional development financing aims to bolster the Egyptian economy’s resilience and competitiveness, particularly amid ongoing economic challenges, geopolitical tensions, and their ripple effects on the global economy.

Abdelatty added that the deal reflects progress made in implementing economic and institutional reforms, particularly regarding the expansion of private sector participation, removal of investment barriers, and enhancement of public finance management efficiency.

He affirmed that these measures strengthen the economy’s capability to withstand external shocks while driving sustainable growth and the transition toward a green economy.

The World Bank Group’s Board of Executive Directors had approved $1 billion in total financing under the program in May 2026.

The approval highlights international confidence in Egypt’s ability to continue structural reforms, meet development goals, and execute policies designed to reinforce macroeconomic stability, boost competitiveness, and improve the business environment.

This financing represents the second tranche in a series of three Development Policy Financing (DPF) operations provided by the World Bank to Egypt on concessional terms.

Aligned with national development priorities and the economic reform agenda, the program focuses on key pillars, fostering private-sector-led job creation, improving public finance management and sustainability, protecting vulnerable groups, and supporting the green economy transition.

World.title: FM, AU representative discuss enhancing AU financial sustainability
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation, and Expatriates Affairs Badr Abdelatty met on Sunday, November 1, 2026, with Donald Kaberuka, the African Union High Representative for Financing of the Union and the Peace Fund, to discuss ways to enhance the AU’s financial sustainability and develop mechanisms for funding its programs and activities.

The meeting touched upon ongoing preparations for the Extraordinary Session of the AU Executive Council, featuring African foreign and finance ministers, focusing on union financing, which is scheduled to take place in Accra later this month.

Official Spokesperson for the Foreign Ministry Nader Zaki stated that Abdelatty emphasized the importance of boosting the AU’s financial resources, advancing self-financing mechanisms, and reducing reliance on external international partners.

He noted that such steps are essential to safeguarding African decision-making independence and ensuring sustainable funding for AU activities, particularly in peace, security, conflict prevention, dispute resolution, and peace support operations.

Abdelatty stressed that the core challenge lies not only in securing financial resources, but also in guaranteeing efficient management and optimal deployment of those funds.

The Foreign Minister underscored the need to push forward with reforming the African Union Commission, streamlining its structures and bodies, and implementing genuine structural reforms to optimize spending efficiency and eliminate redundant mandates.

This approach ensures that available resources are directed toward African priorities to achieve tangible results on the ground.

He expressed hope that the upcoming Extraordinary Session of the Executive Council will yield practical steps to reinforce financial discipline, good governance, and long-term financial sustainability within the African Union.

World.title: Liberia: Spotlight Initiative 2.0 Beneficiaries Highlight Project’s Impact in Bong, through Ministry of Gender
World.content:
BONG COUNTY, Gbelekpala — Beneficiaries of the Spotlight Initiative 2.0 in Gbelekpala, Bong County, have praised the programme for improving their literacy, business management knowledge, and vocational skills as the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection continues its county assessment tour.

By: Patience M. Jones,[email protected]

During the visit, women expressed excitement over the opportunity to meet the Minister of Gender, Children and Social Protection, Gbeme Horace-Kollie, face-to-face and discuss issues affecting their lives.



Community leaders also welcomed the Minister, describing her visit to their community as a rare and encouraging experience that demonstrated the government’s commitment to engaging directly with rural residents.

The visit provided beneficiaries with an opportunity to share their experiences and explain how the initiative is helping women and other community members acquire practical knowledge and skills to improve their livelihoods.

The project, titled Empowering Women to End Violence in Liberia, focuses on strengthening women’s knowledge and skills while promoting their economic empowerment.

Speaking during the visit, Boakia Yamah, Field Officer of the Spotlight Initiative 2.0 under the Hope Consortium in Bong County, said the project began with a community mapping exercise conducted in collaboration with local authorities.

According to Yamah, the exercise initially identified two communities for the programme, but the number of residents interested in participating exceeded expectations.

He explained that more than 350 people were reached during the initial engagement in Gbelekpai, leading to the selection of beneficiaries and the expansion of activities to additional communities.

Yamah said six people were selected to participate in a five-day training-of-trainers session at the Gbelekpai Women’s Centre. Those trained are now helping to facilitate lessons for other participants in their communities.

He explained that the project uses a seven-module learning approach designed to equip women with practical knowledge and skills that can improve their daily lives.

The modules cover literacy and numeracy, business education, savings and loan associations, vocational skills, and digital learning, among other areas.

Yamah said participants had progressed to the fifth module, which focuses on digital learning, while practical vocational training would begin once the necessary materials arrived.

He noted that the initiative also provides a second chance for women and other adults who missed the opportunity to acquire basic education earlier in life.

Through the programme, participants are learning to identify letters and numbers, write their names, sign documents, read simple sentences, and recognize common signs in public places, including hospitals.

The programme also introduces participants to business management, savings practices, and vocational training to help them strengthen their livelihoods and improve their economic independence.

To make the training more accessible, organizers established additional learning sessions in Bangasiri after discovering that some beneficiaries lived outside the initially selected communities.

Yamah said facilitators currently conduct training sessions on Fridays and Saturdays to accommodate participants from different communities.

Beneficiaries Celebrate Improved Literacy and Economic Skills

One of the beneficiaries, Mary L. Sonah, shared her experience since the project began in her community, describing the training as a life-changing opportunity.

Sonah said she previously did not know how to read or write but can now read, write, sign documents, and apply basic business management skills.

She described the opportunity to participate in women’s empowerment activities as a significant step forward for women in Bong County.

Another beneficiary, Gbanago Xarkpalwolo, praised the Government of Liberia and the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection for supporting the programme.

Xarkpalwolo said she had previously struggled with basic literacy but had now learned to read, write, identify numbers, sign documents, and manage a business through the Spotlight Initiative 2.0.

She expressed gratitude for the knowledge she had acquired and pledged to pass it on to her children and grandchildren.

“What I have learned, I am going to pass it down to my children and grandchildren. If I die today, I will die a happy person because of what the Ministry is doing for us,” she said.

She added that before participating in the programme, she had little knowledge of business management and savings.

“From the day we started the training, things have turned around for our good. All thanks to the Government and the Ministry of Gender for equipping us through this project,” she stated.

Government Ownership and Sustainability

During the visit, Minister Gbeme Horace-Kollie emphasized that the Spotlight Initiative 2.0 should be understood as a government-led programme supported by the European Union (EU), with funding channelled through the United Nations (UN).

The Minister stressed that the initiative should not be viewed as a programme belonging solely to the UN, noting that government ownership is essential to ensuring its continuation after external funding ends.

She explained that the government, the EU, and the UN work together to support the initiative, with the UN helping to channel funding and support implementation.

The Minister also underscored the importance of sustainability, urging project officers and community stakeholders to ensure that the programme’s activities continue beyond the current funding period.

She said the government’s involvement from the beginning was intended to encourage communities to take ownership of the programme and understand that its benefits should not end when the current project closes.

The Minister further highlighted plans to organize beneficiaries into Better Savings Groups to strengthen their savings practices and improve their access to financial opportunities.

Under the proposed arrangement, the 270 beneficiaries would be divided into three groups, with the relevant savings institutions registered to support their activities.

She said the initiative’s long-term success would depend on effective coordination, community participation, and the government’s commitment to sustaining the programme.

The Spotlight Initiative 2.0 seeks to support efforts to address violence against women while promoting women’s empowerment and expanding opportunities for women at the community level.

World.title: Liberia’s Maritime Commissioner Leads Delegation to 138th IMO Council Session in London
World.content:
MONROVIA – Liberia’s Maritime Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer of the Liberia Maritime Authority (LMA), Cllr. Neto Zarzar Lighe, Sr., is leading a high-level Liberian delegation to the 138th Session of the Council of the International Maritime Organization (IMO), being held in London, United Kingdom, from November 2–6, 2026.

The five-day session is expected to address critical issues affecting the global maritime industry, including maritime security, the protection of vital international shipping lanes, the safety and welfare of seafarers, freedom of navigation, and enhanced cooperation among IMO member states.

Commissioner Lighe is expected to present Liberia’s positions on these issues, reaffirming the country’s commitment to promoting safe, secure, sustainable, and efficient international shipping.



In a statement issued Sunday evening by Liberia’s Permanent Mission to the IMO, Commissioner Lighe emphasized that protecting international shipping lanes and ensuring the safety and security of seafarers remain key national priorities.

He specifically referenced reported unprovoked attacks involving Liberian-flagged vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz and the Black Sea, underscoring the need for stronger international action to protect commercial shipping and maritime personnel.

“The safety and protection of seafarers and the security of international shipping lanes are matters of critical national importance to Liberia. As a leading maritime nation, Liberia will continue to champion these principles and advocate for stronger international cooperation to safeguard global shipping,” Commissioner Lighe stated.

Liberia holds a Category A seat on the IMO Council and operates the world’s largest shipping registry by gross tonnage, positioning the country as a significant player in shaping international maritime policies and advancing global maritime governance.

The country’s participation in the 138th Council session provides an opportunity to advance its maritime interests while contributing to international efforts to strengthen maritime security, protect seafarers, and ensure the uninterrupted flow of global commerce.

World.title: Gov’t of Liberia, EU, Germany Launch €8.6 Million Aviation Safety Project At RIA
World.content:
Margibi County—The Government of Liberia, through the Liberia Airport Authority (LAA), in partnership with the European Union EU and the Federal Republic of Germany, has officially launched an €8.6 million aviation safety and infrastructure project aimed at transforming operations at Roberts International Airport RIA and strengthening Liberia’s position as a regional aviation hub.

By Yawah Y. Jaivey

The European Union is contributing €7.8 million, while the German government is providing €800,000.



The initiative is being implemented by the German Development Agency GIZ and seeks to modernize critical airport systems while ensuring compliance with international aviation safety standards established by the International Civil Aviation Organization ICAO.

Speaking at the launch ceremony over the weekend at Roberts International Airport, Gilles Matayron, Chargé d’Affaires of the EU Delegation to Liberia, described the initiative as more than an infrastructure development project.

“Roberts International Airport is much more than an airport. It is Liberia’s gateway to trade, investment, mobility, and regional cooperation. Safe and reliable air transport is essential for economic opportunity and business confidence. This project demonstrates that connectivity is not only about building infrastructure, but ensuring it is safe, resilient, and ready for the future,” he said.

Matayron emphasized that the investment directly addresses critical needs in airport lighting, emergency response, airside security, backup power supply and passenger screening systems.

He disclosed that the project will deliver major upgrades across Roberts International Airport, including the installation of modern runway and taxiway lighting systems, improvements to air traffic control, communications and navigation equipment and enhanced power supply and backup systems.

The initiative will also strengthen security screening and wildlife control measures while providing new firefighting vehicles, rescue equipment, ambulances and emergency medical response tools.

For his part, John Z. Buway, Acting Managing Director and Deputy Managing Director for Administration at the Liberia Airport Authority, speaking on behalf of the institution, said that despite the numerous challenges confronting Roberts International Airport, the LAA leadership continues to demonstrate commitment, strong collaboration, and technical expertise in improving airport operations.

“Despite the challenges before us, the Authority has continued to make practical steps to improve our operations and strengthen the security and safety of our airports,” he said.

Buway noted that among the Authority’s ongoing interventions are efforts to improve the airport’s firefighting and emergency response capabilities.

He disclosed that the LAA has procured new fire trucks to enhance its ability to respond adequately to aircraft incidents and other emergency situations.

“These investments demonstrate our determination to strengthen emergency preparedness to protect passengers, aircraft, airport workers, and critical infrastructure,” Buway stated.

The acting LAA managing director further revealed that the Authority’s leadership has continued to upgrade navigation systems, recognizing that reliable navigation equipment is essential to aircraft operations, particularly during periods of reduced visibility and challenging weather conditions.

He noted that these interventions form part of the Authority’s broader commitment to improving operational reliability and bringing airport facilities in line with modern international standards.

Buway also emphasized the importance of investing in human capacity through specialized training and professional development opportunities for aircraft technicians, operational staff and security personnel.

“We are working to ensure our staff have the knowledge, skills, and discipline required to manage the increasing demands of airport operations,” he said.

According to him, infrastructure development alone cannot guarantee aviation safety without competent personnel, effective operational procedures, and a strong institutional safety culture.

He further disclosed that the LAA leadership is intensifying efforts to strengthen operational readiness, address infrastructure deficiencies, improve emergency preparedness and advance corrective measures to meet international aviation safety and security requirements.

Buway said the newly launched project, titled “Action Enhancing Safety and Secure Air Connectivity at Roberts International Airport,” is therefore significant because it complements ongoing efforts by the Authority and provides an opportunity to address some of the airport’s longstanding challenges.

“For us at the Liberia Airport Authority, this project is more than an infrastructure intervention; it is an investment in public safety, public confidence, international connectivity, and the future of Liberia,” he said.

He pledged the Authority’s commitment to working with all development partners to ensure that the project delivers tangible, sustainable, and measurable results.

Buway also expressed gratitude, on behalf of the LAA leadership, to President Joseph Nyuma Boakai, the Government of Liberia, and development partners, including the European Union, the German government, and GIZ, for their continued support and interest in improving Liberia’s aviation sector.

“Together, let’s build an airport that is safer, more secure, more reliable, and better prepared to serve Liberia and the wider international community,” he urged.

Also speaking at the launch, Dr. Tobias Thiel, Director of GIZ African Union, described the initiative as a flagship investment under the European Union’s Global Gateway Strategy, which promotes sustainable and high-quality infrastructure development.

“This was a joint feat of strength. Together, with the support of the European Union, we are proud to bring this important infrastructure project to life,” Dr. Thiel said.

He disclosed that the project is currently in its inception phase, which runs through the end of November. During this period, technical feasibility studies will be conducted and implementation priorities finalized.

Dr. Thiel explained that the project will be implemented under three major pillars.

The first pillar focuses on safety and emergency equipment, including upgrades to airfield lighting, critical power systems, communications, wildlife management, and security screening. It will also provide modern firefighting vehicles, ambulances, and medical equipment.

The second pillar focuses on infrastructure rehabilitation and upgrading, including soil and geotechnical investigations, engineering designs and the rehabilitation of airport aprons, taxiways, perimeter fencing, and access-control systems.

The third pillar addresses operational capacity and maintenance systems, with emphasis on strengthening institutional capacity through airport-specific Standard Operating Procedures SOPs, specialized staff training, and emergency preparedness exercises.

Delivering the keynote address, Transport Minister Sirleaf Tyler praised the European Union and the German government for their support, describing the initiative as a significant investment in Liberia’s future.

“This investment represents a strong commitment to Liberia’s aviation safety, infrastructure development and economic transformation. Roberts International Airport is a strategic gateway for economic growth, international trade, tourism and national prosperity,” Minister Tyler stated.

He reaffirmed the Government of Liberia’s commitment to transparency, accountability and the development of a modern aviation sector that meets international standards.

According to the project framework, the EU-Germany-LAA partnership is expected to significantly improve operational safety at Roberts International Airport, particularly during nighttime operations and adverse weather conditions.

The investment is also expected to strengthen Liberia’s reputation as a safe, reliable, and competitive aviation destination in West Africa.

With modernized infrastructure, enhanced emergency response capabilities, and strengthened operational systems, the €8.6 million initiative represents a major step forward in Liberia’s efforts to develop a modern and internationally competitive aviation sector.

World.title: China Donates 304 Agricultural Machines to Liberia As President Boakai Challenges Officials to Deliver
World.content:
CAREYSBURG, Montserrado County –President Joseph Nyuma Boakai at a handover ceremony of 304 pieces of agricultural machinery donated by the Government and People of the People’s Republic of China to Liberia said although his administration was not responsible for the country’s past failures, it has an obligation to address existing challenges and ensure that citizens benefit from practical development initiatives.

By J.H. Webster Clayeh [email protected]

“We are not responsible for the past. Our promise is to ensure that you have them now,” the President said, emphasizing that Liberians deserve practical solutions rather than continued excuses.



He cautioned officials, particularly those at the Ministry of Agriculture, to prioritize agriculture as a major driver of national development and ensure that the donated equipment is made accessible to farmers across the country.

The Liberian leader urged the Ministry to ensure that the machinery is operated by qualified technicians, warning against establishing agricultural facilities in counties without the necessary equipment and trained personnel to make them functional.

He stressed that the value of development assistance should be measured by the results it produces rather than the ceremonies organized to receive it.

“When people give you gifts, the appreciation is not ceremonial; it is for them to see results,” President Boakai said.

President Boakai further cautioned the Ministry against limiting its engagements to theoretical discussions, urging officials to focus on practical interventions that would make agriculture more productive and viable.

“I have lived long enough to listen to plenty talk; but what I want to see is action,” he noted.

The President also reaffirmed Liberia’s commitment to strengthening its longstanding relationship with China, praising Beijing for its continued cooperation and support across several development sectors.

He expressed gratitude to Chinese President Xi Jinping and Ambassador Yin Chengwu, describing China as a dependable partner in Liberia’s development efforts.

China Reaffirms Support for Agricultural Development

Chinese Ambassador to Liberia Yin Chengwu reaffirmed his country’s commitment to supporting Liberia’s agricultural development, pledging continued cooperation in modernizing the sector, strengthening food security and improving farmers’ livelihoods.

Ambassador Yin said China remains prepared to work with Liberia in advancing agricultural mechanization, sharing technical expertise and providing capacity-building opportunities as the country seeks to transform its agricultural sector.

He described the handover as an important initiative through which both countries are working together to promote agricultural modernization and achieve shared development objectives.

The Chinese envoy emphasized that agriculture remains fundamental to national security and socioeconomic development, noting that improvements in the sector are directly connected to food security, public welfare, social stability and national growth.

He commended President Boakai for placing agriculture at the forefront of his administration’s ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development, describing the priority given to the sector as evidence of the Liberian leader’s commitment to agricultural transformation.

Ambassador Yin also acknowledged the Ministry of Agriculture for its role in advancing the country’s agricultural development, noting that recent efforts have contributed to addressing hunger, strengthening food security and promoting sustainable development.

Drawing from China’s development experience, Yin said his country had consistently prioritized agriculture, rural development and farmers’ welfare through its annual Central No. 1 Document.

He noted that China’s agricultural transformation and poverty-reduction efforts had helped lift more than 800 million people out of poverty, providing valuable lessons for developing countries seeking sustainable economic growth.

“As a partner, China is willing to enhance agricultural development and poverty reduction experience sharing and exchanges with Liberia,” he said.

Ministry Establishes 13 Mechanization Hubs

Meanwhile, Agriculture Minister Dr. J. Alexander Nuetah described the donation as a significant milestone in Liberia’s efforts to transform its agricultural sector, increase productivity and strengthen food security.

“The 304 agricultural machines that are handed over today represent more than a generous contribution.

They symbolize a shared commitment to modernizing Liberia’s agriculture, increasing productivity, strengthening food security, and creating economic opportunities for our people,” Minister Nuetah said.

He disclosed that the Ministry of Agriculture has established 13 mechanization hubs across Bong, Nimba, Lofa, Margibi, Montserrado and Bomi counties to make agricultural machinery services more accessible to farmers.

According to the Minister, the Ministry is working with the Public Procurement and Concessions Commission (PPCC) to develop a private-sector management arrangement aimed at ensuring the efficient operation of the facilities and providing affordable services to farmers.

Minister Nuetah also announced that 130 Liberians, mostly young people, have been selected for a 40-day training program in agricultural machinery operation and maintenance.

He said six Chinese specialists would provide technical support during the training, which is intended to equip beneficiaries with the skills required to operate and maintain the donated equipment.

The Minister noted that the initiative aligns with the National Agriculture Development Plan (2024–2030) and the government’s ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development.

He joined President Boakai in expressing gratitude to the Chinese Government for the donation, reaffirming the Ministry’s commitment to expanding mechanization hubs to the remaining nine counties.

Minister Nuetah said the expansion would begin in Southeastern Liberia to ensure that farmers across the country benefit from the government’s agricultural mechanization initiative.

China-Liberia Agricultural Cooperation Dates Back to 2006

Agricultural cooperation between Liberia and China dates back to 2006, when Beijing began providing significant assistance to Liberia’s agricultural sector.

Following Liberia’s civil conflict, China provided approximately US$1 million worth of agricultural tools and equipment to support efforts to revitalize local food production.

The assistance included farming tools, tractors, rice milling machines, water pumps and other agricultural supplies.

Another major milestone in the bilateral partnership was the establishment of the China-Aided Agricultural Technology Demonstration Center at the Central Agricultural Research Institute (CARI) in Suakoko, Bong County.

Following the signing of an agreement in March 2008, the nearly US$6 million facility was officially handed over in July 2010 to promote agricultural research, mechanization, technology transfer and capacity-building.

The partnership was further strengthened in June 2024 through a Memorandum of Understanding on Agricultural Cooperation, paving the way for expanded collaboration between the two countries.

The latest donation of 304 pieces of agricultural machinery represents another significant step in China’s support for Liberia’s agricultural modernization efforts.

World.title: Liberia: Nimba County Yellow Machine Overturns, Seriously Injuring Garr Gbeassila Town Chief Franklin Yeekpeh
World.content:
Rep. Nehker Gaye

GANTA, Nimba County — What began as a celebration of the arrival of Nimba County’s share of the government’s yellow machines turned tragic on Saturday, October 31 near the Ganta Checkpoint when the Town Chief of Garr Gbeassila, Franklin Yeekpeh was allegedly hit by Nimba County District Number 3 Representative Nehker Gaye’s vehicle.

By Franklin Doloquee / Nimba County

Garr Gbeassila Town is situated on the Ganta-Sanniquellie High Way in District #2 Nimba County.



The celebration began in Sokopa Town, located between Bong and Nimba Counties where a large number of Nimbaians gathered near the St. John River to receive the county’s share of the yellow machines.

The convoy later moved toward Ganta City.

According to reports, the incident occurred shortly before the convoy reached the Ganta Immigration Checkpoint.

Town Chief Yeekpeh, who had joined the celebration from Sokopa Town in Electoral District Number 8, was allegedly struck by Rep. Gaye’s vehicle near the Ganta Checkpoint.

Garr Gbeassila Town Chief Yeekpeh reportedly suffered a serious injury on his foot, which was later amputated following the incident.

Rep. Gaye told FrontPage Africa that after the incident, he took the town chief to the Ganta United Methodist Hospital for medical treatment.

He said he also contacted Nimba County Superintendent Kou Meapeah Gono to ensure that Yeekpeh receives proper care.

Rep. Gaye said his vehicle was behind vehicles carrying the Citizens Movement for Change (CMC) Political Leader and District Number 7 Representative Musa Bility when Town Chief Yeekpeh, who according to the lawmaker, was riding a motorbike, allegedly came from behind and hit his vehicle.

Rep. Gaye further alleged that after the incident, Nimba County Police Commander Lamie Mendee instructed him to take the victim to the hospital before any investigation or scene assessment could be conducted to determine who was at fault.

As of press time, Police in Nimba County had not impounded Rep. Gaye’s vehicle, which remained free.

Meanwhile, Police in Ganta report that more than 35 people have reportedly lost their lives in road accidents around Ganta and its surrounding areas within less than a year, as road accidents continue to occur in Nimba County.

World.title: Liberia’s Agricultural Transformation Gains Momentum as Ministry Receives Final Consignment of Chinese-Donated Machinery
World.content:
Monrovia — Liberia’s ambitious journey toward agricultural modernization and national food self-sufficiency has received another significant boost as the Ministry of Agriculture, under the leadership of Hon. Dr. J. Alexander Nuetah and his team of Deputy Ministers, receives the final consignment of agricultural machinery donated by the People’s Republic of China.

The shipment, comprising 42 containers of agricultural machinery, arrived at the Freeport of Monrovia, marking another important milestone in the government’s ongoing efforts to transform Liberia’s agricultural sector through mechanization, improved productivity, and strengthened international cooperation.

According to the Ministry, the first 15 containers are being moved from the Freeport today, while the remaining 27 containers are expected to be moved in the coming days.



Strengthening Liberia’s Agricultural Transformation

The arrival of the machinery represents another step in the Ministry’s broader efforts to transition Liberia’s agricultural sector from predominantly traditional farming practices toward more modern, productive, and commercially viable agricultural systems.

Under Minister Nuetah’s leadership, supported by his team of Deputy Ministers and technical professionals, the Ministry continues to pursue initiatives aimed at improving agricultural productivity, strengthening food security, supporting farmers, and reducing the country’s dependence on imported food.

The Chinese-donated machinery is expected to contribute to these objectives by strengthening the country’s agricultural mechanization capacity and supporting efforts to improve farming efficiency.

Leadership, Partnerships, and Progress

The latest consignment also highlights the importance of international partnerships in supporting Liberia’s agricultural development agenda.

The Government of China’s contribution reflects continued cooperation between Liberia and China in advancing agricultural development, technology transfer, and food production.

For Minister Nuetah and his leadership team, the arrival of the equipment represents an opportunity to translate international development cooperation into practical support for Liberia’s farming communities.

As the Ministry continues implementing its agricultural transformation agenda, attention will increasingly focus on ensuring that modern farming equipment becomes accessible to farmers and contributes meaningfully to increased domestic food production.

Advancing the Vision of a Food-Secure Liberia

Agriculture remains central to Liberia’s economic development, rural livelihoods, employment creation, and national food security.

The Ministry’s continued emphasis on mechanization is particularly important in addressing longstanding challenges associated with low agricultural productivity, limited access to modern farming equipment, and dependence on labour-intensive cultivation methods.

With the arrival of this final consignment, the Ministry has taken another important step toward strengthening the resources available to support agricultural modernization.

The milestone reinforces the Ministry of Agriculture’s commitment, under Minister J. Alexander Nuetah and his team of Deputy Ministers, to building a more productive, competitive, resilient, and food-secure Liberia.

As the machinery moves from the Freeport of Monrovia, the next critical phase will involve its deployment and effective utilization to support farmers and agricultural production across the country.

For Liberia, the arrival of these 42 containers represents more than the delivery of agricultural equipment; it signals another opportunity to turn the country’s agricultural potential into measurable progress toward national food self-sufficiency.

World.title: Liberia: River Gee Lawmaker Wuo Urges Probe Into Reported Disappearances, Death of Grebo Citizens
World.content:
River Gee County District #2 Representative Isaac B. Choloplay Wuo has expressed grave concern over reports of the disappearance of two Grebo citizens and the death of a Grebo elder in neighboring Grand Gedeh County, calling for prompt, thorough and impartial investigations.

By Bobby B. Addison, contributing writer

In a statement issued October 27, 2026, Rep. Wuo said the reported incidents warranted urgent attention from the relevant authorities, stressing the need to protect lives, uphold the rule of law and ensure that affected families receive credible answers.



According to reports, two Grebo citizens from River Gee County, identified as Godfrey Kligbeh and Ransford A. Zloryou, reportedly disappeared in May 2026, and their whereabouts remain unknown.

More recently, the body of Grebo elder Sam Geekor was discovered on October 23 in Kanneh Clan, Grand Gedeh County, after he was reportedly declared missing.

A coroner’s jury reportedly observed a cut mark on the left side of Geekor’s neck. However, the official cause and circumstances of his death have not been publicly established, and no suspects have been officially identified.

The incidents have heightened concerns within the Grebo community, prompting a traditional demonstration in Zwedru, Grand Gedeh County, on October 26, as residents called for answers.

Rep. Wuo acknowledged the community’s right to peacefully express its concerns but urged residents to remain calm, avoid speculation and allow the relevant institutions to establish the facts through a credible and impartial process.

He also extended condolences to Geekor’s family and other families affected by the reported incidents, emphasizing that every citizen is entitled to life, security and equal protection under the law.

“These incidents must receive the serious attention they warrant, and the families concerned deserve timely, credible information about the efforts being made to establish the truth,” Rep. Wuo stated.

The River Gee lawmaker called on the Grand Gedeh Legislative Caucus, relevant county authorities and the Ministry of Justice, through appropriate law enforcement agencies, to support prompt, thorough and impartial investigations into the reported disappearances and Geekor’s death.

He further urged authorities to pursue all lawful avenues to establish the whereabouts of the missing citizens and ensure that anyone against whom sufficient evidence is established is held accountable in accordance with Liberian law and due process.

Rep. Wuo also encouraged the responsible authorities to maintain open communication with affected families and community leaders, provide appropriate updates as investigations permit, and take lawful measures to protect residents against further harm.

The lawmaker cautioned against allowing the incidents to fuel ethnic prejudice, political interference or premature conclusions about responsibility.

He stressed that no individual or community should be blamed without credible evidence, while warning that no allegation should be dismissed without proper examination.

“Peaceful demands for answers should be met with seriousness, respect, and lawful action,” he said.

“The public deserves a responsible response, not speculation or silence. I urge the relevant authorities to investigate these matters without fear or favor, respect the rights of everyone involved, and pursue accountability wherever the evidence and law support it.

“Our shared responsibility is to protect human life, preserve peace, and ensure that the truth is established through due process,” Rep. Wuo added.

The Office of Representative Wuo reiterated its condolences to the family of Sam Geekor and all families affected by the reported incidents, urging the Grebo community and residents of Grand Gedeh County to remain peaceful while pressing for a transparent and credible response from the relevant institutions.

The lawmaker said the overriding concerns should be truth, lawful accountability, the protection of every citizen and justice through due process.

World.title: Importers, Consumers Decry Rising Prices, Scarcity; Blame Market Restrictions for Unfair Competition
World.content:
MONROVIA – Importers and consumers are raising concerns over reported shortages and rising wholesale prices of eggs on the Liberian market, calling on the government to open the market to more suppliers and ensure fair competition in the importation of the commodity.

They argue that restrictions on egg imports, coupled with declining local production, have created supply constraints, pushed up prices and placed additional financial pressure on petty traders and consumers.

The stakeholders are urging the government to facilitate the issuance of Import Permit Declarations (IPDs) and Import Notification Forms (INFs) to qualified local and foreign companies interested in importing eggs into Liberia.



On June 6, 2023, former President George Manneh Weah issued Executive Order 119, imposing surcharges on the importation of eggs and other commodities as part of measures to protect local production.

President Joseph Nyuma Boakai subsequently extended the protective measures through Executive Orders 135 and 156, issued in 2024 and 2025, respectively.

The President’s support for local poultry production gained further attention following his visit to the Liberian American Poultry (LAP) Farm in Bomi County in May 2025.

A report released by the International Finance Corporation in August 2026 identified LAP and Modern Mills of Liberia as businesses majority-owned by West African Premier Investment LLC (WAPI), an investment fund of the Siblani family.

The companies operate within a broader network of affiliated businesses, including United Commodities Incorporated (UCI), which has interests in trading, manufacturing and agriculture.

However, concerns are emerging over whether the government’s protective measures are creating an uneven competitive environment in the egg market, particularly for UCI, while limiting opportunities for other importers.

Rising Prices, Growing Hardship

A carton of eggs is reportedly being sold at UCI for approximately US$65, while some local stores and shops in Monrovia and surrounding communities are reportedly selling cartons to petty traders for between US$70 and US$75.

At the retail level, individual eggs are selling for between L$40 and L$50 in some areas.

For petty traders who depend on egg sales to support their families, the rising wholesale prices are cutting into already limited profit margins.

A Business Under Pressure

Sally Kiaweh, a mother of four who has sold eggs for more than a decade in Brewerville, outside Monrovia, says the rising cost of the commodity is making it increasingly difficult for her to sustain her business and provide for her family.

She said she now pays approximately US$70 for a carton of eggs, compared with about US$50 several years ago.

“I can buy one carton of eggs for US$70 from the store. This egg business is what helps me pay my children’s school fees and provide food for the family. It is also the business that pays my rent. But things are not fine now,” she said.

Kiaweh explained that despite the higher selling prices, her earnings have not improved because the cost of purchasing eggs has increased considerably.

She also said competition from established stores has further complicated business for sidewalk vendors, as some consumers prefer purchasing directly from shops.

According to her, the situation is worsened by losses associated with what she described as the fragile shells of some locally produced eggs.

Traders Complain of Losses

Kiaweh said some eggs crack or burst during boiling, resulting in significant financial losses for petty traders who purchase them in bulk.

“When I finish boiling the eggs, sometimes I cannot get anything out of them. The shells are very soft, and when you boil them with enough water, many of the eggs burst. The losses can be too much,” she said.

She added that traders sometimes lose more than half a carton, or even an entire carton, because of the problem.

Kiaweh further complained that when traders return damaged eggs to suppliers, they are often told that the damage is not the supplier’s responsibility.

“Sometimes, if you buy eggs by the carton here, they can burst. More than half or even the whole carton can burst. When we take them back to the sellers, they say it is not their fault, and we cannot do anything about it,” she added.

She attributed the rising prices partly to scarcity, increased demand and the limited number of suppliers serving the market.

Kiaweh called on the government to allow additional companies to import eggs, arguing that increased competition could improve supply and make the commodity more affordable.

She also maintained that imported eggs generally have stronger shells than some of the locally produced varieties currently available on the market.

Prince Dennis, 25, another petty trader, also urged the government to promote fairness and competition in the sector.

“When companies were bringing eggs into Liberia, we used to sell them for L$20 or L$25. I want the government to open the market. They should make it fair so people can compete with one another,” he said.

Petty traders are also complaining that some wholesalers fail to provide official receipts after selling them eggs, raising additional concerns about transparency in the distribution chain.

Importers Allege Restrictions

Beyond the concerns of petty traders, importers are alleging that they have been unable to obtain the necessary Import Notification Forms to bring eggs into the country.

They argue that UCI alone cannot adequately meet the growing demand for eggs across Liberia, particularly amid reports of declining local production.

“The demand for eggs now is so high, and one company alone cannot supply the whole market. Because of this, the commodity is becoming scarce,” an importer, who requested anonymity, said.

The importer warned that continued delays in granting qualified local and foreign businesses the necessary approvals to import eggs could further restrict supply and force consumers to pay higher prices.

The importers also alleged that UCI, which they described as the dominant supplier, requires some wholesale buyers to purchase other commodities, particularly sugar, before they can access eggs.

“If you are going to buy eggs from UCI now, they will tell you to buy other goods before they can serve you the eggs you came to purchase. The cost of a carton of eggs there is around US$60,” the importer alleged.

However, Wahab Dhaini, Managing Director of UCI, dismissed the allegations.

“All of this is not true. What do they mean we ran out of supplies?” Dhaini said.

Production Concerns

The concerns over supply have also drawn attention to the production capacity of the Liberian American Poultry Farm, which was expected to produce approximately 1,300 cartons of eggs daily.

However, production has reportedly declined in recent months, contributing to supply constraints in some urban and rural communities.

The reported decline has intensified calls for the government to reassess its import restrictions and consider whether existing protective measures are achieving their intended objectives without placing undue pressure on consumers and small-scale traders.

Calls for a Level Playing Field

Importers, petty traders and consumers are calling on the government to ensure that the issuance of IPDs and INFs for essential commodities is guided by transparency, fairness and the actual supply needs of the Liberian market.

They argue that protecting local industries should not come at the expense of competition, consumer welfare and the survival of small businesses.

While government policies aimed at encouraging domestic production are intended to strengthen local industries, stakeholders maintain that such measures must be accompanied by adequate production capacity and safeguards against market concentration.

They believe allowing more qualified businesses to participate in the importation and distribution of eggs could increase supply, encourage competitive pricing and reduce the burden on consumers.

For petty traders such as Kiaweh, the issue goes beyond business competition. It is about sustaining livelihoods, paying school fees and keeping food on the table.

World.title: President Hichilema calls for stronger partnerships in school feeding programme
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has called for stronger partnerships, investments as well as practical solutions to improve school meal programmes worldwide.

Mr Hichilema has also called for increased investment in research and innovation, stronger supply chains, climate-resilient approaches, clean cooking solutions and new financing mechanisms to support sustainable growth.

He has described Zambia’s successful school feeding programme as an investment in education, nutrition, health, agriculture and national development.

The President said this in a speech read on his behalf by Vice President, Mutale Nalumango, in Lusaka today at the official opening of the 2026 Global Child Nutrition Forum.

He noted that Zambia’s home-grown school meals programme now reaches more than 5.6 million learners across all 116 districts.

“The programme links schools with local agricultural production, aiming to provide meals while creating markets for local farmers and supporting community economies,” Mr Hichilema stated.

He further stated that despite the success, challenges persist that include climate shocks affecting food production, supply, gaps in school infrastructure, and limited access to clean cooking technologies.

The President, however, indicated that Zambia is working with nutrition experts, agricultural stakeholders and development partners to diversify school menus and improve their nutritional value across all the 116 districts in the country.

Ukraine First Lady, Olena Zelenska, says Zambia’s success in the School Feeding Programme is well acknowledged and must be a point of reference.

She stressed that the country’s commitment to turning its vision into action continues to impress the global stage.

Ms Zelenska, who attended the Forum virtually, noted that currently despite the war, Ukraine has about 3 million children benefiting from school meals and further called for equal opportunities in nutritional food for all children.

GCNF Executive Director, Arlene Mitchell, noted that despite world challenges, Zambia continues to thrive in School Meals Programme

Ms Mitchell urged participants from around the world to ensure that their actions and decisions on nutrition support the growth and health of children.

Earlier Minister of Education, Harry Kamboni, highlighted that the forum allows strengthening collaborations of sustainable school meals programmes worldwide.

He commended the government for positive reforms and policies such as the free education policy that have allowed millions of children to enroll in school.

The Global Child Nutrition Forum has attracted participants from Kenya, Cameroon, Ukraine, UAE, United Kingdom, the Republic of Yemen and Nigeria.

Others are from Togo, Sri Lanka, the Kingdom of Sweden, Malawi, Zimbabwe, South Africa and Sudan among others.
