He spoke on 2 November, after days of market chatter about Lara Resende’s ideas. The Selic is the rate that guides what banks charge each other overnight, and it shapes the price of mortgages, business loans and government debt.

Why a Rate-Cap Idea Unsettles Investors

A cap or freeze would mean elected officials, not the central bank, decide where rates sit. Since a 2021 law, the central bank has set monetary policy on its own, and its board members serve fixed terms.

Investors tend to treat that independence as a pillar of Brazil’s credibility. That is why even a denied rumour can move traders.

The idea did not come from nowhere. Lula has repeatedly criticised high rates, and Durigan has called the level of the Selic a bottleneck for the economy.

Where the Selic Stands in the Cycle

The central bank began the year with the Selic at 15.00%. It has since cut by a quarter point five times, most recently at its 16 September meeting, to 13.75%.

Brazil’s inflation target is 3%, with a tolerance band, so borrowing costs remain far above what the official goal would suggest. The next decision, on 4 November, is the first test of whether the cuts continue under political pressure.

What Prediction Markets Say

Bank of Brazil decision in November (Polymarket): no change 83.8%, a cut of 25 basis points (a quarter of a percentage point) 13.0%, a cut of 50 or more basis points 1.6%. About US$133,000 traded; read on 2 November at 7:43 p.m. ET. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

These prices are bets, not polls. Polymarket is a crypto-based exchange where users trade on event outcomes.

What It Did to Brazilian Assets

EWZ, the US-listed fund that tracks Brazilian stocks, slipped 0.9% to US$32.16 on Monday (RT market data). It has lost about 4% since closing at US$33.62 on 28 October.

The dollar-real exchange rate was near 5.44 reais per US dollar late on Monday, little changed on the day. One headline cannot explain these moves, and nothing in the data ties them to the rate-cap story alone.

What It Means for US Readers

A hold at 13.75% keeps Brazilian bonds paying one of the world’s highest yields, which favours dollar investors who lend in reais. Heavily indebted companies such as retailers and homebuilders stay under pressure for longer.

The denial matters most for ADR holders, meaning US-listed shares of Brazilian firms such as Itaú (a bank), Petrobras (an oil company) and Vale (a miner). A market that doubts central bank independence would demand a higher return and push prices down.

What Is Not Known

It is not clear whether Lara Resende’s ideas have any backing inside the presidential palace. Nor is it known whether Lula will raise the subject after the decision.

A confirmation would be a hold or a quarter-point cut announced on 4 November with a unanimous vote. A break would be any official language about administrative limits on rates.

World.content:
LA PAZ · Culture

Pacific opens the theatre run on 7 November, Ricardo Montaner sings on 8 and 9 November, and Pink Floyd Symphonic arrives on 21 November. The month, day by day.

La Paz at dusk, with the Illimani peak behind the city (file photo). Photo: Rio Times library

LA PAZ — This is your guide to things to do in La Paz in November 2026, from theatre and film-music nights to two big ballad concerts. The official rate is 6.96 bolivianos (Bs) to the US dollar, so Bs100 is about US$14; the market-data provider RT showed about 12 bolivianos to the dollar on 2 November, which reflects the gap between the official and street rates, so treat any dollar conversion as approximate.

Todos Santos (1 November) and Día de Difuntos (2 November) are the Bolivian days for honouring the dead, so they are already under way. Most of the month’s shows are weekend events at city theatres and the open-air venue in the Cancha Zapata area, a district of La Paz.

This guide lists only events that appeared on a retrievable listing with a date and venue. None of the pages we could open published ticket prices, so none are given here.

Saturday 7 to Monday 9 November: Theatre and Ballads

Saturday 7 to Sunday 8 November Pacific (theatre) Teatro Raúl Salmón de la Barra, a theatre in La Paz · Tickets via Superticket, a Bolivian ticket seller · Price not published The Hostelworld Events listing describes a stage production about survival, faith and resilience. The listing links to the Superticket page for tickets; showtimes were not stated.

Sunday 8 to Monday 9 November Ricardo Montaner Outdoor theatre, La Paz (venue not named in the listing) · Organiser: TodoTix, a Bolivian ticket seller · Price not published Montaner, the Venezuelan-Argentine singer known for romantic ballads, is listed for two nights. The listing does not name the venue or the start times, so confirm both on the TodoTix page before you buy.

Saturday 14 to Sunday 15 November: Film Music and Musical Theatre

Saturday 14 to Sunday 15 November Avengers Sinfónico Coral Cine Teatro 6 de Agosto, La Paz · Organiser page: tkl.arte.bo · Price not published More than 70 musicians and singers perform Marvel film scores, directed by Fredy Céspedes and Omar Eduardo Garbay, according to the listing. There is no screen; the show is purely orchestral and choral.

Sunday 15 November Epic: The Musical Auditorio Illimani, a concert hall in La Paz · Tickets via TodoTix · Price not published This is a stage musical retelling a classic story; the listing names no author. The listing gives no start time.

Saturday 21 to Saturday 28 November: Rock, Romance and Cinema

Saturday 21 November Pink Floyd Symphonic Auditorio Illimani, a concert hall in La Paz · Organiser page: Vamos Eventos, an events company · Price not published An orchestral take on Pink Floyd albums such as The Dark Side of the Moon and The Wall. Check the organiser page for the start time.

Saturday 21 to Sunday 22 November Álex Ubago Open-air theatre, Teatro al Aire Libre Jaime Laredo, Av. del Poeta, Cancha Zapata · Tickets via TodoTix The Spanish singer-songwriter is listed for 21 and 22 November. Songkick, a concert-listing site, names the Jaime Laredo theatre, which holds about 9,000 people, for the Saturday only, and Hostelworld lists both days, so the second night is less certain.

Saturday 28 November Your Name in Concert Cine 16 de Julio, La Paz · Organiser: Vamos Eventos · Price not published The film Your Name plays on a big screen while musicians perform its soundtrack live. The listing gives the venue as the “July 16th” cinema and no showtime.

Planning Your November in La Paz

La Paz sits at about 3,600 metres, so allow a day to adjust before a late night out, and carry a warm layer for open-air shows after dark. Bring cash as well as a card, since small venues and ticket points may not take foreign cards.

Buy tickets only from the seller named on each event, and check start times there, because several listings gave none. Dates here come from listing pages and may shift.

Not confirmed: we could not open the organiser pages themselves (TodoTix and Vamos Eventos blocked automated access), so venues and dates rest on Hostelworld Events and, for Álex Ubago, Songkick. We found no ticket prices. A Soy Luna farewell show and a Camila concert were also rumoured for La Paz, but we could not confirm either on any listing, and Songkick shows no Bolivian date for Camila, so both are left out.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there a big concert in La Paz in November 2026?

Ricardo Montaner is listed for 8 and 9 November and Álex Ubago for 21 and 22 November. Check the organiser’s page for venues and times.

Where can I see a show at Auditorio Illimani in November 2026?

Epic: The Musical is listed for Sunday 15 November and Pink Floyd Symphonic for Saturday 21 November, both at Auditorio Illimani.

Are there family-friendly events in La Paz this month?

Neither the Avengers Sinfónico Coral listing (14 and 15 November) nor the Epic: The Musical listing (15 November) states an age limit, so ask the organiser.

How much do tickets cost?

The listings we could open did not publish prices. The official exchange rate is 6.96 bolivianos per US dollar, so Bs100 is about US$14.

BRASÍLIA — This is your guide to things to do in Brasília in November 2026, from jazz and choro nights to a Brazilian comedy tour and a ballet. Prices are in reais (R$); at about 5.38 to the US dollar (market-data provider RT, 1 November), R$100 is roughly US$19.

The month has three national holidays: Monday 2 November (Finados, the Day of the Dead), Sunday 15 November (Proclamation of the Republic) and Friday 20 November (National Day of Zumbi and Black Consciousness). The federal government’s 2026 calendar lists Finados and Republic Day, and Law 14,759 of 2023 makes 20 November a national holiday.

This guide lists only events we could confirm on an organiser, venue or ticket-seller page. Ticket fees are added at checkout, and the seller (Bilheteria Digital) showed online sales as closed for every show below when we checked, with box-office sales listed for some, so check the seller’s page before you go.

First Half: Choro Club Nights

Friday 6 November, 20:30 Passo Largo, 15 years Clube do Choro Brasília (a music club for Brazilian instrumental music) · R$80 full, R$40 half (about US$15 and US$7) plus fee · Bilheteria Digital, a Brazilian ticket seller The instrumental trio of Marcus Moraes, Vavá Afiouni and Thiago Cunha marks its 15th anniversary with guest musicians. Half-price tickets require a 1 kg donation of non-perishable food.

Saturday 7 November, 20:30 Báu Revirado, a tribute to Raul Seixas Clube do Choro Brasília · R$70 full, R$35 half (about US$13 and US$7) plus fee · Bilheteria Digital A five-piece band formed in 2011 explores songs beyond the best-known hits of Raul Seixas, a Brazilian rock pioneer.

Tuesday 10 November, 20:30 Claire Michael Group: Tiger Note Clube do Choro Brasília · R$50 full, R$25 half (about US$9 and US$5) plus fee · Bilheteria Digital French saxophonist Claire Michael presents her album Tiger Note with a Franco-Brazilian quartet. The seller’s page showed online sales as closed when we checked.

Wednesday 11 November, 20:30 Tom Jobim: The Music That Enchanted the World Clube do Choro Brasília · R$100 full, R$50 half (about US$19 and US$9) plus fee · Bilheteria Digital Three singers and a piano, bass and drums trio perform songs by Tom Jobim, the composer of The Girl from Ipanema. The seller’s page showed online sales as closed when we checked.

Second Half: Dani Black, Corde Vita and a Comedy Tour

Saturday 21 November, 20:30 Dani Black: A City Called Myself Clube do Choro Brasília · R$100 and R$50 tiers (about US$19 and US$9) plus fee · Bilheteria Digital The singer-songwriter plays songs from his new album with a band. The seller’s page showed online sales as closed when we checked.

Sunday 22 November, 20:00 (doors 18:30) Corde Vita Auditório Planalto, Ulysses Centro de Convenções, Eixo Monumental (the central avenue) · half-price from R$154 (about US$29), full price R$308 to R$418 (about US$57 to US$78) · Bilheteria Digital The seller’s page gives no programme description, so we could not confirm what the show is. It lists a promotional discount of 45% in its current ticket batch. Children under 24 months enter free with a guardian.

Tuesday 24 November, 20:30 Nelson Faria and Sandro Haick: Talking Standards Clube do Choro Brasília · R$100 full, R$50 half (about US$19 and US$9) plus fee · Bilheteria Digital Two Brazilian guitarists play jazz standards and Brazilian classics from their two-volume album recorded in Italy.

Saturday 28 November, 20:30 The Magnetic Guitar of Haroldinho Mattos Clube do Choro Brasília · R$80 full, R$40 half (about US$15 and US$7) plus fee · Bilheteria Digital Guitarist Haroldinho Mattos leads a blues and jazz night with trumpet, saxophone, bass, drums and vocalists, directed by pianist Renato Vasconcellos. The seller’s page showed online sales as closed when we checked.

Sunday 29 November, 19:00 (doors 17:00) Tom Cavalcante and Nelson Freitas Ulysses Centro de Convenções, Eixo Monumental · R$50 to R$1,400+ depending on seat (about US$9 to US$260) · Bilheteria Digital The comedy show runs about 2.5 hours and is rated 14 and over. Half-price tickets are offered to students, teachers, seniors, people with disabilities and healthcare workers.

Monday 30 November and Tuesday 1 December, 20:00 Somos Todes Cinderelles Teatro Unip, a theatre run by the Unip university, SGAS 913, Asa Sul (a south-central district) · R$150 full, R$75 half (about US$28 and US$14) plus fee · Bilheteria Digital A ballet rated 14 and over, with doors at 19:00. The seller’s page showed online sales as closed when we checked.

Planning Your Brasília November

Most of the confirmed shows sit in two places: the Clube do Choro and the Ulysses convention centre on the Monumental Axis. Brasília is built for cars, so check taxi or ride-hailing options for late finishes.

Plan around the holidays: Monday 2 and Friday 20 November give long weekends, and Sunday 15 November falls on a Sunday. Venues may change hours on holidays, so confirm before you travel.

Not confirmed: we could not retrieve ticket pages for a Revelação and Xande de Pilares concert listed for Saturday 28 November, the Rock in Orla festival, the Michael Jackson tribute, the Quattor ballet and several other shows from earlier drafts, so they are not included. The page for Viva Minas on 13 November showed a conflicting year, so we left it out. Where a seller’s page shows sales as closed, ask the venue box office.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which national holidays fall in Brasília in November 2026?

Three: Monday 2 November (Finados), Sunday 15 November (Proclamation of the Republic) and Friday 20 November (Zumbi and Black Consciousness Day), under federal law and the government’s 2026 calendar.

Where can I hear live music in Brasília in November?

The Clube do Choro Brasília hosts shows on most weeks, including Passo Largo on 6 November, Tom Jobim songs on 11 November and Nelson Faria on 24 November. Check Bilheteria Digital for each date.

How much do tickets cost?

Club shows listed here run from R$25 (about US$5) half-price to R$100 (about US$19) full price, plus a fee. Larger shows such as Tom Cavalcante range from R$50 to R$1,400 (about US$9 to US$260).

What does half-price mean at the Clube do Choro?

Half-price tickets at several shows require a donation of 1 kg of non-perishable food, according to the seller’s pages. Students and other groups may also qualify at larger venues.

What is the biggest show of the month?

On the confirmed list, the largest venue is the Ulysses convention centre, which hosts Corde Vita on 22 November and Tom Cavalcante on 29 November. We did not rank events by audience size.

World.title: Lula Allies Press Central Bank for Rate Cut
World.content:
File photo: the Banco Central do Brasil towers in Brasília.

Brazil Economy · Interest Rates · Copom

Published Monday, 2 November, 5:45 p.m. ET · Source: public posts by Brazilian lawmakers, Finance Ministry statements, Banco Central do Brasil

Key Facts The pressure. Lula-allied lawmakers pressed for lower rates and attacked the market on Monday, 2 November, before the Copom decision.

The rate. The central bank’s benchmark Selic stands at 13.75% a year; Copom, the central bank’s rate committee, decides on Wednesday, 4 November.

The reply. Finance Minister Dario Durigan said a rate cap and a reserve sell-off are not being considered.

Prediction markets. Polymarket, a prediction market, puts “no change” at 84.5% and a quarter-point cut at 13.0% (2 November, 5:21 p.m. ET).

Brazil’s election is over, but the argument about money has just begun. Within days of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s runoff win, his allies are leaning on the central bank to cut rates, while investors are betting it will not.

The Copom, the central bank’s rate-setting committee, meets on 3 and 4 November, and its decision on the Selic, the policy rate that sets borrowing costs across Brazil’s economy, lands on Wednesday evening. The Selic is 13.75%, the level it reached on 16 September.

Three Lawmakers Go Public

Federal deputy Lindbergh Farias, a Rio de Janeiro member of Lula’s Workers’ Party (PT), posted on X (formerly Twitter) on Monday that the market is “doing politics and sabotaging our economy.” He wrote that the Selic should not be set by the “mood of the financial market” and pressed central bank president Gabriel Galípolo on rates.

Gleisi Hoffmann, a federal deputy and former PT president, wrote that “this financial market has authoritarianism in its DNA.” Zeca Dirceu, a PT deputy from Paraná, said rates must fall, but not “by force,” and that economic policy cannot be “hostage to the interests of those who earn a lot from high rates.”

Why the Tone Hardened

Before the runoff, forecasters expected the central bank to keep trimming the Selic. After Lula’s win, part of the market began to doubt that, worried about how the new government will handle the budget.

The stock market took the blow first: Brazil’s main index, the Ibovespa, lost about 18% in the week to Friday, its worst week since March 2020, and the real weakened to about 5.44 per dollar. The Selic peaked at 15% and has come down in quarter-point steps since March, to 13.75%.

Fewer expected cuts mean higher borrowing costs for longer, and that is what Lula’s allies are protesting.

A Famous Economist Enters the Debate

André Lara Resende, one of the architects of the 1994 Real Plan that ended Brazil’s hyperinflation, has proposed bringing the Selic down to about 7.5% over 12 months. He also wants a new fiscal and monetary council to set targets over four to five years.

Finance Minister Dario Durigan responded on Monday that proposals to cap interest rates or burn foreign-exchange reserves are not under evaluation. He also said no meeting between Lula and Lara Resende is scheduled.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, a crypto-based prediction market, traders put the chance that Copom leaves the Selic unchanged on Wednesday at 84.5%, against 13.0% for a 25-basis-point cut, with US$132,741 traded (2 November, 5:21 p.m. ET). For December, “no change” is at 68.0% and a quarter-point cut at 25.0%.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

The real closed Friday at about 5.44 per dollar, and the B3 stock exchange was shut on Monday for a holiday. The Ibovespa last closed at 167,921.80 on Friday, 30 October, down 0.75%.

Dollar investors in Brazilian stocks and in the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (EWZ) see the first market reaction when B3 reopens on Tuesday, a day before the decision. A hold keeps borrowing costs high for Brazilian companies, while a surprise cut would put fresh pressure on the real.

What Is Not Known

No one knows yet how Galípolo or the committee will answer the political pressure. The central bank is formally autonomous, and its statement after Wednesday’s decision will show whether it signals more cuts or a pause.

A hold at 13.75% would confirm the market’s doubts; a cut to 13.50% would side with the allies.

World.title: What to Do in Curitiba in November 2026
World.content:
CURITIBA · Culture

A free chefs’ summit on Sunday 8 November, Social Distortion on 15 November, ZZ Top on 20 November and a holiday Friday shape the month. The month, day by day.

The Oscar Niemeyer Museum in Curitiba (file photo).

CURITIBA — This is your guide to things to do in Curitiba in November 2026, the capital of Paraná state in southern Brazil. Prices are in reais (R$); at about 5.38 to the US dollar (market-data provider RT, 1 November), R$100 is roughly US$19.

The month brings a free public gastronomy event with star chefs, two rock concerts from veteran American bands and the start of the city’s Christmas season on Tuesday 24 November. Brazil has three national holidays in the month: All Souls’ Day (Finados) on Monday 2 November, Republic Day on Sunday 15 November and Black Consciousness Day on Friday 20 November.

Only the last creates a long weekend. This guide lists only events we could confirm with an organiser, ticket seller, venue or official source.

Times and prices can change, so check the seller’s page before you go.

Early November: Chefs Come to Town

Sunday 8 November, 10:00 to 16:00 Gastronomy, Identity and Transformation (public day of the Basque Culinary Center’s International Council Meeting) Memorial de Curitiba (a cultural complex in the historic centre) · free admission The Basque Culinary Center, a Spanish gastronomy school and research centre, holds its 16th International Council Meeting in Paraná for the first time. The council meets from 6 to 10 November, with programming in Curitiba and at Iguaçu National Park, and only Sunday is open to the public, with talks, panel debates and live cooking demonstrations led by local chef Manu Buffara.

Mid-November: Rock Night and a Republic Day Sunday

Sunday 15 November Proclamação da República (national holiday) Nationwide · marks the founding of the Brazilian republic in 1889 The holiday falls on a Sunday this year, so it adds no extra day off. Expect normal Sunday opening hours.

Sunday 15 November Social Distortion Live Curitiba, a concert hall, Rua Itajubá, 143 · tickets via 101 Tickets, a Brazilian ticket seller The Californian punk band returns to Brazil for the first time in 16 years, touring its album Born to Kill (May 2026). We could not confirm the start time or ticket prices.

Late November: A Holiday Friday and Christmas

Friday 20 November Dia da Consciência Negra (Black Consciousness Day, national holiday) Nationwide · a national holiday under Law 14,759 of 21 December 2023 The day honours Zumbi dos Palmares, a leader of resistance to slavery in colonial Brazil. It falls on a Friday, so most workers get a three-day weekend, and some shops and services may close.

Friday 20 November, doors 19:00, show 21:00 ZZ Top, The Big One! tour Igloo Super Hall, a concert venue at Rua Dino Bertoldi, 740, in the Tarumã district · standing R$390 to R$780 (about US$72 to US$145), standing premium R$490 to R$980 (about US$91 to US$182), VIP package R$1,285 to R$1,775 (about US$239 to US$330) · Uhuu, a Brazilian ticket seller The Texas blues-rock trio plays its first Brazilian dates in 16 years. Prices vary by half-price and solidarity tickets, and the opening act was not named in the listings we found.

Tuesday 24 November, evening Natal de Curitiba (Curitiba Christmas) opens In front of Teatro Guaíra (the city’s main theatre), Rua Conselheiro Laurindo · free The city’s Christmas season opens with a concert by singer Luiza Possi with a choir and orchestra. The programme runs for 44 days with more than 150 free attractions across the city, and the city has not yet published the start time.

From Tuesday 24 November to 6 January Casa do Natal O Boticário Rua XV de Novembro, near the Ferris wheel · free A small Christmas house is installed on the pedestrian street in the city centre.

Planning Your Curitiba November

Friday 20 November is the busiest day: the holiday, a long weekend and ZZ Top all land together. Book tickets and restaurants early.

Sunday 8 November suits visitors on a budget, since the public gastronomy day is free. Arrive early for a seat at the talks.

Not confirmed: we could not confirm start times for Social Distortion and the Christmas opening, ticket prices for Social Distortion, or whether the Memorial de Curitiba day needs registration. Other concerts reported for November, including Lobão, Cachorro Grande and Gilsons, were not confirmed on a seller’s page and are left out.

Frequently Asked Questions

Are there public holidays in Curitiba in November 2026?

Yes. Brazil has three national holidays in November: Finados (All Souls’ Day) on Monday 2 November, already past, Proclamação da República on Sunday 15 November and Black Consciousness Day on Friday 20 November. Only the Friday creates a long weekend.

Is there a free event in Curitiba in November 2026?

Yes. The public day of the Basque Culinary Center’s council meeting is on Sunday 8 November, 10:00 to 16:00, at Memorial de Curitiba, with free admission.

How much are ZZ Top tickets in Curitiba?

Standing tickets cost R$390 to R$780 (about US$72 to US$145) and the VIP package R$1,285 to R$1,775 (about US$239 to US$330). They are sold on Uhuu.

When does Christmas start in Curitiba?

The Natal de Curitiba programme opens on Tuesday 24 November in front of Teatro Guaíra and runs for 44 days with more than 150 free attractions.

World.title: What to Do in Montevideo in November 2026
World.content:
MONTEVIDEO · Culture

A baroque opera at Teatro Solís on 4 November, a run of arena concerts, and the Copa Libertadores final (South America’s top club-football decider) at Estadio Centenario on 28 November. The month, day by day.

The Rambla, Montevideo’s waterfront promenade (file photo).

MONTEVIDEO — This is the culture guide for things to do in Montevideo in November 2026, from 3 November on. Uruguay’s capital has a full month, with one big night at the arena almost every week.

We could not confirm ticket prices for most events, so this guide gives no peso amounts. For reference, the dollar traded at about 40.2 Uruguayan pesos (market-data provider RT, 2 November), so 1,000 pesos is roughly US$25.

This guide lists only events confirmed on an organiser, venue or tour page. Times and prices can change, so check the seller before you go.

4 and 5 November: Baroque Opera and Arena Pop

Wednesday 4 November, 19:30 Handel’s Theodora, Monteverdi Choir and English Baroque Soloists (a British choir and period-instrument orchestra) Teatro Solís, Ciudad Vieja (the historic centre) · tickets via the ensemble’s website · price not confirmed Conductor Christophe Rousset leads this staged oratorio, with soloists Marie Lys, Iestyn Davies and Alice Coote. Montevideo is one stop on a tour that runs from 2 to 19 November through South America, Europe and the UK.

Wednesday 4 November, 21:00 Jesse & Joy, Latam Tour Antel Arena, the city’s main indoor arena · Tickantel, the ticket service of Antel, Uruguay’s state telecom The Mexican pop duo plays the arena on the same night as Theodora. The Antel Arena calendar lists it as the Latam Tour.

Thursday 5 November, 21:00 Harlem Globetrotters, “100 años de diversión” Antel Arena · Tickantel The US exhibition basketball team brings its trick-shot show to Montevideo. It is a family-friendly night out.

13 to 22 November: Six Nights at the Arena

Friday 13 November, 21:00 Luciano Pereyra, Tour Te sigo amando Antel Arena · Tickantel The Argentine singer plays romantic ballads and folk-pop. The arena calendar says 21:00, so check Tickantel before you go.

Saturday 14 November, 21:00 Midachi, “La despedida” Antel Arena · Tickantel The arena lists this show as “The Farewell”. We could not confirm further details.

Tuesday 17 November, 21:00 Soy Luna, last-show tour Antel Arena · Tickantel Soy Luna is the Disney Latin America teen series about a roller-skating girl. The arena lists it as the “último show” of the tour.

Thursday 19 November, 21:00 El Plan de la Mariposa Antel Arena · Tickantel A well-known Uruguayan rock band returns to the arena.

Saturday 21 November, 21:00 Buenos Muchachos, “En realidad…” Antel Arena · Tickantel, all payment methods accepted The Uruguayan group plays a reunion show that Montevideo Portal, a local news site, describes as the way to close the year. Check the seller for the final start time.

Sunday 22 November, 21:00 Los Fatales, “30 años” Antel Arena · Tickantel Los Fatales, a Uruguayan band founded in 1996 and led by Fata Delgado, mark 30 years with a Sunday-night show.

26 to 28 November: Basketball and a Football Final

Thursday 26 November, 19:10 Uruguay v Canada, basketball World Cup qualifier Antel Arena · Tickantel Uruguay hosts Canada in the second round of qualifying for the 2027 World Cup in Qatar. The Antel Arena calendar lists it as window 5 of the qualifiers.

Saturday 28 November, time not yet announced Copa Libertadores final: Palmeiras v Estudiantes Estadio Centenario, Montevideo’s historic national stadium in Parque Batlle · ticket details to be announced The Libertadores is South America’s top club competition, and Palmeiras of Brazil face Estudiantes de La Plata of Argentina in one match. Expect heavy traffic and full hotels in the city that weekend.

Planning Your Montevideo November

The arena is the main stage: nine dated events in this guide fall at Antel Arena this month, and Tickantel sells for all of them. Buy through the seller named on each listing.

Saturday 28 November is the tightest day. The Libertadores final draws fans from Brazil and Argentina, and hotels may be short of rooms that weekend.

Book accommodation early.

Not confirmed: we could not verify the Dillom rap concert, a fado festival date at Sala Zitarrosa, a festival at Parque Roosevelt, Sodre’s November programme, a 4 en línea show on 28 November, or other Teatro Solís shows, so they are left out. We also could not confirm any public holiday for the rest of the month.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the biggest event in Montevideo in November 2026?

The Copa Libertadores final between Palmeiras and Estudiantes de La Plata at Estadio Centenario on Saturday 28 November. The kick-off time had not been announced in the reports we found.

Which international acts play Montevideo in November 2026?

Jesse & Joy on 4 November and the Harlem Globetrotters on 5 November, both at Antel Arena. The Monteverdi Choir performs Handel’s Theodora at Teatro Solís on 4 November.

Where do I buy tickets for Antel Arena shows?

Tickantel, listed as the seller on the Antel Arena calendar for every November event. Prices were not published on that calendar when we checked.

Can I watch Uruguay play basketball in Montevideo this month?

Yes. Uruguay hosts Canada at Antel Arena on Thursday 26 November at 19:10 in a World Cup qualifier.

World.title: Santiago Marathon 2027 in Chile on 16 May
World.content:
CHILE · SPORT

Key Facts What The Maratón de Santiago 2027, with a 42K marathon, a 21K half marathon and a 10K race.

When Sunday 16 May 2027. Kit pickup runs from Thursday 13 to Saturday 15 May 2027.

Where Santiago city streets, Chile. Kit pickup is at Estación Mapocho.

Tickets Registration has been open since Thursday 15 October 2026 at maratondesantiago.cl. Residents pay CLP 48,300 to 63,250 (about US$49 to US$64); non-residents pay about US$115 to US$138.

Good to know Resident foreigners pay the Chilean rate. Entries are personal and cannot be transferred.

Maratón de Santiago 2027 inscripción is open at maratondesantiago.cl for the 42K, 21K and 10K races through the streets of Santiago, Chile, on Sunday 16 May 2027.

Chilean and resident entries cost CLP 48,300 to CLP 63,250 (about US$49 to US$64), depending on distance. Non-resident foreigners pay roughly double, from about US$115 for the 10K to US$138 for the marathon, so check which rate applies to you in Chile before you pay.

What the race is

The Maratón de Santiago is Chile’s big city road race. It takes over the streets of the capital with three distances: the full 42K marathon, a 21K half marathon and a 10K.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Chile ranks 3rd of 14 with 63.6 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (86); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (38). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The organiser’s pre-sale coverage calls the 2027 edition the “Itaú Maratón de Santiago 2027”, with Banco Itaú as main sponsor. Places are limited.

The organiser’s quotas, as reported by The Clinic and Radio Agricultura, are 11,000 for the 42K, 16,000 for the 21K and 7,000 for the 10K.

Towers of central Santiago, Chile, with the Andes foothills behind. Photo: Rio Times library

Prices: the resident rate and the foreigner rate

Pricing is the main thing expats need to understand. The race has two tiers, and the cheaper one is not only for Chilean citizens.

Bloomberg Línea reports that the resident rate applies to Chileans and to foreigners who live in Chile. For residents, the 42K costs CLP 63,250 (about US$64).

The 21K costs CLP 58,650 (about US$60) and the 10K costs CLP 48,300 (about US$49). Those dollar figures use a rate of roughly CLP 982 to US$1, which is our own estimate from the press numbers, not an official rate.

Non-resident foreigners pay more. The press reports CLP 135,462 for the 42K (US$138), CLP 124,174 for the 21K (about US$126.50) and CLP 112,885 for the 10K (US$115).

That is roughly 2.1 to 2.3 times the resident price. All prices include a 15% service fee.

Even at the higher rate, Bloomberg Línea notes that the US$138 marathon fee sits well below big overseas races such as New York, London or Berlin. We have not checked those comparison figures against the other races’ own sites.

How to register, step by step

General sale opened at 12:00 on Thursday 15 October 2026 at maratondesantiago.cl. Bloomberg Línea also reports a pre-sale on 14 October for Itaú customers, though we could not confirm it on the official site.

The official site has separate registration links for Chileans and residents, and for foreigners. Pick the one that matches your status, because the price depends on it.

The form asks for your full name, ID or RUN, birthdate, sex, nationality, address, phone, email, emergency contact and estimated finish time. A race-time certificate is needed when applicable, according to Radio Agricultura.

We could not find how the organiser defines “resident” or what proof it asks for, such as a Chilean ID card or visa. Read the official rules before you pay, and write to the organiser if you are unsure.

The organiser has not published a sales closing date; places are limited by quota.

Rules, cut-offs and age limits

Runners must be 18 or older for the 42K and 21K. The 10K is open from age 16, and under-18s need parental authorisation.

The official cut-off times are 6 hours for the marathon, 3 hours for the half marathon and 2 hours for the 10K. Be realistic about your pace when you enter your estimated finish time.

Your entry is personal. The site says “Tu inscripción no se vende, cede ni transfiere”, meaning it cannot be sold, ceded or transferred.

If you might not make it, do not count on passing your bib to a friend.

Race weekend in Santiago

Kit pickup runs from Thursday 13 to Saturday 15 May 2027 at Estación Mapocho, the former railway station in central Santiago that now serves as a cultural and events venue. Bring your ID and your registration confirmation.

Past editions started on the Alameda in front of the Palacio de La Moneda, the presidential palace in the city centre. Start times for 2027 have not been confirmed.

The 2027 start point and route have not been confirmed either, so confirm them with the organiser at maratondesantiago.cl closer to the date. Book your Santiago accommodation early, ideally near the centre, so you can reach the start without relying on traffic.

Late May is autumn in Chile, so check the forecast the week before and pack for a cool morning.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the Santiago Marathon 2027 and where do I register?

The race is on Sunday 16 May 2027 in Santiago, Chile. Registration has been open since Thursday 15 October 2026 at maratondesantiago.cl.

How much does it cost for a foreigner living in Chile?

Resident foreigners pay the Chilean rate: CLP 63,250 (about US$64) for the 42K, CLP 58,650 (about US$60) for the 21K and CLP 48,300 (about US$49) for the 10K. Check the official rules for how residency is proved.

How much do tourists pay?

Non-resident foreigners pay about US$138 for the 42K, US$126.50 for the 21K and US$115 for the 10K, as reported by the press. All prices include a 15% service fee.

Can I transfer my entry to someone else?

No. The official site says entries cannot be sold, ceded or transferred.

World.title: Mexico’s Mixquic Cemetery Lights Up Tonight
World.content:
Candles on the graves of San Andrés Mixquic's cemetery, seen from the roof of the San Andrés Apóstol church, pictured on 2 November 2009. Photo: Thelmadatter / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

Mexico City ends its Day of the Dead season tonight with a sea of candles, as families light the graves of their dead at the San Andrés Mixquic cemetery in the borough of Tláhuac. The ceremony, called the Alumbrada, begins at 8 p.m. local time (9 p.m. Eastern Time, ET) on Monday, 2 November 2026.

It closes the Mixquic programme that began on 29 October, and we follow the wider festival in our Day of the Dead live hub. Mexico City is on Central Standard Time (UTC−6), which is six hours behind London and one hour behind New York after US clocks went back on 1 November.

Mixquic Lights Its Cemetery Tonight

The Alumbrada, which means "the lighting", takes place in the Mixquic cemetery in south-eastern Mexico City. Graves there are decorated with marigolds, votive candles and offerings, and families gather around them through the night.

The official programme ran from 29 October to 2 November. It began with tomb cleaning on 29 October and continued on 31 October with the "Rodada del Mictlán", a bike ride.

Pre-Hispanic ball-game exhibitions run from 31 October through 2 November. The programme ends with vigils on 1 and 2 November.

The start time of 8 p.m. comes from the official programme, and we did not reach the Tláhuac borough's own page to confirm it.

Why the Zócalo Catrina Is Still Drawing Crowds

Alfredo Arista, an adjudicator for Guinness World Records, validated the giant Catrina at 33.41 metres (about 110 feet) on 29 October 2026. A Catrina is the elegant skeleton lady that has become a symbol of the holiday, and this one stands in the Zócalo, Mexico City's main square.

The figure is the centrepiece of the Monumental Offering, a public altar dedicated to the engraver José Guadalupe Posada, whose satirical skeleton print Calavera Garbancera inspired the Catrina. It stays on view through Monday, 2 November, and no closing time has been published.

It has fibreglass bones, a steel frame, internal LED lighting and a 27-metre dress embroidered in the Tenango style, a Mexican hand-embroidery tradition, with marigolds and hummingbirds. The Taller de Arte Xibalbá, an art workshop led by director Carlos Báez, built it.

More than 100 people took part, among them artists, engineers, architects, blacksmiths and painters. The square also holds marigold fields and an exhibition called "Ajolotes en el corazón".

What It Means for US Readers

The Alumbrada starts at 9 p.m. ET on Monday, 2 November. We did not verify any livestream or US broadcast of the ceremony.

Mexico City authorities and the city Culture Secretariat are the sources to watch for official figures. Local time is six hours behind London and one hour behind New York.

What Is Not Known

No official attendance or incident figures for 1 and 2 November have been published yet. The Catrina's closing time on 2 November has not been stated.

No poll or prediction market applies to this topic. We will report the figures here once city authorities release them.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the Mixquic Alumbrada?

It is set for Monday, 2 November 2026, from 8 p.m. in Mexico City, which is 9 p.m. ET. The time comes from the official programme.

Where does the Alumbrada take place?

It takes place at the San Andrés Mixquic cemetery in Tláhuac, a borough of Mexico City. Families light candles on the graves of their dead.

How tall is the record Catrina in the Zócalo?

Guinness World Records validated it at 33.41 metres, about 110 feet, on 29 October 2026. It stays on view through Monday, 2 November.

World.title: Your 2027 Marchamo Is Due and the New Sticker Can Only Go On Once
World.content:
You can now check and pay your 2027 marchamo, Costa Rica’s mandatory annual vehicle fee, and you have until Dec. 31 to do it without surcharges. This year the payment comes with something new for your windshield: a ¢1,200 electronic sticker designed to last up to 10 years, and one you can only stick on once.

The National Insurance Institute (INS) opened collection today. This year 2,090,602 vehicle owners have to pay, and INS expects to collect about ¢365 billion (roughly $800 million). By 10:30 a.m. on the first day, the system had logged 1.37 million queries and 1,256 payments.

Before you pay, look closely at the total. On Monday, the INS online calculator added Más Protección, an optional accident insurance policy costing ¢11,900 (about $26), to the amount it showed as the total to pay. The box was ticked by default, and you had to untick it on the next screen to avoid buying it.

After complaints from drivers and a call from the general superintendent of insurance, INS said it would stop pre-selecting the policy from midnight Monday. If you looked up your amount on the first day, the figure you saw may have been higher than what you owe. The optional policy is still available if you want it.

The new 10-year digital sticker covers cars, buses, trucks and other vehicles with a windshield. Motorcycles and special equipment keep the traditional sticker for now. A motorcycle sticker sits outside, exposed to sun, rain and mud, so INS will test the technology on motorcycles in a pilot first.

You receive the sticker when you pay at an INS branch or one of the 2,407 authorized collection points around the country. Its ¢1,200 cost is already included in your marchamo total. In later years you only pay the fee, and the same sticker stays on the glass.

Put it on carefully, because you get one try. Clean the glass, then place the sticker on the inside of the windshield, at the top and in the center. The chip inside is destroyed if you peel it off, a security feature meant to stop stickers from being stolen or moved to another vehicle. If you later replace the windshield or the sticker is damaged, you will have to request a new one through INS.

If you own more than one vehicle, check before you stick. INS President Gabriela Chacón said owners should confirm in the INS Móvil app that the code on each sticker matches the right plate. INS General Manager José Arévalo said the code is tied to your vehicle and should only be shared with someone you trust.

The paper receipt is gone, too. Your proof of payment, the derecho de circulación, arrives by email at the address you give when you pay. You can also download it as a PDF from grupoins.com or the INS Móvil app, or save it to your phone’s digital wallet. If you don’t use email, INS suggested giving a relative’s address and printing the document to keep in the car. Either way, keep a copy handy in case a traffic officer asks for it.

You don’t need to scrape off your 2026 sticker. The Public Works and Transport Ministry (MOPT) said leaving it in place will not get you fined. MOPT expects Traffic Police to switch to new devices in 2028 that can check whether a vehicle is up to date just by reading the sticker. The sticker is not a tracker. It uses passive UHF radio-frequency identification, and INS said it has no battery and no GPS, stores no record of where you drive and responds only when an authorized reader scans it at close range.

To see what you owe, go to marchamo.grupoins.com, choose your vehicle type and enter your plate number without spaces or dashes. You can also call 800-MARCHAMO (800-6272-4266), message INS on WhatsApp at 2287-6100 or use the INS Móvil app. You can pay on grupoins.com, in the app, by phone at 800-TeleINS (800-835-3467), at INS offices or at any authorized collection point.

Your total covers more than the fee itself. Any unpaid municipal parking-meter charges are added, with interest. Property tax makes up about 59% of the marchamo, and the mandatory vehicle insurance about 27%.

That insurance, known as SOA, rose ¢1,643 for private cars, ¢4,487 for motorcycles and ¢10,048 for buses compared with last year. It fell ¢1,672 for light cargo vehicles, ¢834 for heavy cargo and about ¢5,500 for taxis. Sidney Viales, who heads mandatory insurance at INS, said traffic accidents drove this year’s rates. INS said motorcycle riders account for 65% to 70% of the people injured in crashes.

The deadline is Dec. 31. From Jan. 1, unpaid vehicles face surcharges, and driving without a current marchamo can bring fines under the Traffic Law.

World.title: Costa Rica Now Has Its Own Wine Grape After a 50-Year Quest
World.content:
Costa Rica now has a wine grape of its own. Peppevidor, a hybrid bred to grow in tropical heat, was certified as a new plant variety by the National Seed Office (Oficina Nacional de Semillas), capping roughly half a century of work by Italian-born grape breeder Virgilio Vidor. Vidor, 78, says it is the first wine grape developed in Costa Rica to receive official registration. He crossed a wild grape native to Costa Rica with a European wine grape and named the result after his late brother, Giuseppe.

Peppe is the familiar Italian short form of that name. The official notice of his application, filed with the seed office in June 2024, lists the cross as Vitis tiliifolia, a wild grape that grows across Central America, with Vitis vinifera, the species behind nearly all of the world’s wine. That pairing matters because European grapes struggle here for two reasons. They need a cool season to rest and then bud evenly, which the tropics do not provide.

And in warm climates they are vulnerable to Xylella fastidiosa, a bacterium that clogs the vine’s water-carrying tissue and causes what growers call Pierce’s disease. Peppevidor grows without a cold season and resists the bacterium, according to Vidor. He said the grape is at home in Costa Rica because part of its ancestry comes from the local wild vine, describing it as functionally rather than perfectly tropical, since its Costa Rican and Italian genes are mixed.

Vidor said the certification confirms the plant is a new variety, distinct from all others. He added that he was delighted Costa Rica now has the grape, which he said belongs to Costa Ricans. Tasters who have tried wine made from Peppevidor describe it as light red in color, with notes of coffee that they say capture something of Costa Rica.

The Costa Rica Institute of Technology (TEC) carried out the technical examination needed to register Peppevidor as a new variety. Carlos Alvarado, director of the TEC’s Centro de Vinculación, said it was the first time the university had conducted an examination of this kind. He said the experience will allow it to take on more in the future and will be passed on to its students.

Vidor arrived from Italy in December 1972, at 24, with his parents and younger brother. His father’s family came from the Prosecco wine country near Treviso, and the Vidors settled on a farm near Playa Panamá, in the northwestern province of Guanacaste, where they began planting vines.

In the 1970s the farm became the base of a tropical viticulture project financed by the Costa Rican government and the U.S. Agency for International Development, with Vidor as its director. When disease began attacking the vines, he turned to hybridization rather than abandon the effort, searching for a grape that could withstand Guanacaste’s long dry season and tropical pests.

Breeding a grape is slow work. Vidor has said a new hybrid needs at least a decade of trials before its viability can be confirmed or ruled out. The grapes long grown in Costa Rica, such as Isabella, are hybrids developed elsewhere, and until now none bred in the country had been officially registered, according to Vidor.

His farm still works as an experimental vineyard, where he tests hundreds of hybrids. Italy has named him a Commendatore of the Order of Merit of the Italian Republic, one of its highest honors, for his rural development work in Central America and his research on tropical viticulture.

Wine has always been a niche product in Costa Rica, and our few vineyards have relied on varieties bred for other climates. A grape bred here, from a native vine, gives that small scene something it has never had before, a variety that started in Costa Rica’s own forests.

World.title: Prosecutors Find No Costa Rican Victims in Epstein Files Investigation
World.content:
Costa Rican prosecutors have asked a court to dismiss their investigation into possible child sexual abuse linked to mentions of Costa Rica in the Jeffrey Epstein files, after finding no Costa Rican victims and no evidence that any crime took place here. The gender crimes unit of the Public Prosecutor’s Office filed the request with the Criminal Court of San José, which must now decide whether to close the case. The investigation was opened in February on the instructions of Attorney General Carlo Díaz.

Prosecutors worked on the case with the gender violence section of the Judicial Investigation Agency (OIJ) and with international agencies, including the FBI, according to the request. Investigators were unable to identify any Costa Rican minors among the victims of Epstein’s network. They also could not establish that the criminal conduct occurred in Costa Rica,or link any specific person to an offense under Costa Rican jurisdiction.

The police report found multiple references to Costa Rica in the files released by the US Department of Justice, but no specific information or objective evidence to support the theory that prompted the case. Prosecutors described the investigation as having started from a generic suspicion based on press reports that could not be corroborated with material evidence.

The case was filed against unknown persons and no suspect was ever named. When it opened, the attorney general said media reports had placed Costa Rica among the possible countries where such crimes were committed. He also noted that a 2019 legal reform could keep older cases from expiring, since victims can now file complaints up to 25 years after reaching adulthood.

Costa Rica appears hundreds of times in the Epstein files, across emails, phone records and court documents. Many of those references involve child sex tourism, including records from an FBI undercover operation that used a fake travel agency called Costa Rica Taboo Vacations.

Other references concern trips to Costa Rica by people in Epstein’s circle, including his former partner Ghislaine Maxwell. The court has not yet ruled on the request to dismiss the case.

World.title: Gota a Gota Extortion Cases Keep Climbing in Costa Rica, OIJ Data Show
World.content:
Extortion complaints linked to informal gota a gota loans in Costa Rica reached a record 935 in 2025, more than double the 427 filed in 2022, according to data from the Judicial Investigation Agency (OIJ). The trend has not eased this year. The OIJ’s criminal analysis unit recorded 840 complaints from January through Oct. 15, 2026, leaving 95 cases short of last year’s total with two and a half months still to go.

Michael Soto, the OIJ’s interim director, described gota a gota lending as a well-established criminal phenomenon. He also said that people file few complaints, which means the official figures likely understate the scale of the problem. The loans are typically offered without paperwork, guarantors or credit checks, often to people who need cash quickly for medical costs, utility bills or food. Lenders collect payments every day and charge interest that borrowers frequently cannot pay down, turning a small loan into a debt with no clear end.

When payments fall short, collectors turn to intimidation, according to the OIJ. Victims have reported threats at their homes, harassing phone calls and, in some cases, physical attacks. Authorities say the groups also pursue relatives when a borrower cannot pay. Investigators link the organized groups behind the loans to drug trafficking and money laundering. In October, a national team defender was among four people detained in a gota a gota extortion investigation, a case that remains at the investigative stage.

Authorities have also identified a newer variant known as chorro a chorro. It involves loans of millions of colones to borrowers with higher incomes, rather than to people facing an emergency. The yearly figures show the sharpest jump between 2022 and 2023, when complaints rose from 427 to 864. They dipped slightly to 857 in 2024 before reaching the 2025 high.

Across the five years, complaints have been highest in August, September and October, and lowest in December and February. Authorities urge anyone being pressured by an informal lender not to give in to threats and to report the case to the OIJ as soon as possible. Knowing the warning signs of a gota a gota loan can help people avoid the trap before it starts.

World.title: Nearly Two Thousand Chinese Businesses Established in Nicaragua Since Free Trade Agreement Took Effect
World.content:
Nearly 2,000 Chinese businesses have been established in Nicaragua during the first two years of the free trade agreement with China, according to the president of the Asociación Pro-Unificación Pacífica de China en Nicaragua. Shujin Huang made the statement to official media outlets after an event marking the 160th anniversary of the birth of Sun Yat-sen.

He said the association continues to promote additional investment from China, describing Nicaragua as a safe country with a competitive market. The free trade agreement between the two countries entered into force on January 1, 2024. The Banco Central de Nicaragua reported that net foreign direct investment from China reached 29.3 million dollars in 2025.

That figure represented 1.9 percent of the 1,502.5 million dollars in total net foreign direct investment recorded by the country that year. In 2024, any Chinese flows were not reported separately and would have been included in aggregate categories if present at all. Huang said the businesses operate mainly in commerce, with some also active in free-zone maquilas. The relatively low official investment total relative to the number of establishments indicates that most are small-scale operations.

The Asociación Pro-Unificación Pacífica de China en Nicaragua was founded in May 2024 and was officially registered as a legal organization under Ministerial Agreement 24-2024-OSFL, allowing it to operate in its own name under Nicaraguan law. Its founding event included participation by Chinese Ambassador Chen Xi and Nicaraguan officials including National Assembly President Gustavo Porras, Foreign Minister Denis Moncada and Presidential Adviser Laureano Ortega Murillo.

As part of the commercial expansion, construction of a Chinatown complex advances in Managua near the Rotonda Universitaria. The project, also known as Plaza China or Plaza 101, involves a two-story structure of approximately 8,000 square meters with an investment of about 3 million dollars. It is planned to house around 100 businesses operated by Chinese, other Asian and Nicaraguan owners.

The site currently holds roughly 30 businesses. Administrators have described the work as being in an intermediate phase, including installation of a stone arch more than six meters high carved in a dragon style and brought from China. The complex is intended to concentrate commercial activity, gastronomy and cultural offerings. Huang cited the existing Plaza China as an example of growing Chinese capital presence, noting that more than ten foreign-investment businesses already operate there.

Nicaragua and China restored diplomatic relations in December 2021 after Managua broke ties with Taiwan. The free trade agreement was signed on August 31, 2023. Official Nicaraguan statements have presented the pact and related initiatives as measures to expand trade and investment opportunities. The association’s stated goals include supporting Chinese investors and promoting the policy of one China.

As of now, the association continues to encourage further arrivals of Chinese capital. Construction on the Managua Chinatown project remains under way, with officials and association representatives describing it as a visible marker of the commercial presence that has developed since the trade agreement took effect. The Banco Central de Nicaragua has not published a full country-by-country breakdown beyond the 2025 net total that places China at 29.3 million dollars.

World.title: Costa Rica Uses Smartphones to Create 3D Maps of Pacific Coral Reefs
World.content:
A Costa Rican conservation organization is using ordinary smartphones to create detailed three-dimensional maps of coral reefs along the country’s Pacific coast, giving researchers a new way to track the health of underwater ecosystems threatened by rising ocean temperatures and climate change.

The project, led by the nonprofit Raising Coral, is taking place in Golfo Dulce and around Caño Island Biological Reserve, two important marine habitats near the Osa Peninsula in southern Costa Rica. Instead of relying entirely on expensive underwater cameras and specialized equipment, researchers are using Samsung Galaxy smartphones to photograph sections of the reef. The images are then processed into detailed 3D models that allow scientists to examine coral growth, identify damage and measure changes over time.

The technique, known as underwater photogrammetry, involves taking numerous overlapping photographs of the same area from different angles. Computer software combines the images into a three-dimensional reconstruction, essentially creating a digital copy of the reef. These digital models give researchers a much clearer picture of what is happening beneath the surface than traditional visual inspections alone.

Marine biologist María Laura Sandoval, who manages Raising Coral’s South Pacific restoration program, explained that the technology allows conservation teams to examine entire sections of reef rather than relying exclusively on what a diver can observe during a limited period underwater.

The system also makes it possible to return to the same location months later and compare new images with earlier models, helping researchers determine whether corals are growing, declining or recovering. The project uses Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra phones equipped with a special underwater photography feature called Ocean Mode. The technology helps improve image quality and color accuracy beneath the surface.

Once collected, the photographs are sent to researchers at the Scripps Institution of Oceanography at the University of California San Diego, where specialized software transforms them into 3D models. The effort is part of a collaboration involving Raising Coral, Samsung, the marine conservation organization SeaTrees and Scripps.

Tracking the Effects of El Niño

The project comes at an important time for Costa Rica’s Pacific reefs, which have faced repeated pressure from unusually warm ocean temperatures. During the 2023–2024 El Niño event, high sea temperatures caused widespread coral bleaching and losses around the Osa Peninsula.

Coral bleaching occurs when stressed corals expel the tiny algae living inside their tissues. These algae provide much of the coral’s food and color, so their disappearance leaves the coral looking pale or completely white. Bleached coral is not necessarily dead, but prolonged exposure to unusually warm water can prevent recovery and eventually kill it.

Researchers began using the smartphone mapping system in December 2025, initially surveying reefs approximately every four months. Since July 2026, however, the team has increased its monitoring to once a month to better observe possible changes associated with El Niño conditions.

The more frequent measurements should help scientists identify changes in coral cover and growth before they become apparent through less detailed monitoring. According to Sandoval, the technology has already helped produce information for a technical assessment supporting coral restoration around Caño Island. The surveyed areas showed coral coverage ranging from approximately 18% to 40%.

Those figures provide a snapshot of conditions in the areas studied, rather than evidence that the reefs have already recovered.

Restoring Costa Rica’s Reefs

Raising Coral has worked on reef restoration in Costa Rica since 2016, beginning in Golfo Dulce before expanding into other coastal areas. The organization grows coral fragments in underwater nurseries and later transfers them onto damaged reefs, where they can continue developing.

Some corals are attached to specially designed metal structures that hold them above the ocean floor, helping protect them from sediment while creating additional habitat for fish and other marine animals. The current restoration partnership aims to grow and transplant approximately 1,000 corals annually between 2026 and 2029, for a total of 4,000 corals across Golfo Dulce and Caño Island.

But planting corals is only part of the challenge. Conservationists must also determine whether transplanted colonies survive, continue growing and eventually help restore the surrounding ecosystem. That is where the 3D mapping technology becomes especially useful. By comparing models captured at different times, researchers can measure changes in individual coral colonies, examine the structure of the reef and monitor the return of marine life.

The information can also help conservation organizations demonstrate whether restoration efforts are producing measurable results.

Making Marine Conservation More Accessible

One of the project’s biggest advantages is its potential to make underwater research more affordable for smaller conservation organizations. Traditionally, creating detailed 3D maps of coral reefs required costly camera systems and specialized training. The use of smartphones could make the process easier for conservation teams with limited budgets.

Local residents are also participating in the project through Raising Coral’s community training program, which prepares people to work as coral gardeners and assist with restoration and monitoring. The approach creates opportunities for coastal communities to become directly involved in protecting the marine ecosystems that support fishing, tourism and other local activities.

Similar smartphone-assisted reef restoration and monitoring work is also taking place in Fiji, the Galápagos Islands and Indonesia. For Costa Rica, the technology could eventually provide a more practical way to monitor marine habitats beyond the current project sites, although its effectiveness on a larger scale still needs to be demonstrated.

Why Healthy Reefs Matter to Costa Rica

Coral reefs support a wide variety of marine life, including fish, sea turtles, sharks and countless smaller organisms. Around Caño Island, reefs provide habitat for numerous fish species and contribute to the area’s reputation as one of Costa Rica’s better-known snorkeling and diving destinations.

Golfo Dulce also supports important marine ecosystems, although its reefs face additional challenges from sediment carried into the water by rivers and runoff from surrounding land. When reefs deteriorate, the effects can extend beyond the corals themselves, reducing habitat for fish and potentially affecting the coastal communities that depend on healthy marine environments.

Restoration efforts cannot eliminate the broader threats posed by warming oceans, pollution and changing ocean conditions. However, better monitoring can help researchers understand which corals are surviving and where conservation work may be most effective. The new technology also makes the underwater world easier to understand for people who may never have the opportunity to see these reefs in person.

Instead of relying solely on scientific measurements, conservationists can use detailed 3D images to show communities, visitors and potential supporters how a reef is changing. Since Costa Rica has built much of its international reputation around protecting nature, the project offers another tool for understanding what is happening beneath the Pacific Ocean and determining whether efforts to restore its coral reefs are succeeding.

World.title: Alejandro Tabilo Falls to Rafael Jódar Again in Paris Masters Opener
World.content:
Chile’s Alejandro Tabilo suffered another disappointing defeat against Rafael Jódar on Monday, losing 6-2, 6-3 in the opening round of the Paris Masters as the Spanish teenager continued his remarkable rise in men’s professional tennis. Jódar, seeded ninth at the season’s final ATP Masters 1000 tournament, needed just one hour and 16 minutes to eliminate the Chilean on the indoor hard courts of Paris La Défense Arena.

The result marked Jódar’s fourth consecutive victory over Tabilo and his second against the Chilean in less than a week. The two players had met on October 27 at the Swiss Indoors in Basel, where Jódar won 6-4, 6-2. Their quick rematch in Paris offered Tabilo an opportunity to reverse that result, but the Spaniard once again proved too difficult to overcome.

Tabilo, ranked No. 30 in the world, entered the match hoping to end a difficult stretch of results on the European indoor circuit. Instead, he managed just five games against an opponent who has become one of his toughest matchups this season. Jódar, 20, arrived in Paris ranked No. 11 and was competing in his first tournament since entering the world’s top 10 in the latest rankings.

The Spaniard has enjoyed an extraordinary 2026 campaign, establishing himself among the leading young players on the ATP Tour and reaching the Shanghai Masters final in October. His success has also put him in contention for a place at the ATP Finals in Turin, where the season’s leading singles players compete for the year-end championship.

Monday’s victory keeps those hopes alive while adding another difficult result to Tabilo’s recent record. The two players have now met five times in 2026, with Jódar holding a commanding 4-1 advantage. Their first meeting came in March at Indian Wells, where Tabilo recorded a convincing 6-1, 6-2 victory.

At the time, the Chilean appeared to have the upper hand in the matchup. But the balance shifted dramatically during the North American hard-court season. Jódar defeated Tabilo in three sets in the Washington semifinals in August, recovering from losing the opening set to win 6-7(8), 6-4, 6-4.

They met again later that month at the Cincinnati Open, where the Spaniard delivered an even more convincing performance, winning 6-2, 6-1. The pattern continued in Basel last week and again in Paris on Monday. For Tabilo, the defeat extends a frustrating period in which strong performances earlier in the season have given way to repeated early tournament exits.

The Chilean reached the final of the Rio Open in February, losing to Argentina’s Tomás Martín Etcheverry after a competitive three-set match. He also made the fourth round of the French Open and reached the semifinals of the Washington ATP 500 tournament during the summer.

Those results demonstrated his ability to compete at a high level on both clay and hard courts. However, his results have become less consistent during the final months of the season. After reaching the second round in Tokyo, where he defeated American Tommy Paul before losing to Denis Shapovalov, Tabilo exited the Shanghai Masters against Spain’s Pablo Carreño Busta.

He then suffered successive first-round defeats to Jódar in Basel and Paris. The latest result highlights the challenge Tabilo faces against the tour’s emerging generation, particularly opponents who can maintain pressure throughout a match and prevent him from establishing his preferred rhythm.

Tabilo, a left-handed player who reached a career-high ranking of No. 19, has demonstrated that he can defeat leading opponents when his serve and aggressive groundstrokes are working effectively. But his recent meetings with Jódar have exposed the difficulty of reproducing that level consistently against a player whose confidence has grown throughout the season.

For Jódar, the victory represents another step toward the ATP Finals and a continuation of his breakthrough year. For Tabilo, Paris ends almost as quickly as Basel did, leaving the Chilean with another early exit and questions about how to regain his best form heading into the 2027 season.

His immediate challenge will be turning the positive results from earlier in 2026 into more consistent performances against the world’s leading players.

World.title: Costa Rica Reopens Cambronero Highway After Nearly Two-Months
World.content:
Costa Rica has reopened the Cambronero section of Route 1, restoring an important highway connection between the Central Valley and the Pacific coast after nearly two months of closure caused by damage to a temporary bridge. The Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MOPT) confirmed that traffic resumed on Sunday at approximately 5:30 p.m., following repairs to the modular bridge at kilometer 71 of the Inter-American Highway between San Ramón and Esparza.

The reopening comes as welcome news for drivers, freight companies and travelers who have been forced to use alternative routes since September 7, when a tractor-trailer struck the bridge and caused extensive damage to its metal structure. The accident forced authorities to close the crossing while engineers assessed the damage and determined how to repair the bridge safely.

The closure disrupted one of Costa Rica’s main road connections between the Central Valley and the northwestern Pacific region, sending additional traffic onto Route 27 and other roads. According to MOPT, the repairs cost approximately ₡380 million and involved a complicated process of removing damaged components, reinforcing the bridge and reinstalling it.

Before workers could replace the affected sections, they had to construct a temporary support structure capable of holding the bridge’s weight. Crews then removed portions of the bridge deck, moved sections of the metal framework and replaced damaged pieces before returning the structure to its original position.

The work also included reinforcing the bridge and making additional improvements intended to increase safety for motorists. MOPT and the National Road Council (Conavi) said the repairs allowed them to reopen the route earlier than initially expected. Although vehicles can once again travel through Cambronero, authorities emphasized that the repairs are temporary and do not resolve the underlying instability affecting the hillside.

The modular bridge provides a single-lane crossing while the government prepares a permanent solution to restore the original two lanes. Drivers should continue using caution when approaching the bridge, following posted traffic controls and allowing additional time for possible delays.

Some additional work will continue in the area, although authorities have indicated that these activities should not require another prolonged closure. The government is moving forward with a larger project intended to stabilize the hillside and restore the highway to its original configuration.

MOPT and Conavi have received eight bids from companies interested in carrying out the permanent work. Officials expect to evaluate those proposals during the remainder of 2026, with construction potentially beginning during the second quarter of 2027. The project would address the ground instability that originally made the modular bridge necessary and eventually allow the temporary structure to be removed.

However, the timeline will depend on the government completing the contracting process and selecting a company to perform the work. Public Works Minister Efraím Zeledón has also discussed the possibility of eventually adding a third lane in the area, although that idea remains under evaluation and is not part of an approved construction plan.

Cambronero has experienced repeated problems with landslides and unstable terrain over the years, particularly during periods of heavy rainfall. The mountainous section of the Inter-American Highway has steep slopes and difficult geological conditions, making repairs and maintenance especially challenging.

The reopening should provide relief for motorists traveling between San José, San Ramón, Esparza and destinations farther along the Pacific coast. During the closure, drivers were directed toward alternative routes, including Route 27 between San José and Caldera and Route 3 through the Monte del Aguacate.

Those detours increased travel distances and created additional expenses for businesses transporting goods between the Central Valley and northwestern Costa Rica. The disruption was particularly significant for trucks and commercial vehicles, which faced additional fuel costs, tolls and longer journeys.

Tourists driving between San José and destinations in Puntarenas and Guanacaste also had fewer options for reaching the Pacific coast. With Cambronero reopened, drivers once again have access to the Route 1 connection, although the temporary bridge means the crossing has not returned to normal two-lane operations.

For now, the government is asking motorists to drive carefully through the area and respect traffic controls while work continues. The immediate road connection has been restored, but the larger challenge of permanently stabilizing this vulnerable section of Costa Rica’s Inter-American Highway remains unresolved.

World.title: International News: Cost-of-Living crisis sparks massive protests across Europe
World.content:
International News: Cost-of-Living crisis sparks massive protests across Europe

By Zoila Palma: Thousands of people took to the streets across Europe on Saturday, October 31, protesting the rising cost of living, inadequate public services and government policies.

Demonstrations were reported in Germany, France, Spain, Italy, Belgium and Portugal, as a wave of youth-led activism spread across the continent, NBC reports.

Authorities remained on high alert following recent protests that resulted in looting, property damage and clashes with police.

France experienced some of the largest demonstrations, with the Interior Ministry reporting approximately 320,000 protesters nationwide, including 70,000 in Paris.

The government deployed 70,000 police officers to manage the demonstrations after weeks of unrest initially sparked by student concerns over the education system and later expanded to include demands for improved living conditions and social security. More than 560 arrests were reported by Saturday night, while authorities said some protests remained peaceful and others resulted in fires and clashes.

In Germany, the campaign group Gen Z regelt, meaning “Gen Z takes charge,” organized demonstrations in more than 30 cities, including Berlin and Frankfurt. Protesters called for greater investment in education, housing and climate protection while opposing plans to reintroduce mandatory military service.

However, some demonstrations turned violent, with police reporting smashed storefronts, looting and attacks involving stones, bottles and Molotov cocktails in Frankfurt. Protests were also reported in Madrid, Lisbon and Brussels, where police used tear gas and water cannons against some demonstrators.

The demonstrations reflect growing frustration among younger generations and other citizens over economic pressures and government priorities.

World.title: Belize strengthens regional social protection cooperation through SISCA Mission
World.content:
Belize strengthens regional social protection cooperation through SISCA Mission

By Zoila Palma: The Ministry of Human Development, Family Support and Gender Affairs hosted a two-day technical mission of the Central American Secretariat for Social Integration (SISCA) on October 29 and 30, 2026, as Belize continues its Pro-Tempore Presidency of the Central American Social Integration Council (CIS).

The mission focused on strengthening regional cooperation and identifying opportunities to advance social development priorities across Central America.

The delegation was led by SISCA Secretary General Ana Leticia Aguilar, accompanied by Gabriela Ramírez, Head of the Secretariat’s Multidimensional Poverty, Human Capital Development and Social Protection Unit.

On October 29, Minister Thea Garcia-Ramirez and the delegation held a technical meeting in Belize City to plan SISCA’s work for the remainder of Belize’s presidency, which concludes in December. Ministry representatives also presented the country’s social protection system, core programmes and services, including policies and support for older persons.

As part of the visit, the delegation toured Sister Cecilia’s Home for the Elderly, where they observed the care provided and interacted with staff and residents.

On October 30, Minister Garcia-Ramirez and the SISCA representatives also met with Taiwan’s Ambassador to Belize, Amino C. Y. Chi, during a courtesy luncheon, where they expressed appreciation for Taiwan’s nearly three decades of support to SISCA.

World.title: Department of Environment partners with bus operators to promote “Bin it” Anti-Littering campaign
World.content:
Department of Environment partners with bus operators to promote “Bin it” Anti-Littering campaign

By Zoila Palma: The Department of the Environment (DOE) is partnering with bus operators and transportation authorities to strengthen efforts to reduce littering along Belize’s highways and main roads.

The initiative, being implemented under the SICA AZUL Project, forms part of the DOE’s National Anti-Littering Campaign under the theme “Our Belize, Our Responsibility – Bin It!” and aims to improve waste disposal practices within the public transportation sector.

As part of the initiative, the DOE will host a handover ceremony on November 6, 2026, at the Ministry of Sustainable Development and Climate Change’s auditorium at the Green Complex Building in Belmopan.

During the event, garbage bins and public awareness flyers will be handed over to the National Bus Company and the Belize Bus Association for placement inside buses, encouraging passengers to dispose of their waste responsibly rather than littering along transportation routes.

The Department of Transport will also receive appropriately labelled garbage bins for bus terminals to encourage waste separation and proper disposal.

DOE noted that making bins more accessible, while distributing public awareness materials, is intended to promote long-term behavioural change and remind commuters, bus operators and terminal managers that keeping Belize clean is a shared responsibility.

The DOE is calling on the public to support the “Bin It” campaign by using designated garbage bins and helping keep buses, terminals, roadsides and communities clean.

World.title: International News: Haitian gang leader requests UN mediation; warns of Bukele’s “vengeful” remarks
World.content:
International News: Haitian gang leader requests UN mediation; warns of Bukele’s “vengeful” remarks

By Zoila Palma: Wilson Joseph, the leader of Haiti’s powerful 400 Mawozo gang, has written to United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres requesting the deployment of a UN delegation to facilitate dialogue and mediation.
