World.title: First Asian hornet nest in Poland eliminated but experts warn more to appear next year
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s first-ever nest of Asian hornets, an invasive species seen as a particular threat because it preys on honeybees, has been eliminated. But scientists who have studied the colony say that it is likely more will be found next year. Since arriving in France in 2004, Asian hornets, which are indigenous to Southeast Asia, have gradually spread to other European countries. The first confirmed nest to be found in Poland was sighted in a tree in the village of Wielka Wieś near Kraków in mid-October, with individual hornets also being spotted at the apiary of the city’s AGH University of Science and Technology. The nest was removed last week and sent to be studied by a team of scientists at Wrocław University of Environmental and Life Sciences, reports the Polish Press Agency (PAP). Paweł Migdał, from the university’s faculty of biology and animal science, told PAP that the nest was “fairly large” considering the Polish climate, containing around 1,000 workers and several dozen queens and males. The scientists’ assessment of the nest revealed that it contained eggs and larvae, indicating that the hornets inhabiting it were still feeding, he added. “I think we’ll find more of these nests,” Migdał told PAP. “They’re often built in the treetops, which means they’re invisible until the leaves fall in the autumn.” Young queens had already left the nest to establish new ones after overwintering, and have greater chances of surviving the longer and warmer the Polish autumn is, he explained. They seek shelter in warm, dry places, such as underground or in storage areas. With queens measuring 30mm and males about 24mm, Asian hornets, also known as the yellow-legged hornet, are smaller than the European variety, and no more dangerous to humans than European hornets or wasps. The major concern over their arrival relates to their tendency to seek out beehives and prey on honeybees. “Besides killing honeybees, their presence also causes bees in apiaries to stop working,” explained Migdał. “With the European hornet, the bees recognise the threat but, in a sense, continue working. However, the yellow-legged hornet presents a completely new threat to them.” The number of bee colonies in Poland has risen 54% over the last decade to reach two million, thanks in part to a state programme supporting beekeepers. Bees' value to the ecosystem as pollinators is estimated to be worth 5bn zloty (€1.1bn) https://t.co/ElISOc2o2T — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 30, 2022 The scale of the species’ invasiveness is shown by the fact that it releases an average of 150 young queens from its nest, and sometimes even 500 – each of which can potentially create its own nest – while European hornets release just 50, Migdał pointed out. The location of the first nest found in Poland surprised scientists as the closest previously known was in Opava, around 150 km away in the Czech Republic. The hornets therefore probably travelled in a vehicle, although Migdał noted a potential concern that other populations might be found between the two sites. World.title: Polish president in physical confrontation with judges amid power struggle at constitutional court

We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki has clashed physically and verbally with judges involved in an attempt to take control of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK). Afterwards, the president announced that he would hold a series of meetings with political leaders on Saturday afternoon to discuss the crisis. However, it remains unclear to what extent the government, which is in conflict with the opposition-aligned Nawrocki and is backing the judges seeking to control the court, will engage in that process. Meanwhile, the court itself remains surrounded by riot police and anti-government protesters. On Friday, Nawrocki had been flying to Senegal for a state visit when the crisis at the court broke out. He ordered his plane to turn around in midair and return to Warsaw. At around 1 a.m. on Saturday morning, Maciej Berek, a close associate of Prime Minister Donald Tusk who was recently chosen as a new TK judge, shared videos showing Nawrocki entering the TK building amid a confrontation at its doors. The president was heard asking judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, who is leading the attempt to take control of the court, to move out of his way and could be seen pushing his way past her. Afterwards, presidential aide Marcin Przydacz claimed that Korwin-Piotrowska and another judge, Krystian Markiewicz, had “breached the inviolability of the head of state”. Berek denied this and said that it was the president who “barged into judge Korwin-Piotrowska with great force”. Subsequently, a further film showed Nawrocki, after he had entered the building, in a verbal confrontation with Korwin-Piotrowska and others, in which he can be heard telling them, “you are not Constitutional Tribunal judges”. ⚠️Mamy kolejne nagranie z TK. Tym razem prezydent krzyczy do sędziów, że „nie są sędziami” i w otoczeniu funkcjonariuszy SOP wchodzi po schodach na górę. pic.twitter.com/rkhoQLIv94 — Kamil Dziubka 🟡🇵🇱🇺🇦 (@KamilDziubka) October 31, 2026 The conflict stems from a years-long crisis around the TK. Since the current government – a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Tusk – came to power in 2023, it has refused to recognise the court’s legitimacy. That is because three of its judges were unlawfully appointed under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which was widely seen to have brought the court under political control. It also regards the court’s chief justice, Bogdan Świeczkowski, as illegitimate. As a result, Tusk’s government has ignored the TK’s rulings and, until this year, refused to even nominate new judges to fill vacancies that arose on the court’s 15-person bench. That changed in March, when the ruling coalition began filling the backlog of empty seats. So far this year, parliament has chosen eight new judges, meaning that its nominees in theory now have a majority on the court. However, under Polish law, although new TK judges are chosen by parliament, they must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki, who is aligned with PiS, has refused to swear in five of those eight new judges, including Korwin-Piotrowska, Markiewicz and Berek. Those five judges arranged their own swearing-in ceremonies in parliament and submitted their oaths to the president’s office. However, Święczkowski, who before being appointed as a TK judge had served in the former PiS government, refused to accept those five judges on the court. The standoff between the government and president over Poland’s constitutional court deepened today, as Maciej Berek, whom the prime minister recently described as his “right-hand man”, took his oath as a new judge without the presence of the president https://t.co/MrExiJRsEN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 14, 2026 On Friday evening, the judges appointed by parliament this year entered the TK and Korwin-Piotrowska announced that she had suspended Święczkowski for failing to properly exercise his duties. She said that, as the judge with the longest experience, she had assumed the position of acting head of the tribunal. Outside the court, riot police held back protesters, including opposition politicians, who called the events a “coup d’état”. Święczkowski himself was prevented by police from entering the grounds after some of his supporters had used a power tool to cut through the fence. At around 5 a.m., Nawrocki was seen leaving the TK. “There has been a violation of the constitutional order of Poland and a forceful takeover of a constitutional body,” said the president in a statement read by the head of his cabinet, Paweł Szefernaker. The president announced that he would hold urgent consultations with parliamentary groups in an attempt to “restore the legal order”. Those meetings are scheduled to take place on Saturday afternoon. Riot police have surrounded the court and were seen preventing the chief justice from entering https://t.co/xpkp3sjPFn — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 30, 2026 Leading figures from the right-wing and far-right opposition, with which Nawrocki is aligned, have indicated their willingness to engage in talks, as have two of Tusk’s junior coalition partners. Szymon Hołownia, the founder of the centrist Poland 2050 (Polska 2050), confirmed on Saturday morning that his group would attend the talks. He also urged Tusk to sit down at the table with Nawrocki. Hołownia said that his party had “watched last night’s events with concern” and that they “bring shame on Poland”. While he criticised Święczkowski and other PiS-nominated judges, he said that trying to fix the TK “by force” would only “exacerbate its downfall”. On Saturday afternoon, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, leader of the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL) and a deputy prime minister, also revealed that he would personally attend the consultations with Nawrocki. @PL_2050 na wydarzenia dzisiejszej nocy patrzy z zaniepokojeniem. Przynoszą one Polsce wstyd. Nie przybliżają nas do naprawy tego, co zostało zepsute. Jest dla nas jasne, że Bogdan Święczkowski, wraz z nominatami PiS-u, zrobił z TK karykaturę sądu konstytucyjnego. Sytuacja w… — Szymon Hołownia (@szymon_holownia) October 31, 2026 Tusk’s only comment so far has been a social media post saying that restoring the rule of law “requires decisive action”. His justice minister, Waldemar Żurek, announced on Friday evening that he was seeking to have Święczkowski’s immunity from prosecution lifted. On Saturday, speaking to broadcaster TVN, Żurek expressed support for the actions taken by Korwin-Piotrowska. He called Nawrocki’s behaviour at the TK “shameful” and said he “hoped prosecutors will take action, because it is unacceptable for someone protected by presidential immunity to behave in such a way”. Meanwhile, Tusk’s other main coalition partner, The Left (Lewica), announced on Saturday afternoon that it would not attend the talks with Nawrocki. “One cannot accept an invitation from someone who is himself responsible for the current situation regarding the Constitutional Tribunal,” wrote Anna-Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s parliamentary caucus. “The TK is in the hands of independent judges. Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) was plunged into chaos on Friday evening as one group of judges, backed by the government, moved to take control of the court from its chief justice, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition and President Karol Nawrocki. Since the current government – a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk – came to power in 2023, it has refused to recognise the court’s legitimacy. That is because three of its judges were unlawfully appointed under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which was widely seen to have brought the court under political control. As a result, Tusk’s government has ignored the TK’s rulings and, until this year, refused to even nominate new judges to fill vacancies that arose on the court’s 15-person bench. That changed in March, when the ruling coalition began filling the backlog of empty seats. So far this year, parliament has chosen eight new judges, meaning that its nominees in theory now have a majority on the court. However, under Polish law, although new TK judges are chosen by parliament, they must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki, who is aligned with PiS, has refused to swear in five of those eight new judges, citing concerns over how they were chosen or their qualifications. In doing so, he ignored an order by the European Court of Human Rights that the judges be allowed to take up their positions. Święczkowski argued that the ECHR had no authority to issue such a ruling. The standoff between the government and president over Poland’s constitutional court deepened today, as Maciej Berek, whom the prime minister recently described as his “right-hand man”, took his oath as a new judge without the presence of the president https://t.co/MrExiJRsEN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 14, 2026 Rumours have long swirled that the government would introduce those judges onto the court by force. PiS supporters have been camped outside the TK grounds for weeks with the aim of preventing that from happening. On Friday evening, large numbers of riot police were deployed around the TK. On the court’s website, a brief statement appeared, saying that a “break in the activities” of Święczkowski and his deputy chief justice, Bartłomiej Sochański, had been ordered. The statement did not say who had ordered that break, but it cited article 130 of the law on common courts, under which the president of a court or the justice minister can order an immediate break in a judge’s official duties if they are caught in the act of committing an offence. However, Marcin Matczak, a prominent scholar of constitutional law who was also a critic of PiS’s judicial reforms, wrote on social media, that, while the justice minister exercises oversight over common courts, he cannot do so over the TK. “I consider Bogdan Święczkowski to be the worst person to serve as the president of the TK,” wrote Matczak. “I never thought I’d end up defending him, but this legal basis [for suspending Święczkowski] is nonexistent for a million reasons.” Ze szczątkowych informacji, na jakiej podstawie zawieszono B. Święczkowskiego, wynika, że ma to być art. 19 ustawy o statusie sędziów TK, który mówi, że do spraw nieuregulowanych w tej ustawie stosuje się „przepisy dotyczące praw i obowiązków sędziów SN” i art. 130 ustawy o SN,… — Marcin Matczak (@wsamraz) October 30, 2026 Meanwhile, Waldemar Żurek, the justice minister and prosecutor general, issued a statement announcing that he had submitted motions to the TK to waive the immunity from prosecution of Świeczkowski and Sochański. He said that the documents had been “delivered to the longest-serving judge of the Constitutional Tribunal”. That was a reference to Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, one of the TK judges whom Nawrocki has refused to swear in. She told state broadcaster TVP that it was she who had issued the order to suspend Święczkowski from his duties. She justified her action by accusing Święczkowski of blocking judges from taking up their positions and of overseeing irregularities in the assignment of judges to cases, reports Polskie Radio. Korwin-Piotrowska’s claim to have the longest tenure among TK judges relates not to her service on tribunal itself, but to the fact that she first began her judicial career in 1995. 🗣️ “Bogdan Święczkowski narusza zasady funkcjonowania TK. (…) Nie było innego wyjścia” – sędzia Anna Korwin-Piotrowska w TVP Info. pic.twitter.com/22FYJJbQAC — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) October 30, 2026 While the TK website appears to now be under the control of Korwin-Piotrowska, the court’s account on social media service X issued a statement saying that “an unlawful takeover of the TK’s website has occurred”, that “Bogdan Święczkowski remains chief justice”, and that “Korwin-Piotrowska is not a TK judge”. “All persons participating in these actions are committing the crime of a coup d’état,” it added. Nastąpiło bezprawne przejęcie strony internetowej Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. Prezesem @TK_GOV_PL jest nadal Bogdan Święczkowski, a Wiceprezesem Bartłomiej Sochański. Pani Anna Korwin-Piotrowska nie jest sędzią Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. Wszystkie osoby uczestniczące w… — Trybunał Konstytucyjny (@TK_GOV_PL) October 30, 2026 The court’s spokeswoman, Weronika Ścibor, told broadcaster Kanał Zero that “seven people elected as [TK] judges this year” had been escorted into the building by officers from the State Protection Service (SOP), a body responsible for protecting state officials. SOP is subordinate to the interior minister. She said they had entered the grounds of the court through a gate that leads from the prime minister’s chancellery, rather than the main entrance from the street where protesters are gathered. Korwin-Piotrowska also confirmed to TVP that she was one of seven judges who were inside the TK on Friday evening. Rzeczniczka Trybunału Konstytucyjnego Weronika Ścibor komentuje sytuację w TK. Według jej relacji siedem osób wybranych na sędziów weszło do budynku w asyście funkcjonariuszy SOP, natomiast wiceprezes Bartłomiej Sochański nie został wpuszczony na teren Trybunału. pic.twitter.com/VwxU4UrYuz — OficjalneZero (@OficjalneZero) October 30, 2026 The developments at the court prompted outrage from the opposition. PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński declared outside the court that “as of today, Poland has become a police state, and from there it’s a straight path to authoritarianism, and then to totalitarianism”. Kaczyński called on Nawrocki to return to Poland from his state visit to Senegal and defend the court. The president himself quickly confirmed that he had done so, with flight trackers showing his plane turning around in midair and heading back to Poland. Meanwhile, Zbigniew Kapiński, the chief justice of the Supreme Court – a separate entity from the Constitutional Tribunal – told Kanał Zero that he was “appalled” by what was happening, which was “undoubtedly a coup d’état”. Our most tracked flight right now: A Polish government aircraft en route to Senegal is now returning to Warsaw. https://t.co/YdLhQmV8pl pic.twitter.com/Dz9KPgI3eI — Flightradar24 (@flightradar24) October 30, 2026 Tusk, however, issued a statement on social media defending what was taking place at the TK. “Restoring the rule of law is our duty,” he wrote. “After years of PiS-led lawlessness, this is a difficult process, sometimes painful, and it requires decisive action. There is no other way.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland approves first fast-track renewable energy zones
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has introduced its first fast-track zones for renewable energy projects as the coal-dependent country seeks to speed up its transition to cleaner sources of electricity. The regional assembly in Wielkopolska province, western Poland, this week approved plans covering 105.4 hectares across four municipalities, where investors will be able to develop solar farms under simplified planning and environmental procedures. The environment ministry estimates that the changes, introduced under an EU directive, could reduce project preparation times from three to four years down to just one or two years. Pierwsze #OPRO już są! Sejmik województwa wielkopolskiego przyjął dziś pierwsze w Polsce plany OPRO. Obejmą one ok. 105,4 ha w gminach Lwówek, Rawicz, Słupca i Złotów.🔆 ❓Czym jest OPRO? ✅To Obszary Przyspieszonego Rozwoju #OZE, czyli tereny, na których – już podczas ich… — Marek Pogorzelski (@rzeczni_MKiS) October 26, 2026 Under the scheme, planning and much of the environmental assessment will be completed before investors apply for permits, allowing projects to move forward more quickly. Environmental authorities will also have a maximum of 45 days to review projects with a capacity of at least 150 kW. Industry representatives told energy Świat OZE, a renewable energy news service, that obtaining an environmental decision can currently take up to 150 days. The newly designated areas, known as Accelerated Renewable Energy Development Zones (OPRO), will be located in the municipalities of Złotów, Lwówek, Rawicz and Słupca. Together, they have an estimated technical potential of 66-80 megawatts of solar capacity, depending on the arrangement of the panels. Maria Niewitała-Rej, a climate and energy policy analyst at the Reform Institute, a Warsaw-based think tank, told the Dziennik Gazeta Prawna newspaper that while “the scale of the Wielkopolska plan is modest, the adoption of the first resolutions is a step in the right direction”. The creation of accelerated renewable energy development zones stems from the EU’s revised Renewable Energy Directive (RED III), which requires member states to designate areas where renewable energy projects can be developed more quickly. Under the directive, permitting procedures in these zones should take no longer than 12 months for onshore projects and 24 months for offshore projects. EU rules required the first zones to be designated by 21 February 2026, making Poland’s adoption several months late. Polish state mining firm JSW, which is the EU's largest producer of coking coal and one of Poland's biggest employers, has announced that it will cut over 4,000 jobs, 21% of its workforce, by the end of this year as it seeks to stem large financial losses https://t.co/EWP3rAVMaH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 2, 2026 Poland has long had one of Europe’s most polluting energy sectors. The country still produces around half of its electricity from coal, by far the higher proportion in the EU. However, the share of renewables has grown significantly in recent years. It nearly doubled from 14.7% of the energy mix in 2021 to 29.4% in 2025. Onshore wind was the largest contributor last year, accounting for 14.2%, followed by solar at 12.1% and biomass at 1.8%. Poland’s national energy and climate plan, approved in June, envisages coal accounting for just 0-5% of the energy mix by 2040. Around 15-16% will come from nuclear, 7-8% from gas, with most of the rest from renewables: onshore wind (22-27%), offshore wind (18-21%) and solar (14-18%). Poland’s first offshore wind farm has begun to deliver electricity, with Prime Minister @donaldtusk celebrating the development as a "key element of our energy security and sovereignty". The government wants 20% of power to come from offshore wind by 2040 https://t.co/EodvInFmrn — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 10, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish Left seeks to end state funding of clergy’s social contributions as government reform stalls
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The Left, a junior partner in Poland’s ruling coalition, has proposed a bill to abolish the Church Fund, which provides state subsidies for the health insurance contributions of clergy. It says it is frustrated by delays in fulfilling a pledge made by most parties in the wide ruling coalition to reform the fund. However, another coalition partner, the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), says that it will oppose the bill, calling instead for a system allowing taxpayers to allocate part of their taxes to religious institutions of their choice. Senior church figures also say they have not been consulted. 📣 Lewica składa ustawę likwidującą Fundusz Kościelny. Czas na realizację umowy koalicyjnej w zakresie świeckiego państwa‼️ Co zakłada nasz projekt? ⬇️ ✅ Składki na duchownych przestają być w 80 procentach finansowane z budżetu państwa jak dotychczas. 50% składek pokrywać… pic.twitter.com/syqUMdCugr — Lewica (@__Lewica) October 29, 2026 The Church Fund, originally established in 1950 to compensate religious communities for property seized by the communist authorities, provides state subsidies for the health insurance contributions of clergy, for religious organisations’ charitable activities, and for the renovation of religious buildings. It now supports all legally recognised religious denominations in Poland, including those that did not lose property at the time. Last year, the state spent 275.7 million zloty on the Church Fund. This year it has budgeted 272.6 million zloty. Most of this money is then used to cover 80% of clergy members’ social security contributions. Under the bill proposed by The Left, churches would pay half of the contributions, with clergy covering the other half. For regular workers, such contributions are funded jointly by employees and their employers, Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s parliamentary caucus, pointed out, as quoted by the Polish Press Agency (PAP). “We are introducing the same arrangement for priests and members of the clergy.” At least 17.5bn zloty in state funds went to religious bodies from 2021-23, with over 95% going to Catholic organisations, the state auditor has found. In response, the speaker of parliament has proposed measures to reduce and better oversee such spending https://t.co/IN3dpY4La2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 16, 2025 An exception is made in the bill for members of enclosed religious orders and missionaries, who would have their contributions paid in full by their churches. The cost of maintaining historic churches would be covered by the National Fund for the Protection of Monuments, Żukowska explained. Włodzimierz Czarzasty, who is the leader of The Left as well as the speaker of the Sejm, the more powerful chamber in the Polish parliament, said the party did not oppose religion but wanted clergy to be treated equally under the law. “I would like to remind my coalition partners: our coalition agreement includes a commitment to work toward establishing the principles of a secular state in Poland,” he said, speaking alongside Żukowska. “Our patience is running out”. Ahead of the 2023 election, both the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk and The Left pledged to abolish the Church Fund, while the centre-right Poland 2050 (Polska 2050) proposed replacing state funding with voluntary taxpayer contributions. PSL had no equivalent formal party-wide pledge. In 2024, after the coalition came to power, Tusk announced plans to reform the fund and appointed a government working group led by the PSL leader and deputy prime minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. The group’s work has since stalled. Kosiniak-Kamysz yesterday dismissed The Left’s proposal, saying it has “not the slightest chance of support in parliament”. His party, the second largest in the coalition with 32 of 239 MPs, sees the existing fund as an inexpensive form of compensation and will oppose abolishing it, he vowed. Instead, taxpayers should be able to allocate part of their taxes to a religious institution of their choice, a system used in several European countries, to “let the Polish people themselves decide whether or not they want to contribute,” he said, quoted by broadcaster Polsat News. Interior minister Marcin Kierwiński, a member of Tusk’s Civic Coalition (KO), said that he supported reform, but criticised The Left for submitting the bill without consulting its coalition partners. A long-term decline in trust in the Catholic church in Poland has accelerated over the last year, with only 35% of Poles now saying they trust the church. Meanwhile, the armed forces now enjoy record-high trust of 94% https://t.co/ErCBE4HwWR — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 17, 2025 Religious communities also criticised the proposal for not having been discussed with them in advance. In a press statement sent to PAP, the Polish Episcopal Conference (KEP), the main organ of the Catholic church in Poland, said any solution should comply with the country’s agreement with the Vatican, as well as the constitutional principle that relations between the state and religious communities be regulated by mutual agreement. Bishop Jerzy Samiec, head of the Evangelical-Augsburg Church in Poland, the country’s biggest Protestant body, pointed to the significant costs churches face in maintaining their properties, including care homes and other facilities. The Catholic Church, Poland’s dominant religious institution, has seen a long-term decline in public trust, with only 35% of Poles saying they trusted it in 2025. That has coincided with a series of crises in recent years, in particular over revelations of child sexual abuse by members of the clergy and negligence in dealing with them by the church hierarchy. A variety of surveys, including from the church itself, show that religious attendance and identification have been declining in Poland in recent years. A growing number of Poles are turning away from the Catholic church, but not from religious belief itself. This creates challenges for the church, but also for Polish identity, which has historically been linked to Catholicism, writes Katarzyna Skiba https://t.co/udWGzd0X7F — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 18, 2023 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish opposition leader sparks controversy with speech on potential EU exit talks
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Jarosław Kaczyński, the leader of Poland’s largest opposition party, has sparked controversy by appearing to suggest that Poland and some other allied European Union member states could launch the process of leaving the EU if they fail in efforts to reform it. His remarks were condemned by Prime Minister Donald Tusk and other figures from the pro-EU ruling coalition, who have long accused Kaczyński and his national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party of seeking “Polexit” from the EU. However, Kaczyński responded by accusing Tusk of misrepresenting his words, insisting that he wants Poland to reform the EU rather than leave it. Kaczyński pomylił Krynicę z Kremlem. pic.twitter.com/tX0G04krze — Cezary Tomczyk (@CTomczyk) October 29, 2026 The comments in question came in an hour-long speech by Kaczyński at the Krynica Forum, an annual conference bringing together leaders from politics, business and civil society, which he used to outline his vision for sweeping reforms of the EU. Repeating his longstanding criticism of Brussels, Kaczyński warned that there had been a “consistent drive to transform the EU into a centralised state” with too much power over national governments. He also called the European Parliament in its current form a “parody”. But soon, said Kaczyński, “a window of opportunity” for reform may appear because “completely different governments could emerge” in Poland, France and Spain, all of which will hold elections within the year. PiS has previously enjoyed close relations with Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN) party in France and the nationalist Vox party of Santiago Abascal in Spain. The EU is preparing a "German plan" that would "annihilate the Polish state", said Kaczyński as Poland marks Independence Day. He warned that the incoming opposition government will "strive to implement this plan" and called on Poles to "fight" against it https://t.co/QDbxmiaazJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 11, 2023 Kaczyński suggested that Poland, if led by PiS, could work with other like-minded EU governments to push for reform of the bloc by influencing public opinion, identifying breaches of EU treaties, creating a blocking minority in the European Council, and trying to change the EU’s treaties. However, the PiS leader then warned that, “if [those] approaches fail to yield results, the states that want change could conclude a new treaty with the elements we are seeking, but with a delayed entry into force”. Kaczyński then noted that the EU treaties “include provisions specifying the terms under which a state may withdraw from the EU. This all begins with negotiations. And simply begin these negotiations”. “It is a tough approach, a risky one, but the situation is so dire that it is worth employing such a method if all others fail to yield results,” he added. The remarks immediately prompted condemnation from figures in Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right. They accused Kaczyński of effectively calling for Polexit – something they have long claimed he wants, even though PiS has not explicitly called for it before. “Jarosław Kaczyński has just announced that Poland should begin negotiations on the terms of its withdrawal from the EU,” wrote Tusk himself on X. “This is, among other things, what the current struggle in Poland is about – a tough struggle. I do not intend to lose it.” “So they do want Polexit after all,” wrote foreign minister Radosław Sikorski. “Customs borders with Germany, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Lithuania…An end to subsidies for farmers and investments…And they swore on their lives that they’d never do that.” In a video published later on Thursday, Tusk declared that next year’s parliamentary elections would help decide “whether Poland remains in the European Union or leaves it”. Jarosław Kaczyński ogłosił właśnie, że Polska powinna zacząć rokowania o warunkach wyjścia z Unii Europejskiej. O taką między innymi stawkę toczy się dziś w Polsce walka. Twarda walka. Nie zamierzam jej przegrać, nawet jeśli nie wszyscy zagrają ze mną. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) October 29, 2026 Kaczyński responded by saying that “Tusk is lying as usual”. He emphasised that he believes “the EU is needed but it requires thorough reform” so that it “benefits not the elites, but ordinary citizens”. PiS deputy leader Przemysław Czarnek said on Thursday that his party was “considering all scenarios, including the possibility that the EU will kill itself”. However, he added that the priority remained reforming the bloc and “PiS has no plans to leave the EU”, reports the Polish Press Agency (PAP). When PiS was in power from 2015 to 2023, it regularly clashed with Brussels over a variety of issues, including judicial reform, trade, climate policy, and migration. Since Tusk, a former president of the European Council, took power in 2023, his government has greatly improved relations with Brussels. Tusk jak zwykle kłamie. Najwyraźniej wychodzi z założenia, że dzień bez kłamstwa jest dniem straconym… Unia Europejska jest potrzebna, ale wymaga gruntownej reformy. Kryzys i zapaść w jej obecnym kształcie to efekt rządów Merkel i jednego z jej pomocników, Tuska. Nie ma co się… — Jarosław Kaczyński (@OficjalnyJK) October 29, 2026 Poland has been the largest net recipient of EU funding since joining the bloc in 2004. A study published earlier this year found that the country’s economy is 42% larger than it would have been had Poland not been part of the EU. Opinion polls consistently show a large majority of Poles in favour of remaining part of the EU. However, recent years have seen an uptick in support for Polexit, as well as for anti-EU far-right parties. PiS has increasingly found itself competing against such parties for votes. Regular polling by state research agency CBOS shows that, while opposition to EU membership fell to a record low of 5% in 2022, it has subsequently risen, standing at 14% in the most recent survey. World.title: Prague Music Week Brings Czech and International Music Names to Prague
World.content:
From November 4 to 6, Výstaviště Praha will become a hub for musicians, industry professionals, and fans interested in everything happening both on and off the stage.

The fourth edition of Prague Music Week—themed “Women Shaping the Industry”—will feature keynote interviews with Aneta Langerová and Jana Kirschner, as well as discussions with local artists such as Lenny, Jiří Burian, Eva Saija Burešová, Klára Vytisková, and Ventolin.



A newly confirmed guest is singer Ben Cristovao, who will join a panel addressing the surge of AI-generated music.

International guests include renowned PR expert Fiona Bloom, Sziget Festival Operations Director Ádám Kiss, diversity, equity, and inclusion specialist Brechje Merckx, and representatives from Spotify.

Will also join: Finnish music industry professional Maija Talvisto; Christine Osazuwa—founder of Measure of Music and an expert in music data and analytics; Vasja Veber, co-founder of the leading analytics platform Viberate; Kristina Janušauskaitė, Executive Director of the IFPI European Office.

The event will offer practical workshops, speed-meeting sessions, opportunities to receive feedback on one’s own work, a technology expo, industry awards, informal gatherings, and space for forging new collaborations.

Tickets for the festival portion of the program are available for purchase via the GoOut and NFCtron networks.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Prague Music Week (@praguemusicweek)

Conference tickets can be obtained via a voluntary contribution through the NFCtron platform. More information is available at www.praguemusicweek.cz.

Prague Music Week will feature an Expo spanning 2,000 m², showcasing companies and products that are driving the music industry forward.

Throughout the day, attendees can combine conference sessions with exploring new innovations, participating in hands-on activities, and connecting with exhibitors.

The Expo will also include an “Experience Lab,” where visitors can try out new skills and discover the technologies used in producing music events.

World.title: German Rock Legends Scorpions to Play Prague’s O2 Arena in 2027
World.content:
One of the most successful hard rock bands of all time will perform on June 9, 2027, at Prague’s O2 arena.

Fans can look forward to an evening filled with unforgettable hits, iconic guitar riffs, and the electrifying energy that has defined the Scorpions for over six decades.

Led by charismatic frontman Klaus Meine, the band will revisit tracks that have left an indelible mark on the history of rock music, including “Rock You Like a Hurricane,” “Still Loving You,” and the timeless ballad “Wind of Change.”



In 2027, the Scorpions will embark on another extensive world tour titled “Love, Peace & Rock’n’Roll,” following up on their successful “60th Anniversary – Coming Home” anniversary concerts.

The schedule includes approximately thirty performances across three continents—ranging from European festivals and arena shows (including stops in their native Germany) to dates in North and Latin America.

The Scorpions rank among the most significant and influential rock bands in music history. Formed in 1965 in Hanover, Germany, the group has built a global reputation over the course of an extraordinary career, thanks to their unmistakable sound, high-energy live shows, and an ability to connect with audiences across generations. They have sold over 100 million records and performed countless times on the world’s biggest stages.

Their major breakthrough arrived in the 1980s with the albums Blackout and Love at First Sting, which catapulted the band into the global rock elite. It was during this period that hits such as “No One Like You,” “Rock You Like a Hurricane,” and “Big City Nights” emerged—songs that remain an essential part of their live repertoire to this day.

The Scorpions also gained fame for their emotive ballads, most notably “Still Loving You” and “Send Me an Angel.”

A truly special place in their discography is held by the song “Wind of Change,” which became a symbol of the political and social changes at the turn of the 1980s and 1990s.

Inspired by the atmosphere at the end of the Cold War, the song remains one of the most famous rock ballads of all time.

World.title: Sherlock Holmes Exhibition Lets Visitors Play Detective in Prague
World.content:
Visitors can test historical investigative techniques, examine crime scenes and follow clues at a new interactive Sherlock Holmes exhibition in central Prague.

The exhibition, located on the third floor of the Bílá labuť department store, covers more than 2,000 square metres and features over 200 exhibits.

Rather than simply moving between display cases, visitors take on the role of an investigator and work through a series of tasks inspired by the methods used by detectives more than a century ago.



Each visitor receives a detective’s notebook to record observations and clues. The notebook guides them through the exhibition as they investigate evidence, solve puzzles and gradually build their own picture of the case.

One section focuses on the history of criminal investigation around the turn of the 20th century. It includes authentic objects loaned by the Police Museum, ranging from historical fingerprinting equipment and tools used by safecrackers to more disturbing evidence connected with violent crimes.

The exhibition also explores the development of forensic science. Visitors can make footprint impressions, examine insects found at a crime scene, send messages by telegraph and learn how investigators studied bullets and other evidence. Several interactive stations test whether visitors can identify clues and apply the techniques used by detectives of the period.

The literary side of the exhibition looks at the life and work of Arthur Conan Doyle. Visitors can see early editions of the Sherlock Holmes stories and learn more about the author behind one of literature’s most enduring fictional detectives.

A reconstruction of Holmes’s famous Baker Street apartment is among the main attractions. The exhibition then moves into a series of crime scenes where visitors search for evidence and attempt to connect the clues. Some puzzles draw on well-known Sherlock Holmes stories, while others require close attention to details hidden throughout the exhibition.

Period newspapers are also part of the investigation, and visitors are encouraged to look carefully: a coded message may be concealed within the reports.

The final section examines Sherlock Holmes’s lasting influence on popular culture, including books, comics, films and television adaptations. Vintage Sherlock Holmes comic books are also on display.

A scavenger hunt for younger visitors has been added for the current school year, with children asked to find objects hidden throughout the exhibition. The format also works well for school groups, which can divide into smaller teams and compare their discoveries.

Visitors are allowed to take photographs without flash. A full visit typically takes between 90 minutes and two hours, and booking a timed entry is recommended.

Opening hours: Daily from 9 a.m. to 8:30 p.m.

Duration: The exhibition is scheduled to run at least until January 10, 2027.

Admission: Adult tickets start at 380 CZK, while family tickets start at 980 CZK.

World.title: Czech Billionaire Strnad Offers €30 Billion for Ray-Ban Family’s Firm
World.content:
Czech billionaire Michal Strnad has offered €30 billion to acquire Delfin, the investment vehicle of Italy’s Del ​Vecchio family and the key shareholder in eyewear giant EssilorLuxottica.

News of the offer, which was first reported by Italian newspaper Il Domani, comes amid growing tensions within Delfin, whose investment portfolio includes also large holdings in Italy’s ​financial sector.

Il Domani published a copy of a letter dated October 20 ​outlining the offer.



“I am looking for long-term investment opportunities in companies ⁠operating in, or investing in, businesses positioned at the top of their value chain,” ​Strnad said in the letter said, according to the newspaper.

Delfin “perfectly fits my investment approach and ​strategy,” the letter added.

Jan Osuch, a spokesperson for AKIPIA, which oversees some of Strnad’s investment activities outside the defence sector, said the group did not comment “on market speculation or potential business negotiations.”

Strnad earlier ​this year bought a 14% stake in Italian tyre maker Pirelli, opens new tab from China’s ​Sinochem.

Strnad, 34, heads the family’s defence company Czechoslovak Group (CSG) which listed in Amsterdam earlier this year.

Delfin shareholder Leonardo ‌Maria ⁠Del Vecchio, one of the six children of the late Ray-Ban billionaire Leonardo Del Vecchio, confirmed he had been recently informed of an offer for the company received from a foreign investor.

“The work of a lifetime by my father must remain part of ​Italy’s heritage”, he said in a ​statement.

The late Luxottica ⁠founder built his business empire from scratch having grown up in a Milan orphanage.

Delfin’s ownership is divided equally among Del Vecchio’s ​eight heirs: his six children, his widow Nicoletta Zampillo and her ​son from ⁠a previous marriage.

A sale would require a virtually unanimous decision from the heirs, who have become increasingly at odds with one another.

In addition to its stake in EssilorLuxottica, Luxembourg-based Delfin holds stakes in ⁠Italian ​insurer Generali and lenders Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS) and ​UniCredit, for a combined current market value of €43 billion.

Delfin declined to comment. A representative for Strnad was not ​immediately available for comment.

World.title: Prague’s Only Christmas MINT Market to Take Place on November 28–29
World.content:
Don’t leave your Christmas shopping until the last minute this year.

On the weekend of 28–29 November, head to Hall 13 at Holešovice Market and discover original gifts directly from the people who made them.

MINT Market will bring together more than a hundred carefully selected brands from across the Czech Republic, offering a relaxed alternative to the pre-Christmas rush in shopping centres.



On Saturday from 10 am to 6 pm and Sunday from 10 am to 4 pm, visitors can look forward to independent fashion, designer jewellery, ceramics, natural cosmetics, illustrations, original accessories and plenty of Christmas gift inspiration.

And, of course, there will be the relaxed and friendly atmosphere that has become an essential part of MINT Market. The event is suitable for all generations and admission is free.

The youngest MINT Market visitors and their families can enjoy the beautiful NOOK Family Lounge, featuring high-quality wooden toys, a creative play area, a quiet zone with books and space to relax, as well as facilities for babies and parents, including a changing table and a peaceful place for breastfeeding.

There will also be Christmas-themed creative workshops.

MINT Market has been active for sixteen years. During that time, it has become an important platform for small and emerging creators, often directly from Prague, who are given the opportunity to present their products to a wide audience.

Residents of Prague and the surrounding area thus have several opportunities each year to purchase quality products that are literally made by their neighbors – locally, sustainably, and with an emphasis on honest craftsmanship.

MINT Market is not just about shopping. Since 2010, the project has been run by a team of people who systematically support small and local brands and are the only ones bringing high-quality Czech design to more than twenty cities across the country.

What started as a small project has gradually grown into a community of more than 1,500 creatives and a platform that has hosted over 450 events and welcomed more than 1.3 million visitors.

World.title: Czech Government Proposes Voluntary TV and Radio Fees Without State Budget
World.content:
People in the Czech Republic could soon be allowed to decide whether they want to pay television and radio licence fees under a new funding model being prepared by the government.

Prime Minister Andrej Babiš said the Finance Ministry is working on a system that would make contributions to Czech Television (ČT) and Czech Radio (ČRo) voluntary while ensuring the two public broadcasters receive a guaranteed level of funding.

The proposal is expected to be discussed by the coalition council on Monday.



For now, however, the existing system will remain in place. Although the government had initially hoped to introduce changes at the beginning of 2027, Babiš said the legislative timetable makes that unlikely.

Under parliamentary rules, the bill requires a 60-day review period before moving forward. That means its second reading would fall during the Christmas period, delaying further debate until at least January 2027.

The proposed changes have already sparked political and public opposition.

On October 24, the Chamber of Deputies approved in its first reading a proposal to abolish television and radio licence fees. The governing coalition, made up of ANO, SPD and the Motorists party, added the measure to its priority legislative agenda. The vote took place early in the morning after a lengthy parliamentary debate.

Opposition parties have warned that changing the funding system could expose public broadcasters to greater political pressure. Government representatives have rejected those concerns, saying the planned reform does not threaten democratic standards.

Babiš has said the final model must comply with European requirements concerning the independence of public media and predictable funding.

The issue has also prompted demonstrations. On October 25, thousands of people gathered in Prague’s Old Town Square for a protest organised by the Million Moments for Democracy movement.

Participants expressed concern that changes to the financing of Czech Television and Czech Radio could increase political influence over the broadcasters.

World.title: Prague Welcomes a Week of Polish Films and Culture
World.content:
Prague will host a week of Polish cinema and culture from November 9 to 15, as the 3Kino – Polish Film Festival Prague returns for its 13th edition.

The festival will screen 13 feature films representing contemporary Polish cinema, with a program that also includes theater, stand-up comedy, exhibitions, music and events for children.



This year’s festival opens with The Doll (Lalka), directed by Maciej Kawalski. Based on the classic novel by Bolesław Prus, the film is among the most expensive Polish productions ever made and takes audiences to 19th-century Warsaw.

The story explores love, ambition and social divisions, with Marcin Dorociński, one of Poland’s best-known contemporary actors, in a leading role.

Freedom will be the central theme of this year’s edition. The festival will explore the idea through historical events as well as everyday life, personal relationships and decisions that can alter a person’s future.

The program extends beyond the cinema. Visitors can attend theatrical performances, stand-up shows and exhibitions, while this year’s edition will also put a special focus on Poland’s Lower Silesia region.

Among the accompanying events is the opening of photographer Rafał Pawłowski’s exhibition Shadows of Sounds. Another exhibition will mark the 100th anniversary of the birth of Polish filmmaker Andrzej Wajda, featuring a selection of Polish film posters.

The festival aims to bring Polish culture to audiences across Prague, with screenings and accompanying events taking place at several venues throughout the city.

Ticket sales are now open, and the full program is available on the festival’s official website.

World.title: The intersection of sleek design and modern wellness brands
World.content:
Explore how modern consumer brands are elevating their aesthetic appeal by investing in highly customized and visually striking product hardware.

Discover how deliberate styling and tactile materials redefine daily customer routines.

You probably remember when health tools hid inside bathroom cabinets, kept out of sight because their clunky plastic shells felt purely clinical. Today, wellness tools serve as personal fashion statements that you proudly display on living room tables and office desks.

Modern customers want daily items that mirror their curated tastes and fit their personal spaces. When your brand treats hardware design as an artistic craft, you turn simple wellness routines into meaningful daily rituals.

Why Are Wellness Tools Becoming Lifestyle Statements?

Your customers no longer separate wellness routines from their broader aesthetic choices. They curate their living rooms, nightstands, and carry bags with items that express their taste. When you produce clean hardware with balanced silhouettes, you invite buyers to keep your products in plain view.

Visibility drives regular daily use. A handsome object sitting on a counter prompts natural engagement, while an awkward gadget gets shoved into a dark drawer. By focusing on intentional shapes, you build products that seamlessly merge into home decor.

Thoughtful design also influences how customers perceive product quality and long-term value. Smooth finishes, understated colors, and ergonomic details create a premium experience that extends beyond basic functionality. When wellness tools complement personal spaces and individual preferences, they become desirable everyday accessories rather than purely practical devices.

How Do Color and Material Guide Consumer Choices?

Color establishes an immediate emotional connection with your audience. Earthy neutrals, muted pastels, and soft cream tones communicate calm and relaxation before a buyer even reads your ingredient list. If you choose harsh neon finishes, you risk sending mixed signals about serenity and health.

Material choices reinforce that visual promise. When people lift a device made with weighted aluminum or a soft-touch matte shell, their hands register quality. Thoughtful finishes create an impression of quiet sophistication that plain plastic cannot deliver.

How Do You Align Product Hardware with Brand Identity?

Customers judge your company within seconds of unboxing a new device. When you source sleek empty disposable vape pens that match your signature visual tone, you give customers an experience that feels deliberate and luxurious. That visual harmony bridges the gap between everyday utility and curated luxury. Your audience notices when physical hardware matches the graphic polish of your outer box.

Mismatched components break customer trust. You lose credibility when premium outer cartons hold generic items that clash with your voice. Consistent colors, unified fonts, and matching tactile surfaces establish a unified identity from the moment the package arrives.

Why Does Outer Presentation Drive Buying Decisions?

Your retail box acts as an interactive introduction to your brand story. According to data shared by the Forbes Business Council, roughly 72% of shoppers say that package styling directly impacts their purchasing decisions. That finding confirms that visual presentation carries just as much weight as product features.

Shoppers form split-second opinions based on packaging textures, embossing, and typography. If your exterior box looks rushed, shoppers assume the interior hardware lacks care as well. Investing in bespoke packaging signals that you prioritize quality across every single detail.

What Steps Create a Seamless Product Experience?

Building an unforgettable product requires harmony between visual appeal and reliable mechanics. You need a structured approach that guides your production decisions from concept to final delivery.

Structuring Your Hardware Design Strategy

Practical Manufacturing Benchmarks:

Standardize finish specifications: Pick a distinct surface texture like anodized metal or matte coating across all hardware runs.

Synchronize print colors: Match your Pantone shades across cardboard packaging, printed guides, and physical device shells.

Test hand ergonomics: Check device grip and balance to guarantee that the unit feels comfortable during daily handling.

Following these benchmarks keeps your production tight and reliable. Your buyers receive hardware that looks cohesive, feels comfortable, and performs reliably during routine use.

How Does Responsible Material Selection Support Growth?

Modern consumers care deeply about how companies manage resources. Guidance from the Environmental Protection Agency highlights that analyzing how packaging components are manufactured and discarded shapes sound business investments. When you integrate thoughtful materials into your supply chain, you satisfy conscious shoppers while reducing unnecessary waste.

Sleek presentation does not require excess plastic or non-recyclable wraps. By choosing compact paper boxes and recyclable device housings, your brand displays environmental integrity. Customers respect businesses that balance elegant design with mindful stewardship.

Style and practical functionality walk hand in hand across the modern self-care market. When you treat your hardware as an extension of personal taste, you build genuine customer loyalty that outlasts fleeting market trends.

Focus on thoughtful colors, premium materials, and cohesive packaging to make your brand an unforgettable part of your audience’s daily lives. By consistently delivering attractive designs and dependable performance, you strengthen emotional connections with customers and encourage lasting engagement with your products.

World.title: More than 240 Second World War explosives found in Budapest
World.content:
More than 240 explosives dating back to the Second World War have been discovered at a construction site on Üllői Road in Budapest, where Hungarian military bomb disposal experts faced a particularly challenging operation involving fused and damaged munitions.

A huge amount of world war-era explosives found in the heart of Budapest

The Hungarian Defence Forces’ 1st Explosive Ordnance Disposal and River Flotilla Regiment announced that a large quantity of wartime explosives had been recovered from the site at Üllői Road 404, in Budapest’s 18th district. The latest operation took place last Friday, following earlier discoveries at the same location.

According to their statement, 244 explosive devices and remnants, alongside substantial quantities of other ammunition-related material, were recovered.

Soviet, German, Hungarian and American munitions found

The recovered items included explosives manufactured in the Soviet Union, Germany, Hungary and the United States. Among the identified devices were 79 Soviet 82mm mortar shells, 77 German 81mm mortar shells, two German 120mm mortar shells, ten German 7.5cm Ig.R.18 fragmentation grenades and 12 Soviet RG-42 hand grenades.

The experts also found around 100 kilograms of small-arms ammunition, 50 kilograms of shell casing fragments and ten kilograms of explosive material remnants. The operation was made considerably more difficult by the suspected history of the ammunition. Experts believe the explosives from the Second World War may once have been collected in a pit and subsequently set on fire in an attempt to destroy them.

The heat apparently caused some of the devices and their remnants to fuse together, making separation an extremely laborious process. Bomb disposal personnel had to chisel apart the pieces that had become stuck together, according to the military.

A demanding seven-hour operation

The work began at 8 AM and continued until approximately 2.30 PM. The intensity of the operation was illustrated by data from one bomb disposal soldier’s smartwatch: during an activity recorded as “walking”, it registered a distance of 3.21 kilometres and approximately 2,387 calories burned.

The Hungarian Defence Forces said the dangerous remnants were safely dealt with thanks to the personnel’s expertise, perseverance and coordinated efforts, but it shows that unexploded Second World War ordnance can remain a serious hazard decades after the conflict ended. Earlier attempts to dispose of the ammunition improperly can also create complex challenges for specialists today.

The construction site had already seen major discoveries in mid-October, when bomb disposal experts neutralised two Soviet FAB-100 aerial bombs. During the second operation, a further 24 explosives of various types and sizes were also removed.

Authorities warn that anyone who discovers an explosive device or an object that might resemble one must not touch, move or attempt to neutralise it. People should keep a safe distance, mark the location if possible and notify the police by calling 112.

World.title: Budapest to trial its first biomethane-powered bus – try it for free! Here’s where it will run
World.content:
Budapest is set to trial its first bus powered by biomethane (Bio-CNG), a renewable fuel. The vehicle was unveiled in the Hungarian capital on Monday at a press conference held outside MOL’s headquarters. It will begin its trial operation on bus route 132E.

MOL aims to support greener public transport

MOL Group’s key strategic objective is to support the green transition and sustainable urban public transport through smart, practical solutions, said Ambrus Halász, the company’s head of corporate communications.

He added that the group’s fuel portfolio is continuously expanding with products designed to support energy security, competitiveness and the green transition at the same time.

“An important milestone for us was the launch of our first biomethane operation in Szarvas on 14 October. This means that, going forward, we will also be able to supply markets with Bio-CNG,” he said, welcoming the opportunity provided by Budapest’s public transport companies BKK and BKV to test the biomethane-powered bus in the capital.

The pilot project aims to demonstrate that sustainably produced energy in Hungary can also be used to meet the needs of Budapest’s public transport system. MOL hopes to supply an increasing proportion of this type of energy for public transport and other applications in the future, said Ádám Horváth, director of MOL Group’s New and Sustainable Businesses within its Downstream division.

International trends suggest that the fuel portfolio of the future will be much more diverse, requiring several different solutions.

Although fossil fuels are expected to remain the dominant energy sources for some time, there is a growing need for alternatives that offer genuinely more sustainable ways of meeting energy demands, he explained.

“We are working to make our portfolio increasingly green, and to process more and more alternative feedstocks alongside crude oil at our refinery,” Horváth said.

He added that the company is investing in green hydrogen projects not only in Hungary but also in Croatia, with plans to expand into Bratislava in the future. Building a significant biomethane presence within MOL Group is another new strategic priority.

Why is biomethane important for public transport?

One of the main drivers behind this strategy is EU regulation, including the Clean Vehicles Directive. Under the rules, more than half of the buses purchased and put into public transport service between 2026 and 2030 must comply with the directive’s clean vehicle requirements.

Alongside electric and hydrogen-powered vehicles, compressed natural gas (CNG) also qualifies under these requirements.

MOL Group currently feeds seven million cubic metres of biomethane into regional and national gas networks every year, Horváth said. Using existing infrastructure, energy produced in rural areas can therefore be transported to Budapest through the gas network.

Photo: MTI

The company also wants to demonstrate the environmental and economic advantages of biomethane in public transport and establish it as a viable alternative internationally.

When total life-cycle costs are taken into account, biomethane can be competitive with diesel. It also produces lower nitrogen oxide and particulate emissions.

Furthermore, biomethane-powered buses operate much more quietly than diesel vehicles while offering a similar driving range and competitive refuelling times.

If you missed it: Big shake-up for Budapest public transport: capital and suburbs to get one transport system

When and where can passengers try the new bus?

The Bio-CNG bus will operate on Budapest’s 132E route until 4 November, BKK CEO Ádám Bodor announced.

He pointed out that transport is still responsible for 30% of Budapest’s carbon dioxide emissions, with public transport accounting for 3% of the total.

Although most Budapest residents travel by metro, tram or trolleybus, around 1,100 of the capital’s 2,300 public transport vehicles are buses. Most of these run on diesel, making their replacement with electric models one of the biggest challenges facing the city.

Bodor stressed that while switching to electric vehicles is important, other technologies could also contribute to more sustainable transport.

In his view, around 300 buses will need to retain internal combustion engines in the long term to ensure security of supply in Budapest. Nevertheless, testing new technologies and the latest versions of existing ones is particularly important.

BKV currently operates 37 compressed natural gas (CNG) buses, although these will gradually need replacing as they age, he added.

Passengers can use the biomethane-powered bus free of charge, as it will operate as part of the regular timetable during the trial period.

World.title: Inside Hungary’s Versailles: An American producer discovers Esterházy Palace – VIDEO
World.content:
What connects one of Hungary’s most magnificent Baroque palaces, the legendary composer Joseph Haydn and the Hollywood music industry? American producer Ray Brown explores these unexpected connections in a new Magyar Minute video filmed at Esterházy Palace in Fertőd.

Often described as the Hungarian Versailles, Esterházy Palace is famous for its magnificent interiors, extraordinary gardens and rich musical heritage. But beyond the chandeliers and gilded halls lies a fascinating story of aristocratic ambition, wartime destruction and remarkable restoration.

In his latest video for Magyar Minute, American producer Ray Brown visits the palace alongside Alpár Kató, founder of Daily News Hungary, where they are welcomed by Csilla Sütő, managing director of the Eszterháza Center.

During the visit, Brown discovers the remarkable legacy of Prince Nikolaus Esterházy (Esterházy I. (Fényes) Miklós herceg), the palace’s connections to Joseph Haydn and the history behind the composer’s famous Farewell Symphony.

The visit also has a personal dimension. Brown, whose father Harold Brown was a founding member of the legendary American band WAR, reflects on the universal power of music and imagines the palace as a spectacular venue for international concerts and film productions.

The four-minute video also reveals lesser-known details of the palace’s turbulent twentieth-century history, including traces of its Soviet-era past.

Watch the video: Inside Hungary’s Versailles

From its magnificent halls to its nearly 8,000 rose bushes, Esterházy Palace offers plenty of surprises. Discover why this extraordinary destination deserves a place on every visitor’s Hungarian itinerary.

World.title: Son of former Hungarian central bank governor now searched by elite fugitive hunters
World.content:
Ádám Matolcsy, the son of former Hungarian National Bank (Magyar Nemzeti Bank, MNB) governor György Matolcsy, is now being sought by specialised police fugitive-hunting units amid an investigation into alleged economic fraud and corruption linked to the central bank’s foundations. An international and European arrest warrant has been issued for him and his associate, György Stofa.

An elite group is on the hunt for Matolcsy

Hungarian police have transferred the search for the two men to the National Bureau of Investigation (Nemzeti Nyomozóiroda, NNI), which operates within the Rapid Response Police. According to news outlet Telex, the case may have been assigned to the NNI’s targeted fugitive-hunting division, commonly known as the police’s bounty hunters.

This shows that locating and apprehending the suspects has become a priority for the authorities. Matolcsy and Stofa were initially placed on Hungary’s wanted list on 21 October. European and international arrest warrants followed on 27 October. Neither man has reportedly contacted the authorities, and their whereabouts remain unknown.

Specialised units tasked with tracking fugitives abroad

The NNI’s fugitive-hunting officers specialise in locating individuals who deliberately evade law enforcement, often by travelling abroad, obtaining false documents or attempting to establish new identities.

The unit has a record of high-profile arrests, including the capture of Mária Dobrai, better known as Broker Marcsi, in Belize in 2016. It has also helped bring notorious Hungarian fugitive András Lakatos, known as Kisbandi, back to the country.

The officers work closely with foreign law enforcement agencies to find the suspects involved in the central bank scandal, exchanging intelligence to identify and apprehend suspects who may be hiding overseas. According to Telex, several investigators may now be working on the Matolcsy and Stofa cases simultaneously.

Stay up-to-date: Leading Czech magazine portrays Viktor Orbán in handcuffs

Investigation focuses on central bank foundation assets

The investigation concerns alleged financial misconduct involving the MNB’s PADME foundation and the management of its assets. Prosecutors suspect that a controversial securities-lending arrangement involving companies connected to the foundation was designed to transfer control over its wealth to business interests linked to György Matolcsy and his son after the former governor’s departure from office.

György Matolcsy, who led the central bank from 2013 to 2025, was detained on 21 October alongside two associates, former company executive Mihály Valkó and lawyer Tamás Sándor. A court ordered their pre-trial detention for one month on 23 October, although the ruling was not final at the time of reporting, as the defendants appealed. The investigation remains ongoing, and the allegations against Ádám Matolcsy and György Stofa have not been proven in court.

World.title: Hungary to scrap lifetime benefits for former presidents who leave office early, Magyar announces
World.content:
Hungary is preparing to abolish lifetime benefits for former presidents who fail to complete their terms, Prime Minister Péter Magyar announced in Parliament on Monday. The government will also scrap a controversial fund that allows former heads of state to distribute tens of millions of forints to charities and foundations every year.

Speaking before the agenda at Monday’s parliamentary session, Magyar said the government would soon submit legislation to ensure that presidents who leave office before their mandate expires – for example, because of plagiarism or treason – can no longer receive taxpayer-funded benefits for the rest of their lives.

Former presidents could lose HUF 73 million charity budgets

The announcement also addresses a separate controversy surrounding the 2027 budget proposal. The draft budget, submitted on Friday evening, had allocated HUF 73 million per former president for public-benefit donations next year. Under the original proposal, Pál Schmitt, János Áder, Katalin Novák and Tamás Sulyok would each have been able to distribute the money freely among charities, civil organisations and foundations.

The proposal attracted attention after Telex first reported on the allocations. Magyar responded to the newspaper’s Facebook post over the weekend with a brief comment: “I wouldn’t think so. 1 January is still a long way off.”

He has now confirmed in Parliament that the allocations will be amended before the final vote on the budget. The separate funds available to former presidents for charitable donations will also be abolished.

Magyar described the measures as part of the government’s effort to eliminate what he called the remaining privileges of the previous political system.

Photo: MTI

If you missed it: Egyptian president visits Budapest: Railway deal struck, new economic partnerships on the table

Government presents 2027 budget as start of national rebuilding

In his parliamentary address, the prime minister also outlined the broader goals of next year’s budget.

Magyar described the 2027 budget as carefully planned, saying it would only promise what the government could realistically deliver. He called it the beginning of Hungary’s reconstruction and said the government would work to put the country’s finances in order.

He added that the aim was to ensure that Hungarians could once again decide their own future. The government also intends to restore recognition and respect for those who have kept the country running in recent years.

According to Magyar, the foundations are being laid for further measures in the coming years, when economic growth picks up and European Union funding arrives.

He described the 2027 budget as the first step in a longer process, adding that the government had taken that step and would continue the work together.

Magyar to meet German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Berlin

The prime minister also announced several upcoming diplomatic engagements. Next week, he will travel to Berlin for an official meeting with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Magyar said he would be accompanied by the foreign minister, as well as the ministers responsible for the economy and energy, defence and the interior. The Hungarian ministers will also hold talks with their German counterparts.

Next Wednesday, Magyar is scheduled to travel to Dublin, where he will meet the leaders of the other 26 EU member states.

Reflecting on Hungary’s recent foreign policy developments, the prime minister drew a comparison with the 1956 Hungarian Revolution, noting that the country’s freedom fighters were left alone against overwhelming forces 70 years ago.

He argued that Hungary is no longer isolated and now has friends and partners stretching from Prague and Warsaw to Belgrade and Washington.

World.title: Shein and Temu shoppers hit by new EU fee as cheap orders now cost more
World.content:
A new EUR 2 handling fee on goods ordered directly from outside the European Union came into force on 1 November, adding further pressure on shoppers using Chinese online platforms such as Shein and Temu.

EU introduces new fee affecting Shein and Temu orders

Combined with an existing EUR 3 customs charge, some low-value orders could now face additional costs of up to EUR 5 per product category. Consumers ordering inexpensive goods from outside the EU will have to navigate another change to the bloc’s customs rules.

This is due to the Union introducing a new handling fee aimed at covering the growing cost of processing and inspecting imported e-commerce shipments. The EUR 2 Union Handling Fee (UHF) applies to individual product categories rather than every parcel, meaning the final charge will depend on the contents of an order.

Not every parcel will cost EUR 5 more

The new measure follows the introduction of a temporary EUR 3 flat-rate customs duty on 1 July, which applies to consignments valued at EUR 150 or less. The distinction between the two charges is important. While the EUR 3 duty is limited to lower-value shipments, the new EUR 2 handling fee applies regardless of the value of goods sold and shipped directly to consumers from outside the EU.

For example, three identical T-shirts ordered from Shein or Temu may be classified as a single product category, resulting in a combined EUR 5 charge under the two measures. However, if a parcel contains three different product categories, the additional costs could reach EUR 15, writes HVG.

The charges will primarily be collected from platforms, sellers or, in certain circumstances, transport operators. Nevertheless, companies may pass some or all of the costs on to customers through higher prices or separate fees.

Brussels targets the growing e-commerce market

The European Commission says the growing number of low-value online shipments has placed increasing pressure on customs authorities, which must process, assess and inspect millions of parcels. The new fee is intended to help finance these operations while encouraging online marketplaces to take greater responsibility for the goods they sell.

The changes could particularly affect platforms such as Shein and Temu, whose business models have relied heavily on shipping inexpensive products directly from China to European consumers. According to figures cited in recent reports, approximately 5.8 billion low-value parcels entered the EU in 2025, representing a 26 per cent increase compared with the previous year.

The European Commission reportedly estimates that the new charges could generate nearly EUR 6 billion annually for the EU budget between 2028 and 2034.

World.title: Wizz Air flight makes emergency landing at Budapest Airport due to bomb threat
World.content:
A Wizz Air flight travelling from London to Sofia was forced to divert to Budapest Airport on Monday after receiving a reported bomb threat. Hungarian Gripen fighter jets escorted the aircraft, while emergency services and counter-terrorism units were deployed.

Wizz Air flight makes emergency landing at Budapest Airport

The Airbus A321neo turned back over Bosnia and Herzegovina and requested permission to land at Budapest’s Liszt Ferenc International Airport.

The aircraft landed safely at 12:08 local time on Runway 2, according to initial reports. Firefighters, police and counter-terrorism personnel were waiting at the airport, with the aircraft subsequently parked at stand B5. The incident prompted the temporary closure of Runway 2, with all arriving and departing flights redirected to the airport’s other runway, reports Tudásmorzsák.

Hungarian fighter jets scrambled

Hungarian Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi confirmed that the Hungarian Defence Forces had responded to the incident after a bomb threat was reported on the London-Sofia service. According to the minister, NATO’s air defence alert system issued an ALPHA alert, prompting Hungarian Gripen fighter jets to take off within minutes.

The military aircraft escorted the passenger plane to Budapest, ensuring its safe landing before returning to their base in Kecskemét. The minister praised the Hungarian military’s readiness, emphasising its ability to respond immediately to threats to the country’s airspace. Following the aircraft’s arrival, responsibility for further measures was handed over to the police.

Authorities have yet to release further details about the alleged bomb threat, including whether any suspicious items were found on board or whether the threat was deemed credible. The incident remains under investigation.
