World.title: Iraq’s foreign reserves hit $75.3 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s foreign reserves rose to over 113.99 trillion Iraqi dinars (almost $75.3 billion) as of October 15, 2026, according to data released by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI).

The country’s foreign reserves increased compared to September, when they stood at approximately 101.718 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $67.17 billion), local news outlet Shafaq News reported.

Director of the CBI’s Statistics and Research Department, Samir Neama, said that the country’s foreign currency reserves can cover Iraq’s imports for a whole year.

Speaking at the MERI 2026 forum in Erbil, Neama clarified that the CBI is in a very comfortable situation in terms of foreign reserves.

While International Monetary Fund (IMF) reports indicate a capability to finance imports for three to six months, Neama confirmed that the reserves are sufficient to cover the country’s needs for more than a year.

A Standard Chartered economist said in early October that Iraq may resort to the IMF if oil revenues continue to fall and the currency’s devaluation fails to boost state finances as intended.

Standard Chartered chief economist for the Middle East and Pakistan Carla Slim said that any potential program with the IMF could entail structural reforms, particularly regarding the public sector wage bill, to enhance fiscal sustainability, Bloomberg reported.

If the current pace of depletion continues, Iraq’s foreign reserves might fall to roughly $60 billion by the end of the year, down from over $100 billion at the beginning of the year, according to Slim.

The economist indicated that the local currency’s exchange rate may be adjusted again in the future months, based on changes in oil earnings and foreign reserves.

World.title: Australians held in Iraq over ISIS connections may face death penalty
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – 13 Australian men and boys detained in Iraqi prisons over alleged connections to ISIS could potentially face trial and the death penalty by hanging.

Between January and February 2026, the US military transferred approximately 5,700 detainees, including around 2,200 foreigners from 65 different countries, from prisons in northeast Syria to al-Karkh Central Prison near Baghdad due to increasing instability in Syria.

The detainees transferred from northeastern Syria to Iraqi custody earlier this year included the 13 Australian men and boys.

After completing their investigations, Iraqi authorities are proceeding with charges under extensive anti-terrorism legislation that carries the death sentence.

The Australian federal government has stated that it will not engage in the repatriation of the detainees and has refused to intervene or assist in their return.

Human Rights Watch (HRW) has denounced the transfer, claiming that Australia is outsourcing its duties rather than pursuing its nationals domestically. They have also warned of possible torture-extracted confessions, unjust trials, and execution.

There is disagreement among the public and community over the issue. Human rights supporters say that Australia should bring its nationals back to stand prosecution under domestic law, while others maintain that individuals who travel overseas must deal with the laws and legal systems of the host nation.

World.title: Iraqi PM to visit Kuwait, Bahrain
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi is scheduled to visit Kuwait and Bahrain this week as part of a regional diplomatic tour.

Official sources confirmed the trip is set for the current week, with reports noting a visit to Bahrain planned around Wednesday.

Al-Zaidi is expected to hold talks in Kuwait focusing on resolving longstanding bilateral and economic issues, including maritime boundary demarcation, the Mubarak al-Kabeer Port project and its potential impact on Iraq’s al-Faw Grand Port, missing Kuwaiti people and property from the 1990 invasion, and broader regional security cooperation.

The Iraqi prime minister’s agenda in Bahrain is expected to address regional de-escalation, security, strategies to open new economic and investment avenues, and concerns regarding Bahrain’s Shiite community.

As part of the Iraqi government’s effort to foster regional economic integration, handle cross-border security issues, and foster confidence, al-Zaidi has made recent regional visits to Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Syria, Turkey, and Iran.

World.title: Papa Johns to enter Iraq in 2027, plans 25 restaurants by 2035
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Papa Johns, an American pizza brand, has revealed ambitions to join the Iraqi market, with the first restaurant set to open in spring 2027 and a goal of 25 outlets throughout the nation by 2035.

The expansion follows a ten-year renewal of the company’s franchise deal with PJP Investments Group, which extends their exclusive Middle East collaboration until 2036 and formally adds Iraq as a new market.

PJP, which manages Papa Johns restaurants in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan, intends to increase the brand’s regional footprint from 167 to more than 400 by 2036.

Todd Penegor, President and CEO of Papa Johns, said that the company’s entry into Iraq underlines its trust in the Middle East as a crucial region for worldwide growth.

PJP has worked with Papa Johns for over two decades, and its restaurant network has grown dramatically under the ownership of Levant Capital.

The arrangement marks Papa Johns debut into Iraq’s rapidly expanding restaurant and food service business, bringing another worldwide dining brand to the country.

World.title: Iraq plans to expand oil tanker fleet
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Oil Ministry is planning to purchase large oil tankers to increase its ability to transport and market crude oil internationally.

The strategic move seeks to improve financial returns from crude exports while lowering transportation expenses.

The spokesperson for the Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) on Monday that the Iraqi tanker fleet currently comprises six small and medium-sized tankers.

Al-Rikabi explained that the ministry is also considering establishing partnerships with specialized firms in the maritime transport sector.

Crude oil can be stored or transported across the Strait of Hormuz by renting tankers from other businesses, according to al-Rikabi.

The Iraqi Ministry of Oil is considering the purchase of 10 oil tankers as part of its efforts to develop its export infrastructure and expand options for delivering shipments to global markets.

The step is part of the government’s efforts to strengthen the role of the Iraqi Oil Tankers Company (IOTC) and leverage the ownership of maritime transport assets, which would provide greater flexibility in marketing crude oil and managing shipments.

The plan is considered crucial given Iraq’s desire to improve the terms of its oil sales and reduce the discounts associated with certain existing marketing and transportation arrangements.

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair revealed recently that the ministry is considering the purchase of 10 supertankers, with an estimated total cost of $2 billion, according to Attaqa News.

According to Khudair, the projected fleet will have a total capacity of 10 million barrels since each tanker has a capacity of around one million barrels.

Owning these tankers would increase export earnings; estimates indicate that Iraq might save between 30 percent and 40 percent on the losses it presently suffers from price reductions.

World.title: Iraqi British Professor Salman Rawaf criticizes treatment at Baghdad Education Conference
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Prominent Iraqi-British public health academic Professor Salman Rawaf has criticized the organization of the Third Iraq Education Conference at the University of Baghdad after microphones were removed from in front of him during his speech.

A video circulating on social media shows Rawaf expressing frustration over the incident, describing the situation as disgraceful and questioning the organization of an international academic event after travelling approximately 5,000 miles to attend.

Rawaf is a Professor of Public Health at Imperial College London and Director of its World Health Organization (WHO) Collaborating Centre for Public Health Education and Training.

The incident came just days after Rawaf was officially welcomed by University of Baghdad President Professor Alaa Abdulhassan Atiyah Hassan during a meeting focused on strengthening academic cooperation between the University of Baghdad and Imperial College London.

According to the university, the discussions covered joint research, academic exchanges, postgraduate supervision and visiting professor programs aimed at expanding international academic partnerships.

Rawaf is also a graduate of the University of Baghdad’s College of Medicine and has established an international reputation for his contributions to public health.

The removal of microphones during his conference appearance sparked criticism on social media, raising concerns about the treatment of internationally recognized Iraqi academics visiting their home country.

Rawaf subsequently described the incident as an organizational error involving the departure of television channels, rather than attributing it to a deliberate attempt to silence him.

The incident has nevertheless drawn attention to the importance of professional conference management and ensuring that distinguished academic guests are given appropriate opportunities to contribute to Iraq’s educational and scientific development.

World.title: Iraq holds French ISIS suspects accountable for terrorist ties
World.content:
Baghdad – A decade ago, the Islamic State group broadcast its crimes as it recruited radicals from around the world and imposed a brutal system of oppression across swathes of Syria and Iraq.

Years on from the group’s military defeat, accused members are again in the spotlight — this time on trial in Iraq, including French nationals, for atrocities committed against the people trapped in the so-called caliphate.

Trials began in September for 47 French citizens who were transferred from Syria last year, charged with belonging to the group that controlled large parts of both countries between 2014 and 2017.

In its first verdicts handed down last week, Baghdad’s Karkh Criminal Court sentenced nine men to jail terms of up to 20 years.

A 24-year-old defendant, taken to Syria by his mother more than 10 years ago, was given 15 years. AFP is withholding his identity for legal reasons.

When the sentence was announced, the man said in Arabic: “I went to Syria, but it was my mother who chose for me. What is my fault?”

– ‘Deceived’ –

Thousands of people travelled from Europe to join IS during the war in Syria, where it declared a caliphate in 2014.

France, while repatriating hundreds of family members of jihadists, has refused to bring back most of the men accused of involvement, leaving them to face justice abroad.

Many French recruits were from disadvantaged suburbs of major cities and faced limited opportunities. They included descendants of immigrants, as well as converts to Islam.

The group imposed an extreme interpretation of sharia, forcing women and girls into sexual slavery, and jailed or killed anyone who dared speak out against its atrocities.

Fear was the group’s instrument of domination over areas where women were hidden from view and where executions were carried out by bearded militants in public squares, for all to see.

Now, the accused are now being brought to court with shaved faces, wearing orange jumpsuits.

About 1,500 French people are believed to have joined IS.

Among them was Kamel Ben Mbarek, 42, who said he had worked as a driver for the group’s Islamic police in Raqqa, in northern Syria.

“I regret it… because I wasn’t young when the organisation deceived me,” he told the court.

Driven by “anger at the abuses of the Syrian regime”, he embraced an ideology “that retained only certain passages of the Quran” — a manipulation he only realised when he read the holy book in prison.

Fewer than half of the French defendants have appeared so far.

“I regret everything I did. I’ve lost everything,” said Adel Bouaoun, 28, accused of taking part in IS operations in Syria’s Aleppo and Palmyra.

He recounted harsh conditions in Kurdish-run prisons in Syria, saying detainees had died, and described “physical and psychological torture”.

IS was defeated in Iraq in 2017 and then in Syria in 2019 by a US-led coalition.

Thousands of jihadists, along with their families, were left in Syrian prisons and camps under Kurdish command.

Earlier this year, the new Syrian authorities that came to power after the fall of Bashar al-Assad took over the prisons holding the jihadists.

The US army then transferred more than 5,700 detainees of about 60 nationalities to Iraq, including at least five French nationals.

Rights groups have criticised the judicial process, calling it rushed and saying that confessions were extracted under duress.

“This entire procedure is a form of pressure. You have recorded statements that are not mine,” Lakhdar Sebouai, 34, said in court.

Also among those awaiting trial is Adrien Guihal, who claimed responsibility on behalf of IS for the July 2016 attack in Nice, when a truck rammed Bastille Day crowds, killing 86 people.

– ‘Law of the jungle’ –

At one hearing, three defendants were visibly moved when they saw their siblings, who had come from France, for the first time in years.

The judge allowed them to speak together for a few minutes.

In October, French lawyers Matthieu Bagard and Marie Dose, who are defending many of the 47 French nationals, said the Iraqi judiciary had barred them from entering the country to attend the hearings, after they described the detainees’ treatment as “inhumane”.

The two lawyers are calling for the defendants’ repatriation to France so they can be tried there.

Two Iraqi lawyers appointed in their absence refused to speak to AFP.

“Even if his sentence is different, he was tortured like an adult and tried like an adult,” Bagard told AFP, referring to the 24-year-old taken to Syria as a child.

Observers, representatives of the French embassy and journalists are attending the trials.

Rights groups fear death sentences will be handed out.

Before the court, Thomas Barnouin, 45, whose verdict is expected November 18, recalled travelling to Syria at the start of the conflict, convinced that he had a religious duty.

But “the organisation applied the law of the jungle, not the law of God”, he said.

“We did not know that it also wanted to carry out terrorist attacks in our own country, in France,” he added.

“I reject all its crimes.”

World.title: Israel army withdraws after Hebron operation
World.content:
Hebron – Israeli troops withdrew on Monday from an area of the occupied West Bank’s largest city that they had evacuated of its Palestinian residents, following an attack that killed two soldiers in October.

The operation had emptied a neighbourhood in Hebron city where the two gunmen had lived, with soldiers later destroying their homes — a practice commonly carried out by the military as punishment for attacks.

AFP journalists witnessed residents returning to their houses on Monday after the military left, with many in disarray after having been searched by troops.

“This morning, following the completion of all operational activities, the soldiers withdrew from the area of operation in Hebron. Counterterrorism activities throughout Judea and Samaria continue,” an Israeli military official said, using the biblical name for the Palestinian territory.

On October 23, days ahead of close-fought Israeli elections, two Palestinian gunmen attacked an army checkpoint near Hebron, killing two soldiers before being shot dead in a firefight.

The attack sparked the immediate demolition of buildings in the vicinity of the checkpoint, as well as vows of a major retaliatory operation from senior officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

By the following morning, the military had cleared out the residents of the assailants’ neighbourhood, displacing more than 3,000 people, according to the municipality.

The military official said that “soldiers conducted thorough searches of multiple locations, detained and questioned suspects, and located and confiscated four weapons, several vests, and additional military equipment”.

They also demolished the two attackers’ homes and “sealed an underground space located next to” one of them.

– ‘Terrified my children’ –

On Monday morning, an AFP journalist saw that many buildings had been spraypainted with black X’s to indicate they had been cleared and searched.

Mohammad Juaaba, a relative of one of the assailants, said the top floor of the family’s home had been destroyed, adding they planned to move back into the lower floors.

Rubble from the demolition blast was strewn around the house, and other relatives could be seen cleaning up the spaces that were still habitable.

Muhannad al-Tamimi, whose house had been occupied by soldiers since the operation began, returned to a trashed apartment with furniture and clothing littering the floors, mattresses overturned and a child’s bicycle broken.

“On the morning of the operation, I was sleeping in my home. The army stormed my house and blew up the door,” he told AFP.

“They assaulted me, put a gun to my wife’s head, terrified my children, and kicked my little daughter,” he added, also accusing the soldiers of stealing gold and money.

Asked for comment, the military said it was looking into the allegations.

Reem al-Sharif, a Hebron city council member, said the operation had actually covered two neighbourhoods, telling AFP that municipal workers were helping to clean up around the area.

World.title: E-sign for SIR tribunal judges soon, can upload bulk orders on portal
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Having updated the appellate tribunal portal for Bengal around two weeks back to enable judges to rely on documents beyond the 13 listed in SIR order, Election Commission will, within this week, also replace Aadhaar-authenticated e-sign with digital signature certificate as a mandatory requirement for judges to login and upload their orders.

According to sources in EC, two more requests from SIR tribunal judges have been accepted and operationalised. The appellate tribunals platform now enables them to upload their orders in bulk, rather than one at a time. This is expected to save effort and time, given that a large number of orders passed by the tribunals in over a month were not uploaded due to the judges' reservations about Aadhaar authentication screen introduced in Sept this year.

ECINET portal would also allow judges to save their orders as drafts, enabling them to make changes before issuing the final order.

Sources told TOI EC had, nearly two weeks back, tweaked its dedicated portal for the tribunals, adding a 14th category to the list of eligible documents, namely "any other document". This now allows the judges' office to upload a document that the judge, based on their discretion, deems apt to determine a person's eligibility to be included in the electoral roll; even the electoral registration officer or the elector can upload this document on the portal, as per sources.

All SIR orders issued by EC thus far specifically state that the list of 13 documents is 'only indicative'. "DSC-based access for tribunal judges is likely to be cleared before end of this week, with the pen-drive containing the digital signatures under process," shared an EC officer.

TOI has further learnt that EC has already instructed Bengal CEO to work on the tribunal judges' demand for relocation of their offices to a more "convenient and central" location.

World.title: Marital discord no ground for termination of pregnancy: SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

Monday found itself in a predicament on an abortion plea of a woman who sought its approval for termination of her over-six-month pregnancy over the discord with her husband, who opposed the plea on the ground that he also has a right over the unborn child.

A bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan said that termination of pregnancy can be allowed in case of rape and sexual assault or if there is some problem with the foetus, but a case like the present one stood on a different footing. It questioned where society would be headed if a woman could decide to abort on the ground that she was ill-treated or abused by her husband and in-laws.

Stating that the child in the womb is because of love and the father has also a right over the unborn child, SC tried to pacify the petitioner to persuade her not to insist on abortion as the foetus is in a healthy condition.

"It is normal that wife talks against husband and husband talks against wife but it does not mean that you have to terminate the pregnancy on that ground. It is not a case of sexual assault or single woman becoming pregnant.

Where are we heading as a society if the wife says that she wants termination of pregnancy because of her fight with the husband and in-laws... What about the right of the father."

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The petitioner, with whom the bench interacted virtually, said she did not want to carry the pregnancy and she wanted a divorce.





But the husband said that he will take the child after birth and will care and pleaded with the court not to allow termination.

As the bone of contention which sparked the feud was the man's allegation about her character, the bench asked him to first file an affidavit before it to withdraw all allegations as a first step towards rapprochement. It posted the case for Wednesday.

World.title: Investment in renewable energy cushioned Iran war blow: PM Modi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi said India's economic growth has remained high despite the West Asia crisis, whose impact would have been far more serious if the country had not invested in clean energy over the past decade.

Commending India's progress in renewable energy sector, he said efforts were on to add 500GW of non-fossil energy capacity over the next 10-11 years. The PM also pitched for a "clean cooking movement" to reduce dependence on imported gas.

Speaking at the inauguration of Bharat Renewable Energy Summit at Bharat Mandapam Monday, Modi said the ongoing energy crisis had underlined the link between energy security and economic security, making it imperative for countries to reduce dependence on fossil fuels.

"This global crisis has given every country a clear message that energy security is directly linked to economic security. If we continue to remain too dependent on fossil fuels, global economy will continue to be disrupted again and again," he said.

Modi said India had already achieved nearly 300GW of non-fossil installed power capacity, accounting for more than 50% of its total capacity, and was pursuing its target of 500GW capacity by 2030.





India's clean energy sector could offer investment opportunities exceeding Rs 20 lakh crore ($220 billion) by the end of the decade as the country expands renewable energy generation, transmission infrastructure, manufacturing and energy storage. More than Rs 15 lakh crore ($164 billion) had been invested in the sector over the past decade, including Rs 6 lakh crore ($63 billion) in the last two years.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"For all of you, a new sky of opportunities is about to open up in India's clean energy sector," he said, adding it was difficult to find "political and policy stability" like India's anywhere in the world.

Referring to schemes such as PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana and PM-Kusum, Modi said India was making solar power part of citizens' lives. He called on farmers to move beyond solar pumps and become energy producers by installing panels on vacant farmland and along field boundaries. "Annadata should become Urjadata," he said.

In a push to reduce dependence on imported cooking gas, Modi urged startups and innovators to develop solutions that would enable households to use rooftop solar power for cooking. He also pitched for wider adoption of electric vehicles, with households charging them using solar power generated on their rooftops.

World.title: First in 47 years: No operational fatality in CRPF in an entire year
World.content:
CRPF records a year without operational fatalities for the first time in 47 years, with its last such death reported on October 30, 2025

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: CRPF has completed a year without a single operational fatality for the first time in 47 years, despite high-risk deployments across Jammu & Kashmir, Left-wing extremism-hit areas and Manipur."A significant milestone in the history of CRPF - 12 consecutive months have passed without any operational fatality, the last operational fatality being on Oct 30, 2025," CRPF DG G P Singh said Monday. He credited the milestone to modern hardware, better training, strategic planning and high-speed evacuation of injured personnel to medical facilities.CRPF personnel led the battle against LWE in 2026, hitting Maoists in pocket boroughs and eliminating their leadership. In Manipur, CRPF is deployed since violence broke out there in 2023. The state continues to face bouts of violence, many over the past one year..Since 1947, 2,268 CRPF men have been killed in operations, averaging over 28 fatalities a year. The highest toll was 143 in 2010, largely due to a Maoist ambush that killed 75 personnel.A CRPF official attributed zero fatalities to course-correction. Operations are planned, personnel get protective gear, and routine movements in high-risk areas are treated like operational movements.Also, 1.5 times the required force is deployed. "There was not a single casualty during Op Black Forest in Kareguttalu Hills last year, even as 21 Naxalites were killed," he added.A post-analysis found that three-fourths to four-fifths of fatalities occur days after injury. Timely medical care could prevent such deaths, the officer said, adding that air ambulances take injured personnel to advanced hospitals.This is the sixth time CRPF has recorded nil fatal casualties. The last was 24 months between Feb 1977 and Jan 1979.

World.title: Unhappy with Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth, six NCP biggies meet Amit Shah
World.content:
NEW DELHI/MUMBAI/PUNE: With BJP concerned over organisational discord within NCP, home minister Amit Shah late Sunday met senior functionaries believed to be unhappy with party president Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth, and nudged them to resolve their internal rift in the interest of the party.

The meeting was attended by NCP national working president Praful Patel, Maharashtra chief Sunil Tatkare, ministers Chhagan Bhujbal and Hasan Mushrif, and netas Dhananjay Munde and Dilip Patil. Neither deputy CM Sunetra nor Parth was present. Sunetra then called a core committee meet in Mumbai.

Sources said the dissidents' concerns remained unresolved after talks with Sunetra, Parth and his younger sibling Jay.

Days ahead will prove crucial for NCP, which is a part of the BJP-led NDA.

The rift has been brewing over what confidants of late Ajit Pawar see as Parth's attempt to push important decisions through his mother without consulting them. Ajit's sudden death in a plane crash had thrust Sunetra into the leadership. The immediate trigger appeared to be NCP's loss in the lone MLC seat it contested. The Sharad Pawar-led faction won two seats, suggesting some family loyalists may have returned to veteran's camp.





NCP leaders Praful Patel, Sunil Tatkare, Chhagan Bhujbal and others attended a meeting with Amit Shah in Delhi, amid reports of discontent over Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth's leadership

At the meeting with Shah, the group aired grievances, particularly about Parth allegedly riding roughshod over the party, with his mother allowing him to have his way.

NCP seniors, who sided with Ajit during the split with Sharad Pawar, did not criticise Sunetra. However, they resented her allowing Parth to repeatedly call the shots, suggesting she backed him, an unhappy party member said. "Having grown in a political family and married into Pawar clan, she has enough smarts not to sense the unease among seniors," he said.

Ajit's confidants at Shah's residence underlined Sunetra and Parth's isolation.

BJP believes organisational discord in NCP could help opposition, especially NCP-SP, regain ground in western Maharashtra and hurt the governing coalition. Shinde-led Shiv Sena is its third partner. Shinde, a Maratha like Pawars, could use NCP's decline to gain leverage over BJP.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Merger talks between two NCP factions were also raised at Shah's residence, sources said.

Tatkare rejected suggestions that discussions continued. "The curtains have drawn on merger issue. Even seniors of the other NCP faction have said so," he said after the core committee meeting. Hours earlier, NCP-SP MP Supriya Sule had attended INDIA bloc rally in Delhi.

Tatkare claimed there were no differences in the party. But functionaries held another meeting at Bhujbal's Mumbai residence, again without Sunetra or Parth. Chief spokesperson Umesh Patil said attempts were being made to give "unnecessary political colour" to Shah's meeting and create a false narrative of internal differences.

World.title: 'Air fares up by 700%': Don't fly, says SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday refused to urgently list a plea against steep rise in domestic air fares during Diwali season and seeking a direction to Centre to frame a mechanism to cap air fares on domestic routes during festival periods.

The issue of regulation of air fares is still pending before SC, a bench hearing the plea was informed while seeking the court's intervention. But the court turned down the plea.

Advocate Abhinav for the petitioner submitted that fares have gone up 700% amounts to a violation of Article 14 of the Constitution. "Don't travel by air," the bench said.

Centre had earlier told SC that the rules on air fares under Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, will be published in two weeks.

World.title: SC on Diwali: Crackers on Nov 7-8 in 2 time slots, and keep it green
World.content:
SC allows green crackers in Delhi-NCR on November 7 and 8 during specified hours

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Holding that Deepawali has a religious, social, psychological and emotional significance for people, Supreme Court on Monday kept the window open for bursting of green firecrackers on Nov 7 and 8 between 6am and 7am, and between 8pm and 10pm.The court had allowed bursting of crackers at the same time last year too.A bench of Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale directed police and administration to ensure polluting crackers remain out of bounds for people in Delhi, and take punitive action against those who deal in such crackers.While acknowledging Deepawali's significance, the court stressed that the right of an individual to engage in a particular practice, which may have a religious colour, was only a qualified one and not exempt from restrictions allowed by the Constitution."...Allowing the environment to degrade, which results in a health hazard to all living beings, defeats the very purpose of the festivities... All parties before us are ad idem (of one mind) on the fact that bursting of firecrackers is contributing enormously to pollution in Delhi/NCR," it said. Restriction on manufacture and sale of crackers in the national capital will continue after Diwali.The bench, however, did not favour a complete ban on firecrackers.âThough imposition of a blanket ban seems to be the ideal solution, we are of the opinion that this court, at this point in time, is short of adequate data to decide whether or not a complete ban would be the best solution to solve the problem of environmental pollution, caused by bursting firecrackers,â it said.The bench directed district collectors/commissioners, in consultation with the superintendent of police concerned, to identify and designate locations in the NCR to facilitate the sale of green crackers and banned online sale. âThe sale of firecrackers shall be strictly prohibited in any other location, other than the designated ones, including sale through online platforms,â it said.âWe direct the authorities concerned to mandate all manufacturers and traders of firecrackers in Delhi-NCR to furnish a monetary security, which shall be a handsome amount, as determined by them. The said security deposit shall immediately stand forfeited in case any manufacturer or trader of firecrackers violates any of the directions passed by this court,â the bench said.The court noted in its order that bursting of firecrackers, though constituting a religious practice meant to celebrate the occasion, would result in severe environmental pollution, especially air and noise, apart from the creation of solid waste. It said the unregulated practice affected everyone, including the end user and, among human beings, children, disabled and elderly people constituted the most vulnerable groups.âIt is not in dispute that the right to practice, profess and propagate religion conferred under Article 25(1) of the Constitution is certainly subject to public order, morality, health and other provisions of Part III of the Constitution. This court has repeatedly held that âright to lifeâ envisaged under Article 21 of the Constitution includes the right to a healthy, safe and pollution-free environment, and the said position has been crystallised and, hence, requires no repetition.Therefore, the right of an individual to engage in a particular practice, which may have a religious colour, is only a qualified one and cannot go beyond constitutional restrictions,â the bench said.It added that there shall be no manufacture or sale of firecrackers joined in series (âladisâ) and garlands. Use of firecrackers with barium and those not approved by CSIRNEERI as green crackers shall not be permitted.

World.title: SC orders trial in Ram temple donation case; SIT says Rs 2.7 crore stolen
World.content:
SC clears trial of eight accused of siphoning Rs 2.7 crore in Ayodhya Ram temple donations

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Five months after news broke of pilferage of donations at Ayodhya Ram temple, Supreme Court cleared trial of eight people, who figure in the chargesheet filed by the SIT for allegedly siphoning Rs 2.7 crore. It also gave the petitioners, who had sought probe, the status of victims of crime and allowed them to assist in the trial, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.The SIT's status report informed SC that financial and forensic examination extended to cash deposits, transactions, property purchases, construction expenditure, vehicles, jewellery, other assets, and event-related spendings. "The amount of alleged embezzlement is approximately Rs 2.7 crore," the report said.On Monday, solicitor general Tushar Mehta explained to the court the process that involved scrutiny of bank accounts and acquisition of immoveable properties by the accused, as well as examination of CCTV footage that culminated in the chargesheet Sept 23.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the trial court to proceed with the trial in accordance with law. On the large number of petitioners who had sought an independent probe into the donation theft, the bench said the petitioners can be given the status of victims of crime, and in public interest, they can assist the prosecutor and trial court in proceedings.One of the petitioners also sought a direction from SC for an âindependent, impartial, technically competent survey/demarcationâ of the land that was allotted for the temple by SC in its Nov 9, 2019, judgement.He also sought a direction to the revenue and statutory authorities to place before SC relevant records and their comparison with the site plan and actual location of the Ram Janmabhoomi Temple complex to determine if the present complex stands on the land allotted by the court.While Mehta said it is impermissible for the petitioner to seek a virtual reopening of the judgement by a fivejudge bench, the bench said if the petitioner had any grievance about the demarcation of the land, he should approach the civil court with a civil suit.

World.title: Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates: No power disruptions reported as cyclone makes landfall near Kothapatnam
World.content:
The landfall process of the Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ commenced at 1 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) near Ongole, with the observed maximum sustained wind speed of 110 kmph to 120 kmph at the landfall point.

During a teleconference, Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu also enquired about the condition of electricity poles and substations. Energy department officials informed him that no electricity poles had fallen and there were no disruptions to power supply anywhere.

As per updates received at 5.30 a.m., the landfall process is expected to be completed in another two hours. The cyclone has been moving at a speed of 9 kmph over the past six hours. Several districts are forecast to receive heavy rainfall today, including West Godavari, Eluru, Krishna, NTR, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu, Markapuram, Prakasam and Nellore districts. Prakhar Jain, SDMA Managing Director and RTGS CEO, urged people to remain highly alert.

Watch: Days after Cyclone Arnab, Cyclone ‘Murasu’ forms over Bay of Bengal

Several thatched houses collapsed and residents were stranded at Samatha Nagar in Ongole, Prakasam district, following heavy rains and strong winds triggered by Cyclone Murasu. The district administration has initiated rescue operations to evacuate those stranded. The statue of Andhra Kesari Tanguturi Prakasam Panthulu in the Prakasam district Collectorate premises in Ongole collapsed early Tuesday after a large tree fell on it due to heavy rain and strong winds.

World.title: Police foil bid to snatch smuggled gold from woman at Karipur
World.content:
MALAPPURAM

The police foiled an attempt to abduct a woman carrying 817 gm gold worth over ₹1.10 crore at Calicut International Airport, Karipur, on Monday. They also arrested two members of the alleged robbery gang.

The incident took place around 3 a.m. A police team noticed a group behaving suspiciously in the arrival area and kept them under watch. The group followed Abhirami, 27, a native of Vandanmedu in Idukki, after she arrived from abroad.

When Abhirami reached the parking area with a man who had come to receive her, the gang blocked their way and grabbed her trolley bag. The police team intervened when the gang tried to overpower the man accompanying her.

During the struggle, the accused attacked the police and bit home guard Murali Krishna. They also tried to run over a member of the police team with an Innova car while escaping. The officer narrowly escaped from being hit.

The police arrested Sayanth, 28, and Babilesh, 40, both from Kallachi, Nadapuram.

Abhirami and Harshal, 40, a native of Kochi who had arrived to collect the gold, were also taken into custody.

The police said the gold had been sent with Abhirami by Swalih, a native of Thamarassery. Around 10 people had reached the airport in two cars to seize the gold and abduct her.

A search of Abhirami’s baggage led to the recovery of 14 gold plates concealed inside an emergency lamp. The gold weighed 817 gm after cleaning and is estimated to be worth more than ₹1.10 crore.

The gold, along with ₹67,000 allegedly kept to pay Abhirami for carrying it, a car and the two people detained in connection with the gold, were handed over to the Customs Department for further action.

The police said the arrested men had been involved in several similar cases. One of them had lost a hand in a blast.

World.title: No power disruptions reported as Cyclone Murasu makes landfall near Kothapatnam in Prakasam dist.
World.content:
Cyclone Murasu made its landfall near Kothapatnam in Prakasam district, close to Ongole, at 1 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), and was expected to complete its landfall process by 6.30 a.m., Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu was informed during a review with district Collectors and officials at 3.30 a.m.

The Chief Minister directed officials to ensure that people in cyclone-affected areas did not venture onto roads and to take all necessary precautions to prevent loss of life and minimise property damage. He also enquired about the condition of electricity poles and substations. Energy department officials informed him that no electricity poles had fallen and there were no disruptions to power supply anywhere.

Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates

During the teleconference, Collectors briefed him on the ground situation and relief measures. Bapatla district Collector reported heavy rainfall, particularly in Repalle, Chirala and Vetapalem, and said two fallen trees had been cleared immediately.

Nellore Collector Himanshu Shukla said seven fallen trees had been removed and moderate rainfall was prevailing in the district. Prakasam Collector P. Raja Babu said officials had responded to reports of fallen trees at five locations.

Krishna district Collector reported heavy rainfall in Avanigadda and Nagayalanka. In Guntur district, rainfall was recorded in all mandals, but no incidents of electricity poles or trees falling were reported.

NTR district Collector G. Lakshmisha said light showers were occurring at several places. Officials had inspected the Budameru area and found no immediate threat. As a precaution against possible landslides at Mogalrajpuram, some families had been shifted to relief camps.

The Collectors also informed the Chief Minister that arrangements were being made for counting votes in the local body elections alongside cyclone relief operations.

World.title: Cyclone Murasu nears A.P. coast, heavy rain alert issued
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh government sounded an alert in five districts – Bapatla, Palnadu, Markapuram, SPSR Nellore, and Prakasam – as the severe cyclonic storm, Murasu, stayed on course to make landfall between Ongole and Nellore on the intervening night of November 2-3.

The storm is expected to bring very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall to these districts, which reported a rain deficit during the monsoon.

Keep track | Cyclone Murasu Live updates: Cyclone Murasu landfall expected between Nellore and Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh tonight

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the storm is likely to move with a “wind speed of 100 to 110 kmph (and) gusting up to 120 kmph between Nellore and Narasapur”.

In the wake of Marasu, heavy rain fell in the northern districts of Tamil Nadu bordering Andhra Pradesh from Sunday evening, and some parts of north Chennai reported waterlogging.

In Odisha, where rain triggered by Cyclone Arnab caused widespread damage last week, the government evacuated 1.6 lakh people across Ganjam, Gajapati, Malkangiri, Koraput, and Kandhamal districts.

The IMD said the storm was located about 80 km east-northeast of Nellore, 80 km east-southeast of Kavali, 110 km southeast of Ongole, 140 km south of Bapatla, 170 km south-southwest of Machilipatnam, 170 km northeast of Tirupati, and 190 km north-northeast of Nungambakkam in Chennai.

The system is moving towards the coast at 12 kmph, and gales of 70-90 kmph, gusting to 100 kmph, have been reported along the Andhra Pradesh coast. A storm surge is expected in coastal areas to the north of the landfall point, the IMD said.

IMD, Amaravati, issued a red alert for Palnadu, Tirupati, and Nandyal districts on Tuesday, and an orange alert is in place for 12 districts.

In Chennai, as the cyclone’s outer bands brushed Tamil Nadu’s northern coast, the Regional Meteorological Centre upgraded weather alerts for northern districts such as Chennai and Tiruvallur on Monday (November 2, 2026). It warned of squally winds, gusting up to 75 kmph, in various northern districts, including Chennai and Kancheepuram till Tuesday (November 3) morning.

Even as the system moved closer to the coast, there was no major rainfall activity in the central, south-coastal, and Rayalaseema regions until 7:00 p.m. on Monday (November 2). However, northern Andhra, where no alerts were sounded, recorded light to moderate showers.

The impact of Murasu is expected to be less severe than that of Arnab, a very severe cyclonic storm, and the State is focusing on efficient water management.

With 8,000 electricity poles likely to be affected, 31,000 electricity poles have been dispatched from Srikakulam to Krishna district. In addition, 1,000 personnel are expected to reach from Chennai to assist in power restoration works.

The National Disaster Response Force’s 10th Battalion has deployed 14 teams across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana to coordinate with local officials and undertake emergency response and rescue operations.

(With inputs from Satyasundar Barik in Bhubaneswar and K. Lakshmi in Chennai)

World.title: U.S. Supreme Court rejects Trump administration push to set aside thousands of California ballots
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Monday (November 2, 2026) rejected a push for California to set aside thousands of mail ballots from people President Donald Trump's administration claims are non-citizens, a decision that comes on the eve of the pivotal midterm elections.

The high court refused to intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state's voter rolls.

It was the latest in a flurry of election-related litigation the day before the midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress for the last two years of Trump's second term.

In California, the Trump administration had asked the high court to set aside the challenged ballots until the voters' citizenship status could be verified. But officials there said that the list appeared to be filled with errors and that setting the ballots aside could effectively disenfranchise legal voters.

The high court did not detail its reasoning, as is common in emergency decisions. The justices previously rejected Trump's push to restrict mail ballots around the country in September, even though the justices have sided with his administration in a series of other emergency docket appeals.

The Republican Trump administration has prioritized identifying noncitizen voters this year, despite them being rare.

A district court judge previously denied the Justice Department's request and warned that the demand could disenfranchise citizens in Tuesday's midterm elections to determine control of Congress.

Also on Monday (November 2, 2026) in Washington, another federal judge ruled against the administration's efforts to make last-minute demands of California election officials, finding they violated the Constitution. “The Executive Branch has likely violated the Constitution's Elections Clause, which commits authority over election rules to the states and Congress alone,” wrote Chief Judge James Boasberg.

The administration, for its part, said segregating the ballots was a modest request that would eventually allow legal votes to still be counted.

The administration has faced a remarkable string of losses in court in its push, as well as criticism for waiting until a few weeks before the election to make its demands of California election officials with a list that even the Department of Justice admits is not entirely reliable.

During a hearing over whether to lift her own order forbidding the administration from threatening to prosecute election workers who let potentially illegal voters cast ballots, District Court Judge Trina Thompson drilled down on reports of widespread inaccuracies in the Justice Department's data.

“Would you agree there's a high error rate?” Judge Thompson asked Kenneth Kao, a Justice Department attorney.

“That's a fair statement,” Mr. Kao said. “That's why we ask for the registrars' aid in verifying these are all valid voters.”

At the same time, Bill Essayli, the federal prosecutor running the Justice Department's Los Angeles office, said at a news conference he was highly confident the people on the list were not entitled to vote.

“This isn't speculation. This isn't a theory,” Essayli said, later conceding there may be errors on the list.

Voting has been underway in California since early October. All of the state's roughly 23 million registered voters are mailed a ballot. Hundreds of thousands of ballots have already been processed. California election officials have said that finding and setting aside the challenged ballots now would be logistically impossible.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta, a Democrat, said the appeal “reeks of desperation and is another attempt to undermine our elections and trample on the rule of law.”

Lower courts have sided with the state, with a district judge warning that segregating ballots would “wreak havoc” on the midterm elections and erode trust in the democratic process.

“If the Executive can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger,” wrote U.S. District Judge David O. Carter, who was nominated by President Bill Clinton, a Democrat.

A 2-1 appeals court panel upheld his order, with one judge appointed by Mr. Trump and another appointed by President Joe Biden, a Democrat, voting in favor. The third judge on the panel, also appointed by Trump, argued in a dissent that California's unwillingness to separate the ballots encourages the “violation of federal law.”

The Justice Department has sought to move the case along quickly, unsuccessfully asking an appeals court to intervene early.

World.title: Cyclone Murasu brings deluge to parched Prakasam district
World.content:
As the Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ over the Bay of Bengal began to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast near Kothapatnam, around 20 km from Ongole, at 1 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), it brought very heavy rainfall to the two districts of Prakasam and Bapatla overnight.

In one night, the overall rainfall deficit of Prakasam district, which stood at a little over 64% as of November 2, came down to 58.6%.

Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates

Between 8.30 a.m. on Monday (November 2, 2026) and 12 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), there was a lull in the rainfall activity in districts that were likely to be affected by the cyclone. However, as the storm began moving closer to the land, many weather stations in Central A.P. and South Coastal A.P. received received very heavy rainfall of around 200 mm within six hours.

According to the Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES), which provides realtime weather information in all 688 mandals of the State, as of 6 a.m., Naguluppalapadu recorded the maximum of 198.01 mm rainfall, followed by Kothapatnam at 182.25 mm, Acharya N. G. Ranga Agricultural University area in Bapatla district recorded 128.53 mm, Chirala recorded 124.1 mm, Bapatla town recorded 119.75 mm.

Narsapuram of West Godavari district, where the Very Severe Cyclonic Storm made the landfall, recorded 109 mm rainfall. Ongole Urban recorded 106 mm rainfall and Chilakapadu of Prakasam district recorded 104.5 mm rainfall. West Godavari and Krishna districts also recorded moderate showers during the night.

Meanwhile, the landfall process is likely to continue till 9 a.m. The storm may move north-northwestwards and weaken gradually into a cyclonic storm by noon and further into a deep depression by Tuesday midnight. But, the A.P. State Disaster Management Authority(APSDMA) has alerted the public as gale winds may continue in Prakasam and SPSR Nellore districts till noon.

According to reports, vehicles have been stopped in the early morning hours on a highway near Ongole, due to gales of speed reaching 90-100 kmph. (There are two highways, not sure which yet).

A storm surge warning has also been given, as a surge of 1.0-1.5 metres height above astronomical tide is expected to inundate low-lying areas along the coastal line in the districts of Bapatla and Krishna.

A red alert is in place for the districts of Tirupati, Nandyal and Palnadu for Tuesday (November 3, 2026) and an orange alert for 11 other districts.

World.title: Coimbatore Corporation plans AC bus shelters at two locations on pilot basis
World.content:
Coimbatore Corporation plans to establish air-conditioned bus shelters at two bus stops in the city on a pilot basis under the public-private partnership (PPP) model.

The proposed locations are the P.N. Pudur bus stop and the bus stop near Avinashilingam Institute on Mettupalayam Road. The Corporation is currently preparing a Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the project.

The proposed shelters, measuring 20 ft by 12 ft, will have air-conditioning, Wi-Fi connectivity and facilities to display bus routes and real-time bus arrival information. They will also have seating arrangements, ramps and other accessibility features to facilitate the use of shelters by persons with disabilities and other passengers.

The two bus stops were selected considering the passenger footfall, particularly the number of students travelling to and from educational institutions in the vicinity. The availability of adequate space to construct the shelters was also taken into account.

The Corporation plans to implement the project under the PPP model. The pilot initiative is expected to help assess the feasibility of providing similar passenger amenities at other busy bus stops in the city.

World.title: Activists raise concern over Supreme Court order on green firecrackers, traders lament stock availability
World.content:
The Supreme Court’s decision on Monday (November 2, 2026) to allow green firecrackers on November 7 and 8 has raised concerns over its implementation, with environmental activists questioning how the restrictions can be enforced at such short notice and traders warning that the limited window leaves them little time to procure stocks.

Over the years, both complete or partial bans on firecrackers have been openly flouted by people in the national capital.

In 2019, when only green crackers were allowed and several months were given to prepare for implementing it, Delhi still saw the decision being openly flouted and also there was a lack of stock in many shops.

Later, the Delhi government moved to a complete ban, including green firecrackers, for a few months around Diwali, but that too was flouted on a large scale.

Last year, the Supreme Court passed a order similar to this year, lifting the ban temporarily to allow green firecrackers to be burst for a fixed window of time for two days during Deepavali. But this ban was also openly flouted and the air turned toxic with many air quality monitoring stations in Delhi being unable to record the level of air pollution as they maxed out.

“Unless there is a blanket ban on firecrackers, people will burst all types of firecrackers in the city. We have seen that over the years, including last year. Even after the ban was reimposed after Deepavali last year, people continued to burst firecrackers for marriages, concerts and everything else in Delhi,” said Bhavreen Kandhari, an environmental activist.

“There are no green firecrackers available in the market. Also, who will check on the ground, and how, what type of firecrackers people are bursting? The air will be toxic again after Deepavali,” she added.

Difficult to procure, sell

Rajiv Kumar Jain, 68, a member of the Delhi Fireworks Traders Association, said traders welcomed the court order but were concerned that the short notice would leave them with little time to procure sufficient stocks of green firecrackers.

“Our permanent licences have been suspended, and we need to get them reinstated tomorrow. We can sell only on November 4, 5 and 6. That leaves us only one day to get the firecrackers from the manufacturers, which is very difficult,” Mr. Jain said.

“Last year, too, we were allowed to sell for only three days, but we were allowed to sell on Chhoti and Badi Deepavali. This year, however, we are not allowed to sell on either Chhoti or Badi Deepavali,” he added.

The firecracker ban has also been politically contentious. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) repeatedly criticised the Aam Aadmi Party government, which was then in power in Delhi, over the restrictions. After coming to power last year, the BJP government approached the Supreme Court, seeking permission to allow green firecrackers.

World.title: US votes today in midterms that could weaken Trump’s hold on Washington
World.content:
Americans deliver their verdict on Donald Trump’s tumultuous second presidency on Tuesday in midterm elections that threaten to shatter his grip on Washington, with Democrats poised to seize the House and challenge for control of the Senate.

Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Trump’s legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. A Senate defeat would also threaten his ability to appoint Supreme Court justices and senior officials.

The election amounts to a nationwide judgement on Trump, with the mood turning sharply against Republicans amid anger over soaring living costs and the war on Iran.

All 435 House seats and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are at stake, along with governorships in 36 states. Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands.

Trump returned to office last year promising to bring down prices, but inflation, tariffs and fuel costs inflated by the Middle East conflict have squeezed Americans.

The 80-year-old’s approval rating has hovered near the low 30s.

In the suburbs of Atlanta, Georgia, retired teacher Jane Callum, 77, was among Democrats canvassing for Senator Jon Ossoff who framed the race as a watershed moment for the country’s future.

“I really feel an obligation to do everything that I possibly can to change the direction that our country is going in now, and put it more on the path to democracy and away from autocracy,” she told AFP.

Economic discontent

Republicans insist that Trump’s tax cuts and immigration crackdown will benefit Americans and they are portraying Democratic candidates as left-wing radicals.

But in his final public campaign appearance Monday, Trump barely touched on the economy and spent most of the time in a rambling talk about his problem-plagued renovation of Washington’s Reflecting Pool.

“This is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime,” he said, 26 minutes into the speech, before quickly returning to talking about renovations.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer branded it a “pathetic closing message.”

Some Republican supporters remain confident.

“We’re going to win. As a matter of fact, we’ve probably already won,” Texas military veteran Yvonne Clouser told AFP.

But while Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority, the battlefield is extending into conservative states like Kansas, Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska.

Democrats must also defend competitive seats, including in Michigan, where a bitter internal dispute saw congresswoman Haley Stevens endorse Republican Mike Rogers rather than the Democratic nominee, Abdul El-Sayed.

Decision Desk HQ’s final forecast forecasted 241 House seats for Democrats against 194 for Republicans, and a narrower 52-48 Democratic Senate majority.

Disputed results?

Polls can underestimate one party’s support, and Republicans hope their voters turn out in force on Election Day.

More than 57 million Americans had already voted early before Tuesday, indicating the high energy.

The campaign has attracted more than $11 billion in political advertising, while billionaire Trump ally Elon Musk has poured hundreds of millions of dollars into Republican political efforts.

As soon as polls close, concerns will mount over whether results will be accepted by the Republicans.

Trump, who tried to overturn his 2020 election defeat, has repeatedly alleged widespread voter fraud and accused Democrats — with no evidence — of cheating.

The Justice Department, run by a close Trump ally, has already sued to potentially block certification of Alaska’s Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses, although a court ruled against the effort on the eve of the election.

And the Supreme Court rejected on Monday an emergency bid to force California to set aside the mail-in ballots of more than 20,000 people on the grounds they may not be American citizens.

Trump, who will watch the midterms results at the White House on Tuesday night, signalled that if he does lose control of Congress he could simply defy Democrats.

“I veto everything,” he told a podcast on Monday, although he said he might strike deals with Democrats eventually.

World.title: Govt slashes high-speed diesel price by Rs7.76 per litre, petrol by Rs3.40
World.content:
The government on Monday slashed the price of petrol by Rs3.40 per litre, and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7.76.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs374.51 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs395.20.

The prices are applicable for Nov 3 (Tuesday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

However, under a new arrangement, oil refineries would contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a monthly cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This would allow a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price on consumers’ end.

“The [petroleum levy] impact on estimated total country volume of Rs. 14.71/litre shall be surrendered by refineries @ Rs49.02/litre on their sales to [oil marketing companies],” reads a document by Ogra.

The government announced the arrangement during a press conference in Islamabad, held by Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar.

“I am grateful to all the refineries that saw the public is in difficulty and with the government’s help … increased their throughput,” Malik said, adding that these refineries had made profits from this throughput in the last three months.

“They were requested to take a step to support the public during this difficult time, and I am glad that they listened to us … the Rs15 increase that was coming in the petrol prices on Friday, they helped the government with that. Because of that, we were able to maintain the price.”

On Oct 27, Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad to discuss his party’s demand to provide relief to the public by abolishing the levy.

The two sides agreed to form a joint committee of the JI and the government to consider the expansion of the ongoing fuel relief scheme , being offered to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc since Sept 17 .

For his part, Rehman declared that his party would march to Islamabad in protest of the petroleum levy in mid-November if the government did not announce any major relief by then.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Additional input by Khaleeq Kiani

World.title: Govt enlists oil refineries to shield citizens from global price hikes
World.content:
The government said on Monday that oil refineries would bear a burden of approximately Rs15 billion each month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than what it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

The statement came at a press conference in Islamabad addressed by Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar.

Addressing the conference, Malik said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had made efforts to meet with oil refineries and consult with them regarding interventions to ensure that people got the cheapest petrol amid impending steep fuel price increases, including an increase of about Rs15 that would have taken effect on Friday.

“I am grateful to all the refineries that saw the public is in difficulty and with the government’s help … increased their throughput,” the minister said, adding that these refineries had made profits from this throughput in the last three months.

“They were requested to take a step to support the public during this difficult time, and I am glad that they listened to us … the Rs15 increase that was coming in the petrol prices on Friday, they helped the government with that. Because of that we were able to maintain the price.”

He added that more improvement would be seen by the public, expressing his gratitude to the refineries for standing with the government to provide assistance to the public during a time that had caused everyone difficulties — even the government as it struggled to procure oil at increasing prices.

As a result of this step, he highlighted, a load of approximately Rs15 billion a month would be borne by these refineries, allowing petrol to be sold at a rate Rs15 per litre cheaper than what it would be in the international market.

He expressed his hope that the crisis in the Middle East would soon move towards a peace agreement and that the government could advance with its purposes of “taking the system towards improvement, deregulation and refinery upgrades”.

“The government doesn’t want to be cruel to anyone,” Malik stressed, saying that it intended to take actions “with consultations, keeping the public’s interests in mind, in a fair way”.

He added that before the crisis, the premium of the refineries was $5 per barrel, and even today a $20 limit had been established. He further said that the government would have to step in and protect the public in case of further difficulties.

Tarar also addressed the conference, noting that the premier’s vision “from the first day” had been to put as little burden on the country as possible.

He said that even though the situation in the Middle East had affected every economy, including that of Pakistan, “our macroeconomic indicators have remained largely stable — Pakistan’s economy hasn’t taken as much of a hit as other countries”.

Regarding Friday’s situation, when petrol prices were increasing in the international market, he said that PM Shehbaz had directed refineries to absorb the price hike in order to prevent the Rs15 increase.

“During this difficult time … I think this is a great effort, as a result of which the public has been saved from this difficulty,” the information minister said.

He also discussed the fuel subsidy scheme announced by the premier on Sept 13, saying: “If you told me two months ago that there would be a scheme in which, upon SMS registration, motorcycle users get a weekly concession of Rs500 on petrol, and 800cc car users, every 10 days, get 10 litres of petrol for Rs100 less per litre, then I would have told you that it’s probably not possible to implement such a scheme.”

He praised PM Shehbaz’s “will power, intent and empathy for the public” that served as the foundation for the scheme.

Tarar highlighted that the number of unique users who had registered for the scheme had now crossed 15 million. He said that about Rs27bn had so far been allocated towards this relief and highlighted its success.

“This is a unique relief that is not available in the rest of the world,” he said, referring to both the fuel subsidy scheme and the steps taken by the government to prevent the increase in prices on Friday.

Answering questions, Malik said that he was the “biggest advocate for deregulation” and for bringing competition into sectors, seeing it as the way to protect people’s welfare and deliver good service.

However, he pointed out, “Have you seen any incident in the last 50 years that has been happening in the last six to eight months? What rules-based order do you want to adopt in the middle of this disaster?”

He stressed that once the crisis in the region ended, the government would make efforts to return to deregulation; however, currently the focus was on public relief.

The two ministers also stressed that there was no fuel shortage and that the country’s needs were being met even during difficult times. Malik said that November’s supply was fully covered, while decisions would be taken on supplies for the winter months of December and January and the prime minister had directed any necessary steps to be taken to ensure supplies.

The price of high speed diesel has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

The government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

As of July, fuel prices are now fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices.

World.title: PTI lawyer Salman Safdar says he met Imran, Bushra Bibi at Adiala jail
World.content:
PTI lawyer Barrister Salman Safdar on Monday said he met with party founder Imran Khan and his spouse, Bushra Bibi, at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail, where they are both incarcerated.

Imran has been in prison since Aug 5, 2023, while his wife was arrested on Jan 17, 2025 in a separate case in which the couple were sentenced.

The IHC has allowed Imran twice-a-week meetings — on Tuesdays and Thursdays — with his family, lawyers and other associates. Despite multiple court directives, Imran’s meetings with his family and party leaders have been largely restricted in recent months.

In a post on X on Monday, Safdar said the meeting was his first with Imran after seven months and with Bushra in 11 months.

The last time he met Imran, the Supreme Court designated him as amicus. However, this time he met Imran Khan as his lawyer.

It lasted 40 minutes and was “insufficient to cover all cases [and] legal matters”, the PTI counsel contended.

“Both briefed me on their health conditions [and living] conditions and gave Fresh instructions for some legal matters and cases,” he wrote on X.

PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram told Dawn that he spoke to Safdar in detail.

“Salman told me that the meeting was held in connection with a number of applications which have been filed in courts to arrange meetings with Imran Khan,” he said.

“Salman has told me that he reached Adiala Jail at around 4:30pm and the meeting continued for around 40 to 45 minutes. However, he said that it was not sufficient time for the meetings, as there were so many cases which had to be discussed and as the meeting was being held after such a long time.“

Replying to a question, Akram said that no political issues were discussed during the meeting, which he added was also attended by Bushra Bibi. Safdar spoke about the cases and asked about future strategy.

When asked about Imran’s health, Akram replied that although health issues were discussed, the PTI would only speak about the legal cases.

Barrister Safdar’s last publicly reported meeting with Imran was held on April 8 this year, a day after the Islamabad High Court (IHC) directed authorities to arrange the meeting.

His previous meeting on Feb 10 with the former premier was also on the directives of the Supreme Court, where concerns about Imran’s health were raised.

Imran’s eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January. While he has undergone eye procedures at the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), his family demands that he be shifted to a hospital of his choice.

The government and the opposition have been engaged in a blame game , with the latter accusing the former of a lack of transparency on the matter, of not ensuring appropriate treatment for Imran, and of not allowing his personal physicians access to him. The government denies these allegations.

Imran was sent to jail for a three-year term on Aug 5, 2023 for concealing details of Toshakhana gifts. However, he and Bushra are also serving a 14-year sentence in a £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case .

The couple were convicted in another Toshakhana case in December 2025, with 10-year and seven-year terms handed to them. The PTI founder also faces pending trials in terrorism cases related to the May 9, 2023 riots .

Imran’s sisters Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan, along with opposition leaders, have staged frequent sit-ins outside the Adiala jail demanding the PTI founder’s release.

They remain unable to stage more sit-ins since their detention in late September under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, as the PTI geared up for a protest march to Islamabad.

World.title: At Kazakhstan forum, Pakistan presents Karachi and Gwadar ports as 'strategic gateways' for Central Asian trade
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan can serve as an important trade and transit corridor for the landlocked Central Asian countries, providing them with access to international maritime trade routes and global markets, Minister for Board of Investment (BoI) Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh said on Monday.

He made the remarks while addressing the opening session of the Second Tianshan Forum for Central Asian Economic and Quality Investment, being held in Kazakhstan’s Almaty.

The minister termed Pakistan’s three major seaports — Karachi Port, Port Qasim and Gwadar Port — “strategic gateways that could facilitate regional trade, strengthen transportation links and provide alternative routes for the movement of goods”, according to a press release by the BoI.

Sheikh particularly underscored Karachi’s importance as Pakistan’s major industrial and commercial hub, noting that its established industrial base, business infrastructure, financial institutions and port facilities offered significant opportunities for trade, industrial partnerships and foreign investment.

He also highlighted Gwadar’s potential to further strengthen regional connectivity and economic cooperation.

Regional connectivity was “not merely about linking roads, ports and markets, but also about connecting economies, creating investment opportunities, generating employment and building shared prosperity across the region”, he remarked.

The minister invited regional and international investors to explore opportunities in key sectors, including energy, infrastructure, logistics, transportation, manufacturing and trade. He emphasised that improved connectivity and reliable energy supplies were essential for unlocking the region’s economic potential, the BoI statement said.

Highlighting the importance of regional cooperation, the minister acknowledged the contribution of the Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (Carec) Programme in promoting transport connectivity, facilitating trade and supporting economic integration among participating countries.

He observed that Carec provided a valuable platform for strengthening economic partnerships between Pakistan and Central Asian states, the statement said.

The minister emphasised that Pakistan’s strategic geographical location, youthful population, industrial capacity and seaport infrastructure positioned the country to play an important role in connecting Central Asian economies with international markets.

The Second Tianshan Forum will conclude in Almaty on Tuesday under the theme “Strengthening Resilient Connectivity and Quality Investment in Central Asia”.

According to information provided in its official agenda, the two-day forum is a follow-up to the success of the inaugural Tianshan Forum for Central Asia Economic Cooperation, and is aligned with the new Carec Institute Strategy 2026–2030, as well as the Carec 2030 Strategy Midterm Review Rolling Implementation Action Plan.

“In 2026, the Carec region continues to face a highly uncertain external environment. Rising geopolitical tensions have raised energy and food prices, disrupted transport and logistics, and weakened the reliability of trade corridors,” the agenda said.
