World.title: Araghchi outlines Iran's seven-day plan for potential negotiations with US
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 3. The agenda for potential negotiations between the United States and Iran will be based on the terms of a seven-day plan previously proposed by Tehran, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in a post on his Telegram channel.

"The plan currently under consideration is, in fact, an initiative originally put forward by Iran, known as the 'seven-day plan.' It sets out Iran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Under the proposal, if these conditions are met, the strait would be reopened on the sixth day, while negotiations between Iran and the United States would resume on the seventh day," Araghchi said.

He recalled that the plan had been presented in New York during a session of the UN General Assembly.

Elaborating on its provisions, the minister said that the United States was required to take a number of steps on the first day, while the Strait of Hormuz was to be reopened by the second day, with shipping volumes restored to their previous levels.

According to Araghchi, the commitments expected of Washington are outlined in the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding.

He noted that, under Article 9 of the document, the United States must refrain from imposing new sanctions on Iran and increasing its military presence in the region.

"We demand that all new sanctions imposed since the signing of the memorandum be lifted, or that the size of the armed forces be reduced to its previous level. Furthermore, the issue of ending the blockade is also on the agenda," the Iranian foreign minister said.

Araghchi also noted that the discussions included previously envisaged concessions concerning petroleum products. The remaining terms, he added, are set out in a written document submitted by Iran.

World.title: The neutral capital: Could Ashgabat become a channel for U.S.-Iran de-escalation?
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 3. The International Conference and Exhibition on the Development of Construction, Industrial, Chemical and Energy Sectors of Turkmenistan (CIET 2026) will be held in Ashgabat on November 3-5. It will bring together more than 800 delegates from over 55 countries, including representatives of government agencies, international investors, financial institutions, industrial enterprises and technology companies. The program includes bilateral B2B and B2G meetings, providing foreign companies with an opportunity to engage directly with Turkmen government agencies and enterprises, assess the country's investment potential and explore prospects for commercial cooperation.

Against this backdrop, Ashgabat is welcoming representatives of two countries whose relations are at the center of the international agenda - Iran and the United States. On November 2, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi arrived in the Turkmen capital at the head of a delegation comprising diplomatic, economic and parliamentary representatives. A visit to Ashgabat by S. Paul Kapur, U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs, is scheduled for the same period. According to the U.S. side, he will visit Ashgabat and London from November 2 to 9. In Turkmenistan, he is expected to meet with business representatives to discuss opportunities for expanding U.S. investment and commercial activity. A practical component of this engagement will be the U.S.-Turkmenistan Business Council's business mission, scheduled for November 4-5 and organized in coordination with the U.S. Department of State alongside the annual bilateral consultations. Thus, both visits coincide with CIET, which provides foreign companies with a platform to hold discussions with Turkmen government agencies and potential business partners.

The economic dimension of the Iranian visit is reflected not only in the stated agenda of Araghchi's talks. On October 28, Ahmet Gurbanov, Deputy Foreign Minister of Turkmenistan, met in Ashgabat with Hamid Ghanbari, Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister for Economic Diplomacy. The sides discussed the development of trade and economic ties, as well as cooperation in energy and industry. During the meeting between the two foreign ministers on November 2, they also addressed bilateral cooperation alongside regional and international issues. For Tehran, Turkmenistan is important as a neighboring market and a partner in energy and cross-border logistics, as well as a participant in transport routes linking Central Asia with Iran and, further, the Persian Gulf.

U.S. engagement with Turkmenistan has also become more systematic. In May, the Turkmen-American Business Cooperation Association (TABCA) was established in Washington D.C., and its first business forum brought together more than 50 companies from the two countries representing logistics, e-commerce, information technology, education, consulting and services. That same month, an event dedicated to Turkmenistan's economic development and prospects for expanding trade and investment cooperation with the United States was held at the headquarters of the International Monetary Fund. It brought together more than 80 participants, including the ambassadors of both countries, representatives of the U.S. Department of State and Department of Commerce, the World Bank, the IMF, business associations and the private sector. Another notable political signal was the meeting held at the White House on May 29 between U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Turkmen Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov. The sides discussed trade and economic cooperation, energy, transport connectivity and the diversification of routes for Turkmen gas exports.

Washington's interest is not limited to its bilateral relations with Ashgabat. Through the C5+1 format, the United States is developing cooperation with all five Central Asian countries, addressing regional issues related to energy, transport infrastructure, critical minerals, digital technologies and investment attraction. These areas were included in the agenda of business sessions held during the meeting of Central Asian foreign ministers with the U.S. Secretary of State in Samarkand on October 19. In this context, Turkmenistan is important to the United States as a potential participant in broader regional projects, particularly in energy, transport connectivity and the diversification of trade routes.

The coincidence of the Iranian and U.S. visits with CIET 2026 takes on an additional diplomatic dimension amid the ongoing confrontation between Washington and Tehran and efforts to find ways to resolve it. Public statements by the leaders of both countries in recent days indicate that the diplomatic track remains open, despite harsh rhetoric and the continuing risk of further escalation. Asked by reporters about the progress of negotiations with Iran on October 31, U.S. President Donald Trump said: “They're going fine.” He added, however, that Iran “makes a deal and then backs out,” before concluding: “They wanna make a deal. We'll see if they make a deal.” U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio also confirmed that contacts were continuing, stating: “There are multiple talks; talks have actually never stopped. There's been active conversations going, both - in some cases directly but often through intermediaries. And the President's preference in any challenge around the world is to try to solve it diplomatically and peacefully, if possible.” Thus, Washington has publicly confirmed that negotiations are continuing, including through intermediaries, and expressed a preference for a diplomatic settlement, although this does not eliminate the differences between the two sides.

On the Iranian side, President Masoud Pezeshkian said on November 2, during a meeting with governors and mayors of major cities: “We are trying to resolve the issue through dialogue; in this matter, the Supreme Leader has also granted the government certain authorities.” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, commenting on diplomatic efforts during his visit to Ashgabat, reported that intensive contacts were continuing through Qatari and Pakistani intermediaries. “We have stated our specific conditions and presented our prepared plan. Now everything depends on how much political rationality prevails on the American side and whether there is a willingness to choose the reasonable path of diplomacy,” the minister said. Thus, both sides have publicly confirmed that the possibility of a diplomatic settlement remains open, although their positions on the conditions and sequence of further steps remain substantially different.

Against this backdrop, Ashgabat finds itself at the center of coinciding diplomatic activity involving two countries whose relations remain highly strained. Turkmenistan's status of permanent neutrality, its geographical location and its accumulated experience in multilateral diplomatic formats allow the country to be viewed as a potentially important venue for regional diplomatic engagement. This role received additional political and legal recognition in the Ashgabat Declaration, adopted on December 12, 2025, at an international forum marking the 30th anniversary of Turkmenistan's permanent neutrality. In paragraph 11, the participants encouraged the effective use of the territories of neutral states for peace negotiations and conflict resolution, and also noted Turkmenistan's proposal to establish a Chamber of Mediation for Peace on its territory under the auspices of the United Nations. A similar approach is reflected in the third operative paragraph of UN General Assembly Resolution 79/274 of March 21, 2025. At the same time, the UN document stipulates that the proposal to establish such a Chamber remains subject to consideration by UN member states and the Organization's system. This provides an international normative basis for Ashgabat's potential role in mediation. Whether the coincidence of the visits could lead to any practical diplomatic developments remains an open question.

The significance of a possible diplomatic settlement extends far beyond U.S.-Iranian relations. One of the main factors behind the conflict's global impact is the situation around the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for oil and liquefied natural gas supplies. According to the International Energy Agency, an average of around 20 million barrels of oil and oil products passed through the strait daily in 2025, accounting for approximately one-quarter of global seaborne oil trade. The strait also carries around 19% of global LNG supplies. The consequences of disruptions are already being felt in global energy markets. On November 2, Sultan Ahmed Al Jaber, CEO of the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC), said that global oil inventories had fallen by nearly one billion barrels since the beginning of the crisis, while transportation and logistics costs had risen from 5% to 30% of the cost of a barrel. Further escalation could therefore increase pressure not only on energy markets but also on international trade, supply chains and inflation, he noted.

Efforts to find diplomatic mechanisms for resolving the crisis are not limited to Qatar and Pakistan, through which contacts between Washington and Tehran are currently being maintained. Oman, which previously hosted direct U.S.-Iranian negotiations, remains interested in playing a mediating role. At the same time, China's diplomatic engagement has intensified. On November 2, Chinese President Xi Jinping discussed the situation with Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq, while Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi held separate meetings with representatives of Iran and Saudi Arabia, urging the parties to seek a political solution. Beijing also announced an upcoming visit by its special envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia. The expansion of diplomatic channels shows that resolving the crisis is viewed as a task affecting the interests of a broad range of countries. In this context, Turkmenistan's neutral status and its readiness to provide a venue for possible peace talks could represent an additional diplomatic resource.

Thus, the assumption that the coincidence of the U.S. and Iranian delegations' visits to Ashgabat could have an additional diplomatic dimension is based on a combination of circumstances: ongoing contacts between Washington and Tehran through intermediaries, intensified international efforts to find a way out of the crisis, and Turkmenistan's role as a neutral state willing to facilitate peaceful dialogue, as recognized in international documents. This would not necessarily require a direct meeting between representatives of the two countries in the Turkmen capital. Potential contacts could take place through the Turkmen side or other intermediaries, even if the U.S. and Iranian delegations are not in Ashgabat at the same time. Of course, there is currently no confirmation of any such contacts, and the coincidence of the visits alone does not prove that an arrangement of this kind exists. Nevertheless, a legitimate question arises: could Ashgabat, which is welcoming representatives of both countries amid ongoing diplomatic efforts, become another channel for seeking ways to de-escalate the U.S.-Iran confrontation?

World.title: Explosions reported on the Iranian island of Qeshm
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 3. At least five explosions have been heard on Iran's Qeshm Island, located in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has announced that it captured two US surveillance drones and shot down another.

The causes of the explosions remain unknown. Further details are expected to be released later.

"The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has reported the capture of two US surveillance drones and the downing of another unmanned aerial vehicle," the statement said.

World.title: Azerbaijani chess player Mahammad Muradli places eighth at KazChess Masters
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 3. Azerbaijani chess player Mahammad Muradli is having a difficult run at the KazChess Masters international tournament in Almaty, Kazakhstan.

The grandmaster, who entered the competition as its highest-rated participant, is currently eighth among 10 players after eight rounds.

Muradli, rated 2662, has scored 3.5 points, recording two wins, three draws, and three defeats.

Belarusian grandmaster Denis Lazavik leads the standings with 6 points. Russia's Daniil Dubov and Uzbekistan's Shamsiddin Vakhidov share second and third places with 5.5 points each.

Muradli is therefore 2.5 points behind the tournament leader.

The round-robin tournament will conclude on November 3. In the final, ninth round, the Azerbaijani grandmaster will face Daniil Dubov.

World.title: Vance says progress made in US-Iran talks aimed at ending conflict
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 3. Some progress has been made in negotiations between Washington and Tehran aimed at ending the conflict, U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance has said.

Speaking to reporters at Andrews Air Force Base near Washington, Vance noted that the two sides had held a series of productive consultations.

"We have had useful consultations with the Iranian side. I also spoke with U.S. President Donald Trump about this issue approximately an hour ago," he said.

According to the vice president, the negotiations have yielded some progress, but both sides intend to continue their efforts to achieve more substantial results.

"Both the president and I are quite optimistic about the prospects of reaching an agreement through negotiations. We will continue working toward that goal," Vance emphasized.

It should be recalled that U.S. President Donald Trump previously said he did not intend to resume military operations against Iran immediately after the November 3 midterm congressional elections.

He also expressed confidence that Washington and Tehran could reach an agreement to end the conflict.

World.title: Uzbekistan, US discuss expanding cooperation in artificial intelligence at Seattle forum
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 3. An international forum aimed at strengthening Uzbek-American cooperation in artificial intelligence was held in Seattle as part of Seattle AI Week.

The event brought together around 60 representatives from the technology, education, business, and government sectors.

The forum was organized by the Consulate General of Uzbekistan in Seattle, the American-Uzbekistan Chamber of Commerce (AUCC), IT Park Uzbekistan, and the World Digital Technology Academy (WDTA).

Participants included professionals from Microsoft and Meta, executives of AI companies, representatives of Harvard University, the University of Washington, and Northeastern University, officials from the Seattle city government, and representatives of innovative technology companies.

Discussions focused on opportunities for establishing partnerships between US and Uzbek companies and organizations. Particular attention was paid to training young professionals in digital technologies, supporting startups in entering international markets, and leveraging artificial intelligence to address practical challenges.

A separate session was dedicated to the application of AI in areas directly affecting people's daily lives and the development of urban infrastructure. Participants explored the potential of emerging technologies to improve water resource management, enhance municipal services, and strengthen road safety.

Following the forum, the Consulate General of Uzbekistan in Seattle and WDTA signed a framework memorandum of understanding aimed at fostering cooperation among experts, universities, and companies from the two countries.

The parties also agreed to explore joint educational initiatives and opportunities to implement pilot projects in Uzbekistan.

The forum provided a platform for identifying practical areas of Uzbek-American cooperation in artificial intelligence, education, and digital technologies.

World.title: Chronicles of Victory: November 3, 2020
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 3. The Azerbaijani Army launched a counter-offensive, later called the "Iron Fist" operation on September 27, 2020 in response to the large-scale provocation of the Armenian armed forces on the frontline.

The 44-day Karabakh War put an end to nearly thirty-year-occupation and resulted in the restoration of Azerbaijan’s territorial integrity.

Trend presents the chronicle of the 44-day Karabakh War.

- Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev and Russian President Vladimir Putin held phone talks.

- The Armenian armed forces were forced to retreat by sufferinglosses.

- During one day the list of the destroyed military equipment of the Armenian armed forces was announced.

- Armenia violated the ceasefire regime on the state border.

- The Azerbaijani Army has a full advantage over the Armenian armed forces.

- Another UAV of the Armenian armed forces was destroyed.

- The Armenian armed forces fired at Azerbaijan’s Fuzuli district by using Smerch multiple launch rocket system.

- The reconnaissance and sabotage group was destroyed in the direction of Azerbaijan’s Zangilan district.

- A video footage showing the destruction of two more ammunition depots of the Armenian armed forces near Khankandi city has been released.

- The Armenian head of regiment fled, but the servicemen went missing.

- The commander of the Armenian armed forces’ tank battalion was killed, several tanks were destroyed as a result of explosion.

World.title: US official confirms strikes on Iranian targets in Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
The US has conducted strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz, according to a US official.

Iranian state television reported that explosions were heard on Qeshm Island, which is an Iranian island in the strait.

The official, who was not authorised to comment publicly and spoke on the condition of anonymity, said the US had targeted "Iranians using surface-to-air missiles against US assets".

Qeshm Island is in the Strait of Hormuz. (AP: Asghar Besharati)

The strikes, which appeared to be limited as opposed to a full return to hostilities, came on the eve of the crucial American midterm elections.

President Donald Trump has previously said the US would not launch strikes on Iran before the midterms.

The unpopular Iran war and the resulting impact on US fuel prices and other parts of the economy has been a vulnerability for Republicans as they try to keep control of Congress.

Vice President JD Vance told reporters earlier on Monday, local time that he had just spoken to Mr Trump about talks with Iran and said that "the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement".

AP

World.title: This Samoan superman is the World Cup's greatest comeback story
World.content:
As he prepares to lead his nation into a World Cup semifinal against Australia, sometimes Ronald Volkman still can't believe this is happening.

He'd have settled for one NRL game this year with Parramatta and after what he's been through, that really would have been enough.

But instead the best season of his budding career will continue when he lines up for Samoa against the Kangaroos with a World Cup final berth up for grabs, standing on the shoulders of giants with the whole rugby league world watching.

It still feels more like a fantasy than a reality for the 24-year-old, even as he's living it.

"I didn't see myself playing NRL and I didn't see myself playing for my country, in a World Cup, on the biggest stage," Volkman said.

"I grew up watching this, I'm still pinching myself that I got to get on these fields.

Ronald Volkman will start in the halves for Samoa against Australia this weekend. (Getty Images: Cameron Spencer)

"The players in this team, you look left, you look right, you see guns. It gives you so much confidence in what you can do and that you can take it to the next level."

It has been a long journey. It was only a few years back that Volkman thought his football career was over.

Bad shoulder and hip injuries in 2023 scuppered a move from the Warriors to St George Illawarra the following season, sending Volkman to rock bottom in a full year out of the sport.

The physical pain was such that Volkman could barely move and without the game he loved he lost his way.

He stopped training and put on weight. He didn't know himself and when he was out and about, he'd pull his hood up so nobody would know him.

Mates would reached out to support him, but Volkman often ignored them, trapped in a downward spiral with a heart set on suffering, haunted by football dreams he could barely remember.

At his lowest depths, he leant on the things that mattered most to him.

Ronald Volkman's career and life fell apart after he left the Warriors. (Getty Images: Brendon Thorne)

"A big one for me was my faith. I fell down to that faith, my God, my loved ones, my family and my partner family," Volkman said.

"They were there for me during those tough times and it'd be slack for me not to take the opportunity I've had this year and showcase my talent, not for myself but for my loved ones.

"They've been through it as much as I have."

There's a lot of loved ones to repay.

Volkman is one of eight siblings and Samoan on both sides of the family. Growing up they'd go back to the islands every second year.

His father, Tas, wept tears of joy when his son debuted for the Warriors in 2022 and did so again when Volkman made his rugby league return in a pre-season trial for Parramatta last year.

Volkman did the same during the Samoan anthem on Sunday night but Emeline, Tas's mother, doesn't give as much away.

She still lives in Samoa, in a village called Vaitele Tai in the western outskirts of Apia, where she watched her grandson come on against Tonga and score a key try.

Loading Instagram content

Volkman played the final 27 minutes after Chanel Harris-Tavita strained his hamstring while kicking for goal, sparking a Samoan revival that just fell short despite the Toa outscoring Tonga four tries to three.

"I got rattled in the ribs early and struggled to breathe for about five minutes, but it's so good to be out there with my usos (brothers)," Volkman said.

"The first thing I thought was about Chanel. You never want to see a teammate go down like that and to me the way to honour him, to show respect, was to get on and do a job.

"He did a pretty good job for the majority of the game and it made my job easy."

Ronald Volkman has rebuilt his NRL career with Parramatta this year. (Getty Images: Darrian Traynor)

Volkman's play — the sharp feet, quick hands, a nose for the tryline and a big shot on Tongan backrower Siua Wong — would have been familiar to any Parramatta fans in the record-breaking crowd.

He made his NRL return for the Eels last year and just getting back at all and having his shoulder hold up was a blessing, even if they lost the two games by a combined total of 88-24.

This season, with the highly-rated Jonah Pezet arriving for one year, Volkman didn't expect to play any first grade.

But instead he relieved the injured Pezet in Round 6 and never looked back, playing every game for the rest of the season and signing a new two-year deal with the Eels in September.

He finished the year a blue and gold fan favourite, with Volkamania running wild among the Parramatta faithful.

In 2027 he'll act as a back-up to Mitchell Moses and Jarome Luai, but the latter has already had an impact on Volkman through Samoa camp.

"He's given me confidence to do what I do," Volkman said.

"The way he trains and prepares himself during the week is relentless.

"He's such a competitor but that's all I can say, because if he hears this he'll think I love him."

Tonga and Samoa can be Origin for the new century The scale and spectacle of Tonga's Rugby League World Cup win over Samoa was not just an instant classic, it proved a demand for this clash that rugby league must find a way to supply.

But before Volkman and Luai are club teammates they will be brothers in arms against Australia, starting in the halves together as the masters of Samoa's chaos.

A win over the Kangaroos would be a glittering prize at any time but with a World Cup final berth on the line the stakes are even higher it shapes as the biggest night of Volkman's career.

It would be Samoa's second and Volkman remembers watching the first four years ago and dreaming of being a part of it. Now, against all odds, that dream is real and the best could still be yet to come.

"I'd just started my first pre-season with the Warriors and it was mind-blowing, to see Samoa on the biggest stage," Volkman said.

"We have the chance to do it again next week, so let's do it. I can't wait."

World.title: North Korea denies role in Binance heist as customers withdraw billions
World.content:
North Korea has denied US allegations that it was behind the $US6.3 billion ($9 billion) heist of cryptocurrency exchange platform Binance as "absurd rhetoric" and proof that Washington remained hostile towards the country.

In a statement published by North Korean state media, Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of leader Kim Jong Un, denied the country was responsible for carrying out last week's hack, thought to be the largest financial heist in history.

Who is behind world's largest crypto heist? Almost $9 billion in cryptocurrency was hacked from exchange company Binance, but who was behind the attack?

Ms Kim also warned the country had "issues to reconsider" over US hostility.

"The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK as a 'cyber criminal state,' claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organization 'supported' by the DPRK was involved in the incident," she said in the statement.

"But the US assertion is absurd rhetoric and nothing new.

"It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads international public opinion as if all the cyber crimes in different parts of the world are our deeds."

On Saturday, the FBI accused a North Korean state-sponsored unit known as TraderTraitor of carrying out the hack and stealing billions in crypto.

The FBI says North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit TraderTraitor is behind the heist. (Pexels: Tibe De Kort)

The US bureau said it had observed TraderTraitor converting stolen assets into a cryptocurrency called Ethereum and expected it to launder the assets further.

"The FBI maintains its commitment to protecting the virtual asset community by identifying, mitigating, and disrupting North Korea's illicit cybercrime and virtual asset theft activities," a statement read.

Cybersecurity experts said North Korean hackers were among the world's most prolific crypto thieves, with the proceeds used to help fund the country's weapons programs.

North Korea has denied all allegations of its links to cryptocurrency theft and other cybercrimes.

Ms Kim said North Korea would reconsider unspecified issues in light of the "very unpleasant US hostile attitude".

It comes as Pyongyang remains silent on US President Donald Trump's offers to resume US-North Korea summit diplomacy.

Experts have indicated Pyongyang may be weighing its options.

Customers withdraw billions

Binance customers withdrew about $US4.64 billion ($6.6 billion) worth of assets after the company lifted its temporary suspension on Sunday.

Zhao Changpeng is the founder and CEO of Binance, which has moved to reassure its users following the hack. (Reuters: Benoit Tessier)

"Between 06:00 and 15:30 UTC on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion," the company said on X.

"Our team continues testing rigorously the remaining networks and assets.

"Rest assured that market conditions are stable."

The company said it had recovered 90 per cent of the stolen assets by using company money.

Reuters/ABC

World.title: Ditching the shame as a sex worker living with a disability
World.content:
In my unconventional body, I chose unconventional work — sex work.

At first, it was all about earning money, but I quickly realised that it was the best kind of work for me.

I have a genetic connective tissue disorder, hypermobile Ehlers Danlos Syndrome (hEDS), making everyday activities difficult.

Over the past two decades, sex work has worked for me more than any other career.

My origin story

I started sex work as a single mum, struggling to arrange and pay for care for my four school-aged daughters while I worked shifts as a nurse.

I enjoyed both jobs, but was worried about stigma and our safety so I kept sex work a secret for 21 years.

Back in 2003 when I started sex work, I could earn more between the hours of 9am and 3pm on any given day than I ever could for a full week of night shifts on the ward.

Over time, my disability became more challenging, and the physicality of the work became impossible.

Sex work became my primary income.

I'm not the only sex worker with a disability

I feel privileged to share my personal story of juggling multiple professions with sole parenting.

It wasn't easy and for most of my life, the sex work has been just as invisible as my disability.

Hilary is passionate about destigmatising sex work. (Supplied: Hilary Caldwell)

I know a lot of sex workers who live with disabilities.

The autonomy and the flexibility of shorter work hours for more income makes it attractive.

For me, sex work brought financial independence despite remaining single and being refused NDIS.

If you were at any of the gym or Pilates classes I go to, you might consider me athletic.

At the age of 60, all my joints are loosey goosy. It's made sex work a lot more fun!

Not so much fun however, is the pain and dysfunction caused by having faulty and too-elastic connective tissues in my muscles and joints, gut, blood and lymph vessels, as well as in my skin.

The benefits of sex

Experiencing the ongoing effects of hEDS has made me especially grateful for sex work.

Sex exercises the muscles around my rusty and too-loose hip joints. Strength is my treatment plan.

Does scheduling sex improve intimacy? The concept can be helpful for couples who need to make time and space for intimacy, but it doesn't always hit the mark. Here's why.

Good sex provides a natural endorphin rush and pain relief. It's taught me about my body.

Even the orgasms I have at work act like chemical boosts to my sense of wellbeing, connection and care.

I have biologically enhanced and real affection for my long-term clients.

Enjoying my body sexually has re-enforced my libido like a life force.

Sign up to the ABC Lifestyle newsletter Get a mid-week boost and receive easy recipes, wellbeing ideas, and home and garden tips in your inbox every Wednesday. You’ll also receive a monthly newsletter of our best recipes.

Some of my work is with clients who also have disabilities.

Working with disabled clients helps me appreciate my abilities. I know all too well the benefits of feeling pleasure in bodies that often hurt and don't function efficiently.

Living through the loneliness epidemic also helps me remember the importance of loving human touch and increases my compassion for all people.

Ditching the stigma

Growing up, I was encouraged to be modest.

On most days I pass for a heteronormative, educated, feminine woman.

But when I'm seen as a "polyamorous queer whore", as I like to describe myself, I have been refused services and suffered embarrassing comments from professionals.

Being on the receiving end of slut-shaming has helped me notice how we are all indoctrinated to feel shame about sex, and that different genders are shamed in different ways.

It has only been two and a half years since I came into my power and came out in my book Slutdom: Reclaiming Shame-free Sexuality.

Hilary became fascinated with the way society treats sex workers. (Supplied: Hilary Caldwell)

Like many women, I have also suffered violence from men. Unlike other women, I have been harmed because I am a sex worker and not so much while working as one.

I remember the times I felt that my modesty and invisibility would keep me safely protected by men.

But I’ve discovered that I draw power from sexual pride and it funds my independence – even with a disability.

I didn’t start sex work because of my disability.

It is only now that I have come to appreciate how working in sex has minimised the effects of hEDS.

Keeping myself as fit as an athlete for work has turned into an investment. Pleasure in my skin reduces pain and helps me sleep.

Nowadays, I really do enjoy being known as a GILF (granny I love to to *), providing GFE (girlfriend experiences).

Dr Hilary Caldwell is a sex worker, sex researcher and writer living in Canberra/Ngunnawal and Ngambri Country.

World.title: David Jones facing 'alarming' financial speculation just before Christmas
World.content:
Iconic department store David Jones is being forced to defend its future viability, as the Australian retailer faces speculation about store closures and misses a crucial filing deadline.

The department store's key lender has already chipped in extra cash before Christmas to allow David Jones to stock up before the busy festive season.

Hilco Capital would not confirm the amount but the ABC understands it to be about $10 million.

Do you know more? Email our journalist on terzon.emilia@abc.net.au or em.terzon@proton.me

"Hilco remains supportive of the business and any inference otherwise is false," the lender said in a statement.

The ABC has confirmed that David Jones just missed a deadline to file its most recent financial year reports to the corporate regulator, ASIC.

Meanwhile, there is ongoing media speculation that the retailer is going to call it quits on several stores inside Westfield shopping centres.

It currently has 38 stores nationally.

David Jones is owned by private equity firm Anchorage Capital Partners.

A spokesperson for that Australian firm said it would not comment on speculation.

But the spokesperson noted David Jones was reviewing its store network and was in discussions with stakeholders to put itself "on a viable financial footing".

David Jones's future is unclear. (ABC News: Fletch Yeung)

A key union that represents retail workers, the Shop, Distributive and Allied Employees Association (SDA), said it was reaching out to workers at David Jones informing them of their rights if the retailer went under.

"The reports of David Jones' predicament are alarming," the SDA noted in a statement.

It is understood at least one major fashion brand has pulled some of its stock from David Jones amid concerns the retailer could not pay its bills.

Suppliers have also already been put on extended terms this year to give David Jones more time to pay for stock.

David Jones was first founded as a corner shop in Australia in 1838 and today has multi-level department stores across Australia that sell everything from cosmetics to shoes and fashion.

Its main rival is the ASX-listed Myer, which early last year voted to merge with Solomon Lew's apparel brands Just Jeans, Jay Jays, Portmans, Dotti and Jacqui E.

That merger was billed as a way for Myer to keep relevant in a changing retail landscape, where younger generations are increasingly shopping online or opting for second-hand apps such as Depop.

World.title: Lindsay Clancy lawyer urges judge to dismiss case or put it back on trial
World.content:
Lindsay Clancy's lawyer has urged a judge to either dismiss the murder charges against her or put her back on trial.

Warning: This story contains details that may be distressing for some readers.

A hearing held on Monday, November 2, in Plymouth, Massachusetts, marked the second time Ms Clancy has been in court since a mistrial was declared, after jurors were unable to agree whether she was legally responsible for killing her three young children.

In September, the jury was split 11-1 in favour of acquittal.

Ms Clancy's defence team moved to dismiss the murder changes on double jeopardy grounds, arguing the conditions for declaring a mistrial were not met.

Under US law a mistrial can only be declared if every other option to proceed has been exhausted.

Ms Clancy's lawyers argued the judge should have removed a juror who favoured conviction, and then allowed jury deliberation to continue.

Judge William Sullivan did not immediately rule on Monday.

Ms Clancy's lawyer, Kevin Reddington, implored him to decide quickly.

He also pressed the Plymouth District Attorney, Timothy Cruz, to reveal whether he plans to try Clancy on murder charges again.

"I am not going to have this woman sit incarcerated for the next year, or two or three," Mr Reddington said.

" I want a trial and I want it with you and I want it this spring. "

Judge Sullivan scheduled another hearing for November 16, and the prosecution said it intends to retry Ms Clancy if the case proceeds.

He also suggested a new trial could be held in March next year.

What happens to Lindsay Clancy now?

Mr Cruz is yet to announce whether prosecutors would ‌retry Ms Clancy on first-degree murder charges, which carry a mandatory sentence of life in prison without parole if she were ‌convicted.

Prosecutors have several options before them, including seeking her conviction on lesser second-degree murder charges, which would give her the option to waive a jury trial and proceed before ‌a judge.

Ms Clancy has been held in a state psychiatric hospital in Massachusetts before and during trial and would remain in custody through a second trial.

Kevin Reddington has urged the court to investigate a juror he accused of being untruthful. (AP: Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger )

Clancy lawyers argue case should have been dismissed

Ms Clancy's lawyers argued a mistrial could have been avoided had the judge been more thorough interrogating jurors about their breakdown in deliberations.

The jury's foreperson sent two notes indicating that a lone juror, Michael Desronvil, wasn't following the court's instruction to follow the rules regarding reasonable doubt.

After receiving the notes, Judge Sullivan spoke with each juror, reminded them of their duties and explained what constitutes reasonable doubt. He asked whether they could apply the law to the case, and all said yes.

Judge William Sullivan suggested a new trial could be held in March 2027. (AP: Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger)

Mr Reddington urged the judge to investigate Mr Desronvil, who he accused of being untruthful on his jury questionnaire and improperly using his phone during jury deliberations.

Judge Sullivan told Mr Reddington to stop using the juror's name in open court; he had placed a standing order to seal the names of the jurors to protect them from abuse.

However a number of jurors, including Mr Desronvil, had done interviews in the media, which led Mr Reddington to say that the juror's name "was all over the internet".

"Why don't we all dial this back a little bit," Judge Sullivan said.

Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague said the judge had struck the right balance.

"It is clear from the record this juror did not refuse to deliberate. He refused to agree," Ms Sprague said.

Jennifer Sprague said during the hearing the judge found the right balance in his directions to jurors. (AP: Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger)

Mr Desronvil said in an interview he was certain of Ms Clancy's guilt, but other jurors wouldn't listen.

His lawyer, Heather O'Connor, urged the judge on Monday not to investigate his conduct any further, saying he had simply done his duty as a juror.

She also disputed the allegations of improper phone use.

"If that's enough to put a juror under oath, to search their phone, to pull their history, then the lesson [for] every future juror in this Commonwealth is simple: Agree with the majority or potentially be investigated," Ms O'Connor said.

ABC/Wires

World.title: Shadow health minister sponsoring access for gambling group boss
World.content:
Ministers are sponsoring passes to lobbyists seeking to influence them directly, with Labor and Liberal MPs also providing access to gambling lobbyists, according to the first disclosures of who has direct access to politicians at Parliament House.

For the first time the public has been able to see which federal politicians are providing access for lobbyists to parliament, following a decision by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to tighten access and disclosure rules earlier this year.

Among the first tranche of disclosures are two passes for gambling lobby group Responsible Wagering Australia, which represents bet365, Sportsbet, Betfair and others, and has been co-sponsored by Labor and Liberal MPs.

Shadow Health Minister Anne Ruston is the primary sponsor for Responsible Wagering Australia's chief executive Kai Cantwell, while Labor senator Raff Ciccone sponsors its other pass, with Senator Ruston also a secondary sponsor.

Kai Cantwell was previously chief of staff to Anne Ruston before becoming head of the peak gambling body. (ABC News: Dave Sciasci)

Mr Cantwell was the former chief of staff to Senator Ruston while she was minister for families and services.

Senator Ruston declined to comment.

Several cabinet ministers have also been revealed to be pass sponsors, granting access to lobbyists seeking to directly lobby them on portfolio issues.

Energy Minister Chris Bowen and Industry Minister Tim Ayres are sponsors of Benjamin Oquist, former executive director of progressive advocacy group The Australia Institute, who now leads climate advocacy at lobbying firm DPG Advisory Solutions.

Ben Oquist, whose partner is Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young, is granted access to parliament house by Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen and Industry Minister Tim Ayres. (ABC News: Stuart Carnegie)

Finance Minister and Minister for Women Katy Gallagher is the sponsor for the National Foundation for Australian Women, a feminist group advocating for gender equality.

Greens leader David Shoebridge is the only political party leader in the first tranche of disclosures to provide a pass, which he gave to the Australian Peace and Security Forum, a group seeking to dismantle the AUKUS agreement.

Gas lobbyists employed by wide range of Labor and Coalition MPs

Pass sponsorship is not necessarily an endorsement of that lobbyist's views.

For example, One Nation senators Malcolm Roberts and Sean Bell, Shadow Treasurer Tim Wilson and Shadow Communications Minister Sarah Henderson are the sponsors for Digital Defence, a group that supports the government's Digital Duty of Care laws to make social media giants responsible for online harms, despite those MPs all being opposed to the reforms.

Several gas lobbyists are sponsored by Labor MPs, even as the sector lobbies against the government's proposal to require gas producers to reserve supply for Australian consumers first.

Canberran MP David Smith is a sponsor for gas lobby group Australian Energy Producers, while Victorians Jana Stewart and Sarah Witty are sponsors for Hawker Britton Group, which counts Woodside and ConocoPhillips among its clients.

MPs say they're outnumbered by lobbyists Inside Parliament House, hundreds of lobbyists freely roam the corridors advocating for corporate interests. Critics say it's a problem.

Labor MPs Rob Mitchell, Mr Smith, Joanne Ryan and Tony Sheldon also sponsor passes for Hawker Britton Group, while Dan Repaholi and Shadow Energy Minister Dan Tehan are sponsors for Alinta Energy, and South Australians Steve Georganas and Tom Venning are sponsors for Adelaide-based gas producer Beach Energy.

American oil and gas giant ConocoPhillips also directly engages at least one lobbyist, whose pass is sponsored by National MP Colin Boyce and Labor MP Mike Freelander.

The first Sponsored Access Card report provides only a peek behind the curtain of who has access to the nation's decision-makers, with just over 100 passes detailed, and the Department of Parliamentary Services admitting it still has a backlog of 1,086 cards issued under the previous system that require new assessment and processing under the updated rules.

Mr Albanese announced changes to access for lobbyists in June following a review, setting out new disclosure requirements, and changes to what areas of parliaments lobbyists could access.

Call for National Lobbying Act

The Australian Democracy Network says the new rules still leave out as many as 80 per cent of lobbyists, who are not required to join the lobbyist register because they are employed "in-house" in government relations roles by companies, rather than operating as a formal lobbyist with corporate clients.

Its senior campaigner Christian Slattery said there were gaps around who lobbyists were engaging with.

"Australians still can't see the full picture," Mr Slattery said.

"The new transparency system doesn't give meaningful information to the public about who our elected representatives are meeting with, when they're meeting them, or why.

"Australia needs a National Lobbying Act that applies the same rules to all people engaging in professional lobbying, requires proactive ministerial diary disclosure, and establishes an independent regulator."

Independent senator David Pocock said those lobbyists should be brought into the fold, and the "revolving door" of exiting MPs and staffers joining industries they previously regulated should be ended.

"More transparency over lobbying passes is a hard-won win for the community, the result of sustained pressure from right across the country. It also shines a light on the cosy relationship between industries like gambling and gas with the government," Senator Pocock said.

"The government needs to finish the job of reforming our broken lobbying laws. That means strengthening the lobbying code, extending it to every lobbyist, closing the revolving door between government and the industries it regulates, and bringing in penalties that bite."

World.title: Trump's not on the ballot, so what does he have to do with the midterms?
World.content:
Voters across the US are at the precipice of a major date on their electoral calendar — the midterm elections.

Millions of Americans are heading to the polls to elect hundreds of members of Congress in a campaign already marked by threats of interference and even party infighting.

The results will largely be seen as a referendum on Donald Trump's presidency and could determine how much power he wields in the second half of his term.

Let's dive into what's at stake and how the results could shape the 2028 presidential election.

What are the midterm elections? Why do they matter?

The midterms mark the middle point of a president's four-year term when Americans elect their representatives in Congress.

The Congress is made up of two chambers — the House of Representatives and the Senate.

All 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 of the Senate's seats are up for election.

Of the 50 US states, voters in 36 of them will also be electing their next governor to four-year terms.

The Republican Party, also known as the Grand Old Party or GOP, currently holds a slim majority in both the House and the Senate, so we're in for a tight race.

The cardinal rule with the midterms is that the incumbent party, in this case Trump's Republicans, typically lose ground, while the opposition party that isn't in power historically gain seats.

For Democrats these elections therefore offer a chance to take back congressional power.

The results will determine who controls Congress, which passes federal laws that impact the lives of hundreds of millions of Americans.

If Democrats retake the House it will set the stage for two years of clashes and serve as a major roadblock on Trump's agenda.

Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed's campaign in Michigan is a test of whether the insurgent left can win in a purple state. (Reuters: Rebecca Cook)

How many seats do Democrats need to take control of Congress?

All 435 seats in the House are up for grabs but only 40 are considered to be competitive races.

Democrats need a net gain of three seats to take the House, which means just a handful of races could dictate who controls the chamber.

The Senate is a different story. It's made up of 100 seats, 35 of which are up for election.

Only about 12 of them are considered competitive with the rest in either reliably Republican or reliably Democratic states.

About one third of the Senate and all of the House of Representatives is up for election. (Reuters: Elizabeth Frantz)

Republicans currently hold the Senate with 53 seats, while Democrats and independents hold 47 seats.

Democrats need to pick up four Senate seats to reach 51 to take control of the upper chamber.

Republicans can afford to lose a maximum of three seats and still win the Senate with 50 seats. That's because in a 50-50 Senate the vice president, currently Republican JD Vance, can cast a tiebreaker vote.

That makes the Senate race more of an uphill battle for Democrats than the House race.

Could Democrats retake the House? What happens then?

The short answer is yes. Analysts and prediction markets currently tip the Democrats to win the House.

If Democrats win the House they will make it much harder for Trump to advance his agenda.

A Democratic-controlled House would also bring more aggressive oversight of the Trump administration with more investigations, subpoenas and congressional hearings.

The president could also face another effort to impeach him if the Democrats gain ground in the midterms.

What has changed since the last election?

A lot has changed since Americans last voted, including the maps used to decide who represents them in Congress.

Congressional maps have been redrawn in 10 states in a process known as redistricting.

Usually that happens every 10 years, but when Texas redrew its map to favour Republicans it set off a domino effect in other states, sparking fights over political representation and voting power.

A showdown in Texas could shape the future of Trump's presidency Texas is the site of a massive political showdown that could have a direct influence on US President Donald Trump's ability to continue his agenda. Here's a basic breakdown of what's going on.

The Cook Political Report estimates Republicans have gained a net five additional seats from the redistricting battles, potentially giving them an advantage before a single vote is cast.

There have also been major Federal and Supreme Court rulings that advocates say have weakened the Voting Rights Act — the landmark legislation designed to prevent racial discrimination in voting.

Voting rules have become a major flashpoint, particularly over voter eligibility and access to mail-in ballots.

How does Donald Trump fit in to all this?

Presidents are not elected in the midterms and Trump is not on the ballot, but he will dominate the contest.

Despite record low approval ratings in national polls, the president is positioning himself as the Republican party's best asset.

He and his advisers have suggested he's the only person who can mobilise the MAGA faithful and help Republicans avoid steep losses in an election cycle with historically low voter turnout.

In early September, Trump headlined a first of its kind Republican midterm convention which was dubbed "Trump-a-palooza", putting himself dead centre of the party's campaign.

His message to voters is that although his name won't appear on the ballot, his administration, legacy and agenda will be at stake.

The Republicans are at risk of losing control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. (AP)

The president has also weighed into most congressional races across the country, issuing political endorsements for his preferred candidates, which have overall proved to be influential.

For Democrats, Trump and his policies offer an obvious campaign target. They are framing the midterms as a chance for voters to check his power and push back on his agenda.

What could the result mean for the 2028 presidential election?

A strong midterms result will shape America's political landscape ahead of the 2028 presidential race.

A big win for the Democrats would give the party momentum heading into 2028 and a much stronger platform to challenge Republicans on.

Loading...

If Republicans retain control of the House and Senate it will strengthen the Trump administration's ability to pursue its agenda and could put the party on the front foot in the lead up to 2028.

Either way, the results will offer an early sign of voter sentiment, and a glimpse at the issues and candidates that could drive the 2028 contest.

Governor races will be also be closely watched for potential presidential contenders, as a strong performance in the midterms would raise their public profile in either party.

World.title: Laptops down: Year 5 NAPLAN tests return to pen and paper amid backlash against devices
World.content:
NationalVictoriaEducation Laptops down: Year 5 NAPLAN tests return to pen and paper amid backlash against devices Alex Crowe November 3, 2026 — 1:41pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Year 5 students will return to pen and paper for NAPLAN tests in Victoria from 2028 after education ministers agreed to scrap online testing in primary schools in response to declining academic results. Education ministers decided to return to handwritten testing for the cohort amid a growing backlash against classroom technology, with some advocates of limiting device use arguing the reversal does not go far enough. Year 5 students will now join year 3 students and take the tests by hand, but whether years 7 and 9 students will take the test offline hasn’t been decided. All primary school NAPLAN participants will use pen and paper from 2028. Justin McManus Australia recorded its worst result in the most recent Programme for International Student Assessment, with the global test revealing Australian students spent an average of 2.6 hours a day on digital devices, compared with the OECD average of 1.7 hours a day.



NAPLAN results also reveal about a third of Australian students are failing to meet literacy and numeracy benchmarks. The Heads Up Alliance, a growing community of parents lobbying against digital devices, said scrapping online testing for year 5 students was just a start. Related Article Education ‘Humans were built to learn from other humans’: The schools capping screen time Ahead of the education ministers’ meeting on Monday, the alliance wrote to every minister, reminding them that tens of thousands of parents and teachers had signed a petition calling for the restoration of handwriting as a core education policy. “Changes to year five NAPLAN are a start,” they said in a statement. “But stay with us; with your continued support, there’s a lot more to achieve.”



NSW Education Minister Prue Car is pushing for years 7 and 9 NAPLAN to also be pen and paper tests. “The evidence from our classrooms points clearly to the ongoing value of handwriting and its importance for student development and engaging a different way of learning,” she said. “We’re listening to teachers and families who want a sensible, balanced approach to technology use in schools.” Victoria has led the way in reducing digital device use and banning mobile phones in public school classrooms. From the start of the 2027 school year, students at all government, Catholic and independent schools will also be required to have personal devices, including smart glasses, phones and smartwatches, switched off and stored during school hours.



State school pupils in years 3 to 6 will also be restricted to 90 minutes of screen time a day from next year, while pupils in prep to year 2 will have minimal exposure to devices. Teachers at state secondary schools will be required to plan device-free learning, although time limits won’t be enforced. Victorian Education Minister Gabrielle Williams said she supported the shift to pen and paper testing for year 5 pupils and would consider her position on years 7 and 9 students making the shift, alongside her interstate colleagues. “Victorian students are the best in the nation in NAPLAN – and we support these changes that will help lift results even further,” she said. World.title: ‘Oh God, so it’s all my fault’: Albanese and King Charles joke over travel backlash
World.content:
WorldEuropePolitical leadership ‘Oh God, so it’s all my fault’: Albanese and King Charles joke over travel backlash David Crowe Updated November 3, 2026 — 1:40pm ,first published November 3, 2026 — 9:02am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

St John’s, Antigua and Barbuda: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has hit back at critics of his overseas travel as he joked with King Charles about the number of times he was asked why he was attending this week’s Commonwealth summit in the Caribbean. With the Coalition arguing he should not be overseas, Albanese acknowledged the economic pressures at home and insisted the government was working “each and every day” to lift living standards. Loading But Albanese also shared a light-hearted exchange with the King about the political attacks. The prime minister responded to media questions on Monday morning by arguing it was in Australia’s interest to be at the Antigua summit, before adding: “At the personal invitation of King Charles, of His Majesty, I agreed to come to this meeting.”



A few hours later, Albanese met the King and told him that he had been asked “why are you here?” and chosen to name the King as one of the reasons. The remark was caught on video and microphone as the two spoke at the launch of an environmental initiative. “I said because His Majesty invited me,” Albanese told the King about his remark to the media. The King replied: “Oh God, so it’s all my fault – oh, no.” He made the remark with a smile. Anthony Albanese mingles with King Charles and Andrew Forrest at the Commonwealth summit in Antigua. Jenny Magee While he joked with the King about the political dispute, Albanese sharply rebuked Opposition Leader Angus Taylor and others in the Coalition for saying he should not go to the summit – known as the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) – because of economic news at home.



“They often quote John Howard as their oracle, and on this John Howard is right,” Albanese said. “Australia is a participant in the Commonwealth, and at the personal invitation of King Charles, of His Majesty, I agreed to come to this meeting. “And it’s important that we engage in the world. The world is complicated, is complex, is turbulent, and in these uncertain times, it’s important [to be here] for Australia’s national interest.” Albanese has met British counterpart Andy Burnham and will tomorrow talk with Canadian leader Mark Carney at the summit, discussing how national economies deal with the energy price shocks from the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham holding the Rabbitohs hat he was given by Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese ahead of a bilateral meeting. Getty Images



At a press conference in Antigua on Monday, Albanese spoke of “middle powers” working together – a major theme in an address by Carney to the World Economic Forum in Davos. Switzerland earlier this year. While Carney argued that middle powers needed to help each other when US President Donald Trump was imposing tariffs and other penalties on allies, Albanese used the term without any direct criticism of the US. “This is an opportunity to engage with the countries in our region to show leadership on behalf of the Pacific, but also to engage with middle powers and to strengthen Australia’s economic position,” he said. “And it’s never been more important to connect with the world because the world has never been more interconnected.” He named trade, the global economy and the development of artificial intelligence as some of the issues to be discussed with other world leaders.



Howard attended each meeting of the Commonwealth Heads of Government during his time as prime minister. Related Article Updated

Political leadership Albanese warns world leaders of growing threat to democracy after Haines attack Taylor argued on Sunday that Albanese should not go to CHOGM because of the economic conditions at home, despite Howard’s example. “The reality is in a normal set of circumstances, of course, the prime minister should go to CHOGM – and John Howard is right on that,” Taylor said on 2GB on Sunday. “The problem is this is not a normal set of circumstances. We are going to have the seventeenth interest rate rise under Labor if the Reserve Bank moves on Tuesday, as is widely expected, and this is on the government’s watch.”



Taylor argued the government did not have spending under control and was not putting downward pressure on inflation and interest rates. The federal government’s gross debt is forecast to surpass $1 trillion this financial year. The budget papers do not forecast a surplus or specify a timeframe to paying off the debt, while interest payments continue to rise. While Treasurer Jim Chalmers claimed the budget in May delivered $26.1 billion in savings over several years, the budget deficit is tipped to deteriorate. It is forecast to be $28.2 billion this year and $31.5 billion next year. Asked whether the government was making enough savings in the budget to ease pressure on inflation, Albanese insisted he and the cabinet were acting on the economy. “My message to Australians is that we’ll continue to work each and every day to keep our economy stronger, and that includes engaging in global trade and engaging in the world,” Albanese said.



British Prime Minister Andy Burnham raised the prospect of more international travel for Albanese next year when the UK hosts the G20 summit in Manchester. Related Article King Charles III King Charles joins Albanese, Forrest aboard climate ship “We’ve got the chance, you and I, to cut the first steel on the first AUKUS sub sometime next year,” Burnham told Albanese when they meet on Monday night (about 11am on Tuesday, AEDT). The AUKUS submarine will be built to a design being used by the UK and Australia for a new fleet for the long-term, with the first of them to be made in Barrow-in-Furness, north of Liverpool. Albanese and Burnham also discussed Australia’s proposal for changes to the visa rules for young British working holiday makers so that more of them are required to work in regional areas to continue their visas. There was no announcement of any change.



Burnham prefaced his remarks to Albanese with words of sympathy for Victorian MP Helen Haines, who is recovering from an attack last month that forced surgeons to amputate both her legs. “We send our thoughts to Helen Haines,” Burnham said. He added that the attack on Haines raised broader questions about violence against politicians on all sides. Cut through the noise of federal politics with news, views and expert analysis. World.title: Alan Jones trial live updates: SMH journalist Kate McClymont asked about Herald articles in former 2GB broadcaster’s indecent assault, sexual touching trial
World.content:
Warning: Graphic content

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of former 2GB broadcaster Alan Jones’ indecent assault and sexual touching trial in the historic Downing Centre Local Court in Sydney.

Today, The Sydney Morning Herald’s chief investigative reporter, Kate McClymont, has been called to give evidence by the Crown.

Kate McClymont arrives at the Downing Centre Local Court this morning flanked by Herald editor Jordan Baker, left, and deputy editor Nick Ralston, right. Audrey Richardson

Jones, 85, is standing trial on 19 counts of indecent assault and two counts of sexual touching without consent against five male complainants between 2003 and 2020. He has pleaded not guilty to the charges and denies the alleged physical acts occurred.

All five complainants have now given evidence in court. The trial has heard McClymont spoke to three of the men when she was investigating allegations against the broadcaster, which culminated in a series of reports.

Support is available from the National Sexual Assault, Domestic Family Violence Counselling Service at 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732) or the Men’s Referral Service on 1300 766 491.

World.content:
